Heading: Hot seat - Indian Express
Content:
Mahilpur Football Academy will never like to remember this day as they were stunned by a brilliant fight-back by the Indian Football Association, Kolkata after they were sitting pretty with a 1-0 lead in the first half. Eventually, IFA Kolkata were rewarded for holding on to their nerves as they registered an emphatic 2-1 win over Mahilpur to sail into the semi-finals. IFA Kolkata will need many more such miracles in their semi-final bout with Chandigarh Football Association who are unbeaten in this tournament with five successive victories.

Both the Mahilpur and IFA Kolkata teams got number of opportunities to go up but their players failed to covert these into goals due to the pressure riding on them. However, it was Rajbir Singh senior who broke the deadlock in the 27th minute as he pounced on a perfect cross from left flank and executed a perfect volley which the IFA goalkeeper failed to stop. Both the team pushed harder, trying to outdo each other and come up with a goal. However, their quest was broken by a long whistle by the referee, signaling the end of the first half. The second half brought new players, and hence few flavour into the match. Barely three minutes had passed when IFA scored through Deepankar Sarkar's header in the 48th minute. The goal not only restored parity for the team but also infused a new life into the players. However, Prabhakar Naskar's produced the goal of the match-a sizzling 20-yard footer that proved to be the golden goal for their team as IFA cruised into the semis to lock horns with CFA.

Earlier, favourites Mohun Bagan thrashed Cantonment Senior Secondary School Board of Jalandhar by 10-0. They will compete with St Stephen's Academy for a final spot.

Chandigarh Football Association defeated Madhya Pradesh by 3-0 while Rohit Football Academy, Orissa got the better of Steadfast Football Academy, Mumbai by 5-3.

Heading: Eyeball to eyeball on Nano, Buddha, Mamata blink - Indian Express
Content:
Beautiful People

CNBC TV 18

Sunday, 1.30 pm

Rating ***

What's it about?Chat shows and interviews are hugely famous on Indian television and they cater to a wide audience. So for a new chat show to click, there has to be a very special element in it. As the name of the show suggests, it gets up, close and personal with the rich and the famous from the entertainment and sports industries. From professional alliances to personal lives, this talk show has your favourite celebrities sharing some special secrets and rare anecdotes.

Who's in it?The features editor of CNBC TV 18, Anuradha Sengupta, is the conventional host, asking questions, sharing anecdotes, keeping the viewers glued to the television set. Along with her warm appeal, she brings top-notch celebrities from various walks of life on the show. Beautiful Poeple promises to showcase some candid moments with superstars like Deepika Padukone, Lewis Hamilton, Aamir Khan and Farhan Akhtar.

What's hot?The show, although restricted to just the host and the guest, keeps you engaged, mainly because of its outdoorsy settings. Most of the episodes are shot at Out of the Blue, a Mumbai restaurant, and for each interview the set is designed in a unique manner to go with the mood and the personality of the guest. Sengupta makes for a good host, asking the more controversial questions in the most subtle manner. Her in depth knowledge of the subject and the way she strikes a rapport with her guests instantaneously is remarkable. The show begins with the introduction of the guest through childhood photographs, glimpses of achievements and special moments in his/her life.

What's not?The chat show sometimes reminds you of another popular talk show of yesteryear—Face to Face with Karan Thapar. The show like any other does get monotonous after a while, especially if the guest on a given day isn't quite on your favourites list. Also, the fact that the guest and the anchor are made to sit diagonally doesn't help the cameraman's cause, who is mindlessly panning his camera from one end to the other.

Should you be watching it?For the Bollywood lover, this is the ideal show to meet your favourite guests and get to know them better. And those wanting to peek into the lives of other interesting personalities, could tune into it once in a while and try their luck.

Heading: Govt forms society to develop software in Bangla - Indian Express
Content:
Singur TRUCE : Land-for-land with minimum disturbance is the broad agreement; Mamata suspends agitation

The two-year-old crisis over Singur which had forced the Tata Motors to think in terms of shifting the Nano car project out of West Bengal seemed headed for a resolution late tonight as a land-for-land agreement, first reported by The Indian Express, was reached at the first face-to-face meeting between West Bengal Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee and Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, capping three days of intense bargaining.

As part of the agreement, the state government will return land "to the maximum within the (Nano) project area and the rest in adjacent areas as early as possible" to all those farmers who have not taken compensation, Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi, who played a key role in talks between the two sides, told reporters at Raj Bhavan.

Banerjee, in turn, announced the immediate suspension of her party's two-year-old agitation on the issue and the fortnight-long sit-in demonstration at the factory site.

There was no immediate reaction from the Tatas who had earlier made it clear that there could be no compromise on the land holding pattern in Singur.

Reading from a prepared text of the understanding reached between the two sides, Gandhi said: "The government has taken the decision to respond to the demands of those farmers who have not received compensation, by means of land to be provided to the maximum within the project area and the rest in adjacent areas as early as possible. Towards this, a committee will be constituted to ascertain the scope and settle the modalities within a period of one week. During this time, the government will urge the vendors not to make any constructions. Mamata Banerjee is making an announcement regarding the suspension of the agitation from Singur. The government and those who have been agitating on behalf of the farmers will cooperate with each other for the benefit of the industry, agriculture and ancillaries."

The talks, marked by twists and turns, was salvaged from the verge of collapse this evening following a last-minute demand by Banerjee, after a consensus was reached earlier, that land of all farmers acquired of vendors of ancillary units of the Tata Motors Nano car plant at Singur be returned to farmers. The near-breakdown of talks was, however, resolved at the initiative of Gandhi.

After the meeting, Banerjee said: "It is a victory for us. You have seen how we have fought for the Singur farmers for the past two years. We are happy."

Bhattacharjee did not make any comment. The announcement of the truce was greeted with bursting of crackers in many parts of Kolkata. Celebrations were on at Singur too as Banerjee headed there to make a formal announcement.

Earlier in the day, CPM general secretary Prakash Karat, asked about Singur, told reporters in New Delhi: "We are of the view that the Tata's small car project goes ahead and measures are taken for rehabilitation of those affected."

The West Bengal Left Front committee also met at Alimuddin Street where Bhattacharjee briefed the partners about the land-based rehabilitation package that had been offered during the negotiations. The Front partners authorised him to seal the final rehabilitation package with the Opposition.

Heading: Battala locals, police rescue 65-yr-old woman from streets - Indian Express
Content:
The research centre plans to host 15,000 pages of Rabindra Rachanabali in unicode format on its website

The West Bengal government is forming an autonomous society to develop systems and software in Bangla and other regional languages.

"The Society for Natural Language Technology Research (SNLTR) is a part of government's initiative to popularise Bengali language and literature with the help of modern information technology," IT Minister Debesh Das said.

The IT department has already sanctioned Rs 1 crore for one year to the society, which is currently located at Salt Lake. The society has one government representative in its managing body.

For a start, SNLTR in collaboration with IIT Kharagpur and a private software development company will soon release "Baishakhi", a standardised Bangla Linux distribution software in public

domain.

The software will allow office computation in Bangla along with a Bengali spell check system integrated with the Bangla Linux system.

"The society is working on standardisation of Bengali codes and a unicode compliant Bangla keyboard layout," Das said. Computer experts believe that Bangla texts lack standardisation, which makes the output neither universally accessible nor usable, unlike English. The society promises to make Bengali user-friendly on computers and create language resources, systems and devices.

SNLTR, in collaboration with Bengal Engineering and Science University, has begun work on a Bangla dictionary and a word list in accordance with the Paschim Banga Bangla Academy spelling convention.

The society plans to host 15,000 pages of Rabindra Rachanabali in unicode format on its website.

With IIT Kharagpur as its research centre, the society will also create a search engine of indexed and categorised Bengali literary works.

"We will also create a script of Tagore's musical notes in a computer software format. We are taking the help of IIT Kharagpur in this endeavour," said professor Dwijesh Kumar Dutta Majumder, president, SNLTR.

"We will collect multidimensional databases of modern Bangla texts in electronic format and analyse them with the help of computer technology," Majumder added.

The research centre will also develop tools and software like optical character recognition system for printed Bengali script to assess the accuracy of scripts.

Heading: City beautification project fails to take off - Indian Express
Content:
A Group of locals and police came to the rescue of a 65-year-old woman who had taken shelter in the portico of a house on Hari Ghosh Street in Battala.

Three days ago, when locals saw the woman in the area they did not pay any heed to her, but those who did, were surprised to find out that she was an MA in Political Science from the Calcutta University.

"The way she spoke to us indicated that she was educated," said Mohan Karmakar, a resident of Hari Ghosh Street.

She told the locals that she was Aparajita Ghosh and was a resident of Sinthee in north Kolkata.

She claimed that her parents died a long time ago and she did not have any relatives. The house that she lived in had to be sold off due to debts.

"Ghosh told us that she had been living on the streets in Sinthee for quite sometime," Mohan said. The locals fed her for the next two days.

"She had only a sheet of cloth to cover herself," Mohan added. She was, however, not ready to move into anyone's house.

Considering her condition, the locals then informed the police.

"Initially, we thought that the woman was another vagabond and we would have to shift her to an old age home. But we were surprised when she started speaking," said a police officer who had gone to pick up Ghosh.

The police said the woman was recently injured and was admitted to the RG Kar Hospital. But after she was discharged in August, she landed up at Hari Ghosh Street.

The police have admitted Ghosh to the Calcutta Medical College Hospital. "We hope she finds a proper place to spend her life," a police officer said.

Heading: Metro withdraws ladies coaches from trains - Indian Express
Content:
"Mission Beautification" — a project undertaken by the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) to beautify major street crossings in the city — has failed to take off even two years after its conception.

According to a civic official, KMC has received thousands of applications from several private companies seeking permission to beautify the crossings.

The applicants fulfill all the criteria given by the corporation, but the proceedings of the advertisings and parks department are causing the delay.

The KMC official said the companies would be given the go-ahead on the condition that they would not use the beautified portion for commercial purpose.

Besides, if any company puts up a hoarding mentioning its name on it, it will have to pay a tax to the civic body.

"We were facing some problems in the project. But we expect that the "Mission Beautification" will be executed soon," Mayor Bikash Bhattacharya said.

The civic body had invited private companies to beautify major crossings in the city in August 2006, after which, the area near Uttam Kumar's statue near the Tollygunge Metro station was beautified by a private company. However, private players are still waiting for the KMC's nod to beautify other city crossings like Park Circus Seven-Point crossing, Shyambazar crossing, Beckbagan and Gariahat crossings.

Heading: China inaugurates its consulate in Kolkata - Indian Express
Content:
The Metro Rail, Kolkata, has withdrawn the new system of special ladies compartments in its trains with effect from September 8. The authorities have now decided to revert back to the old system of reserved seats for women in all compartments.

"After commuters started complaining that the new system was inconvenient for both men and women, we have decided to go back to the old system," a spokesperson for Metro Railways said.

"Reserving two compartments for women at the two ends of the train served no purpose. Commuters arriving at the last moment and those in a hurry tend to board these reserved compartments," said Ishita Sengupta, a daily commuter on the Shovabazar-Maidan route.

According to authorities, Metro motormen had to face the commuter's fury, as the new system was chaotic. Moreover, with two compartments reserved for women, the other six used to witness a heavy rush of commuters. The Metro authorities had introduced the two reserved coaches for women on a two-month trial on September 1.

Content:
The relationship between India and China is growing stronger, said Chinese Foreign Minister Yang Jiechi, who inaugurated the Chinese consulate in Kolkata on Sunday.

"The inauguration of Chinese consulate in Kolkata is a good sign and it shows the sincerity of China in improving its relations with India. Your foreign minister is a good friend of mine and tomorrow I am going to meet him. You will get the answers of your questions tomorrow," Jiechi said when asked why China played a hostile role at the Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) meeting at Vienna.

Minister for External Affairs Pranab Mukherjee, who attended a book launch programme at the Kolkata Press Club, refused to comment on China's role at Vienna saying that it was China's internal matter.

"China and India have a long history of mutual cooperation. The two countries together formulated the doctrine of Panchsheel. We are ready to work with India. The improved relation between the two developing countries has its roots in the common aspirations of their people. I am confident that China and India will enjoy a long-term friendship," Jiechi said.

"When poet Rabindranath Tagore visited China, he wrote that he felt at home in our country. I also feel at home in Kolkata. I was a small boy when I first heard about this city. This city is the cradle of culture and civilisation and my next visit to the city will be soon," the Chinese foreign minister added.

Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi, who was also present at the function, said the opening of the consulate would mark a new era of friendship between the two countries.

Heading: China Foreign Minister to meet Pranab today: you will have all answers on our stand in Vienna - Indian Express
Content:
Sonja is a waitress in a countryside restaurant in the Bernese plateau of Switzerland. Engaged to her boss, she has a secure life-plan. Until a Bollywood film crew lands up for a shoot. The highly gifted cook of the crew woos her relentlessly and soon she is faced with a dilemma — a choice between security and status on one side and passion and magic on the other...

Bollywood film crews have been coming to Switzerland for decades to shoot dream sequences or honeymoons. And now, Switzerland hits back with its own home-grown Bollywood film, Tandoori Love. Made in the Swiss German dialect and English, the film was premiered before a packed audience at the lakeside open-air theatre in Zurich last Saturday.

The film takes a comic look at the clash of two totally different, rather contrasting cultures. "I love Indian culture and its chaos," says Oliver Paulus, writer-director of the film. "And you can imagine what happens when this chaos enters a Swiss village where everything is so perfectly organised." He says he had often heard irate hotel and restaurant owners swear they would never again want to have an Indian film crew in their midst. But over the years this attitude has changed. People are more open-minded now and they see the advantage it brings — India is one of the fastest growing tourism markets for this country, thanks to Bollywood.

"Tandoori Love is not a Bollywood film, it is a film completely different from anything you've ever seen. It is presenting Bollywood to a Swiss audience in a way that can be more palatable to them" insists Paulus. Isn't Bollywood already well accepted and understood by Swiss audiences? "No," he says. "Bollywood film screenings are confined to Arthouse Cinema and viewed by intellectuals who have an interest in alternative cultures." Or perhaps are watched by the immigrants comprising Turkish, East European and Middle Eastern nationalities.

But with so many songs, such emotions and drama, Tandoori Love does come across as being in the same genre as the thousands churned out in Mumbai's dream factory, with a few Swiss characters and situations thrown in.

Paulus chose the cast very carefully, subjecting even well-known actors to a screen test. Lavinia Wilson, a German actress, aspiring to make it big in Hollywood plays Sonja (pronounced Sonia). Vijay Raaz, whom we all know from numerous Hindi movies but remember most for his comic role in Monsoon Wedding, "is a marvellous actor," according to Paulus. Shweta Agarwal (whom we know from TV serial Dekho Magar Pyaar Se) plays the tantrum throwing diva who, accompanied by her mom on shooting sets, is giving the director and the producer (played by Ganesh Yadav and Aasif Sheikh) constant jitters.

He says he did a lot of research for the film, saw hundreds of Hindi movies including A, B and C grade ones, studied the lives and work of cooks in India, met dozens of film personalities in order to write the story (actually co-write with Stefen Hillebrand) from two different points of view, bringing in the mutual prejudices that the two cultures have towards each other. Incidentally, the Indians are often referred to as "Tamils" an epithet that has a slightly pejorative connotation here in the aftermath of the Jaffna war that brought almost 25,000 Sri Lankan Tamil refugees to this country. Over the years, these Tamils have actually endeared themselves to the native population with their hardworking, docile and clean ways. But they nevertheless remain consigned to the lowest rungs of Swiss society, as they perform mostly menial jobs. Whereas the Indian expatriates here, some of whom might be Tamils, constitute a highly skilled segment of the workforce.

Born in 1969 in Dornach, a small town near Basel, Oliver Paulus studied film making in Germany's Baden Wüttemberg and won several awards and worldwide acclaim for his earlier films like "When the right one comes along", "So long, my heart" etc. Is there a common strain that runs in all of his movies? "There is," he admits. "All my movies have as their leading character an underdog, who has a dream, wants to achieve something and has to fight for it. I find the subject emotionally touching, when there is someone on the fringes of society but is proud of himself, believes in himself and strives for something." In Tandoori Love, Raaja, the cook, is such an underdog.

Is there a scope for more such films based on Bollywood themes? "I don't see much space for that. But who knows, that might just happen." He expects the film to strike a chord with the NRI populations worldwide as he thinks most NRIs may be able to relate to the clash of cultures as shown in the movie.

The film was screened in Zurich under the auspices of the Gruezi India festival organised by the Indian Association of Zurich to commemorate 60 years of Indo-Swiss Friendship Treaty. It is now slated for a screening at the Goa film festival in November which would be attended by the Swiss prime minister.

Heading: Cheers to Couture - Indian Express
Content:
Why is BJP shouting? Only following Atal govt policy on test moratorium: Pranab

A day after the Nuclear Suppliers Group granted India a waiver for nuclear trade, Chinese Foreign Minister Yang Jiechi arrived here on a three-day visit to India but declined to comment on his country's stand at Vienna which upset New Delhi a great deal.

Scheduled to meet External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee in New Delhi tomorrow, Yang Jiechi, who formally inaugurated the Chinese consulate in Kolkata, told reporters: "You will have all the answers tomorrow."

Earlier, Mukherjee, who too was in Kolkata, refused to comment on the Chinese stand. "I would not like to comment on what role was played by which country. This is their internal matter. Every country has its right to express its own sovereign will. As far as China's Foreign Minister's visit to India is concerned, he is a distinguished guest. I welcome him," he said.

Mukherjee hit out at the BJP for running down the Vienna agreement, reminding the party that it was the NDA government under Atal Behari Vajpayee which had declared a unilateral moratorium on nuclear testing after the 1998 Pokharan-II tests and the UPA government was following the same policy.

"Why is the BJP shouting now?" Mukherjee said, adding he had spent "the whole of Friday night" talking to counterparts in countries which were reluctant to give India the NSG waiver. As reported by The Sunday Express, New Delhi had to summon the Chinese envoy in New Delhi — around 3 am Saturday — to convey a demarche for acting contrary to the earlier assurance of not blocking a consensus.

Can test if warranted: Kalam
* US Secretary of State Condoleeza Rice says time "very short" for Cong approval of deal
* Former President A P J Abdul Kalam says India can conduct a nuclear test "in supreme national interest" if international situation warrants
* Congress president Sonia Gandhi meets Prime Minister, congratulates him on NSG waiver
* CPM's Prakash Karat says party goal will now be to see that the next government takes steps to terminate the 123 Agreement

Heading: Basu in hospital, under observation for 7 days - Indian Express
Content:
India's first Couture Week is carrying forward the leftover legacy of high fashion

When bespoke clothes were a rarity in the rest of the world, India munificently subscribed to the theory of couture and luxury. And now with the inaugural HDIL India Couture Week starting in Mumbai on September 16, the celebrated dressmakers of the country have an excuse for extravaganza, an event to extol high fashion — with all its expensive frills.

"The market for couture is huge; this was long overdue," says Sunil Sethi, president, Fashion Design Council of India (FDCI), who has been toying with the idea for long and has finally etched out a schedule. And names that tickle the aesthete's senses — Anamika Khanna, Ashish Soni, JJ Valaya, Manav Gangwani, Manish Malhotra, Pallavi Jaikishan, Ritu Kumar, Rohit Bal, Suneet Varma, Tarun Tahiliani and Varun Bahl — will come together.

Some may have doubted if couture would survive its founder, Charles Worth, but Tahiliani says there is a reason it thrived in India: its fabled luxury belongs more to the world of couture than it ever did to pret. "Detailed designs with semi-precious metals woven into clothes are what we adore. It is therefore befitting that we have a Couture Week to service bridal wear and elevate it with contemporary finishes," he says.

The hopelessly old-fashioned styles and the price tags, starting at five figures, however, ensured that couture clients weren't many. "But in a country appropriately named Golden Peacock, luxe clothing is still a passion and has been part of our heritage for hundreds of years. The extreme lifestyles of Indian maharajas and the grandeur of Indian costumes and textiles are legendary," says Bal.

For Bahl, couture is what strikes a balance between invigorating styles and fantasy. But for Kumar, the Couture Week has been the much required outing for Indian textiles. "Of late, many Indians have been associating couture with the luxury brands of Europe. The Couture Week is going to be an eye-opener for India's indigenous textiles," says Kumar.

The event, which will be held at the Grand Hyatt from September 16 to 21, will have just two shows a day. "It isn't just clothes, but the settings and choreography too will be worth a watch," says Tahiliani, who feels the week will be in complete contrast to the pret weeks. "This is going to be theatrical," he promises.

Heading: Folkata Confata - Indian Express
Content:
Veteran CPM leader Jyoti Basu was admitted to the AMRI Hospitals around 11.35 am on Sunday after a CT scan conducted on Saturday revealed a blood clot in his brain. On Friday, Basu had injured himself when he fell down in the bathroom of his Indira Bhavan residence in Salt Lake.

According to the doctors, though his condition is stable, Basu will be kept under observation for the next seven days.

He is under the supervision of a 10-member medical Board led by Dr R N Bhattacharya with Dr M K Chettri as the chief adviser.

A medical bulletin released by the AMRI Hospital authorities stated: "He is fully conscious and oriented. A CT scan done yesterday revealed a collection of blood clots on the brain surface (Left Hemispherical Acute on Chronic Subdural Haematoma)."

It added: "The management of such a condition is (done by) removal of clot by Minimal Invasive Neurosurgery. The final decision on the operative process will be taken after detailed assessment, especially his cardiac status, by the medical board."

State Transport Minister Subhas Chakraborty and his wife Ramala accompanied Basu until he was

admitted to the hospital. Later, External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee paid a visit to Basu.

Mukherjee's visit was followed by that of Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee and state Health Minister Surjya Kanta Mishra.

Mishra, who is a doctor himself, said after visiting Basu: "I have spoken to him. His condition is

stable, but will be under observation. There is no need for surgery at the moment."

Heading: Bhiwani Boys to grace boxing bastion Kolkata - Indian Express
Content:
From Singur to Raj Bhavan

The marathon meetings at the Raj Bhavan during the last three days over the Singur deadlock had its own share of light moments.

Becharam Manna, convenor of the Singur Krishi Jomi Rakkha Committee, was awestruck by the grandeur of the Governor's house.

Manna, a person with humble background, was so enthralled by costly chandeliers, furniture and artifacts of the Raj Bhavan that he could not stop himself from getting photographed. He took out his mobile and clicked his own photo with the walls of the Bhavan forming his background.

Later, after having lunch with Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi, he was heard saying, "I never dreamt of entering Raj Bhavan, let alone having lunch with the Governor."

Choked expressway, hounded officials

Nowadays, the officials of National Highway Authorities of India (NHAI) are a harried lot of people. Since the Calcutta High Court directed the NHAI to clear the choked stretch of Durgapur Expressway in Singur which has been overtaken by Trinamool Congress supporters, the officials are being "hounded" by mediapersons.

With the situation at the expressway showing no signs of improvement, journalists are leaving no stone unturned to question the NHAI officials. "The media would hound me all through the day and it was becoming difficult for us to step outdoors. I had gone out to the local market to buy vegetables and even there I was stalked. It made my life a hell," said a senior official of the NHAI at Durgapur.

A nostalgic Subhash defends auto drivers

Reminiscing one's youthful days is always a riveting experience. But when a maverick minister like

Subhash Chakrabarty treads the nostalgic path at a public function, it makes everyone sit up and listen.

During a recent interactive session at the Bengal National Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BNCCI), the state transport minister defended the autorickshaw drivers of Kolkata in a unique way.

"They (the autorickshaw drivers) can never be a minister like me or a businessman like you. Even if we would like to, we cannot put an end to autorickshaws. Most of the drivers are young people. They remind me of myself 27 years ago when I did not even dream of being a minister, let alone being a minister for 27 years," Chakrabarty said.

Shaping policies the MIT way

Finance Minister Asim

Dasgupta's association with Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) is a well-known fact.

That he inspires the state government policies with the lessons of his MIT connection became obvious at a recent public function organised by the state education department. There Dasgupta spoke about his rendezvous with MIT's most famous professor of linguistics Noam Chomsky and how those meetings influenced some of the policies of the state government.

"In 1977, when we met Noam Chomsky, he had emphasised on the need for learning the mother tongue. So, our decision of withdrawing English at primary level was not wrong," Dasgupta said referring to the Left Front's government decision to withdraw English as a subject in primary schools during the 70s. Dasgupta did not stop there. "Around five years ago, when Chomsky had visited Kolkata, I had the privilege of interacting with him again. He had then spoken on the importance of learning English. We later decided to reintroduce English at the primary level considering the changed scenario," Dasgupta added.

'Obey traffic rules or join CPM rally'

The CPM's grand rally on September 1 had thrown the city traffic out of gear and the traffic policemen had a tough time trying to bring in some order on the streets. With CPM supporters virtually seizing Kolkata's main roads, some traffic policemen even lost their temper. When a taxi driver tried to bypass a "no entry" sign, a traffic sergeant was seen unleashing his fury.

When the driver tried to argue, the policeman retorted: "Why are you arguing with me? Go and ask your leaders. Go and ask Biman Bose. If you can't obey traffic rules, go and join the rally instead."

CAB's mantra:

award the losers

Jagmohan Dalmiya-led Cricket Association of Bengal's (CAB) top brass did the unthinkable this week when it appointed the coaching responsibility of the state's talented Under-19 team to a person who had recently flunked in the official examination for basic-coaching.
Madan Ghosh, a stalwart cricket coach in Maidan, recently failed to clear the Level 'A' coaching license examination conducted by the

country's cricket board.

Just two days after this embarrassment, the CAB pompously

appointed Ghosh as the U-19 coach amid protests from various sections of cricketing community.

Heading: For me, Puia’s paper has always been clean: Karim - Indian Express
Content:
Vijender, Jitender in city for promo, felicitation programmes : Selector stunt in Bhatinda deals Qamar knock-out blow

A little over two weeks after Vijender and Jitender Kumar took Indian boxing to dizzy heights with a heady show in the 2008 Beijing Olympics, the star pugilist duo is scheduled to spend almost the whole of Monday attending a number of programmes in the city.

The Bhiwani boxers will be felicitated for their Olympic achievement here this evening at a city hotel by a popular shares and securities agency. Plans are on to ferry Vijender and Jitender around at a couple of boxing hotspots in Kolkata. The city, which produced Md Ali Qamar, used to be a traditionally boxing powerhouse till recently.

Meanwhile, the controversy over ther handling of Md Ali Qamar at the ongoing Nationals in Bhatinda, Punjab, seems to have left a bad taste in the mouth. Just as India's first ever Commonwealth Games gold medal winning boxer was preparing to relaunch himself after an injury-marred sabbatical, in the 2008 Nationals, he was left surprised by the Indian Boxing Federation's (IBF) decision to make him a selector.

"I was surprised on being told that I have been made a selector. At first I thought my coach was joking when he broke the news to me. I thought I would compete this year (representing Railways) and test myself," said the 28-year-old, who is in Bhatinda now for the big event.

"Par chalo dekhte hain (but let's see what I have to do). I haven't decided, I am still confused," added Qamar, whose last appearance at the Nationals was in 2006 in Hyderabad where he lost in the first round itself.

Qamar was made selector during the IBF's elections last Friday. The panel also has World Cup bronze medalist V Devarajan and 1962 Asian Games gold medalist Padam Bhadaur Mal.

The three-time national champion, who picked up a nagging nose injury soon after his 2002 Manchester Commonwealth Games gold, says he still has the power and motivation to compete. With the Indian Boxing Federation planning a pro-league, he is tempted to take the plunge.

"I know I have a career left in the ring. If at 27, Akhil Kumar can be a world class boxer, so can I, since I am just a year senior to him. I don't know what to do right now," he said.

Qamar recalled the phase after the 2002 Commomwealth Games, saying: "Railways promised me a double promotion, but I got only one in 2002 and I refused that. In 2004, I was offered another promotion, but this time, I accepted after being told that the second promotion would follow. I wish I been told about it in 2002. But that's a closed chapter now. But tell me, is it my job to run after officials with my certificates?"

He continued: "Now, they tell me that my achievements are old. I was the best boxer of the 2003 Nationals, I have six medals in the seven Nationals I competed in, and three of them are gold. I don't know what to say."

The 2002 Commonwealth Games gold remains the most cherished memory of his career but if there is one regret that the pint-sized pugilist has, it is missing out on competing at the Olympics.

"How I wish, I could have done that. I missed out by a whisker during Athens Olympics qualifiers. That was the lowest point of my career. I have competed everywhere but couldn't make the Olympics and that hurts," he said.

For somebody who started boxing at the age of 10, the sport is now an addiction and once he is done with landing blows himself, Qamar plans to teach his tricks to the upcoming talents as coach.

In fact, he already coaches at a couple of academies in his home state of Bengal and plans to do a course from NIS Patiala before making coaching a full-fledged career.

"Coaching has always been on my mind, but I don't plan to open an academy. I want to go and teach everywhere. But I will do a course from NIS," he said.

With Indian boxing at an all time high, close to 350 pugilists are vying for the honours in what promises to be an electrifying senior Men's Championship in the backdrop of Vijender Singh, Akhil Kumar and Jitender Kumar's glorious Olympic performance in Beijing.

Vijender, the Olympic bronze winner in the middle-weight category, Akhil (54kg) and Jitender (51kg) will, however, skip the meet as they recover from the aftermath of a euphoric but draining Olympics, landing a major blow to defending champions Railways' hopes of retaining the title.

Vijender, in fact, has ended his Railways stint by taking over as a DSP in Haryana Police. Akhil and Jitender, however, are yet to decide on whether to stay with Railways or take over as DSPs in Haryana Police.

Heading: Narratives of Memory - Indian Express
Content:
PC Lalwampuia was in a deep dark dungeon. But in that darkness was a flicker of light. The young Mohun Bagan striker followed that light and got out of the jail.

Last year, Lalawmpuia had hit the headlines for all the wrong reasons. On many an occasion he had transgressed the disciplinary codes. Carlos Pereira, who coached Bagan last season, took the easiest way out, which was to distance himself from the player. Still, Lalawmpuia's talent convinced the club officials and his team-mates to keep faith in him. In came the new coach Karim Bencherifa and helped resurrect the footballer's career.

With 8 goals from 12 CFL Premier Division matches this season, Lalawmpuia has become the darling of the Bagan crowd. Bencherifa, however, feels he is yet to hit his peak and has miles to go before he makes a mark at the international level.

"I had a one-on-one with him after I took over. I told him, as far as I was concerned his paper was absolutely clean. I was not at all concerned over what had happened in the past. But I also told him that if he didn't meet his professional responsibilities, he would be out," Bencherifa told The Indian Express.

Pep talk apart, what are the other factors that brought about the change? "He is getting a lot more balls in the penetrative zone this time. We have been playing attacking football, which suits his style of play. For a player to get out of the hole, nothing can be better than on-field success. He is getting support upfront that is helping him in scoring goals. The beauty of this side is that we have an excellent team spirit and the players back each other. Lalawmpuia did all the hard work all right, but without the support from his colleagues he couldn't have turned the corner."

The coach has a word of caution though. "Success can be short-lived if you don't make it a habit. He has the potential to be an asset for the Indian team. The Asian Cup should be his target. And to meet the target he has to be consistent. He is going through a learning curve and will have to travel a fair distance before he becomes a force at the international level. His skipper Baichung Bhutia should be his role model," Bencherifa observed.

Indeed, Baichung and also Jose Barreto have been playing a big role to keep Lalawmpuia focused. In fact, they persuaded the club management to continue with the youngster for one more year. They were right on the money.

Meanwhile, Bagan coach keeps his fingers crossed as far as the CFL title is concerned. A win over George Telegraph on Tuesday is likely to see them through. "It would be just another match for us that we aim to win. We are playing good football and the best thing is that the boys don't give up till the last minute. That has been reflected in our performance," Bencherifa concluded.

Heading: Managing Act - Indian Express
Content:
Histories and memories always had the best stories to tell. Stories that were inspirations and eye-openers, stories made of realities and half-truths. And stories that could unfurl in movements and melodies. Such a story, it is, of the Parsi community in India and danseuse Mallika Sarabhai lost no time in unearthing the potential for a visual treat that lay hidden under the dog-ears of history. Thus we have And Then They Came To India, a dance theatre scripted and directed by Sarabhai which will be in Kolkata on September 12. "The idea of communicating history in a colourful and lively manner always interested me. The close-knit Parsi community, and their influence in the cultural landscape of India is something that fascinated me," says Sarabhai. Reason why she decided to mix the myths with the truths, the past with the promises, and bring the untold out of the closet. And Then They... opens with tales from the times preceding the birth of Zarathustra, progresses to exploring the birth of Zoroastrianism, the rise of Islam and culminates in the final escape of the Parsis to India.

"Dance theatre is literally a mingling of dance, theatre and story telling, in the form of a sutradhar, here a spinning dervish," says Sarabhai. There is very little that the Parsis have, in dance forms so to speak, so the danseuse incorporated Middle Eastern influences in her work.

Recreation of the past remains largely incomplete without costumes and Sarabhai saw to it, that And Then They...turned out to be closest to the historic reality. "The costumes were created after intensive research, from Persian paintings and books on Zoroastrianism that I got from my Parsi friends," says Sarabhai. The performance that will be touring 18 cities, which comes in a 45-minute package, has music scored by Jaya Nair, Darpana Musicians and Eero Hameenniemi and will also feature Sarabhai's daughter Anahita Sarabhai.

Condensing a cultural history into a 45-minute performance couldn't have been easy. The task was daunting and the Persian history has stories that could 'last several nights', but Sarabhai wanted colour in her creation. "I chose things that were fun to enact and could be beautifully visualised and realised. Of course, I did have to dramatise the very important bits of history also," says the danseuse.

Parsi history, like most others, is dramatic and eventful. It's just that it is neither talked about extensively, nor featured regularly in creative endeavours. This made Dr Villoo Morawala Patell, founder of Avesthagen Limited, a life sciences corporation, throw his weight behind Sarabhai's creation. "The way Mallika conceptualises and retells stories we might have heard hundred times over is fascinating," says Patell.

So, how does the danseuse expect a culture-specific production like And Then They... to reach out to a cross-section of audience? "Kolkata always had an eye for history — even if it isn't its own. And with the recent Tata Nano stand-off, it might be a good time to rethink what the Parsis stand for," she laughs.

Heading: Jungle Raj - Indian Express
Content:
With Indian bands becoming bigger and popular, the band manager has become indispensable. But what do the mini Brian Epsteins do?

Delhi's electronic outfit Jalebee Cartel is busy making music for their upcoming gig in Mumbai, but it is Ritnika Nayan, their manager, who has been working late nights and early mornings for the past two weeks. She is getting everything, apart from music, in place for the show. "The money aspect has been negotiated with the promoters, and I have to finalise the logistics and travel details," says Nayan, as she awaits the band's flight tickets and hotel bookings.

Coordinating everything from the band's travel and business deals to recording contracts and endorsements, the managers, the mini Brian Epsteins, make sure that their mini Beatles can focus on music. "Managing a band means taking care of every aspect of the singers' lives, leaving them free to concentrate on their music," says Vijay Nair, 24, who started his company Only Much Louder six years ago and manages acts like Pentagram, The Raghu Dixit Project and Them Clones, among others.

Dhruv Jagasia, 28, has been managing the folk-rock band Indian Ocean for the past two years and is presently travelling with them for their back-to-back shows in South Africa. "Before the show, I make sure the sound check starts on time and all other technical aspects are taken care of," he says, "and during the show I emcee and network with people."

While it is not a conventional career, it seems to be becoming a viable one. "If a band does well, we do well and vice-versa," explains Nayan. While a manager can earn anything up to Rs 50,000 a month, it can go higher depending on the artist one is managing. "It is a seasonal business, since the number of shows goes down in summer," says Jagasia, who also manages MiDival Punditz. When he is not a band manager, he moonlights as an RJ and actor.

Most well known bands get 6 to 20 shows a month, while some like Indian Ocean have 85 shows a year. And their managers have their hands full. "Sometimes I feel I'm a travel agent. I'm always booking airline tickets," grins Nayan. But next she will be booking tickets to India as she is planning to fly down international artists. Subir Malik, whose company Parikrama Inc. manages Soulmate, Mohit Chauhan and Bandish, says, "Sometimes you get bands who have really bad attitude." Nair adds, "It's natural for something to go wrong before or during a show. It is up to the manager to set it right," says Nair. Their bands may not evoke Beatles-like frenzy, but there are some Epsteins in the making.

Heading: Anyonya Co-op Bank on revival path - Indian Express
Content: The National School of Drama is ready with its new production —  German playwright Bertolt Brecht's In The Jungle of Cities that has been adapted as Mahanagro Ke Jungal Mein. The multilayered story deals with a wealthy merchant and a clerk locked in a battle between commerce and idealism. "India is fast turning into a society that upholds all kinds of indulgence. One cannot survive without working, and this is where the commercial structure steps in," says director Robin Das, who graduated from the NSD in 1976. Though the elaborate sets and costumes recreate Chicago of 1912, Das has given the play a strong Bollywood feel with bright colours, a peppy opening song and hip-swaying dances. The characters retain their original name— Shlink, Garga, Jan— but mouth Hindi dialogues. "Changing the setting to Delhi and giving the characters Indian names would have been underestimating the intelligence of the audience," says Das, who believes the aesthetics, the message and, of course, the irrepressible need for entertainment will draw people to his play.

Heading: MSU commerce faculty gets new officiating dean - Indian Express
Content:
Authorities hold extended AGM; decide to form a nine-member committee to work towards the revival of the bank

In an extended Annual General Meeting (AGM), which continued for more than five hours on Sunday, authorities of the Anyonya Cooperative Bank Limited (ACBL) have decided to form a nine-member committee to work towards the revival of the bank.

ACBL, Asia's first cooperative bank, has been struggling since September 14, 2007, when it was put under Section 35 of the Banking Regulation Act. The bank incurred a loss of Rs 1.42 crore and closed in March 2008 due to non-functioning.

Sunday's AGM, however, discussed a detailed revival plan, which included inviting shareholders and merging with the Maharasthra-based Saraswat Cooperative Bank and other cooperative banks, said ACBL authorities.

The meeting also discussed issuing preferential shares and other long term deposits to infuse around Rs 60-65 crore and revive the bank's functioning. Three to four reputed industrial houses are willing to help the bank at this critical time. However Prataprao Bhoite, ACBL, Vice President (VP) refused to divulge any details.

Bhoite said: "We will put our best efforts to revive the bank. One of the main agendas to be discussed at the AGM will be the appointment of a vice- president and a president in ACBL."

He added: "ACBL has three nominees for the post of president, while nominations for the post of VP are yet to be determined."

Heading: Woman pushes sons to well, jumps into it - Indian Express
Content:
The M S University has appointed Prof Ashok Hingorani as the new officiating dean of the Commerce Faculty a month after Prof Parimal Vyas resigned as the officiating dean. The university authorities accepted Prof Vyas's resignation on Saturday.

Prof Hingorani is the senior most professor in the Commerce Faculty and has been persuaded to accept the offer although he was reluctant earlier.

It is learnt that Prof Vyas resigned after he allegedly felt humiliated over an admission of a student who was backed by a local political leader.

Prof Ramesh Goyal, MSU Vice Chancellor (VC) said: "Prof Vyas resigned due to personal reasons and now Prof Hingorani has been appointed as the new officiating dean of the Commerce Faculty. He has 33 years of experience with him."

It is to be noted that it was only in January this year that Prof Vyas was appointed as the officiating dean after Prof SK Singh completed his two terms as Commerce Faculty dean.

Prof Vyas refused to assign any reason for his resignation. He said: "It has been seven months that I have served as an officiating dean. I express my gratitude towards the university authorities who have accepted my resignation, tendered a month ago." Incidentally, Prof Hingorani and Prof Vyas, both happen to be from the department of Commerce and Business Administration.

Prof Vyas said: "I will continue to be the Head of Department (HoD) of the department."

Heading: Cops reluctant to wield ‘mouse’ - Indian Express
Content:
A Thirty-year-old woman committed suicide by jumping into a well after pushing her two sons into it. One of them, however, managed to survive.

According to Sehra police, Kailash Solanki first pushed Vijay (4) and then Dilip (8) into the well, on the outskirts of Tarsam village near Sehra in Panchmahals district on Saturday evening. Vijay held on to the roots in the well and survived. Villagers came to his rescue after hearing his cries for help. Kailash and Dilip were already dead by the time the villagers arrived.

Vijay was taken to the Sehra Government Dispensary for treatment. The police are yet to take his side of the story as the child is undergoing treatment.

Sehra police said family dispute between Kailash's husband and her brothers could be the reason behind the incident. A complaint has been filed by Kailash's husband Khummansinh Jaswantsinh Solanki. The police do not rule out foul play as a land dispute is going on between Jaswantsinh Solanki and his four brothers.

Heading: Radio jockeying is now music to youngsters’ ears - Indian Express
Content:
The state government's ambitious project to cyber-connect police stations across the state by October seems to have hit a road block. A large number of police personnel, mostly of the rank of sub-inspectors and assistant sub-inspectors are reluctant to handle the 'mouse.' They say the Rs 900 fees for the programme and the certificate examination is too high, given their salary, though the police department has said that the amount will be refunded.

Senior police officers said that since the last two years, the deadline to make the staff computer literate is being extended, but it has not made any impact at the grassroots level. The police top brass across the state has, nevertheless, made computer literacy 'unofficially' mandatory for promotions.

An IPS officer said on condition of anonymity: "It is like 'charity begins at home' situation. Those who are imposing computer literacy are themselves not interested in holding the mouse because they have either neared their retirement age or lack an interest in computers. The project has seen countless deadlines and if stringent parameters are not officially set, the situation will continue to remain the same."

Senior officers said the Home Department Integrated Information Technology (HDIIT) software is expected to bring a sea change in policing. The project plans to connect all the police stations in the state and will start from the cities and slowly percolate down to the district level. But to operate on the HDIIT interface at least 30 per cent of the police force in a police station must be computer literate.

Sub-Inspector M K Motwani, who is the computer centre in-charge at Vadodara said the project will be officially launched in October 2008. "The HDIIT project for the police department, which is initiated in collaboration with a private firm, is expected to standardise police reporting formats including the First Information Report and inquest," said Motwani.

He added: "Under the system, each Investigating Officer for a particular case will himself enter the data of the case on the computer. Initially, two persons from a private data entry firm will assist the police officers. The server will be based in Gandhinagar where the data will be stored."

...but middle-rung officers eager to learn computer basics
With speculations rife about HDIIT, there is a mad rush among the policemen, especially those in the middle-rung, to learn basic computer concepts. A policeman from Vadodara said on condition of anonymity that though it's hard on the pocket to pay Rs 900 for the training and examination, given their salary of Rs 4,000, they have to take the test to advance their career prospects. Vadodara Police Commissioner Rakesh Asthana said the training for the policemen is government sponsored. Another senior police officer said if the policemen are spending money from their own pockets to learn computer, it will be refunded back.

Heading: 2 new medical colleges in state soon - Indian Express
Content:
The high of climbing the corporate ladder and the lure of the boardroom seems to be fading fast. Youngsters of Ahmedabad are now looking at life with a much wider perspective. With radio-jockeying in their mind, they want to air their views with some intelligent talking.

In 2001, just about 1,400 candidates had turned up to try RJing at the city's first ever RJ hunt. Now, not less than 1,000 candidates per RJ hunt queue up for the job. From medical students, MBA and engineering students, doctors, lawyers, BPO and call centre employees, almost everybody forms part of the wannabe RJ crowd.

Jignesh Vasavada, the Cluster Programming head of a radio channel said: "In the coming years apart from the already established job profiles, a lot of new job profiles will be created. RJs will thereby find various diversions in the same industry if they choose to retire. With Bollywood looking at FM channels as an important promotional tool, airing interviews and releasing music, radio is attracting an increasing number of employees and RJs form a major part of the crowd".

1Reena Vyas gave up

her job as a finance consultant with an IT company to play an RJ.

Her salary is almost half of what she had been earning. For her, it is the passion of creativity that drives the industry and today she is satisfied with the creative space it provides her with.

Aditi Raval quit her career in modelling and performing dance shows and has now assumed a new name — RJ Aditi. The driving factor is the desire to become a household name. "I was not thinking about money, but glamour was definitely in my mind. Today, I can think of so many things I can do after I retire," she said.

RJ Dhwanit, who gave up a well-settled job as an administrator with the Life Insurance Corporation (LIC), feels that avenues open to an RJ are immense.

"Despite the fact that the duration of this profession is limited, I have no reason to get worried. I have come into the industry looking out for creative satisfaction and a breakaway from the mundane job schedule. I have realised that related career options will give me that. Five years from now I don't see the newer lot looking for security," he said.

While Dhwanit has started writing a book and is working on a music album in Gujarati; he is also confident about making a career as a trainer for future RJs.

Heading: Space exploration exhibit to be installed in Science City - Indian Express
Content:
Announcement made for Palanpur, Mehsana; Bhuj, Patan also get approval

The Gujarat Health Department has announced the setting up of two new medical colleges in the state, while approving two others within a span of one week as part of its initiative to bring down the number of outbound medical students.

Palanpur and Mehsana will get two new colleges, while approval has been given for colleges at Bhuj and Patan. Valia and Kesarsal medical colleges were denied approval for shortage of staff and infrastructure facilities under the Medical Council of India (MCI) guidelines.

The big question, however, is that with an already existing staff crunch in medical colleges across the state, how will the new medical colleges be staffed?

On August 27, the High Court had ordered the transfer of students of Valia Medical College to Surat Medical College. Kesarsal Medical College, Ahmedabad is also facing threats of closure, as both colleges have not seen a new batch of students for the past four years.

According to MCI norms, a medical college requires 150 teaching staff per 100 students. Clearly, the number of teaching staff in the six government medical colleges in the state is inadequate. Medical colleges across the state have 25-30 per cent shortage of medical staff at present and 60 per cent staffers below teaching staff are missing. Out of the six government medical colleges, five posts of deans and superintendents are lying vacant.

The overall teaching staff (professors, associate professors and assistant professors) in B J Medical College Ahmedabad is 200 (approx.), Medical College Baroda is 200 (approx.), Government Medical College Surat is 256, M P Shah Medical College Jamnagar is 300, Government Medical College Bhavnagar is 128 and Pandit Dindayal Upadhyay Medical College Rajkot is 130. This totals to 1,214, as compared to the required 1,400 against 925 seats.

Although the Health Department is upbeat about the opening up of new medical colleges, the decision is being looked at with suspicion. "When there is a persisting problem of inadequate number of staff in medical colleges, what is the meaning of transferring staff from one college to another and opening up new colleges? In the recent past, 75 staffers have been transferred from the BJ Medical College alone to other colleges," said Manish Doshi, Senate Member of the Gujarat University to BJ Medical College, which is affiliated to the Gujarat University.

Bipin M Patel, state Secretary, Indian Medical Association (IMA), said: "If a new medical college is not able to fill up vacant seats, it will not be recognised. It has happened in the case of Valia. However, the government's decision to bring up the retirement age of medical teachers from the present 58 years to 62 years and the pay scale can be of some help."

Health Minister Jay Narayan Vyas, however, said: "The present problem of medical students migrating to other states has only one solution and that is the opening up of new colleges. While we have announced two new colleges, the problem of teaching staff is also being addressed simultaneously. A committee has been set up under K K Shah, the Vice-Chancellor of North Gujarat University to address the issue and the results will be clear in a year's time".

Heading: IG (CID) P K Jha passes away - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat Council of Science City has announced its plan to install an exhibit on space exploration in the State Level Energy Park, being developed at the Science City in Ahmedabad.

The exhibit, 'Vyom- Exploration of Space,' will be set up inside the Science City premises under the Special Area Demonstration Program of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Union Government.

A R Mohanty, Chartered Engineer at Science City, Ahmedabad, said: "When we talk about energy from space, it mainly refers to ways and means of concentrating solar energy into space using satellites equipped with Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) systems".

He added: "The CSPs are huge parabolic mirror systems which focus a large area of sunlight into a concentrated beam, which is then used as a heat source for a conventional power plant. So our prototype will have a CSP Satellite concentrating solar energy into a high intensity beam, transmitting it to Earth, which will then be shown being used as the heat source. The exhibit will come up very soon".

The State Level Energy Park, which will house the CSP exhibit, is a joint effort of MNRE, Gujarat Energy Development Agency and the Gujarat Council of Science City. It will be the first State Level Energy Park of Gujarat. It is being built at the cost of Rs 1.6 crore and is spread over a hexagonal grid area of about 9,000 sq. m.

While explaining the objectives of the Energy Park, Mohanty said: "This is being done with an aim to demonstrate the efficacies of renewable sources of energy, to spread awareness while highlighting their needs and also to promote the use of renewable energy devices".

The exhibits at the park are classified according to the five basic elements or Panch Mahabhuta as propounded in ancient Indian Philosophy. These elements are Tej — energy from the sun, Marut — energy from the wind, Ap — energy from the water, Kshiti — energy from the earth, and Vyom — exploration of space.

Tej exhibits include a solar house, solar water heater, solar cooker and solar street light; the Marut includes a wind pumping mill and a wind turbine; Ap has ocean thermal energy converter, tidal power generator and a wave power generator and Khsiti exhibit demonstrates the use of geothermal energy generators.

Heading: Speeding truck kills 3 pilgrims - Indian Express
Content:
P K JHA, a 1986 batch IPS officer from Bihar, passed away at Sterling Hospital in Ahmedabad on Sunday afternoon after a prolonged illness of Wilson's Disease associated with brain haemorrhage and liver and kidney failure. He is survived by his wife and three children — a son and two daughters. He was last posted as Inspector General of Police, CID (Crime).

Dr Harsh Toshniwal, an Infectious Diseases specialist who treated Jha at the Sterling Hospital said: "He had a history of Wilson's Disease, a genetic disorder. Moreover, his liver was not working well. Later on, he had developed brain haemorrhage, following which his kidneys got infected."

According to Dr Toshniwal, Jha was under treatment since August 18 and was declared dead on Sunday around 3 pm. For the past several days, he was on life support system.

Jha (47) had done his B Tech in Civil Engineering. Known as a man of operations in police circle, Jha had investigated several high-profile cases such as the murder of Chetan Battery in the Sabarmati Central Jail and the murder of Pankaj Trivedi allegedly at the behest of some senior officials of the Swadhyay Parivar in Ahmedabad. The report he had submitted to the Gujarat High Court about the status of the Sabarmati Central Jail had created a lot of controversy.

Heading: Privileges to STs being flouted at Gujarat Vidhyapith’s Tribal institute - Indian Express
Content:
Three pilgrims were killed and 12 others injured when a truck hit their vehicle standing on the highway near Agiyol-Berna stand in Sabarkantha district on Saturday night.

The truck driver is absconding. Gambhoi village police have registered a case of rash driving and causing death by negligence against the unidentified truck driver.

The three deceased have been identified as Shantilal Prajapati, Sanjay Prajapati and Mukesh Prajapati, all from Sanjeri village in Zalod taluka of Dahod district.

The pilgrims were on their way to Ambaji, Gambhoi police said. The 12 injured have been admitted to Himmatnagar Civil Hospital for treatment.

Heading: 34 wind mills power ONGC project - Indian Express
Content:
The norms and policies of the system of the Protective Discrimination, which grants special privileges to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in India, seem to be openly flouted by the Tribal Research and Training Institute (TRTI) of Gujarat Vidhyapith.

In its 46 years of existence, the TRTI had reserved seats for ST candidates in its recruitment procedures just once. At present, the ST representation in the institute is limited to just two staff members in class I and class II categories.

The issue came to light after the institute, in reply to an RTI application, divulged details of its recruitment notifications from 1962 to 2008.

The RTI reply said that up till 1993, the institute had not provided Scheduled Tribe reservations in any class of employees in its recruitment procedures.

The only time ST reservation was given in TRTI was in 1995, wherein the Director's post was reserved for an ST candidate. In the most recent recruitment notification of June 2008, the institute has mentioned that one out of the total three vacant posts will be reserved for OBC candidates. There is, however, no mention about ST candidates.

The notifications for the years 1974, 1978, 1979, 1980, 1983, 1986 and 1991 do not mention anything about ST reservation.

In 1994's notification, there is a clause which says that out of all the candidates who apply for the posts, SC/ST candidates will be preferred. But there is no clause of reservation as such. A similar clause for SC/ST preference reappears in the 2001 notification.

According to TRTI's Director, Chandrakant Upadhyaya, there are a total of 21 posts in the institute, including all class I, II, III and IV posts.

"We have one class I employee, one class II employee and two peons in our institute, who belong to the Scheduled Tribe. Some posts are vacant right now. We will be filling them soon," he said.

Heading: Eye check-up camp for animals, birds in Rajkot - Indian Express
Content:
The country's premier oil producing public sector company, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC), has made its foray into the wind energy segment. It formally commissioned a 50 mw wind power project on the coast of Jakhau, some 125 km from Bhuj in Kutch District, on Saturday.

Costing over Rs 300 crore, this is the first project of ONGC in the domain of wind energy, a renewable and green source of energy. Under the project, a total of 34 wind mills, having power rating of 1.5 mw each, have been installed along the coastal plains by the Suzlon Energy Ltd.

These machines will supply power to ONGC's oil installations at Ankleshwar, Ahmedabad, Mahesana and Vadodara through the power grid of the Gujarat Energy Transmission Corporation Ltd (GETCO).

While inaugurating the project, ONGC Chairman and Managing Director R S Sharma, said: "As India's main energy solutions provider, this is our first pilot project to make the country self sufficient through alternate sources of energy. Its success has encouraged us to venture into this field in a bigger way."

He said that seeing the success of the pilot project, they may announce more projects to harness wind energy. "We plan to move forward in this direction, but I cannot disclose anything, as being a government organization, we need to complete certain formalities before making any announcements," he added.

Sharma praised the ONGC and Suzlon teams of engineers for completing the project in record time and thanked GETCO for quickly arranging the transmission of wind power for use in their installations in central and south Gujarat.

Meanwhile, D K Pandey, Director (Exploration), ONGC, said that the Commission, in association with experts from British Petroleum (BP), has undertaken a search survey for oil and gas in the Kutch basin. The result of this survey would be available only after three to four years, he added.

Heading: State grants Rs 150 cr to develop six cities - Indian Express
Content:
More than 70 animals and birds suffering from ophthalmic problems were examined by a team of local veterinarians and experts from Anand Veterinary College

A special eye check-up camp for animals and birds was organised by the city-based NGO, Karuna Foundation, at the Cattle Camp in Aji Vasahat area on Sunday.

More than 70-odd animals and birds suffering from ophthalmic problems were checked by a team of veterinary doctors from the Anand Veterinary College and the Superintendent of Rajkot Zoo Dr. M G Mardia.

The camp received tremendous response from various places, including Rajkot, Gandhinagar, Jamnagar, Morvi and Bhuj. Though most of the animals and birds were cured at the camp through small surgeries, a few have been referred to the Anand Veterinary College for cataract surgeries.

A female elephant from Morvi, which lost its left eye to an injury, was treated for an ulcer on her right eye, which was impairing her vision. The doctors said that now that the ulcer has been cured, the elephant will soon be able to see with her right eye.

Besides the elephant, two parrots, one horse, two buffalos, 14 cows and 18 dogs were treated as special cases at the camp.

Narotambhai Popat of Karuna Foundation said this is the first time that an eye check-up camp for animals and birds has been held in the state. "We have treated over 70 animals and birds in this camp. We have also provided drops and medicines free of cost. A team of experts from the Anand Veterinary College and local veterinary doctors carried out small surgeries on a few animals. Around 12 dogs have been sent to the Anand Veterinary college for cataract surgery, as the procedure was not possible here," he said.

Heading: Mahant’s entry barred into four districts - Indian Express
Content:
The government has allocated Rs 150 crore as special grant to the six municipal corporations of Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Rajkot, Bhavnagar, Jamnagar and Junagadh to help them create necessary infrastructure in their respective cities. Surprisingly, the Surat Municipal Corporation does not figure in the list.

In a statement, State Urban Development Minister Nitin Patel said on Saturday that the six municipal corporations will utilise the amount for carrying out various developmental works in their respective towns. The development works relate to water supply and drainage, solid waste management, filtration plant, basic amenities in slums, sanitation and upgradation of public roads.

The funds provided by the government will help the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation to implement different projects such as building of a four-lane railway overbridge near the Sola Crossing and construction of a new multi-storey building for the L G Hospital in the city. Similarly, the Vadodara civic body will be able to construct an indoor sports complex and overhead water tanks at Kalali and Bapod.

The Rs 100 crore funds allocated among these four municipal corporations of Rajkot, Bhavnagar, Jamnagar and Junagadh will help them create basic civic amenities and infrastructure facilities for their citizens, the statement said.

Four of the six civic bodies that have been provided with the funds, fall in the Saurashtra region.

Heading: Modi-bashing did not pay, admit BJP rebels - Indian Express
Content:
For the first time in the history of Junagadh, a temple head has been barred entry into Junagadh, Amreli, Porbander and Rajkot districts for alleged involvement in crime.

Mahant Rudranand, head of the Khdkhadiya Mahadev temple, located on the outskirts of Chorwadi village near Junagadh, was allegedly involved in serious crimes, which included the killing of wild animals, making of country medicine without any legal procedure and harassment of the village people.

About a year ago, the villagers of Chorwadi had staged an agitation against Rudranand and had demanded immediate police action. The village had remained closed for a couple of days in protest. Some 200 villagers had also staged a dharna in front of the collector's office and submitted a memorandum to the district collector against the Mahant.

An officer of the Bilkha town police station said: "More than half-a-dozen complaints have been registered against the mahant. He was involved in serious offences including attempt to murder, encroachment of government land, atrocities and threatening people."

Offences have now been registered against the mahant with the Bilkha town police station under Sections 307, 504, 506(2) of the IPC and under the provisions of the Atrocity Act.

Finally, the Bilkha police prepared a proposal to ban the mahant's entry into Junagadh and the adjoining districts. Following the police proposal, District Magistrate Ashwini Kumar issued an order banning the mahant's entry into the districts, which was implemented on Saturday, the police said.

The police action has come as a surprise to a section of sadhus here. A Junagadh based Sadhu said: "For the first time, action has been taken against a sadhu in this region. Police action is unfortunate, but the sadhus should also not cross their limit."

Heading: Row over appointment of prosecutors - Indian Express
Content:
New party to follow BJP's original ideology in letter and spirit

The Bharatiya Janata Party rebels seem to have learnt their lesson. Partying ways with the BJP to lead an anti-Narendra Modi campaign during the 2007 Assembly polls, their efforts boomeranged. Now when the rebels are all set to form the New Maha Gujarat Party, they have said it won't be anti-Modi, but anti-BJP.

The general feeling in the rebel camp is that the Modi-bashing, spearheaded from the platform of the Sardar Patel Utkarsh Samiti, has only benefited the Chief Minister. They believe this was probably the reason why their campaign did not yield any positive results during the Assembly elections. The rebels have acknowledged that focus on Modi and the Patel community were two mistakes due to which the SPUS campaign did not click with the electorate.

The rebel party leaders have said the new party will be an "ideological replica" of the original BJP, which has allegedly failed to live up to the expectations of the people. The party plans to tap the sentiments of the people on issues such as the Ramjanm Bhoomi, Mandir Nirman and the softening of the Hindu stand by reaching out to the minorities.

Former Bhavnagar MLA Sunil Oza said the new party's ideology will remain as that of the BJP's, but will be followed in letter and spirit. "It will be based on Hindu ideology for sure, but will not be like the BJP, which no longer delivers on its promises. The party will follow Pandit Din Dayal Upadhyay's fundamentals on integral humanism," he said.

Former Home Minister Gordhan Zadaphia said the new party will go against both the BJP and the Congress. Oza said the new party will, however, support Modi on issues like terrorism and POTA.

Under the guidance of former Chief Minister Keshubhai Patel and Suresh Mehta, the SPUS comprising second rung state BJP leaders like Zadafia, Oza, Rajkot Rural MLA Siddharth Parmar, had joined hands with the Congress to defeat Modi in the 2007 elections. Most of these leaders have roots in the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS).

The rebels further said they ought to have formed a party before the elections itself rather than forge an alliance with the Congress as part of the anti-Modi campaign.

"Had a new party been formed before the elections, we would have certainly won 12 to 15 seats. But our alliance with the Congress only benefited the BJP," said Parmar.

Incidentally, most leaders like Patel, Kanshiram and Mehta have already distanced themselves from the rebels.

Around 5,000 people are expected to gather when the party is officially launched on September 25 at Ahmedabad. The rebel leaders are trying to give it a shape which they hope will strike the right chord with the people.

The leaders are, however, not sure whether the new party will take part in the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections. "As of now, the focus will be on building up the organisation. The decision to take part in the election will be taken later on," said Zadafia, who once worked hard to build up the BJP at the grassroots in the state.

Heading: Constable shoots at shop owner in Mirzapur - Indian Express
Content:
The legal wrangle in the Ahmedabad serial blasts case is yet to begin inside the courtroom, but it has already started one on the outside. The debate is about the appointment of the Special Public Prosecutors (SPPs) for defending the state government during the trial of the case.

Four prominent city-based advocates — Sudhir Bhrambhatt, J M Panchal, Mitesh Amin and H M Dhruv— have recently been appointed as SPPs for the July 26 serial blasts case, which claimed more than 55 lives.

Of these, Panchal and Amin appear against the state as defence counsels in the Sohrabuddin Sheikh fake encounter case of November 26, 2006. In addition, Panchal is contesting one more case against the state, the Suresh Thakore murder case of 2007.

According to legal experts, this is in violation with the rules of the Gujarat State Legal Department. The department has now issued a notification in the form of a booklet: "Law officers' conditions of service rules and rules for the conduct of the legal affairs of government," a copy of which is available with the paper.

According to Rule 2 G (5) of the notification, SPPs have been included in the category of the state government's law officers. Rule 6 of the same notification bars any law officer from appearing against the state, without the prior consent of the state government's Remembrancer in Legal Affairs (RLA).

M H Shah, the state legal secretary and RLA, said: "Since they were already appearing as defence counsels in a case against the state before being appointed as SPPs, it can be presumed that the concerned authorities were aware of this. But after their appointment as SPPs, it has become mandatory for them to seek prior consent from my office before appearing in any case against the government. We can take required action and can even cancel their appointment as SPPs, if a violation of rule is established."

Shah added: "An SPP can be allowed or refused to appear in a case against the government. But it depends on the nature of the case, on the basis of which the Home Department can request for an action."

When asked if Panchal and Amin will be allowed to continue as defence counsels in the Sohrabuddin case and as SPPs in the serial blasts case, Shah said: "Well, if someone objects to this on strong grounds, we can ask the Home Department to inquire into the matter and submit a report. Necessary actions can be taken on the basis of that report."

Bhrambhatt, Panchal, Amin and Dhruv were officially declared as SPPs in the serial blasts case last month. Panchal was not available for comments, but Amin said: "We have been appointed as SPPs by the state government and are not violating any rules."

Defence counsel in the serial blasts case, Hashim Qureshi alleged that the appointments were made on vested interests. "The court had capable government pleaders and there was no need to appoint SPPs. I will raise objection to these appointments before the concerned authorities."

Heading: UP begins its first-ever intensive survey on child malnutrition - Indian Express
Content:
A constable with the city police shot at a shop owner in the mutton bazaar area in Mirzapur on Sunday morning. The victim, Mehmood Khan, received a bullet injury on his right leg and is under treatment at the V S Hospital here.

Mystery, however, shrouds the incident. Even as investigations are on, both Khan and Mukhtiyar Saiyed (43), the police constable, have now lodged cross-complaints against each other.

Khan has alleged in his statement that Saiyed used to extort money from the shop owners in the area. When he refused to pay Saiyed, the latter shot him, he said. The incident occurred around 7.30 am. After the incident, an enraged group of shop owners reportedly started beating Saiyed.
