Commuters in Noida had a harrowing time on Monday, after over 300 bus drivers and conductors went on a strike in the city.

The protesting drivers and conductors are demanding that conductors should not be penalised if any passenger was found without a ticket. Another demand was parity with DTC rules and regulations. "In Delhi, if a passenger is found without a ticket, a penalty of Rs 100 is imposed on him or her. Here, in addition to that penalty, the conductor is also fined Rs 250 by the ticket checker. In all air-conditioned buses, drivers get 20 paise for every kilometre," Puran Singh, leader of the bus drivers' and conductors' union, said.

It was the public that bore the strike's brunt. "I have to reach office in Maharani Bagh and have been waiting for a bus for the past one hour. At least, the public should be warned that bus drivers are going on a strike so that we can arrange for some other conveyance," Narendra Kumar, a resident of Noida, said.

The strike also marred the induction ceremony of six new buses under the Sravajan Hitaya, Bahujan Sukhaya Scheme, announced by Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati. The buses were to be inducted at the Noida bus terminal but had to be flagged off from the Anand Vihar Interstate Bus Terminal instead.

The newly inducted buses will start from Ghaziabad and make their way to Delhi via Noida. "Our aim is to connect various districts of UP with Delhi," Ashok Kumar, regional manager, Noida transport department, said.

Heading: DIAL widens approach road to domestic terminal - Indian Express
Content:
Granting a clean chit to the Delhi Police, DIAL made it clear that the Gypsy was not on the runway, and that it was parked 50 metres away from it in the apron area and would not have posed any danger to the Lucknow-bound Kingfisher flight.

The incident occured around 7.30 pm, when the aircraft started rolling in for take-off. The plane was going to take-off from secondary runway 27/09, when the pilot noticed the headlights of a vehicle.

"The commander of the aircraft noticed an orange light and a set of red lights at the end of the runway," a Kingfisher spokesperson said. The pilot immediately informed the ATC and the Apron Operation Command Centre and rejected the take-off, before safely taxiing back to the bay.

"Seeing the lights from more than a distance of 2 km, the pilot might have felt the vehicle was parked on the runway," Arun Arora, of DIAL's corporate communications said.

However, when DIAL's follow-me vehicle went to check, it found the Delhi Police gypsy was parked at a comfortable distance, in the service area at the end of the secondary runway. This area is close to the Air Force technical area, from where VIPs board aircraft. President Pratibha Patil was scheduled to fly on Sunday.

"Upon investigation, it was found that a police vehicle was positioned on the Service Road near the runway 27 threshold, with its head lights and red beacon switched on. It was an authorised police vehicle operating on an approved service road, due to VIP movement in the adjacent technical area. At no time was it on the runway nor did it pose a risk to any aircraft," Arora said.

The Kingfisher flight subsequently departed at 8.17 pm. DIAL has sent a detailed report to the DGCA. DIAL's follow-me vehicle told personnel in the Delhi Police Gypsy to switch off their lights so that the pilots are not distracted.

"We have been handling VIP security for a long time and our officers know the exact procedure to follow. When nothing wrong was done, there is no point of taking action against anyone," a senior Delhi Police officer said.

Heading: Click to dine - Indian Express
Content:
DIAL widens approach road to domestic terminal

Getting stuck in traffic just meters away from the domestic terminal at Indira Gandhi International Airport, with just a few minutes for your flight to take off, might soon become a thing of the past.

The approach road to the domestic terminal has been widened from 10 to 18 metres. Work on widening the road finished last week and Delhi International Airport Ltd (DIAL) has now started work on widening of the exit road as well. "We expect to finish widening the road by the end of this month," a DIAL spokesperson said.

The exit road, from the petrol pump roundabout to the old NH 8, will be widened from 9 to 14 metres. "I was pleasantly surprised to see the wide, newly tarred road. Instead of the usual honking and driving in second gear, I managed to drive along pretty comfortably," Gopalan Nair, a government officer, said.

However, people are also using the additional space as a free car park, avoiding the parking fee at the airport lot in the process.

Elsewhere, DIAL has hired landscaping experts from Singapore and Malaysia to start landscaping work from the Dwarka roundabout to the approach road to domestic terminals 1A, 1B and arrivals.

Last month, the same landscaping experts worked on the 4 km stretch between the Radisson Hotel traffic intersection and the international airport, lining the route with palm trees. Road signs have also been redone. Changes were also made to the road kerbs to make them more passenger friendly. "The domestic terminal route will also be landscaped along similar lines," the spokesperson said.

The wall enclosing Mehram Nagar village will also be concealed with plants and trees. "The wall was broken in several places and wore a very dirty look. So, our landscape artists have suggested covering it up with green cover," the spokesperson said.

Heading: HC asks co-op society registrar to explain Ashadeep allotment delay - Indian Express
Content:
Now, you can book a table and order online

If there's one thing that's sure to kill your appetite on an evening out, it's the waiting game — waiting to get a table, waiting for someone to take your order and then waiting to be served. A new food website says it has the answer. Log on to www.aplacetodine.com and you can, not just book your table but also order your food online.

"What more, you could get gifts like sunshades, laptop bags and coffee mugs if you order online," says Shiva Srinivasan, CEO of Biznet Technolgies, a US based IT solutions company, who started the website.

The site has handled over 150 table bookings and online orders ever since it started in July. "We started with Delhi since it is the hardest market to tap in terms of the number of restaurants, location and preference of the people. Once we are successful in Delhi, it will be easier to sell this concept to other metros," says Srinivasan, a die-hard foodie.

The site lists over 160 outlets across NCR. "You can sift through menus, reviews, facilities and special offers of each restaurant," he adds. Though he has invested more than one crore rupees in the venture, the service is free for both clients and restaurants. One needs to log in and travel down the step-by-step guide on location, type of cuisine, type of restaurant and operation timings.

And if you're too lazy to log on, there's always the telephone. Call or SMS the toll free number for instant "food counseling". "When you send an SMS, our call centre contacts you and helps you decide on your order. The information is relayed back to the restaurant immediately," he continues.

There's another reason to order online, smiles Srinivasan. "We offer discounts from 10-15 per cent on online orders. This is due to our tie ups with the restaurants," he explains. The website will be launched in Bangalore, Chennai and Hyderabad in October.

Heading: Govt withdraws case against activist, 2 professors - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court has directed Registrar of Cooperative Societies (RCS) U K Worah to explain the "deliberate defiance" of judicial orders to start the allotment process for Ashadeep Group Society in Dwarka.

"Let contemnor (RCS) be present to show cause as to why he should not be punished for contempt of court for deliberate defiance of the order of the court," Justice Shiv Narayan Dhingra directed in a recent order. The case has been posted for hearing on December 18.

The High Court had on October 5, 2007 directed the RCS to prepare a list of members for allotment and forward the same to the Delhi Development Authority on or before November 15 last year.

With the High Court framing a mechanism to initiate "genuine allotment" in a recent order, Ashadeep Society patrons now face the prospect of starting the entire process right from scratch, solely on the insistence of the RCS.

The battle began for Ashadeep in 2004, with the society approaching the High Court seeking reasons for delay in allotment. The High Court concluded the matter on October 5, 2007 and directed the then registrar of cooperative societies to begin the allotment process by verifying documents. DDA was directed to allot flats according to draw of lots by December 31, 2007, the petition said.

In January this year, the High Court reiterated its previous order and warned the registrar's office of legal action in case of non-compliance with its orders. Opposing the High Court's order, the registrar's office filed a special leave petition with the Supreme Court in March.

Following which, the Supreme Court on May 5 directed the CBI to forward original documents of Ashadeep Group Housing Society within a month. The apex court also gave the registrar's office a deadline of three months to complete the allotment process. In contravention, the petition stated, the RCS on August 26 intimated to the society to submit its entire gamut of records for fresh verification.

Heading: They stopped to lend a helping hand, ended up as victims - Indian Express
Content:
Charges were filed against the three for holding demonstration against the 1997 murder of student leader Chandrashekhar

After 11 years of precious judicial time, the state has decided to withdraw the case of rioting and assault against a political activist and two professors, who had protested against the murder of former JNU Students' Union President Chandrashekhar in 1997.

Chandrashekhar was shot dead at a public square in Siwan, Bihar, and MP Shahabuddin has been accused of masterminding the killing.

The present case was instituted against Kavita Krishnan, currently one of the editors of Liberation, the monthly magazine of the CPI (ML) and Shiv Mangal and Vinod Kumar, professors of Delhi University, for staging a demonstration at the Parliament Street on April 24, 1997.

They were formally charged under various penal provisions pertaining to rioting, obstructing public servants, assault and mischief by the trial court in February last year.

Armed with permission from the government, Additional Public Prosecutor S K Berwal had recently moved an application before the court, requesting it to withdraw the prosecution against the three, contending the move was in "public interest".

According to the application, withdrawal of the case was in the interest of justice, as the demonstration was not against any individual but an outcome of public outrage against Chandrashekhar's killing.

The accused were either students or teachers and continuing their prosecution would be detrimental to their career, read the application, moved in accordance with the Code of CriminalProcedure.

Taking into account the content of the application, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (ACMM) A K Kuhar has given his nod for the withdrawal of the case against the trio.

"The prosecutor has fairly applied his mind to the facts of the case and I also subscribe to his opinion that withdrawal of such cases will be in the interest of justice. The accused were students and senior teachers of the university without any criminal background," noted the ACMM in a recent order.

The court then passed the acquittal order and directed the cancellation of their bail bonds, submitted by them while obtaining the bail. Kavita Krishnan, a former national president of All India Students' Association (AISA) dubbed the state's decision as "amusing," as it came after much delay.

"We never denied our participation in the protest but that was all. Lodging a criminal case against us was not fair," said Krishnan.

Krishnan added though the present case has met its logical conclusion after 11 years, Chandrashekhar's murder trial was still on and justice remained elusive there.

Heading: Spurred by opponents, Sheila plans show of strength at Sonia rally - Indian Express
Content:
Two Delhi Police personnel and four passersby could never have imagined that going to help victims of a road accident would turn into a nightmare. Newsline visits the shocked families of the victims as they try to come to terms with the tragedy that struck last night in Gopalpur village near Timarpur in North Delhi.

Aftab Ahmed Qureshi
Aftab Ahmed Qureshi, an auto mechanic and a resident of Chand Bagh in Bhajanpura, was travelling on his motorbike with his assistant, Raju, when they stopped to help the policemen shift the injured into the PCR van, before they became victims of another speeding vehicle. Aftab's father, Ikhtiyar Qureshi, who got to know of his son's demise only at 9 am, said, "All through the night we kept asking the police if they had any information of our son. They told us that they knew nothing." His wife, Noorjahan did not come to the police station. Aftab was to get married after six months.

Raju
Raju's sobbing mother, Angoori Devi, also a resident of Bhajanpura, said, "I don't know how it happened and can't believe my son is gone."

Virender Yadav
Virender Yadav, who died in the incident, owns six auto-rickshaws and had gone to Burari for some work last night. He was a resident of 1716, Himmat Gali, Sita Ram Bazar area and a native of Bihar. His eldest son, Surinder said, "He had been living in the Capital for the last 15 years and had bought auto-rickshaws to earn a living." Virender's dead body was taken to Bihar as his parents live there.

MP Gupta
MP Gupta was returning to Karawal Nagar where he lives when he met with the accident. His wife and three daughters survive him. His younger brother, Manoj Kumar said, "He owned a shoe showroom in Sant Nagar and was coming back home when the mishap occurred."

ASI Baltar Singh
ASI Baltar Singh's family is in Punjab and has been informed of the mishap by senior police officers.

Mithan Lal Sharma
Head constable Mithan Lal Sharma's family, gathered at Teerath Ram Hospital at Rajpur Road, was waiting for him to be shifted to the general ward as he was declared stable and out of danger. Wife, Shakuntala said, "He had asked another person to call us from his mobile. He told rescuers to take him to Teerath Ram Hospital and that we should reach there." Sharma has two sons — Neeraj and Dheeraj. Neeraj works in a private company while Dheeraj is a class XI student.

A resident of Nathu Colony in Burari, Lal, suffered injuries in his head and abdomen. "Papa said he was helping the accident victims and the PCR was about to take the injured to the hospital. It didn't start despite repeated attempts and within seconds a truck came and hit them all of a sudden," Neeraj, Lal's elder son said.

Killer roads
Aug 9, 08: Three persons, including a young woman, were killed and four badly injured when the jeep carrying them collided head-on with a truck coming in from the wrong direction on the Delhi-Noida (DND) high-speed expressway in the early hours of Saturday. Two deceased were employees of the HCL call centre.

Aug 1, 08: Four persons were killed and as many injured when the driver of a mini-truck, apparently dozed off at the wheel and the vehicle overturned at a traffic intersection in Punjabi Bagh.

Oct 8, 07: A Blueline claimed seven lives. The accident took place on Mathura Road in Badarpur, near Aligaon crossing when a route no 460 bus crushed around 15 people standing on the pavement, waiting for buses. The driver was allegedly drunk.

Heading: Rs 39 lakh relief amassed, DU dept does its ‘duty’ for flood victims - Indian Express
Content:
With internal pressure mounting on the Congress in Delhi after the rallies of the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Bahujan Samaj Party last week were termed highly successful, Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit on Monday held a meeting of MPs, MLAs and councillors to plan for the rally on September 17. Sonia Gandhi will be attending the rally on the issue of unauthorised colonies and the message from the CM was clear - make sure there is a huge gathering.

Instructing councillors to make sure the crowd is "very visible" at the rally, Diskshit said the party should "tell the people what the government has done for them during its rule."

The rally will be held on September 17 at the Ram Lila ground, where the BJP had held its 'unauthorised colonies mahasangh' last week to talk about the problems of the more than 40 lakh people from these neglected colonies.

A decision was taken at the meeting to mobilise the "masses" to claim votes on the move to regularise the 1409 colonies. The chief minister asked party workers to put up posters of Sonia Gandhi all over the city. DPCC chief J P Agarwal asked workers to present a united front before elections.

All Congress leaders were called in and everyone was invited to speak, including Sajjan Kumar, who is said to be leading his own faction within the party. The move, an MLA told Newsline on the condition of anonymity, was aimed at "crushing factionalism in the party and joining hands before the elections."

However, senior leaders Ajay Maken and Jagdish Tytler did not attend the meeting, reportedly because they are out of town.

While MLAs and MPs claimed that the BJP had been misleading people, decision to distribute the provisional certificates for regularisation of the colonies at the rally was also announced.

As reported by Newsline last week, Sonia Gandhi will be giving away the certificates to some people.

A source in the DPCC told Newsline that "Four to five people will be called in from one of the colonies to receive the certificates from Sonia Gandhi."

Party workers have been instructed to start preparing the ground for a massive turnout.

Leader of Opposition in MCD Jai Kishan Sharma said councillors would now "reach the common people to set forth the message of development initiated by our government."

Heading: Sweet delights - Indian Express
Content:
Newspaper cutouts narrating the bleak story of Kosi's curse pasted alongside handmade posters seeking contribution for the survivors and rehabilitation in flood-ravaged Bihar. That's what students at DU's Department of Social Work are working on, of late.

And their efforts have not gone in vain: the department has generated Rs 39 lakh worth relief in cash and kind, in little over a week.

Ridhi Gupta, a final-year student MA student of social work, though does not expect brownie points, for that is what, she said, the department is about. "Helping the needy is part of our curriculum," she said, matter-of-factly.

The department has begun an initiative called UDAI — University for Developed Action and Integrated Learning — to provide relief to the flood victims, as also to bring back experience of the situation at Ground Zero to the university. On August 28, the department sent a volunteer team of seven students and a teacher to Bihar.

And on Sunday, a similar team was sent — this time with the relief material.

Dr Seema Sharma, a teacher at the department, said they received "generous amount of help" from NGOs, DU authorities, and RWAs. "We sent 65 sacks of material, each containing six boxes, with the students on Sunday," Sharma said. "The team already there says the situation is worse than what is reported in the media."

Those left behind are busy filing posts on the blog www.dswdu.blogspot.com and maintaining the 24-hour helpline. The site gives a detailed report of activities of the department, and also highlights stories of death and misery in the districts ravaged by the curse of Kosi.

So, where does that leave time for study? "Every day five MA first-year students and as many students from MA final year are given the task of maintaining relief work," Ridhi said. "It is done on rotation basis, so every student ends up working as well as studying."

Heading: Blueline runs over biker in South Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
A Belgian chef turns simple desserts into sinful treats

A cake is just a cake until it gets a magic touch. Then, it turns into an exotic treat that melts deliciously in your mouth," says Dries Delanghe, a 20-year-old pastry chef from Belgium. On his second visit to India, he is giving his magic touch to the new line of cakes, pastries and mousses at Choco La, a chocolaterie-cum-cafe.

"Desserts are globally popular now, but it is innovation that'll drive things in future," he says while training the Choco La chefs. For Delanghe, fresh out of a culinary college in Belgium,

creating a pastry comes easy. "It all began with an interest in my father's little restaurant and my sweet tooth," he says. Back home in Belgium, he works with Puratos, a chain that owns 150 hotels across the world.

We sampled some of his creation: the chocolate mousse cake with mirror finish was soft and moist. The almond cake burst with an assortment of apple, cherry and lemon fillings and tasted as if it was straight out of an Indian grandmother's oven. "I haven't brought my Belgian influences to the pastry shelves," he chuckles. The chef's favourite chocolate and raspberry macaroons are also worth a try.

However, the mango and white chocolate gateaux was quite disappointing. It neither tasted fruity nor was there any trace of the special ingredient the chef told us about — jasmine tea. Choco La will begin to stock the new line from November.

Heading: Live & haywire - Indian Express
Content:
A 22-year-old salesman was killed after he was run over by a Blueline bus in Hazrat Nizamuddin area of South Delhi on Monday.

The police said the accident was reported near the Nizamuddin police station around 9.30 am. The Bluelines have claimed 80 lives so far this year. Police officers said the victim, Ranjeet Kumar, died in his attempt to save his pillion rider and colleague, who fell on the road after his bike brushed another vehicle.

"Kumar's bike was brushed slightly by a car and his bike swayed. Shalu Pandit, his colleague, fell on the road. He rushed to her aid and pushed her to the other side of the road and was crushed by the bus," a senior officer said.

The police said both Kumar and Shalu were rushed to AIIMS, where Kumar was declared brought dead. Officers said bystanders caught hold of the driver, who was later handed over to the police. He has been identified as Ishwar Soni and a case of rash and negligent driving has been registered against him, the police said.

Officers said Kumar was an employee of Barclays Finance in Daryaganj and was on his way to office.

Heading: A new kebab factory - Indian Express
Content:
It was a scene straight out of the movie as the cast and crew of Rock On created a frenzy among those present and flooding the venue at Select Citywalk in Saket on Saturday evening for the concert organized by Big FM. The event also created the worst traffic snarl of the week and, at the venue, jostling elbows, rowdy men and body odour were hazards the organisers had clearly not bargained for.

All this would have been forgiven if only Farhan Akhtar could perform well in real life. Although ill, Akhtar sang Pichle saat dino mein, Rock on, Socha hai and more. "I'm not well but then one has to do what they have to do," he smiled before getting on stage. He can sing a bit, but his lack of experience on stage stood out when he sang out of sync with the mixed tracks.

Accompanying Akhtar was Arjun Rampal, who, with his signature bandana, stepped onstage with a guitar that he mimed playing for a couple of songs. "I had learnt the guitar for three months and the chord progression is not so easy to pick up at my age. But it sure is fun," he quipped. It's hard to believe this, since his fingers were stuck to the fret, unmoving during guitar solos or chord shifts, just like his performance in the movie.

Purab Kohli, who did his rendition of I will survive along with Luke Kenny did not play any instrument but the two made up by prancing around the stage interacting with the audience. The performance that opened with songs from Akhtar's previous movies— Dil Chahta Hai, Don and Lakshya—ended with Sinbad the sailor from Rock On until the incessant encore from the crowd got Akhtar to sing the title track again. With director Abhishek Kapoor, producer Ritesh Siddique and actors Koel Puri and Shahana Goswami joining the others on stage, the show certainly had energy but musically, was quite a dud.

Heading: Barricades along Yamuna no deterrent for people tossing waste - Indian Express
Content:
A friendly neighbourhood eatery in Noida promises great food at competitive prices

Their spicy Murgh Malai Kebab was a hit in the East Delhi Mall. Now, Kabab Krazy, better known for having counters in food courts in malls, has just opened its first fine dining restaurant in the buzzing Sector 18 market in Noida, serving a variety of Indian and Lebanese kebabs.

This 70-seater restaurant has two levels, the first for the lounge and the second for dining. The interiors are trendy with ornate metallic panelling and lagoon-blue ceiling lights, never mind if they're hardly in sync with typical North West Frontier cuisine. The seating is slightly cramped, though diners are unlikely to notice this once they get absorbed by the menu, extensive, by any standards.

Kebab Krazy serves over 20 kebabs with names like Kibbeh Mishwey and Bullet Kebab, with an assortment of options for vegetarians. "We have devised the menu with over 80 per cent dishes being Indian and the remainder being Lebanese, Turkish and Iranian. And we have kept all the old-time favourites in our menu to maintain a familiarity with the customer. Gradually, we will introduce more Lebanese and Turkish kebabs," says Shreeparna Khaitan, the promoter of Kabab Krazy.

Must try
The Kibbeh Mishwey (Arabic lamb kebabs) which came with accompaniments of tabbouleh, hummus and Baba Ghanoush were deliciously succulent. In desserts, don't miss the chocolate chuski, flavoured with vodka for that extra kick.

Give a miss
We tried the Indian and Western (Lebanese, Turkish, Iranian) kebab platters. The portions are generous. The shaami kebab was fairly regular and the rest came with liberal doses of spice.

The Bullet Kebabs or Turkish meat balls taste just like seekh kebabs , the only difference being in the shapes.

On the cards at Kebab Krazy, says Khaitan, are flambéed kebabs, made of assorted fruits.
Meal for two: Rs 1,400
Contact: 95120- 4245204
Location: J-9, sector 18, Noida

Heading: Open Season - Indian Express
Content:
The bridge between ITO and Laxmi Nagar over River Yamuna, similar to the ones at Nizamuddin and ISBT, has always been a congested link for commuters. The Delhi Government plan to put up iron meshes along bridges to check river pollution does not seem to be working. People continue to throw waste, especially flowers and other materials used in pujas, after after cutting open the fence.

The 10-foot-high wire barricades, shaped like an inverted 'L', were meant to bar people from tossing things into the Yamuna. The state government had installed the barriers along all the major bridges in 2003 as part of its 'Save Yamuna' campaign under the Yamuna Action Plan-I. Signboards with messages were also put up on all the bridges to discourage people. Now, the iron meshes have been neatly cut, rendering the carefully-designed structure less effective.

Officials say while the design for the iron meshes on these bridges over Yamuna were prepared by the Environment Department, they were constructed by the Public Works Department (PWD), responsible for maintaining them. "The idea was not only to stop but also create awareness among the people of Delhi not to dump plastics, garbage and other polluting agents in the Yamuna as it contributed to the deterioration of the river," said an official with the Environment Department.

Environmentalists say lack of a sustained public awareness campaign is the culprit.

"Any protective measure to curtail pollution is as good or bad as its weakest link. If the meshes were so easy to be bypassed by people, what was the point in putting them up?" asks Manoj Mishra, convenor of the Yamuna Jiye Abhiyan.

"It is unfortunate that the meshes have been broken, and people do not realise the importance of keeping the river clean. Yamuna is the lifeline of Delhi," he adds.

PWD Minister Raj Kumar Chauhan, maintained he was not aware of the problem. "I will get the meshes checked and repaired at the earliest. Some people steal iron parts to earn money. But I'll make sure a proper check is put on the same," he said.

"Such projects have no meaning unless implemented properly. The Delhi government should have roped in its member schools of eco clubs, who could have been made monitoring wardens."

"School children should have been involved in a continuous campaign of that nature. You need to be more proactive in educating the public than putting up such physical barriers," he said.

Heading: Double-mishap: 6 dead in Timarpur - Indian Express
Content:
The first ever India Couture Week involves big money and bigger ambitions

Till Delhi took away the pret week, Mumbai had always been considered the fashion capital of India. Now, India Couture Week, sponsored by real estate company HDIL, will be held between September 16-21 at Grand Hyatt in Mumbai, with 11 of India's leading designers showcasing their couture lines. "Couture is an inherent tradition with us. I am glad that finally there is a platform to bring together India's indigenous couture, particularly the rich textile tradition that we have," says Ritu Kumar, whose show will be the opening act for the event. The veteran designer will showcase her bridal line, with a strong emphasis on ethnic India crafts.

Clothes apart, there's a lot more to look forward to. In a departure from the pret week traditions in Delhi, the Mumbai event will see each designer creating their own ramps, and adding their own touches to their show. So, the conventional notion of a ramp in the centre of the show area is likely to have a face-lift. "Since couture is all about luxury and opulence, each of the designers will get about 22 hours to do up the show area exactly the way they want. Besides, the Fashion Design Council of India (FDCI) is not sparing any expense to provide these designers with the best infrastructure possible," says Sunil Sethi, president, FDCI. Even though the organisers are tight-lipped about the money involved, sources claim that as much as Rs 25 lakhs have been sanctioned to each designer just for stage management. This apart, the FDCI and HDIL are investing a huge amount to ensure that the opening event is nothing short of spectacular.

The inaugural couture week is also the launch pad for HDIL, one of India's largest real estate players looking to enter the world of leisure, hospitality and retail development. "We were looking at a suitable opportunity to showcase our capability as a sponsor. So this seemed to be the perfect setting for us," says Sunny Dewan Wadhwan, MD, HDIL, who has entered into a three-year-contract with FDCI for the same. Interestingly, even though the week is a little awkwardly placed, with the wedding season too close, a lot of interest has been generated among the NRI community. "We had an option of not doing it this year at all or having it around this time. We chose to start from this year. Next year, we'll look to moving the week ahead to July," says Sethi.

Apart from Kumar, participants include Ashish Soni, Tarun Tahiliani, JJ Valaya, Rohit Bal, Varun Bahl, Anamika Khanna and Pallavi Jaikishen. "It's our chance to live out our fantasies. I am doing a collection inspired by autumn. It's a rich interpretation and I am looking forward to playing it up with an equally apt setting," says Delhi designer Manav Gangwani.

The 11 shows will be spread out over the week, with two shows a day after the first day. Even though there will be no formal grand finale, Manish Malhotra and Rohit Bal will showcase their collections on the final day.

Heading: Karanuday bows out in first round - Indian Express
Content:
It was an accident on top of an accident. And it left six persons, including a policeman, dead and three others injured at Gopalpur village, near Timarpur village in North Delhi on Sunday night.

The accidents occurred in a matter of minutes — between 10.45 and 11 pm, the police said.

Vipin Kumar, 18; Mathura Prasad Gupta, 40; Aftab Qureshi, 24; Raju, 20; Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) Baltar Singh, 45; and Virender Yadav, 27, died. Head Constable Mithan Lal Sharma; Prabhu Yadav, 21; and one Rohit are in hospital, one of them said to be serious.

Timarpur police said they received a call at 10.45 pm, informing them about the first accident. "A PCR van reached the spot within minutes and found that an auto-rickshaw, driven by one Vipin Kumar, had hit the motorcycle of Mathura Prasad Gupta, a shoe shop owner heading home, in Karawal Nagar, Northeast Delhi," SHO, Timarpur, Rampal Singh said. "The policemen were shifting the injured into the PCR van when a container truck sped in and hit them."

The truck (registration HR 38J8675) also hit Vipin's auto and Gupta's bike, besides smashing into another PCR van and an auto whose occupants had stopped by to help, Singh said.

The truck zoomed in seemingly from nowhere as ASI Baltar Singh assisted victims of the first accident. Meanwhile, Virender Yadav (dead) and Prabhu Yadav (in hospital) stopped their autorickshaw to see what had happened, SHO Singh said. "Head Constable Mithan Singh had also stopped his PCR to assist them. He was on way to the Daryaganj DCP office, where he is posted," he said.

Two others — Aftab Ahmed and Raju — also stopped their motorbike to help the injured. They were headed home, in Bhajanpura, East Delhi.

In a matter of seconds the truck had either left them dead, or sent them battling in hospital.

Vipin, Gupta and Altaf Ahmed died on the spot; the other three succumbed to injuries in the hospital. The truck driver, SHO Singh said, is absconding. "We are not sure whether the truck was carrying a helper; no one saw them. We have sent out police teams to locate them," Singh said.

Singh said two more policemen — Constable Brij Bhushan, who was driving the PCR, and gunman Constable Pradeep — escaped unhurt as they were sitting in front seats of the two police vans. Timarpur police have registered two cases: one against auto-driver Vipin, and against the absconding truck driver.

Out on joyride, teen 'triggered' mishaps
Vipin Kumar, 15, who was driving the autorickshaw involved in the first accident, is a Class IX student who did not have a licence, the police said.

A native of Mathura (UP) till recently, he came to Delhi barely months ago. His father Angad Singh, also an auto-driver, said he was out on work when the teenager decided to borrow the auto-rickshaw of a neighbour, one Kewal Singh, and headed out on a joyride.

"Kewal Singh and his wife had gone to Balaji (a temple near Jaipur) last night, and Vipin took the keys from their relative and went out," Angad Singh said.

The family lives in Surender Colony, Jharoda Kalan.

Heading: From war-torn Kabul, women get frames of hope dipped in reality - Indian Express
Content:
The ITF men's circuit finds its way to the DLTA's tennis complex this week, and as play got underway today, the sound of racquet hitting ball found itself competing with the racket of heavy machinery as the stadium readies itself for the 2010 Commonwealth Games.

And even though 17-year-old Karanuday Singh's match took place some distance away from all the noise, the wild card entrant could not find enough concentration to get past his first-round opponent N Prashanth.

Ranked 120th on the ITF Junior Circuit, a combination of unforced errors and a poor first serve percentage put paid to his chances of advancing further in the draw.

Singh has been carrying out his summer training at Tennis Val, an academy in Valencia for the past two years, and he believes the tough regime on the Spanish clay courts has helped him immensely.

Last year, he reached the final of three consecutive tournaments on the junior circuit, winning two of them, and from 2008, he has begun playing on the senior tour.

The results may take their time coming, but the transition from under-18 to the men's circuit is far from a cakewalk.

"It's very different from playing in India because it's clay over there, but it helps your game a lot. The coaching pattern is not that different, but the intensity with which everything is done is so much more," he says.

Tennis Val is also frequented by world No 5 David Ferrer of Spain, who started practicing as a 17-year old.

"It's a better environment, you get to hit more balls and the rallies last longer. Today, the longest rally was maybe ten shots. On clay, it can go up to 20, or more. You need a lot of energy to soak it up," adds Singh.

Prashanth, who entered the main draw after a successful qualifying campaign, won this match 6-4, 6-3.

Tiwari wastes no time
QUALIFIER Abhijeet Tiwari took just 33 minutes to get past I-Ta Chen of Chinese Taipei, defeating him in this first round match 6-2, 6-0.

Last year's under-18 national champion Vijayant Malik, though, failed to make it past sixth seed Hsin-han Lee of Chinese Taipei, losing a close first set tie-break on his way to a 7-6 (5), 6-1 defeat.

In the only other singles match of the day, qualifier Nikunj Siwach beat Yannick Nelord 2-6, 7-5, 6-4, to make the second round.

Heading: Uphaar: CBI says Ansals’ punishment not enough - Indian Express
Content:
A year ago, Yalda Noori, 20, would not have envisioned stepping outside the house to work, let alone visiting another country. The shy girl, who lived as a refugee in Iran and Pakistan for eight years before returning home to Afghanistan in 2004, is now a painter with the Centre For Contemporary Arts Afghanistan (CCAA), in Kabul.

The institute is the only one of its kind with an arts centre for women in the war-ravaged country.

"I feel I can live and draw with freedom at CCAA," says Noori, who joined up last year. She is one of 18 artists participating in the first exhibition of paintings by Afghan women held outside the country. Some 40 works would be on display at Indira Gandhi National Centre for Arts (IGNCA), Janpath, beginning Tuesday.

And bringing about this silent revolution is Prof Rahraw Omarzad, former refugee and currently director of CCAA and a lecturer at the Faculty of Fine Arts in Kabul University. "When Yalda joined our centre her sole aim was to draw decorative pieces for her home. Today, she wants to become an artist and earn — and that's a good sign," says the 45-year-old, who set up the art centre with wife Manezah Hewad in 2004.

But archetypal pictures of Jam minaret in Buzkashi, or street scenes of Kabul do not form part of the exhibition. Instead, barbed wires in a canvas awash with red, broken concrete; veiled women; a lone green twig growing on a slab of stone are splashed in vibrant colours. The creations are flagrantly energetic and political, and spring from the isolated environment the girls grew up in.

"At CCAA, we stress on originality of thought," Omarzad says. "So they (students) have not been taught even the history of arts in Afghanistan."

His wife and CCAA co-founder Hewad says, "If you copy images of the bustling bazaar, or the Bamiyan Buddha, it is not a creation; it is good for hanging on the wall."

Take, for instance, 'Double Standards' by Nabila Horakhsh, 21: the canvas, sliced in two halves, depicts the imbalance in Afghan society with a male shoe on one side and a female band amid a green background on the other. "It is not the medium but the message that is more important for me," Horakhsh says..

Having lived for five years as a refugee in Peshawar, the Literature graduate from Kabul University now wants to become an art teacher. "Kabul," she says, "is changing; and the change is perceptible in the way women are stepping out and shouldering responsibility."

Geety Natiq, 25, considers herself lucky: for having joined the centre recently and for working with the design company Fazah, set up by a French national specialising in Afghan creations. "I am earning, and I can support my family," says Natiq, recently engaged to a man of her choice.

First exhibited in Kabul this February, the exhibit will travel next to Italy, USA, Spain and China. In India, it will be exhibited in Kolkata from September 19 to 27.

(In Delhi, exhibit on till Sept 14)

Heading: Infighting in Kasauli BJP comes to fore - Indian Express
Content:
The CBI on Monday told the Supreme Court that it supports the plea of Uphaar Victims Welfare Association for enhancing the punishment of brothers Sushil and Gopal Ansal in the 1997 Uphaar fire tragedy that claimed 59 lives.

The brothers were sentenced to two years' rigorous imprisonment by the trial court last November under IPC Section 304-A (causing death by rash and negligent act).

Appearing for CBI, senior advocate Harish Salve told the Bench of Justices B N Aggrawal and G S Singhvi that the Ansal brothers, who owned the theatre, deserved to be convicted for offences under the much graver IPC Section 304 — culpable homicide not amounting to murder — that carries a maximum punishment of life imprisonment.

Salve said the Uphaar tragedy was not merely a fire accident, for the Ansals were illegally running a carpet showroom within the theatre premises, which in turn precipitated the blaze. He said instead of having seven to eight exit doors there was a single exit in the hall available to those watching the film Border on June 13, 1997.

He also said an office was being run illegally on the terrace, adjoining the balcony, which made the victims' escape difficult.

Salve submitted that the trial court had failed to consider these alleged illegal activities of the Ansals and had let them off lightly with a two-year sentence. His contention came in response to a query from the Bench: whether CBI supported the application filed by the victims in High Court seeking enhanced punishment for the Ansal brothers.

Heading: 19-year-old mowed down by truck - Indian Express
Content:
The conflict between two warring factions of Kasauli Bharatiya Janata Party over the issue of welcoming Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal during his visit to Rihun village on Saturday has once again brought party infighting to the fore.

After Saturday's development, certain leaders of the party have decided to take up the issue with the state as well as central party high command, claiming that local MLA Dr Rajeev Sahjal was allegedly promoting factionalism in the party.

Sources in the party said trouble started when some frontline leaders of Kasauli BJP, along with a large number of supporters, assembled near Kumaharhatti on Saturday to welcome the Chief Minister, who was to inaugurate a private hotel at Rihun village. On receiving this information, certain loyalists of Dr Rajeev Sahjal reportedly succeeded in persuading the Chief Minister to change his route. Dhumal was earlier scheduled to travel via Barog, but the cavalcade was later diverted via Kumaharhatti bypass.

Party sources said this caused great resentment among party workers who had assembled near Barog. On the other hand, Dr Sahjal welcomed the Chief Minister with garlands.

Heading: The Lyngdoh effect? - Indian Express
Content:
A 19-year-old boy died and a man was injured after a speeding truck hit their motorcycle near the Sector-42 petrol pump around 4.30 pm on Monday. The deceased was identified as Anil Kumar, a resident of Sector 56. His uncle Uma Shanker, who was riding pillion, is admitted in the Government Multi-Specialty Hospital in Sector 16. The duo was on their way to the house of a relative in colony number 5 when the mishap occurred.

An eyewitness, Ranjodh, said: "The accident occurred within a fraction of a second. The truck driver fled even as Anil lay in a pool of blood. However, I managed to note down the registration number of the truck and gave it to the police."

The truck driver is yet to be identified, said police. "A case has not been registered yet as Uma Shanker is unconscious and unable to give a statement," said a police officer.

The deceased was pursuing graduation from a private college and was formerly employed with a call centre. He is survived by his father, a roadside tea vendor in Sector 22, an elder brother and sister-in-law.

Heading: Guv calls for focused approach to literacy mission - Indian Express
Content:
Election fervour cools as PU enforces rules

'Students of all departments are requested to collect their stickers without which entry to the campus would be prohibited' — this announcement greets all entering the three gates of the Panjab University. Without a doubt, preparations for the Panjab University Campus Students' Council (PUCSC) elections are in full swing.

But the usual excitement seems missing with heightened security acting as a dampener on poll spirits. With the recommendations of the Lyngdoh Committee being implemented in letter and spirit, the students' organisations seem to be treading with care.

Campaigning in the previous years was characterised by a show of strength with hordes of supporters accompanying the candidates to different departments. This year, the task has been left to a handful of students.

The limit of Rs 5,000 per candidate as campaign expenditure is another deterrent for the students' organisations. Now, the homogenous hoardings with larger-than-life photos of the candidates are missing.

The profile of the candidates and the focus of the elections have also witnessed a shift — lesser-know faces have been thrust into the limelight with the party taking centrestage.

Earlier, the candidates were popular names, whose posters adorned noticeboards all year long. But in a curious departure from tradition, this year Panjab University Students' Union (PUSU) as well as Students' Organisation of Panjab University (SOPU) announced the names of two hitherto unknown students as presidential candidates even as Tejpal Singh Cheema (PUSU) and Brinder Dhillon (SOPU) were continually projected as candidates.

Apparently, finding suitable candidates has become a difficult task for the organisations. Last year, elections were held in only five city colleges after over 70 per cent of the candidates were rejected under the criteria laid down in the committee report.

But the elections will go on. As says Vikas Rathee, president of Indian National Students' Organisation (INSO): "The leaders may keep changing but the work done by the organisation will stay."

Heading: No rest for those on the campaign trail - Indian Express
Content:
On the occasion of the 42nd anniversary of International Literacy Day, Governor Prabha Rau gave out a message to have a focused policy to educate adults under the Continuing Education Campaign. The CEC was the third phase of the Literacy Mission that was launched in the country in 1988, but it could not take off in Himachal except in Mandi district.

Today, as the Governor addressed the state-level celebration of Literacy Day, organised by the State Resource Centre and the Education Department, she said, "The trend started by the literacy mission should not be abandoned midway and should be taken ahead with a special programme for continuing education of adults."

She said the CEC was devised as a farsighted technique of enhancement of capabilities of human resource by educating them with special techniques. She expressed concern over the fact that of the over four lakh adult illiterate in Himachal, 71 per cent were women. "They also require special focus, which can be done by replicating the success of the literacy campaign during the mid-Nineties," she said.

Chairman of Himachal Gyan Vigyan Samiti Kuldeep Tanwar said Himachal needs to devote about Rs 10 crore for the CEC. "In case the state does not find support of the Centre, Himachal should not hesitate to replicate the model of Bihar, where one lakh Saksharta Abhiyaan volunteers are taking the CEC ahead with state funds."

Principal Secretary, Education, P.C. Dhiman said the state government was aware of the need of the hour and a policy for special sections such as illiterate and tribal areas was under discussion with the Centre.

Meanwhile, Principal Secretary, Health, Deepak Sanan said improvement in literacy has shown a positive effect in immunisation of children and campaigns such as total sanitation campaign.

Heading: Govt sitting on probe report into bad roads - Indian Express
Content:
A list of achievements, more promises, pulling down opponents and reciting couplets to charge the atmosphere — all was well on the penultimate day of campaigning for the Panjab University Campus Students' Council (PUCSC).

To expeditiously cover all prospective voters on the campus, every students' organisation divided its supporters into groups which were allocated a particular set of departments. As the candidates are relatively unknown faces, 'star campaigners' have been enlisted to accompany the 'rookies'.

The evenings are reserved for visiting the hostels. The candidates are never disappointed here with sloganeering and cheering continuing well into the night. "The time for campaigning depends on the kind of crowd we expect at a certain place. In the afternoons, canteens and hotel messes are the busiest places," said a candidate.

Door-to-door campaigning is also a favourite strategy among parties. Candidates can be seen meeting everyone personally and soliciting votes.

The campaign has also taken a hi-tech turn with candidates even approaching prospective voters through social networking sites.

PUSU
With the infighting among the Panjab University Students' Union (PUSU) members finally resolved, campaigning has started in full swing. President Tejpal Singh Cheema and former PUCSC president Parminder Jaswal led the campaign today. They visited different departments and motivated the students to vote. A meeting to finalise the panel was also held.

SOPU
Supporters of Students' Organisation of Panjab University (SOPU), after a two-hour long protest outside the V-C office, finally got their act together and went campaigning round the campus. Although the party has declared Sahil Nanda as the presidential candidate, president Brinder Dhillon continues to be the visible face as well as the voice of the organisation. Dhillon said: "We will focus on issues like better facilities for hostellers, central university status for the university and upgrading infrastructure."

INSO-SOI
The Indian National Students' Organisation (INSO) and Students' Organisation of India (SOI) are jointly contesting the elections. President Vikas Rathee and former general secretary Sunny Bhardwaj campaigned in different departments on Monday.

"If elected, we will fight against the increasing commercialisation of education, discontinue self-financing courses and introduce group insurance policies for students," said Rathee.

Heading: Scribes up in arms over police raid at newspaper office - Indian Express
Content:
The inquiry report, revealing ignored norms, was submitted four months back

It's been over four months that an inquiry report relating to ignored specifications in the construction of roads in Kangra district was submitted to the state government, but no action has been taken yet.

Sources in the Public Works Department said the probe was ordered in August 2007 after the then government received complaints of bad roads that needed strengthening, not only from locals, but tourists as well.

Some of the complaints indicated that sub-standard material was used in the construction of these roads and norms were ignored. These roads lead to Dharamshala from Gaggal and Malan. The issue had echoed in the Vidhan Sabha as well.

The roads were repaired after the then chief minister, Vibhadra Singh, took strong notice of the matter and directed the Public Works Department to carry out repairs and initiate a probe. But, within a year, the condition of the roads deteriorated again.

The roads have developed many potholes, craters and even the tar has been washed away due to rains. Two private agencies had executed the work and the Public Works Department had supervised it.

The Centre had allotted about Rs 17 crore for upgrading these roads, the length of which is nearly 30 kilometres.

Confirming that the inquiry report had been submitted to the government about four months back, Chief Engineer (North) N.L. Sharma said action would be taken against those who did not follow specifications in strengthening the roads. He also promised that the repairs would start as soon as the rains stop. The Chief Engineer said the PWD had suffered a loss of about Rs 70 crore in the shape of damage to bridges and roads due to heavy rain in Kangra, Una and Chamba districts.

Heading: 6 pilgrims dead during Manimahesh yatra - Indian Express
Content:
The Sangrah Police in Sirmour district on Sunday raided the office of a vernacular daily on the basis of a telephone call from an unidentified person.

The District Journalists' Association, under the leadership of their president S.P. Jerath, today submitted a representation to Sirmour Deputy Commissioner Pushpinder Rajput to be sent to Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal.

The journalists' body has demanded action against the police officials who acted without verifying the facts.

The journalists said some unknown person called up the Sangrah police, saying that Jai Parkash, a correspondent with the daily, was involved in supplying drugs. They said the police immediately raided the office of the daily but could not find anything illegal. They have urged the CM to take action against the officials concerned.

Heading: Election Commission seeks explanation from Punjab Police - Indian Express
Content:
Over six lakh pilgrims visited the famous Manimahesh Lake (Dal Lake) and took a holy dip during the yatra, which officially began on Janmashtami and concluded today. As many as six pilgrims died during the two-week-long yatra.

Till Saturday, four lakh pilgrims had visited the holy lake and nearly 75,000 people visited the lake on Sunday. Additional District Magistrate, Bharmaur, Naresh Kumar Lath said the unofficial figures of pilgrims could be more.

It is learnt that the lake had partially frozen due to sub-zero temperatures.

The HP Mountaineering Institute had set up a camp at Gauri Kund for the pilgrims. Besides, the administration had also made arrangements for a helicopter service that was operated by a private company from Bharmaur to Gauri Kund.

Giving details of the casualties during the yatra, Additional Superintendent of Police, Chamba, Devinder Chaudhary said six pilgrims died during the period of the yatra. Chaudhary said that while Ajeet Singh of Bassi village in Kangra district had died due to a heart attack yesterday, Vijay Kumar of Dina Nagar in Gurdaspur district died on September 6.

He said Vijay Kumar, a DSP in a Gurdaspur sub-jail, fell into a deep gorge in Hadsar and died. Other victims were Chiman Lal of Mirthal in Punjab, who died of a cardiac arrest on Sept-ember 3.

Parkash Chand of Jwali in Kangra district died in an accident on August 23 and Kulbhushan Kumar of Surjera village in Una district died due to a heart attack on August 21.

Heading: Virk’s family not cooperating for investigation: Patiala SSP - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab State Election Commission has sought explanation and clarification from Moga police regarding the appointment of four police officials as incharge of the various police stations, after the announcement of the Nagar Council elections.

Inspector Satnam Singh; Inspector Pushpinder Singh; Sub Inspector Rajesh Hastir, incharge CIA; and Ram Singh, Incharge Moga City Division I are among those against whom the complaint was lodged with the State Election Commission.

The complaint had been lodged by Punjab State Congress Committee president Mohinder Singh Kaypee and Moga Congress MLA Joginderpal Jain. SSP Moga Ashok Baath confirmed that the clarification has been sought by the Election Commission.

The SSP added that he had sent the inquiry report to the Commission on Sunday evening. Sources say the district has claimed that these police officials were appointed before the announcement of the Moga Nagar Council elections, or the implementation of the code of conduct.

The SSP denied any misuse of official machinery favouring the ruling party, and any intimidation of the Congress candidates. The SSP also assured the Election Commission that fair, free and peaceful elections would be conducted. He stated that there was no need for the deployment of central forces, as demanded by the Pradesh Congress.

When contacted, MLA Joginderpal Jain said Commission had sought a clarification from the very persons against whom the complaint was lodged. He said that the inquiry should be conducted by an independent agency.

The Congress had complained to the the Commission about police high-handedness, interference in the election process at the instance of the ruling Akali Dal and intimidation of the Congress candidates.

Heading: Protesting teachers try to storm SAD office - Indian Express
Content:
The family of former Punjab DGP SS Virk is not cooperating with the Special Investigation Team (SIT) formed to investigate the disproportionate assets case registered against him, according to SSP Patiala SK Asthana. The SSP is is the Investigating Officer in the case.

For the second time, the team returned empty-handed after finding the family's house locked.

At about 3.45 pm today, a team of SIT officials, along with 20 officials from various departments, came for the assessment of the house, belonging to Virk. After finding the house locked, the team took measurement of the wall and gate, and left after about half and hour.

The team included members of Public Works Department, Building and Roads, Sewerage, Electricity, Horticulture and Architecture.

SSP Asthana said, "The family is not cooperating with us for the investigation. We have again served them a notice for September 15. According to the security personnel deputed outside the house, the earlier notice had not been given to Virk."

SSP Asthana added that that the photocopy of the notice was in the court, as Virk's lawyer wanted a stay on the assessment proceedings. "The security guard said that the lawyer took the photocopy. Virk's lawyer had also moved the Mohali court for a stay on the assessment proceedings. Since no stay was granted, we filed the reply in the court today. It will come up for hearing in the court on September 15."

The team had earlier come on September 1, and given a notice for today. "If they do not cooperate, then we will take the legal course. We will move the court for assessment of property, and obtain orders for the purpose,'' stated SSP Asthana.

Heading: Uproar likely in the Assembly on last day of session - Indian Express
Content:
Hundreds of protesting ETT teachers attempted to storm inside the Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) building in Sector 26 today afternoon. Their attempt was foiled by UT police.

The Elementary Teachers Training (ETT) teachers complained that despite repeated reminders, their grievances have not been redressed.

Police used force to ensure that the protesting teachers, numbering over 400, did not create a ruckus.

President of ETT Adhyapak Sangh Jaswinder Singh Sidhu said the teachers are demanding transfer of all Zila Parishad schools to the Education Department. "The government had promised this during the elections, but have done nothing in this regard," he complained.

Sidhu added that the interference of the local Panchayats is creating problems for the teachers.

Dr Daljit Singh Cheema, Political Advisor to the Chief Minister, reached the spot to discuss the issue with the teachers. Sidhu said an ultimatum of a week has been given to the government to address these demands, failing which they will intensify their protest.

Heading: Rs 2,500 crore bungled in name of school education - Indian Express
Content:
The last day of the Assembly session on Wednesday is likely to decide the next course of action for former CM Capt Amarinder Singh and three others, including two former Cabinet ministers, in wake of the report tabled in the Vidhan Sabha recently. The report indicted all of them for "misuse of office" and "corruption" in the Amritsar land deal case.

Sources said that while their disqualification seems unlikely, the House has other options. It can recommend registration of a case against the indicted members. A harsher action, though, has the potential of making the former CM a "martyr", say sources.

The issue can also be left in abeyance, since the SAD-BJP MLAs will be content with Amarinder and others holding the "indictment tag." The Assembly session on Wednesday is likely to be a stormy session, with both the Treasury bench MLAs and the Opposition MLA preparing a strategy to lock horns.

The Congress is likely to stall the proceedings of the Assembly over the report. SAD has called a meeting of its MLAs two hours before the session begins on Wednesday. The Congress MLAs, who have been picking loopholes in the legality of the composition of the committee, will adopt a tough posture in Amarinder's support to ensure that the proceedings of the House are stalled.

Harish Rai Dhanda, the chairman of the committee which has indicted the former chief minister and others, today gave an ambiguous statement on the issue. Addressing newspersons today, Dhanda said the committee was set up with the consent of Congress Leader of Opposition Rajinder Kaur Bhattal.

"The list of the Congress MLAs was given by Bhattal. Their MLAs also attended 15 meetings, but later expressed dissent," said Dhanda.

An advocate who has been advising Amarinder on the issue said the matter is pending before the High Court. "Besides, the issue concerns the proceedings of the previous House. It cannot be taken up by the House in the present composition," he said. Both the Akali Dal and the BJP have issued a whip to ensure the presence of all members in the Assembly on Wednesday, the last day of the session.

Heading: State meets DAP, urea shortage - Indian Express
Content:
During its previous tenure, SAD-BJP govt availed grant of Rs 500 crore over five years, but little achieved at ground level

Despite the fact that Punjab Government availed a grant of Rs 2,500 crores from the Centre in the name of setting up and implementing the Elementary Directorate (ED) in the state, little has been achieved at ground level in this regard.

It is learnt that from 2000 to 2005, the state availed a grant of Rs 500 crore each year for revamping school education. The objective was to stem the rot in school education in the state, especially at the primary and middle level.

Like other states of the country, Punjab had adopted the Elementary Directorate system in 2000, as part of the National Education Policy of the Centre. This was done during the previous tenure of the Akali-BJP government.

Sources point out that under this system, schools would have been classified in two categories. Schools up to Class VIII would be considered elementary schools, and those from Class IX to XII would be regarded as senior secondary schools. The grant had been provided by World Bank, and the state government availed it for five consecutive years, from 2000 to 2005.

Little has been achieved in this regard, though. The state continues to have 12,000 primary schools. Under the Elementary Directorate system, there would have been no primary schools.

The scheme also envisaged that Trained Graduate Teachers (TGTs) be appointed for Science, Maths and English, Class IV onwards. But till now, the government has done nothing in this regard.

According to rules, TGT teachers should have passed Class XII with science, maths and English. But senior officers in the Education Department point out that the state government has not bothered with this stipulation while recruiting teachers. According to an official, though the recruited teachers might be well-qualified, they may not have done Class XII with these subjects.

Another senior officer in the Education Department wondered what has the state government done with the grant, since infrastructure in schools has not been improved. From time to time, teachers' associations have written to Director Public Instruction (Elementary), Punjab Education Secretary and the Education Minister to set up the Elementary Directorate, but to no avail.

When contacted, DPI Jagdish Singh Khatra refused to comment on the matter. Education Minister Punjab Upinderjit Kaur too evaded a comment on the issue. When questioned in this regard, District Education Officer (Elementary) Joginder Das said the scheme was to be implemented by the state government, and district level officers had little to do with it.

Heading: SAD planning show of strength in Patiala - Indian Express
Content:
50 per cent of the urea each year is sent by the Centre

Punjab, which was told by the Centre to meet the DAP and urea shortage on its own, has asked the wheat growers not to panic as the supply was adequate.

DAP shortage is one of the major concerns for the wheat farmers. B S Sidhu, Director, Agriculture, said, "Though we may not have surplus DAP or urea, but there won't be shortage. We have about 70,000 tonnes of DAP at present and the Centre has promised 1.5 lakh tonnes in September and another 1.75 lakh tonnes in October.

This will help us in sowing season, which will start on October 30."

However, Sidhu said, "A lot also depends on the Railways that has to bring DAP to Punjab. Hope there is no delay on their part."

Notably, 50 per cent of the urea each year is sent by the Centre under the Essential Commodities Act, while Punjab meets rest of the demand through its plants in Nangal and Bathinda. Wheat sowing on 35 lakh hectares in Punjab begins in November and the total demand for urea is 12.5 lakh tonnes and DAP 5.5 lakh tonnes.

Heading: Mumbai cops seek help in tracing cheat - Indian Express
Content:
After the show of strength by former chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh on the home turf of CM Parkash Singh Badal, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) is getting ready to hold a massive rally in Rajpura on the occasion of stone-laying ceremony of the thermal plant on September 29.

Sources said besides CM Parkash Singh Badal and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, senior Akali and BJP leaders from the state would address the rally.

"We will try to gather over two lakh persons from Patiala, Lehragagga and Fatehgarh Sahib," they said.

Punjab Tourism and Jails Minister Hira Singh Gabria held a meeting in the city on Saturday to make arrangements for the rally.

Paramjit Singh Sidhwan, political secretary of Sukhbir Singh Badal, said, "The SAD wants to show the residents of Amarinder's constituency the development that has taken place under their rule."

Former Samana SAD MLA Surjit Singh Rakhra said the venue was right for a show of strength.

Sources said the SAD was now wooing the Backward Classes ahead of the Parliamentary polls.

Gabria, who is also the chairman of SAD's Backward Classes Cell, claimed that they would hold rallies all over the state to expose the Congress that was playing with the sentiments of the poor.

However, Patiala MP Preneet Kaur said the success of the Lambi rally had forced the SAD to plan this rally.

Heading: Workers of co-op sugar mills threaten suicide - Indian Express
Content: The Mumbai Police have asked the Amritsar Police for help in tracing a man who sold fake MBBS and MD certificates to an imposter father-son duo, Brijbhushan Kaul and Varun. The accused, identified as Dogra, allegedly hails from the city. Kaul and his son used to impersonate as a Navy officer and a paediatrician, respectively, and dupe several jewellery shops in Delhi, Goa, Punjab and Haryana. They were arrested along with Kaul's wife, Meenakshi, two days ago, from a hotel in Mumbai. Police sources said Kaul had bought fake degrees for himself and his son. Amritsar SSP Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh said they would extend all possible help.

Heading: Gobindgarh Fort to be opened for public on Oct 2 - Indian Express
Content:
Castigating the SAD-BJP government for not keeping the pre-poll promise, over 75 workers from various cooperative sugar mills across Punjab have threatened to commit mass suicide outside the residence of Cooperatives Minister Captain Kanwaljit Singh in Chandigarh on September 16.

Members of the Cooperative Sugar Mills Workers' Federation said the SAD-BJP combine had promised that the six closed mills would be run by the government.

They said they have not been given benefits, including timely payment of wages and merging of DA with salaries, which have been awarded by the Haryana government. "Over 5,000 labourers from these sugar mills have not been paid their wages for over a year," said Balwinder Singh Zeera, state convener of the federation.

Karnail Singh Lakhimpura, president of the workers' body, said mass suicide was proposed seeing the indifference of the government.

Kusumjit Kaur Sidhu, Financial Commissioner, Cooperatives, said the government was aware of the demands of the labourers and they would be met soon.

Heading: Revenue up, but picture not rosy - Indian Express
Content:
After a long wait, the public can now have a peek into history, as the Gobindgarh Fort of Maharaja Ranjit Singh is set to be handed over to the civil administration on October 2.

About two years ago, Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh had handed over the keys of the fort, which was occupied by the Army, to the then chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh.

Deputy Commissioner K S Pannu said an expenditure of Rs 10 crore was likely to be incurred on the conservation of the fort, which dates back to 1760 and had housed the residence of British General O'Dyer, besides the treasury of Maharaja Ranjit Singh and the 'Phansi Ghar', where the Indian freedom fighters were hanged. Pannu said the Ministry of Culture and Tourism was yet to decide on the entry tickets. The work on the construction of the boundary wall around the bastion has been completed, he said.

Initially known as Bhangian Da Qila, the fort was rebuilt by Maharaja Ranjit Singh in 1808.

Heading: On a high - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab has not made any provision in the budget for meeting the additional expenses that the Pay Commission's new pay packages will entail

For cash-starved Punjab, it has been a good year so far. Robust value added tax (VAT) collections in the first five months of this financial year have resulted in Punjab setting an ambitious target of raking in Rs 7,200 crore, a jump of Rs 1,500 crore from last year.

A good wheat harvest has brought in a record Rs 180 crore as purchase tax, and paddy looks equally promising (over Rs 200 crore more). Besides, the revenue from stamps and registration is also showing signs of revival after plunging by Rs 400 crore last year.

But it is not yet time for celebration for Punjab, as its macro-economic condition still remains worrisome. It is still meeting a part of its revenue expenses from borrowings (about Rs 5,000 crore) and its interest on debt is touching Rs 4,800 crore.

While borrowings are mounting, the repayment of principal amount is also due from 2013.

Even by most optimistic estimates, the additional inflow from VAT, stamps and registration et al will add another Rs 750-1,000-crore net revenue to the state exchequer. But Punjab has not made any provision in the budget for meeting the additional expenses that the Pay Commission's new pay packages will entail.

In fact, its financial position is so precarious that it does not have enough to even meet the first three months' expenditure if it were to implement the Pay Commission recommendations.

Also, Punjab may not be able to sustain the tempo of 40 per cent growth in VAT collections achieved in the first half of this year; these are likely to reduce towards the other half of the year, as is the case every year.

"Though we are expecting VAT collections to touch Rs 7,200 crore, we are also looking at an overall jump of nearly 25 per cent this year," says Excise and Taxation Commissioner A. Venu Prasad.

The Excise and Taxation Department is, however, hopeful that registering of 15,000 new dealers, setting of commodity-wise targets for inspectors and better scrutiny, investigation and billing system, besides more manpower and higher tax compliance, will see this trend grow in the years to come.

Heading: Commercial Break - Indian Express
Content:
You once said films are like marriages.
Yes, it's a gamble. We say yes to it in the beginning as we are excited about the project, without knowing the outcome.

I thought Cash was an interesting project and it would be a hit, but all in vain. When it comes to marriage it's the same. I am not ready for marriage now as I am very hyper and restless.

But I am checking out guys.

You mother says she is seriously looking for a groom for you.
Yes she is and she doesn't mind me being in a live-in relationship. I wish to know the person well enough before I get married.

You are very choosy in selection of movies. What made you sign Hijack which is done by a debutant director?

I took a break from working and did what I enjoyed - learnt Russian ballet. At that time, I saw the industry as a neutral person. I realised that I want to work with young, upcoming and talented directors. I was moved by the script of Hijack as it is based on a realistic situation.

What is your next project?
It is Shivam Nair's Exchange Offer opposite Rahul Bose. It's a romantic movie. I'm learning how to play a guitar for the movie. Rahul is from a different school of thought and is very hard working.

Heading: Airline told to pay Rs 10,000 for deficiency in services - Indian Express
Content:
Tired of playing the 'bubbly' Punjabi mummyji, actor Kirron Kher is making a conscious change with Saas, Bahu and Sensex

If there's someone who always looks elegant in Bollywood, it's her. From her sarees to her jewellery to her impeccable sense of style, Chandigarh's own Kirron Kher takes the cake, icing and all. On home grounds once again, this time clubbing a Satya Paul do at the Taj along with the promotion of her forthcoming film 'Saas, Bahu aur Sensex', Mrs Kher arrived looking - we'll say it again - elegant as ever.

Donning a flowing chiffon saree matched to the T with her own jewellery, she walked in at the store full of gushing ladies. "It's always good to be home. You have no idea how lucky you are to be in such a nice city," dimpled Kirron who made sure we caught the trailer of 'Saas, Bahu aur Sensex' before a conversation. First things first.

She's no longer a Punjabi mummyji onscreen. "It was getting too stereotypical. Of course playing Punjabi comes easy but it's time to give it a break," mentioned the actor who is now stepping out as Mrs Sen in the film. "There were umpteen reasons to do this film. One, it's Warner Brothers' first release in India and also the story is so different and so is my character," Kirron runs us through the script that brings in loads of women - kitty party types to affable homemakers - and a stock broker. "I still know nothing about the stock markets. Interestingly, once the trailers have gone on air, I have started getting calls from investors," chuckles Kher who once again will be seen pulling out her own ensembles and jewellery in the film, both of which are understated and elegant (that's the third use of the word!). "I have always worn my own...even in Devdas," tells Kirron who mentions Khamosh Pani and Devdaas as some of her most favourite works. "That's the kind of watchable cinema that I am looking to do," Kirron's list for the year includes 'Dostana', 'Kambakht Ishq' and 'Action Replay' and as she says so herself, 'you won't see me play a Punjabi mummyji again except in Dostana.'

Speaking of her real avatar, son Sikander Kher has made his debut this year and with two films under his belt, hope he's done Mum proud. "He got rave reviews and is already working on a few more projects," answers Kher who doesn't dish out advice to his son at the drop of a hat. "Today, kids are independent. Of course we discuss work at home but in the end the decision is theirs alone," the real mum sums it up for now. Here's looking forward to Mrs Sen!.

Heading: SOPU protests against Law dept chairman’s ‘double standards’ - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed MDLR Airlines to pay Rs 10,000 as compensation on account of deficiency in services.

The Kolkata-Chandigarh flight landed at Delhi instead of its stated destination (Chandigarh).

The airline as well as the travel agency — Aadish Tour and Travels—has been asked to compensate for the difference in airfare.

The complainant Vinod Kumar, a resident of Sector 33, had purchased a return ticket for the Kolkata to Chandigarh flight on February 6 for Rs 12,300

In Kolkata, he reported at the airport two hours prior to the scheduled time but was told that the flight was delayed.

Kumar alleged that the airlines failed to inform him regarding the delay and did not provide any meals during the five-hour waiting period. The complaint states that the flight landed at the New Delhi airport around 10 pm. From here, the airlines arranged an ordinary bus to ferry the passengers to Chandigarh.

MDLR Airlines refused to accept the court's summons and the judgment was ex parte.

The forum found it to be a clear case of harassment. "The flight landed at the wrong destination and the passengers were kept waiting. Moreover, the travel agency did not bother to arrange an alternative flight from Delhi to Chandigarh. It even refused to refund the fare from Delhi to Chandigarh, for which it did not render any service," observed the forum.

Heading: With strict guidelines in place, city colleges yet to find ‘suitable’ candidates - Indian Express
Content:
High drama prevailed outside the VC's office at the Panjab University on Monday after SOPU members raised slogans against the chairperson of the Department of Laws for his alleged 'double standards'.

The students went to meet the vice-chancellor to protest against Chairperson Shashi Sharma for allegedly stopping them from campaigning in the class while permitting the INSO for the same.

SOPU leader Barinder Singh Dhillon, said, " With just a day left for the canvassing we had gone to the law department to address students but the chairman denied us permission. The INSO members were, however allowed to address the classes. The code of conduct should be applicable to all parties."

The V-C called a meeting where the chairman was asked to narrate his side of the story. Sources revealed that the chairman had denied giving permission or denying the same to any student organisation.

Shashi Sharma, when asked for his comment said, "I cannot allow outsiders to enter my department and for that matter Barinder Dhillon is an outsider since he is not a student of the varsity. I cannot stop him from entering the varsity as that is for the authorities but I can certainly stop him from entering my department".
