Dean Students Welfare Naval Kishore said, "We have sought a written report from the chairman with regards to the incident following which appropriate action would be taken."

Heading: History revisited - Indian Express
Content:
While the canvassing for the students' council elections has picked up momentum in the University, the activity is virtually absent in the colleges.

With the strict guidelines of the Lyngdoh Committee in effect, students are finding it difficult to zero in on the names of the candidates.

For most party workers, attendance is one of the most important criteria. "Students seldom attend all the lectures in the college. It is difficult to find candidates who have attended at least 75 per cent of the lectures and that is why we have not decided on the panel as yet," says Karan, a PUSU supporter at the Government College, Sector 11.

Even in DAV College, Sector 10, parties including SOPU, PUSU and SOI are yet to finalise their candidates.

With the nominations to be filed by Tuesday, the parties are busy shortlisting the most suitable candidate. Some parties also see an alliance or two happening with other parties due to which they are not releasing the names of their contestants.

Simrat Gill, President, SOI at DAV College, "Talks are on with other parties. We may enter into an alliance with the INSO. As all this will be clear by evening, our panel will be decided after that."

Students from INSO have however formed their panel, contradicting the SOI's claim of an alliance.

Giving the details of their panel, Presidential candidate Karamvir Singh said, "We have shortlisted our candidates and will file the nominations tomorrow morning. While Dishant Nalwa of BCA II will contest as General Secretary, Kulvir Singh of B A First year will be the candidate for Joint Secretary."

The party is yet to finalise the candidate for Vice-President.

Even in Government College for Girls, Sector 11, the election atmosphere is not really charged.

Says Reena, a SOPU supporter, "Since it is a girls' college, so things takes place in an organised manner and since the coming of Lyngdoh Committee, it has become all the more streamlined. The spice seems to have gone out of elections."

Heading: ‘Student elections are no longer a show of money and muscle power’ - Indian Express
Content:
Early 1970s:Indirect elections used to be held back then. The department representatives from all the teaching faculties would elect two vice-presidents who worked under the Dean Student Welfare, who was the president. Nagender Singh, a leader from Congress, was elected in 1974 and Jagmohan Kang, then an Akali supporter, was elected as the vice-president in 1975. This was followed by the period of Emergency, during which no elections were held.

Emergency period:This period saw the emergence of the Progressive Students Union (PSU). Dr Ajaib Singh, a member of the Punjab Public Selection Commission, was its founder president. The students' demand for holding direct elections was finally agreed to and Bhupinder Khosa was elected as president in 1977.

1982:PUSU emerged successful in breaking the dominance of PSU over the elections. Rajinder Deepa from PUSU was elected as president in this year. He was re-elected in 1983. After 1984, the Punjab government banned elections.

1997:Direct elections started in Panjab University from this year. Since then, the Panjab University Students' Union (PUSU) and the Students' Organisation of Panjab University (SOPU) have dominated the Panjab University Campus Students' Council (PUCSC). However, Munish Anand from PUSU was elected as the president in the 1997 elections. The founder president of SOPU Dyal Pratap Randhawa won the election to the post of president for the next two consecutive years.

Post-1997:A long stint by PUSU leaders followed post-1997. M S Kang in 2002 and 2003, Rajwinder Singh Lucky in 2004 and Amandeep Singh in 2005 — all were from PUSU.

2006:Dalvir Singh Goldy from SOPU put a stop on this winning streak, who was elected the president in 2006. However, the seat again went to PUSU with Parminder Jaswal as the president in 2007.

ABVP, NSUI, HSA, HPSA have never had too much of a following. In the last two years, INSO has emerged as an important party. The party has been in power in alliance with SOPU in 2006 and PUSU in 2007. This year, the party is fielding its own presidential candidate after having tied up with SOI, a party backed by the SAD. This could emerge as a strong third front in the present elections.

Heading: PU elections losing steam? Students doubtful over alliances - Indian Express
Content:
September is that month of the year for which students wait eagerly, as it is the time for the Student Council elections and the entire campus is full of enthusiasm. Party supporters are busy wooing potential voters and brainstorming to form an alliance, which may increase their chances of winning the elections. 

After the guidelines of the Lyngdoh Committee came into force, the pomp surrounding the elections has gone down. Though car rallies to show party strength are still held, the overall atmosphere is not that upbeat as compared to previous years.

Panjab University elections have always been synonymous with a vulgar display of wealth and muscle power. Spending thousands of rupees on fuel for the car rallies and sneaking outsiders into the hostel to use them in time of need: all these were once prominent features of PU elections. For the last two years, all this has undergone a significant change. While earlier, anybody who had the potential to spend money blindly, could contest the elections but now parties are keeping in mind that the candidate should be a regular student, thanks to the Lyngdoh Committee recommendations. Billboards, manifestos and lavish parties no longer form a part of the election campaign. Though student bodies do feel that this has limited their area of interaction with the students, Lyngdoh Committee has, by and large, played a positive role in the student elections.  

For one, the guidelines have helped streamline the entire procedure. The elections no longer mean a show of muscle power, rather it has become more a case of nominating a candidate who commands a good reputation in the campus. Also the parties cannot print manifestos and spend money in any way they wish.

They are also trying not to indulge in any violence for it may mar their chances of contesting elections in the future as well. More or less it was a wise decision on part of the varsity to implement the guidelines as it has made the elections a free and fair affair.

Heading: Please withdraw our security: Runaway couple tells HC - Indian Express
Content:
With a feeling that the pomp and show will just last for a short time span and later the parties would have nothing much to talk about, the students at the Panjab University do not seem to be much interested in the forthcoming student elections.

Though elections are a hot issue at the varsity, students seem to be not much bothered about the same.

Narender Kaur from the BMS department says: "I am not bothered about the elections, my studies are my priority and I have little interest in student politics."

Voicing similar views, Ved, a student from the Department of Laws said, "There is no research and development in the university but no political party has taken up the issue. All they are bothered about is in settling their personal scores and winning the elections as a matter of pride."

Students also raised fingers on different parties forming alliances with each other.

A few students said: "One day we hear that different parties have issues against each other and the next day we know that the two have formed an alliance.

Another student from the Department of Laws said, "Students contesting elections have no ethics at all. One day they are seen fighting with each other and suddenly the very next day they form an alliance. All these parties are just bothered about satisfying their egos."

Politics is a dirty game in which all students do is waste their time. In case the elections are to be held, they should be done in a refined manner and students should atleast have some issues to fight for. These were a few thoughts that were echoed by the students at the university.

Heading: Non-payment of wages to Pakistani convicts: DGP (prisons) to explain - Indian Express
Content:
In a rather unusual case, a runaway couple today requested the Punjab and Haryana High Court to reduce the number of the security personnel for "protecting" them from their parents.

Reason: the five security guards were proving to be an irritant and deterrent for the couple to enjoy their married life.

The security had been granted by the High Court to the couple of village Gharunda, Karnal, after they moved the court demanding protection from their parents and relatives. The two had married against the wishes of their families.

The parents of both had strongly objected to the inter-caste marriage, the court was told.

A petition demanding police protection was filed by the couple on June 23 this year. Since the parents and relatives of the couple were present in the court and strongly objected the marriage, the court had directed the Karnal Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) to grant five security guards to the couple.

The High Court had also stayed any adverse action against the husband of the woman in the wake of an FIR filed against him by the parents of the woman.

Since then, five security guards had been deployed with the couple, including a woman guard.

The five guards were on a 24-hour duty with the couple and also accompanied the two on their honeymoon. Irritated by the 'unwanted' company, the couple moved the High Court seeking permission to reduce the security. Apart from invasion of privacy, the couple submitted that the security be reduced since they were unable to bear their expenditure.

Allowing the application, the High Court has directed the Karnal SSP to decrease the number of security guards. Moments after the orders were pronounced, the wife was seen requesting a police officer to withdraw the entire security. The woman told the officer: "Please withdraw the entire security, we don't want them."

Heading: Rodrigues asks MC to manage solid waste scientifically - Indian Express
Content:
With regards to a letter written by Pakistani convicts in the Patiala Central Jail, which was later converted into a PIL, the Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed the Punjab Director General of Police (DGP), Prisons, to file an affidavit.

Fourteen Pakistani convicts had written to the High Court demanding directions to the Punjab government to release their monthly wages of five years.

The letter was written by Mohammad Iqbal and 13 others confined in the Patiala Central Jail. They have been imprisoned for a period of 10 to 15 years for various offences.

"Since we have no money, we are facing lots of hardships. Directions may be issued to the jail authorities to release our monthly wages from January 2003 to 2007 as per the Punjab Jail Manual," the letter written by the convicts states.

Taking note of the accusations, the Patiala Sessions Judge had also sought a report from the jail superintendent. Clarifying his stand, the superintendent had submitted that the convicts had been paid their wages for the year 2003 and the rest would be paid shortly.

The convicts have also sought permission for the court to work in the jail factory to enable them to earn wages.

Taking note of this, the High Court today directed the DGP to file an affidavit explaining as to why the wages are not being released to the prisoners.

Sessions judges to file report on conditions in jails
Taking note of the "inhuman conditions" prevailing in various jails in Punjab, the Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed five District and Session Judges to file their respective inspection reports.

The five Judges have also been directed to file replies, if they have not inspected the jails falling in their jurisdiction, as to why they have not inspected the jails. The judges of five districts — Ludhiana, Jalandhar, Amritsar, Gurdaspur and Ferozepur —- have been directed to submit their reports. The directions were passed in wake of a letter written by President of SAD, Amritsar, Simranjit Singh Mann to former Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court Justice V K Jain.

Mann had highlighted the inhuman conditions prevailing in the jails as he was himself lodged in one of the central jails in Punjab. Giving a detailed description of the inhuman conditions, he said prisoners were not given proper attention.

The letter was then converted as a public interest litigation (PIL). The judges have been directed to file their inspection reports within four weeks.

Heading: Administration finalises 16 houses to host tourists under Bed & Breakfast scheme - Indian Express
Content:
To review the progress of solid waste management by the Municipal Corporation, UT Administrator and Punjab Governor General S F Rodrigues (Retd) visited the garbage collection site near the Solid Waste Management Plant in Dadumajra.

During the public hearing session on September 1, the residents of the colony had apprised the Administrator of the problem. Following this, the Administrator had directed Municipal Commissioner Dr Roshan Sunkaria to tackle the problem immediately.

Accompanied by secretary M P Singh, General Rodrigues discussed the issue with Finance Secretary Sanjay Kumar, Dr Sunkaria and other senior officers of the Corporation.

He directed them to manage the waste in a scientific way by adopting advanced technological measures for a polluted environment poses a serious risk to the residents and could lead to infections and diseases.

The staff has also been asked to suitably cover the garbage with earth and to subsequently evolve a system of treating liquid waste and channelising treated water to Patiala-ki-Rao through a sewage treatment plant.

General Rodrigues asked the MC officers to make the project environment-friendly by constantly monitoring the work, followed with corrective measures so that there is no inconvenience to the residents of the colony.

The Governor also reviewed the renovation work at the Tagore Theatre and discussed the seating plan, light and sound system, interior decoration and other infrastructure support. He also discussed the parking plan in the theatre premises and stressed the need for optimal utilisation of space in the complex.

The residents of Dadumajra have been facing a tough time due to the non-functional solid waste management plant. Since the garbage is not being processed, it remains at the dumping ground. This gives way to foul smell and is proving harmful to the health of the residents. The MC has already issued notice to J P Associates, which is responsible for the plant.

Heading: Cultural events, discounts galore on World Tourism Day - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Administration has finalised 16 households under the recently launched the Bed and Breakfast scheme. These households have been classified under two categories — gold and silver — depending upon the facilities being extended to the visitors by these households.

A Sector 22-based Arora family became the first city family to receive a family of Ornoy from Israel on Tuesday night.

The Chandigarh Tourism Department has also done extensive publicity for these households under the scheme and even put up the relevant information pertaining to such households on the Tourist Information Centres, ISBT-17; Tourist Information Centre, Plaza, Railway Station, Chandigarh Airport and the Tourism Department in Sector 9.

Be it the posh Sector 2, Sector 9 or places like Manimajra, Sector 30-A, Sector 19-A, 21-A, 34-D or Sector 43-B, families from almost all sectors of the city have come forward and expressed willingness to be included as service providers to foreign tourists under the scheme.

The Tourism department has constituted a committee of officers, who respond to the applications submitted under the scheme by residents, discuss it and after paying a visit to the household and meeting members of the family, approve to include the same under the Bed and Breakfast scheme.

"It becomes our responsibility to check and see if the conditions and environment offered at a particular household suits the requirements of a tourist. We need to see if the facilities being offered to a tourist at a particular household matches the requisite standards. Only after reaching a satisfaction level, we approve of a household to be included under the scheme," said a senior UT official.

TheAdministration had received the Centre's approval for the scheme on March 24. The Administration plans to keep a minimum tariff of about Rs 850 to Rs 1,100 per day, which will include a bed, breakfast, parking space, attached washroom and air-conditioning.

Accommodations measuring more than 7.5 marlas can be covered under the scheme, provided the owner of the accommodation stays at the property which has a safe-parking space, air-conditioner and an attached washroom.

Heading: ‘Let us collaborate with compassion for the girl child’ - Indian Express
Content:
Come September 27 — World Tourism Day — and the UT Administration will be offering a number of attractions and events for city residents. Be it the much-awaited inauguration of the revamped Tagore Theatre or the recently set up Le Corbusier Centre, both would be inaugurated on September 27.

Besides, the Administration shall also be organising a series of performances at the airport, railway station and tourist destinations such as Sukhna Lake and Rose Garden.

Speculations are also being made regarding offering of certain discounts at various Industrial and Tourism Corporation food joints and hotels in the city on the day.

"A number of performances shall be organised at the Tagore Theatre for celebrating both the World Tourism Day as well as the inauguration of the revamped theatre, besides various other related events and activities in other parts of the city," said an official.

According to another senior official, "The entry to the theatre is more defined now, unlike before the renovation. A glass roof and glass walls have been constructed to define an extremely appealing entry to the theatre. There is a café with a seating capacity of over 800 persons. Even the stage is multi-functional now, which can be changed in size. The new light and sound system installed in the theatre would add on to the pleasure of viewing in the theatre."

Heading: Beauty to meet history at Bhima Devi museum in Yadvendra Gardens - Indian Express
Content:
The Nawashahar experiment, in which pregnant women were monitored to curb female foeticide, has remained a hot topic of discussion.

The experiment initially showed good results as the skewed sex ratio in the district was set in reversing order. But doubts were raised about its sustainability and intrusive modus operandi (which sociologist Dr Ravinder Kaur of IIT Delhi referred to as 'policing of pregnant women').

It was contended that the experiment was tantamount to the state employing anti-women tools. It smacks of serious civilization bankruptcy and shows utter lack of respect for women's privacy, said the critics. But these voices were branded as reflections of wooly-minded feminists and knee-jerk reactions of sociologists.

The Chandigarh Union Territory model, in contrast to that of China, is participatory, inter-sectoral, non-intrusive and accords privacy to the dignity of women. It builds on the inter-connectedness between education, empowerment and enforcement strategies. Most importantly, it is not individual or official centric; it primarily banks on creating social capital which negates the idea of the state having to act as a chowkidar outside every household.

It is in tune with the ideals of civil society, which are predicted on the public acting as stakeholders for the larger, common good. Its awareness campaigns, for instance, believe in engaging doctors, academia, priests and anganwadi workers with equal respect accorded to each one of them.

It is patient, yet focused, in its approach and sensitive to the fact that it is attempting to deal with the centuries-old patriarchal mindset. For example, the recent trend, as reported in a section of the media, that the general public in Chandigarh has been increasingly responding to appeals for financial help to save a girl child in need of critical healthcare comes as a major vindication for the ongoing awareness campaign against female foeticide.

For, the paramount objective of the UT model is to create an environment where the girl child is considered an asset rather than a liability.

There are many, however, who want instant results. Sadly, fighting female foeticide is different from playing T20 cricket matches. It does not follow corporate logic or the rules of time bound input-output analysis. The issue cannot be treated as a mere number game — the skewed sex ratio of this magnitude is essentially a civilisational crisis.

Hence, our endeavour to correct it must also befit our civilisation's ideals of democracy, consensus, building and partnership. Let us therefore collaborate with compassion but without calculator.

But at the same time, it is essential that the state enforce the Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PNDT Act) with firm resolve. But we must realise that this is not enough given the enormity of the problem and its sheer volume. The law may act as a deterrent but for sustainable change, we also need to acknowledge the conviction of the conscience.

The Chandigarh Union Territory model is exactly that — instead of grapping with numbers, it is dealing with minds.

Heading: Children traffic park in Panchkula a story of neglect - Indian Express
Content:
The scenic beauty of the Yadvendra Gardens at Pinjore is all set to get a touch of history with plans afoot to have a museum at the Bhima Devi temple.

"The Bhima Devi temple has as many as 100 sculptors of historical importance and as the entire temple was in the form of Panchaytan style. The special museum is also being constructed in the same format," said Madhav Acharya, Deputy Director, Haryana Archaeology and Museums department.

He added that construction work is on the verge of completion with the last finishing touches being given to the interiors.

To facilitate the visitors, the museum would be attached to the Yadvendra gardens in such a way that the tourists visiting the garden can also visit the Bhima Devi temple using the same entry ticket.

"We have moved the proposal and the final go ahead is expected anytime. As the work is on the verge of completion, the museum is expected to open for visitors in another two months time", added Acharya.

The residents of the district believe that it would further add to the variety already available at the Yadvendra gardens.

Talking to Newsline, Manohar Aggarwal, a resident of Pinjore said, "Till now it was all entertainment and enjoyment at the Yadvendra Gardens.

With the coming up of the museum, education and history will also be part of our visits."

Heading: Ruckus at DGP office: Woman threatens to kill self - Indian Express
Content:
A pending electricity bill of nearly Rs 35 thousand in the name of the Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA) has ensured that the Panchkula Children Traffic Park, Sector 12 remains without electricity. The officials in the traffic police department also claim that the HUDA has been requested several times but to no avail.

"It has been over a year that the pending electricity bills of the Children Traffic park have not been paid by the HUDA who are responsible for its maintenance. When children from various schools visit the park and ask us for demonstrating the various traffic rules, we draw a blank," said a traffic police official on condition of anonymity.

The official held the HUDA responsible for the poor maintenance of the park where several diversion signs have started fading.

"It is sad that not only is the traffic park without electricity, the park is not being maintained at all by the HUDA. Most of the diversion signs and indications shown to demonstrate various traffic rules have completely faded away. The tiles of the pavements in the park have also come out and are in need of immediate repair," added the official.

Meenu Gupta, a resident of Sector 12 and a regular visitor to the park said, "The very aim of the park gets defeated if the various traffic light points in the Children Traffic park are not working.

As I am a school teacher, I come with my students to the park so that they could learn about how traffic lights function and study the various diversions and safety rules. With the traffic lights being non-functional and diversion signs on the verge of fading away, it seems to be a futile exercise."

A senior HUDA official said on condition of anonymity that they are aware of the pending bills and would soon get the problem solved.

Heading: Don’t extend court timings, cut down on lunch break, stop tea breaks: Bar - Indian Express
Content:
Ruckus was created at the Director General of Police (DGP) office in Sector 6, Panchkula, on Monday, after a resident of Mustafabad village in Yamunanagar district, threatened to commit suicide when she was not allowed to meet DGP Ranjive Dalal.

The woman claimed that she was manhandled by the Yamunanagar police along with some shopkeepers, which resulted in her miscarriage in 2007.

"Shamshida came to the office and threatened to kill herself by putting herself on fire. An FIR was lodged with the Yamunanagar police in July 2008, where the woman had stated that she was beaten up by the Yamunanagar police and local shopkeepers in 2007. She suffered miscarriage when she was assaulted," said a police officer.

He added Shamshida had come to the DGP office a few days back.

"She had created a similar scene a few days back. We have inquired but there is no evidence of what she claims. But still the case has been handed over to AIG (Administration) Charu Bali.

Heading: A cut across borders: Indian doctor gifts life to Pak infant - Indian Express
Content:
Strongly protesting against the extension in court timings by the Full Court, various speakers addressing the General House today demanded that the tea break taken by the judges be stopped.

Expressing strong resentment against the decision taken by the Full Court without taking the High Court into confidence, the General House passed a resolution on Monday.

The resolution stated that the duration of lunch be reduced by five minutes and the practice of tea break be put to an end. In future, any decision concerning the administrative functioning of the High Court be taken in consultation with the High Court Bar by the Full Court, the resolution further read.

It was also resolved by the General House that the court working hours remain from 10 am to 4 pm, as laid down in the High Court rules.

The speakers also questioned the rationale behind implementing only one direction of the Malimath Committee report. The Full Court had stated that the extension in court timings was a result of the Malimath Committee report. Reading out various chapters of the report, which was out in November 2003, the advocates questioned as to why the directions pertaining to judges were not being implemented.

Addressing the General House, Rupinder S Khosla, president of the High Court Bar, shared his conversation with Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur and other Judges of the High Court regarding the issue.

"The Malimath Committee report dates back to 2003 and is not binding on the courts," Khosla said. He added that most of the judges do not hold the court till 3:45 pm.

Advocate J S Toor, speaking on the occasion, said the advocates do not want to impress that they do not want to work but any decision to be taken in this regard will have to be taken after taking the High Court Bar into confidence.

On the other hand, strongly resenting on the absence of senior advocates in the General House, Advocate A K Sinha said: "It is surprising that there is hardly any senior advocate of the Bar present to attend a meeting on such a sensitive issue."

Expressing deep concern over the Judge-bribery case which recently shook the High Court, the advocate questioned as to what actions were being taken by the Chief Justices to transfer judges who are prima facie found guilty of misconduct.

The speakers refused to accept the move calling it completely unacceptable and a forced decision.

"Let the judges take their tea or coffee inside the court rather than retiring in their chambers and consuming 15 to 30 minutes," said Advocate Naveen Chopra.

What does the Malimath Committee report read with regard to Courts and Judges?
The Chief Justice of the High Court may issue circulars:

A. That immediately below the cause title of the judgment order the following particulars will be entered
* Date of conclusion of arguments.

* Date of reserving the judgment.
* Date of pronouncement of the judgment.

At the bottom of the judgment, the following particulars will be entered:
* Date when the dictation was completed.
* Date when typing was completed and placed before the Judge
* The date when the judge signed.

B. The Court Officer shall enter in a separate register:
* The time when the Judge assembled.
* The time when the Judge rose.
* Copy of this record shall be sent to the Chief Justice on the same day and put up on the notice board.

Malimath Committee's report on Judiciary
The Committee is deeply concerned about the deterioration in the quality of judges appointed to the courts at all levels. The Constitution of a National Judicial Commission is being considered at the national level to deal with appointment of the judges to the High Courts and the Supreme Court and to deal with the complaints of misconduct against them. The mere entrustment of the power of appointment to the National Judicial Commission will not ensure appointment of competent and upright judges. We need a process to ensure objectivity and transparency in this behalf.

Cash at judge's door: Judgment on Bansal's bail application deferred
The Court of Special CBI Judge Jagdeep Jain today deferred the judgment over the regular bail application filed by former Haryana additional advocate general Sanjeev Bansal in the "Cash-at-judge's-door" case. The orders have been deferred till September 18 after the defence counsel sought time and requested the court not to pronounce the orders. The defence counsel sought time on the ground that they want to wait till September 16, the date on which the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is to file its reply against the anticipatory bail filed by co-accused Ravinder Singh. "We requested the court not to pronounce the orders and grant us time so that the final outcome of the anticipatory bail filed by Ravinder Singh can be seen," said Advocate N K Nanda, one of the defence counsels for Bansal.

Bansal and the other three accused in the case will be produced in the Court on September 13. The bail application of Sanjeev Bansal and arguments on bail application filed by Rajiv Gupta will come up for hearing on September 18.

Heading: 11% posts in UT lying vacant: study - Indian Express
Content:
An 11-month-old girl from Pakistan got a new lease of life after she was discharged on Monday following a successful cardiac surgery by doctors at the Fortis Hospital in Mohali.

Yusra was brought by Rotary's Chandigarh chapter to Mohali from Karachi, where her father, Fida Hussain, works in an airline company and her mother, Bushra Hussain, is a homemaker.

Yusra's parents found her turning pale and blue when she was barely 2-month-old. On consulting various doctors in Pakistan, they were told that Yusra had no chance of survival.

"It was on the internet that I researched for the best hospitals that could treat Yusra. I wanted a hospital that had skilled doctors and excellent infrastructure and facilities," said an emotional Hussain. He added, "I zeroed-in on the Fortis Hospital because of their JCI and NABH accreditation and Dr T S Mahant because his reputation as a cardiac surgeon has spread to Pakistan also. I specifically requested Rotary to bring us here and I am glad they did so."

Dr Mahant, executive director, Cardiac Surgery, Fortis Hospital, said, "When this child came to us, she had Tetrology of Fallots (TOF), a congenital heart defect, which had made her a blue baby. After thorough investigations, a heart surgery was conducted on her to rectify the problem and I am happy that she has shown remarkable progress and will be able to lead a normal life now."

The doctor added that heart problems in children should be rectified at the earliest. "The sooner the right diagnosis and treatment is given to the child, the higher is the success rate of survival," added Mahant.

President of the Rotary Club S K Duggal said, "Rotary has been very active since 1999 in helping to bring patients from various places to the best medical care available. We have already helped 30 patients from Pakistan and are glad that Yusra was able to get the best medical help at Fortis Hospital."

Heading: Supervisor falls to death at PCA Stadium - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 11 per cent of posts in the Chandigarh Administration are lying vacant, revealed a census of the Government Employees, 2007, released by the Administration today.

According to the statistics, against the total 22,674 sanctioned posts, the Administration has filled up 20,261 posts.

The Directorate of Economics and Statistics, (Statistical Cell), Chandigarh Administration, brings out the Census of the Government Employees Chandigarh Administration-2007 and 'Census of the Public Sector Undertaking and Local Bodies Employees of Chandigarh Administration' every year.

Special Secretary Finance-cum-Director Economic and Statistics Raji P Shrivastava released the report today. The publication is 19th in the series.

It also indicates the number of employees belonging to scheduled castes (SC), scheduled tribes (ST), other backward classes (OBC), ex-servicemen, handicapped persons, religion-wise, sex and on deputations from Punjab, Haryana and other states.

Total recruitment made on ad-hoc and on regular basis; number of employees retired on superannuation, voluntary, compulsory, died in service, terminated, resigned and backlog of posts reserved for SC, ST and OBC and posts abolished during the year 2006-2007 had also been shown.

Heading: With eyes on poll, ‘cash-rich’ Patiala MC starts new projects - Indian Express
Content:
A construction supervisor and a resident of Hanumangarh in Rajasthan died after falling from the top floor of the Punjab Cricket Association (PCA) International Stadium at Phase IX in Mohali on Monday.

The incident took place when Roop Singh, around 30 years, was supervising the ongoing construction and renovation work at air-conditioned lounge and commentator's box at level III of the stadium and put his foot on plywood instead of the concrete structure. He fell down to his death, said the PCA authorities, who attributed it as accidental.

Singh, who was engaged with a leading construction company which was awarded contract of the construction and renovation work at the stadium, was rushed to the nearest private hospital, where he was declared dead on arrival.

The Mohali police have initiated inquest proceedings under Section 174 of the CrPC before shifting the body to the Civil Hospital mortuary, where it will be kept till next of his family members arrive. "We have informed his family members and would proceed further according to their statement," said a police officer.

Heading: Mohali to get Rs 20,000 cr in next three yrs: Sukhbir - Indian Express
Content:
The cash-rich Patiala Municipal Corporation has decided to start numerous projects for the city, including development works worth Rs 5 crore.

These comprise re-carpeting and cleaning of roads, clearing of dumps and streetlights in various parts of the city.

Sources said the MC has already gone ahead with tenders worth Rs 4.5 crore that include repair work, streetlights and other important works in the entire city. "The House has passed the tenders and in the coming few months, things will definitely improve for the best," a source said.

Councillors in Patiala, meanwhile, claimed that they had numerous projects in their wards that were hanging fire due to shortage of funds. With ample funds now, things were looking positive. "We have visited our wards, repair works are on and it looks like the problem of providing clean drinking water and sewage facility will now be tackled," a councillor told Newsline.

Senior MC officials stated that a budget of Rs 5 crore was in the offing and before the parliamentary elections next year, the MC wants to prove that the SAD government is doing its bit. "While Rs 1 crore is in the shape of a grant, another Rs 4.5 crore has been given by the government to help finish pending works," they said.

Patiala Mayor Ajit Pal Singh Kohli said the government is determined to improve the basic civic facilities in the city, and shortage of funds would not be a hindrance anymore. "All councillors have been told to approach the office with their pending works and tenders have been floated for the same," he said.

Heading: Young Indian footballers are talented: Kuehn - Indian Express
Content: If Dipankar Sarkar had succeeded to chip the ball over the CFA goalkeeper into the goal, it would have been a different story for Indian Football Association, Kolkata. But it was not meant to be as they suffered a 2-0 loss at the hands of Chandigarh Football Association, who have won all their matches in the Administrators Cup.  Thirteen proved to be unlucky for IFA as Gagandeep Singh headed the ball into the net to give his team the lead in the 13th minute. The second goal was a stunner. K C Lal executed a perfect pass to Lalnunthlunga, thus splitting the IFA defence to pieces and Lalnunthlunga blasted a powerful shot from 20-yard into the goal. Meanwhile, favourites Mohun Bagan were tried to utmost level ST Stephen's Academy before going down to the Kolkata champions by 3-0. CFA will battle it out with Mohun Bagan in finals onTuesday.

Heading: MNSS, Rai declared as overall winners - Indian Express
Content:
With the city police not heeding their demand of dropping some clauses in the norms set up for issuing license for cyber cafés, the Pune Central Cyber Café Association, fearing action, has filed a writ petition with the Bombay High Court challenging the norms set up by the state government for issuing licenses for the business while seeking the unwanted clauses.

"A few of the clauses in the norms set up by the state government for seeking licences for cyber cafés are unnecessary and creating problems in running the business," Association President Rahul Pokale pointed out at a press conference. He said that the police have warned of action against the cyber cafés after the Ganesh festival for not possessing the licenses for it despite it being pointed out that some of the clauses are causing obstacles to obtaining of licences.

The clause of seeking a 'no objection certificate' from the Pune Municipal Corporation's (PMC) Health Department is unjustifiable as cyber cafés are not eating joints, Pokale said. He added that the clause requiring submission of building plans for cyber cafés does not hold significance as documents are not available with the civic administration for old buildings.

The provision of sufficient parking for visitors at cyber cafés — in accordance with the development control rules for commercial establishments — is not justifiable, he said. There are over 1,000 cyber cafés in the city and only one of them has been able to get a license from the police department.

The police check on cyber cafés comes after the increasing number of cyber crimes and alleged used of cyber cafés by anti-social elements.

Heading: Gitansh’s ton propels Ludhiana - Indian Express
Content:
If Chandigarh football is looking technically more sound and entertaining, then it's all due to the training of these young players at Agidus Brown Sports School, Leipzig, Germany. Andre Kuehn, director of the Sports School, is on his second visit to Chandigarh to attend the on-going Administrator's Cup and exchange programmes with the players and the coaches of Chandigarh Football Association.

"Sandhu said that he wanted to have a German coach so that the players could learn the German technique and, in turn, improve their football. So, my basic work was to appoint a coach and organise friendly matches at the stadium," says Andre who is all praise for the young Indian footballers. "They are very talented and know how to play football. I have seen group of 17 players and 11 out of them are very good to play for this age. The level of their game is improving," he adds.

Terming sports in Chandigarh as 'very organised' he showers heaps of praise on good football grounds and sports complexes but he warns that the referees should not be lenient while inspecting a match. "The referees need to learn more about football. If a player indulges in foul game then the referee should stop the match there and speak to the player and the coach. By doing so, the player stops committing fouls which improves the level of the game," says Andre.

Putting more stress on technique and coordination, the director says that the players also need to have a good physique to play the full 90 minute as football is a very tough game. "Indian players are physically much weaker than the German players. That makes a big difference. After a rigorous training for five days, we conduct friendly matches for them on the weekends in Germany. Although they lose by a large margin, the exposure they get and the lessons they learn from these games helps them a lot," shares Andre who is in India till September 19.

Giving example of Michael Ballack, the Germany national captain and a native of East Germany, he says that budding players in East Germany looks upto him as an inspiration and Ballack's success in other countries motivate them to play good football. "Young Indians also need a player to look up to," says Andre who will sit with players and coaches and make plans to exchange many more programmes to improve the standard of football in Chandigarh. "His arrival has motivated the players and I am sure the players will gain a lot from his rich experience. We are looking forward to send the third batch of players to Germany in the coming month," says Harjinder Singh, coach at Sector 42 Sports Complex.

Heading: Amit, Sandeep surge ahead - Indian Express
Content:
MNSS School Rai were declared the overall winners in both the categories of the 25th All India IPSC Aquatic Meet being hosted by Yadavindra Public School, Patiala, NSNIS. As many as nineteen teams from public schools across the country participated in this event.

Anjali Nair from Modern School was adjudged best swimmer in the girls' u-14 section while in the boys u-14 category Karan Raj Sohi from RIMC, Dehradun was declared the best.

In the girls u-17 Bharti Dagar from MNSS was the topper while Prashant Tokas from DPS, RK Puram was the winner in the boy's section. In the u-19 section Shloka Joshi from Modern School claimed top honours girl's category while Abhishek Chugh from DPS, RK Puram was the best in the boy's section.

Heading: Candidates scanned, strategies dissected and promises analysed - PU gets ready for September 12 - Indian Express
Content:
The in-form Amit Verma ousted Vinay 3-0 (54-27, 61-17, 38-30) to move ahead in the senior snooker section, during the 23rd Chandigarh Billiards and Snooker Championship being held in Chandigarh.

In an easy outing, Sandeep Duggal defeated Deepak Miglani 3-1(18-67, 60-28, 44-25, 77-25) to sail into the next round. In senior billiards, Rahul Garg shocked Satnam 2-0 (100-74, 100-89) to earn the win. Pramod kumar outplayed Aman Khulla 2-0 (100-60,100-61), while top seed Arif of IOC also won his encounter.

Heading: Dharna over, but work yet to start - Indian Express
Content:
The different contesting parties at the Panjab University students' elections finalised their presidential candidates on Monday. With all the parties having new faces, the fight has become all the more intriguing.

SOPU-NSUI Presidential
candidate:Sahil Nanda
Background: Fourth year student at the University Institute of Engineering and Technology. Contesting for the first time.
Promises and Issues: Health insurance for students and better infrastructure and hostels. Sahil states that being from UIET, his main focus would be on uplifting his department. For the UIET department, he promises better hostel facilities, canteens and infrastructure. The development of a students' centre in the varsity, reducing the cost of food and reviving cultural programmes like Goonj features in his list of promises.
Strategy: Believe in yourself and never promise what you cannot fulfil. "I believe that in case one promises or commits something, then he or she should fight till the end to achieve the same. Fighting till the end leads to victory and I am sure of the same for me and my party," adds Sahil.

INSO-SOI Presidential
Candidate: Sukhdev Kundu
Background: Senior research scholar with the UGC at the Environment Science Department and is contesting for the first time.

Promises and Issues:Topping the list of issues is the central varsity status issue for the PU with all the existing quotas for the university students.
Implementation of Group Insurance Policy for PU students from this year and a separate hostel facility for research scholars are part of his promises. The right to vote in PUCSC elections for students including 'Department of Evening Studies' students and issues of parking and canteen are his priorities.

Strategy: To reach out to the majority and motivate them to vote. Also, to take note of the issue of prospective voters and work on them once the elections are won.

Background: Fourth year student at UIET. Contesting for the first time.

Promises and
Issues:Topping the list is the central varsity status he assures in getting the said status for the varsity once he wins the elections. The other promises include checking the increasing fees and providing better hostel facilities for students. For his own department, the candidate intends to have better canteen, hostels and roads.
Strategy: Randhawa believes in teamwork and says that the party is bound to be successful as it was in past.

ABVP Presidential
Candidate: Prashant Thakur
Background: Final year student at the Department of Laws and is contesting for the first time.
Issues and Promises: The central varsity status for PU spearheads their promises. The party aims to include an employment cell at every department to help students get jobs. Also, the party believes in maintaining peace in the campus and doing away with the unwanted elements in the varsity.

Heading: In Buddha’s M-deal, Tatas find very few safeguards - Indian Express
Content:
Despite Sunday's truce, work at Tata's Nano project in Singur remained suspended. The Tata Motors authorities restricted access to the site for vendor companies, construction company officials and staff.

"We have got no signal yet. Until we do, we prefer to wait and watch. It may take days, but until further orders are given work in the plant will not resume," said an officer at the Tata Plant.

The project area wore a barren look, with only a few policemen and a handful of labourers loitering around.

Unfazed by Tata Motors decision not to resume work, Local TMC legislator Rabindranath Bhattacharjee, meanwhile, said he has already drawn up a plan to identify land from inside the project area to be returned to farmers. Bhattacharjee was made the chairman of the committee formed yesterday to identify the land to be returned.

"It is Tata's decision not to start work. We had an agreement with the government and I will start work of identification of land," said Bhattacharjee.

According to him, around 250 acres are available inside the plant. "All I need is to identify it physically. There is land available in areas including Tal Bhomra, Singher Bheri, Khaser Bheri, Gopalnagar and other areas," he added.

The committee is expected to start working from tomorrow.

With the dharna over, Singur, meanwhile, breathed a sigh of relief. The 21 makeshift stages were dismantled this morning and the Durgapur Expressway returned to normalcy.

The villagers — those who voluntarily gave up their land and those who did not — were happy with the outcome of the talks.

"We fought for the past two-and-a-half years and have now forced the government to heed to our demands. I have lost my daughter in this fight, but still I am happy," said Monoranjan Malik, father of Tapasi Malik.

Told that the Tata Motors is yet to decide on resuming work, he said: "Why should the Tatas go? They should be satisfied with the land we give them and stay here."

The sentiment was his alone. In the various villages of Singur, be it Beraberi, Khaserbheri, Bajemelia or Joymollah, people unanimously wanted Tatas to start work again.

"We were never against the Tatas. We want everything to be normal here and the Tatas to start working. We are happy that the ordeal is over. We will get land back and more money," said Purnima Koley, a resident of Koleypara. Purnima's land was acquired by the state government but she did not take the compensation cheque.

"We don't support her (Mamata) but now as everything has fallen in place, we want the plant to start. The nonsense called agitation has ultimately ended," said Sandip Dey, whose family has voluntarily given up 2 acres for the project.

Sandip is one of the youths working as an apprentice in the engine shop of Tata Motors. "I have got a job with the Tatas and now I want them to stay here and start production. I do not want them to move out of Singur," he added.

Heading: Woman attempts suicide on reality show sets - Indian Express
Content:
SINGUR: Can't take call till clarity on deal (with Mamata), say Tatas; won't disturb project map: govt

If it was tough to bring Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee and Mamata Banerjee to the same table, it's now clear that what lies ahead is tougher: implementing an agreement that gives Mamata her face-saver and convinces Tata Motors that its economic interests have not been sabotaged for politics. It's not going to be easy.

At the heart of this dilemma lies the controversial — and vague — land-for-land deal agreed upon which prompted Tata Motors to put on record its disapproval: "Tata Motors Ltd. is distressed at the limited clarity on the outcome of the discussions between the state government of West Bengal and the representatives of the agitators in Singur...Tata Motors is obliged to continue the suspension of construction and commissioning work at the Nano Plant. We will review our stated position only if we are satisfied that the viability of the project is not being impinged, the integral nature of the mother plant and our ancillary units are being maintained and all stakeholders are committed to develop a long term congenial environment for smooth operations of the plant in Singur."

No wonder then that hours after this, State Industries Minister Nirupam Sen told Tata Motors managing director Ravi Kant that the government would keep its promise on not disturbing the mother plant. "Mamata Banerjee's statements have created some confusion. On the issue of relocating the vendor park (where the ancillaries are), neither the Chief Minister nor the government gave consent. We will evaluate how much land can be given away without disturbing the project cluster," he said. "The state government is trying sincerely to hold them back."

Of the farmers who have rejected compensation are many whose land falls in the 645-acre premises of the mother plant and in the 290-acre vendor park. Officials said there was a "disconnect" between the government and Tata Motors with some saying the company was not consulted on the "fine print of the agreement."

Many officials admit the land-for-land deal is a messy one and the government will work hard to push the pension scheme as a substitute.

The Tatas also resented the fact that "people with limited knowledge are taking a call on the project." This was a reference to the four-member committee formed yesterday.

It includes local Trinamool MLA Rabindranath Bhattacharya, and Becharam Manna, a Singur Panchayat member who's responsible for protests at the site. And Subrata Gupta of West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation and Neelam Meena, Hooghly DM. They meet tomorrow noon.

Heading: Deal with the Tatas made public at last - Indian Express
Content:
Raising questions over the craze surrounding reality shows again, Tania Saha (21) reportedly attempted suicide on Monday afternoon at the Nehru Children's Museum on the sets of a reality show.

The television channel authorities have denied that the girl was a participant in the programme Fatafati — the same reality show which hit the headlines after the death of Prasun Adhikary. But sources said the girl, after failing in the programme's audition around 3.20 pm, took everyone by surprise at the spot, consuming poison from a bottle she carried with her.

As she lost consciousness, the organisers rushed her to a local nursing home, where she is still admitted and still unconscious.

Soon after, a team from the Hastings Police Station went to the Nehru Children's Museum and later to the nursing home. They are now waiting for Tania's version of the story before deciding on a course of action. No FIR has so far been lodged yet.

The episode brings back chilling memories of the August 9 incident, when Prasun Adhikary, a 23-year-old caretaker of a hotel in Medinipur fell to his death from the fifth floor of the hotel building after an alleged wrangle with the organisers of the show.

Heading: Bronze boys enthral Kolkata school - Indian Express
Content:
The state government finally made a certain portion of the deal signed with the Tata Motors public on Monday. Parts of the deal have been posted on the official website of the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC), which was signed on March 7, 2007. contents of the deal

Incentive package by other states: The incentive package given to Tata Motors by Uttarakhand/Himachal Pradesh consists of 100 per cent exemption from Excise Duty for 10 years. And 100 per cent exemption from Corporate Income Tax for first 5 years with 30 per cent exemption from Corporate Income Tax for next five years.

Demand of Tata Motors: The Tata Motors showed interest in locating the plant in West Bengal, provided the West Bengal government gave Fiscal incentive equivalent to the value of total incentives it would have received by locating the plant in Uttarakhand/Himachal Pradesh. The "Government of West Bengal offered to match the financial incentives in equivalent terms and invited TML to set up the Small Car plant in West Bengal".

Land acquired: The WBIDC was in possession of 997.11 acres of land, which had been acquired under the Land Acquisition Act. Of this, an area admeasuring 645.67 acres will be leased to Tata Motors for setting up the Automobile Project including the small car plant, while an area admeasuring 290 acres will be leased to the vendors of this Automobile Project approved by Tata Motors — ancillary and component manufacturing units.

Lease Amount: The land will be given on a 90 year lease with an annual lease rental of Rs 1 crore per year for first 5 years with an increase at the rate of 25 per cent after every 5 years till 30 years.

Loan by the government: The state government has also provided a loan of 200 crores to Tata Motors at the rate of 1 per cent interest per year repayable in 5 equal annual installments starting from the 21st year from the date of disbursement of loan. The loan will be disbursed within 60 days of signing the agreement.

Electricity: The government also promised to provide electricity for the project at Rs 3 per KWH.

Heading: Mamata confident govt will stick to deal - Indian Express
Content:
Olympic medalists Vijender Kumar and Sushil Kumar spend the afternoon at Purushottam Bhagchandka Academic School

It's been almost three weeks since Vijender Kumar, Sushil Kumar and Abhinav Bindra turned into national heroes following India's unprecedented medal rush at the Beijing Olympic.

And just when you thought the euphoria may finally be dying down in this part of the country, where cricket and football are perennial fodder for sports lovers, India's new posterboys Vijender and Sushil dropped in to a city school, and made fans and the media go crazy.

In a welcome break from the gruelling Singur deadlock, Beijing Olympic Bronze medalists Vijender and Sushil flew down the city this morning, and spent their entire afternoon at a little-known Purushottam Bhagchandka Academic School in Kolkata.

Their visit to the city finished with the state sports department felicitating the duo for their remarkable achievement at the Beijing Olympic.

After spending a while at the school campus ground with hundreds of children surrounding them, it was when Vijender and Sushil went about a stroll down the classes that the media ran amok.

The two guests were scheduled to visit a few classes and sit through them. But the entire exercise turned into a mess as shutterbugs and television crew jostled with one another for space, eventually cutting short the programme.

"It's a very nice feeling to be here among so many children. We have been through so many programmes. But this one is special," said an excited Sushil Kumar.

"I am thrilled to see so many children, fans and mediapersons turning up here just for us. It's a special occasion for us and we will not forget it soon," Vijender said just as he and Sushil were whisked away by the organisers to avoid media rush.

The day-long trip for the Bhiwani boxer and Najafgarh wrestler was organised by a share and securities management company. Although the duo maintained that they had a field day at the school, the media rush on their visit left a bad taste in the mouth.

Heading: Ancilliary units in the dark, work still suspended - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee refused to react to Tata Motors' statement regarding its Singur plant on Monday. She said her party was confident that the state government will abide by the agreement reached.

The Tata Motors' statement that it will not resume work at the Nano plant as long as there wasn't any clarity on the outcome of last night's talks did not concern the party. "What Tatas have said is not related to us. The agreement was signed between the leader of the Opposition Partha Chatterjee and Industry Minister Nirupam Sen in the presence of the constitutional head (Governor)," she told reporters. "I want the Tatas to stay here," Banerjee said in reply to another question.

"Why would the government deviate from the agreement? Do not mislead the people. It is a people's issue," she told reporters in reply to a question.

Banerjee, who announced suspension of the two-week-long dharna on Sunday, said the Government has agreed to give as much land as possible within the project area and the rest in an adjacent area as early as possible.

Meanwhile, in New Delhi, the Congress party welcomed the resolution. "We hope the state Government shall not undertake any such measure like Singur in any part of Bengal without a comprehensive package and with the due consent of all parties and without undermining the farmers' interests," state Congress chief P R Dasmunshi said here.

"Had the state government been serious enough to understand the interests of farmers, things would have been taken in a better direction long back. However, better late than never," he said.

Heading: Judge maintains his humble composure - Indian Express
Content:
As efforts continued for rehabilitation of unwilling farmers, the fate of the ancillary units, which are to come up on the vendor park adjacent to the mother plant, is still in the dark.

None of the companies have received any official word — either from WBIDC or from Tata motors — regarding the return of land or suspension of work.

"The agreement between the government and the Save Farmland Committee is shrouded in obscurity," said Udayan Banerjee, Executive Director of Sharda Motor Industries Ltd, which owns 7 acres land in the vendor park.

"We are not clear if land will be taken out of the vendor park or not. There is no official word from WBIDC, from whom we had purchased the land," Banerjee added.

No work has taken place in the ancillary units for the past 15 days, and work has been suspended for another week. "The environment is still not conducive for work at the site," he said.

Sharda Motor has already completed 97 per cent of construction and imported machinery to the site. Certain welding imported machinery has been lying in the Kolkata port for the past 10 days due to the agitation in Singur.

"We have to pay the Kolkata Port for each day that is wasted," said Banerjee.

Similar is the case of the Endurance Group, which has purchased 8.01 acres for itsancillary units. "Ancillary units cannot be moved. If vendors move even across the road, transportation costs will go up a little. The whole idea is based on a very cost-effective model," said Biswajit Choudhury, Vice-President (Marketing), Endurance Group. No official word has been received on the whole situation as yet.

"The Tatas have to review their decision. We all want the problem to be solved permanently, even if it requires waiting for a while," said G S Valia, Director, Operations, Anand Motors Pvt Ltd.

"While West Bengal debates the Nano issue, extensive testing of the lakhtakia car is underway on the Aurangabad-Pune road.Nano cars are already undergoing extensive testing there," said Choudhury.

Heading: Smaller groups not happy - Indian Express
Content:
"Though an agreement has been signed between the state government and the Trinamool Congress, it will take some time before the entire process of alternate land return is worked out," said former chief justice of the Bombay High Court Chittotosh Mukherjee, who has now become a household name in Kolkata.

The octogenarian judgewho helped the Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi mediate between Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee and Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee is still his humble self.

After taking charge as the legal advisor, Mukherjee had made it clear that a solution to the impasse was only possible if both parties were willing to find a middle path.

"Now the four-member committee will earmark the land to be returned to the unwilling farmers. The entire process will take time," he said.

Mukherjee was born on January 1, 1929. Entering the legal profession was a natural choice for the young man who had completed his Masters from Calcutta University in 1951.

His grandfather, Sir Asutosh Mukherjee, was the chief justice of the Calcutta High Court.

His father, Rama Prasad Mukherjee, had also been an acting Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court.

He obtained a First Class in the Preliminary, Intermediate and Final Law Examinations of the Calcutta University and stood first in the Intermediate and Final Examinations.

Soon after, Mukherjee enrolled as an advocate in the Calcutta High Court on November 24,1953.

He was appointed as an additional judge of the Calcutta High Court on April 2, 1969 and became a permanent judge from November 25, 1970, at the age of 40.

On November 1, 1986, he was promoted as the chief justice of the Calcutta High Court and was transferred as Chief Justice of Bombay a year later.

He retired on January 1, 1991.

Heading: Malaysia envoy keen to promote tourism, trade - Indian Express
Content:
The smaller groups that formed a chunk of the 21 member Singur Krishi Jami Rakha Committee (SKJRC) headed by Mamata Banerjee are not fully satisfied with the agreement that was signed between the government and the Krishi Jomi Raksha Committee on Sunday.

Many said that the problem is far from over and these small outfits with committed members might again get together to start another round of agitation.

Many independent associations had joined hands with Banerjee on the Singur issue. Almost all of them had set up camps in Singur during the 15-day dharna and were sharing the 21 manchas that were set up. After Banerjee reached an agreement on Singur with the state governments, some outfits — specially those with an Naxalite mindset — have said that problem is far from over.

"The Singur movement began mostly for the landless and non-registered farmers. But in the truce with the state government there has been no mention about these people," said Manik Mondal, leader of Group for Rural Alternative Movement, an NGO.

Heading: Czech scientists found guilty - Indian Express
Content:
With Malaysia becoming a preferred destination not just for tourists and corporates from West Bengal, but also for couples looking forward to tying the knot in the scenic locales, both the state government and the diplomatic community of Malaysia in India are keen that the state gets a direct flight from Malaysia.

"The West Bengal Government has urged me to take up the issue of starting a direct flight to Kolkata. We will urge the Malaysian Airlines to begin operations as soon as possible," said Dato Tan Seng Sung, the High Commissioner of Malaysia, at an interactive session with Indian Chamber of Commerce in Kolkata on Monday.

Earlier in the day, Sung met state Minister of Tourism, Manabendra Mukherjee and discussed the issue. He also sought from the tourism department the statistics of tourists visiting Malaysia from West Bengal. The delegates accompanying Sung assured that a small aircraft could possibly be worked out with the Malaysian Airlines, if not a dedicated flight.

About two years ago, the Malaysian Airlines had started a flight on the route, but the services were soon discontinued because of the dearth of passengers.

Expressing satisfaction over business and trade between India and Malaysia, Sung said India's Free Trade Agreement (FTA) with ASEAN Countries, including Malaysia, facilitates positive trade opportunities between both the countries.

He added that for bilateral trade facilitation, another treaty — Comprehensive Economic Cooperative Agreements (CECA) — is being worked out between both the countries. "The third round of talks on the agreement will be held in the second week of October," Sung said . Emphasising that Malaysia is next only to China and India in outsourcing business , Sung welcomed Indian BPO companies to set up their regional headquarters for the south Asian market in Malaysia.

The members of the delegation pointed out that the presence of Malaysian companies in India is mostly in the domain of construction of bridges and highways.

At present, the Malaysian investment in India is $250 million, said Sung, before his scheduled meeting with Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee on September 9.

Heading: Basu stable, say doctors - Indian Express
Content:
The two Czech entomologists arrested in Darjeeling recently with samples of insects, have been found guilty of violation of the Wildlife Protection Act and the Bio-diversity Act.

The Chief Judicial Magistrate of Darjeeling, U K Nandy delivered the judgment on Monday evening. Petr Svacha and Emil Kuchera were present in the court. The sentence will be pronounced on Wednesday. The act has a provision of imprisonment for up to seven years.

The judge has granted them interim bail, said their counsel Taurang Pandit. The scientists will consider the possibility of appeal only after getting a copy of the judgment, he said.

Svacha and Kuchera were arrested on June 22 from a hotel at Srikhola in the Darjeeling district. Around 200 species of beetles, butterflies, moths and other rare insects, collected from the Singalila National Park, were seized from their possession.

The Forest Department had filed a chargesheet against them on August 11 for violating various sections of the Wild Life Protection Act and Bio-diversity Act. The trial had started before the CJM court on August 25. The scientists, who were in Darjeeling jail, had been granted bail on July 25.

Heading: BESU students’ council polls expected in October - Indian Express
Content:
A day after CPM leaderJyoti Basu was admitted to the AMRI Hospital in Kolkata, doctors confirmed that his condition had continued to be stable on Monday.

"He had his breakfast and lunch today," said a doctor of the 10-member medical board supervising Basu's health. The board is led by Dr R N Bhattacharya, with Dr M K Chettri as the chief adviser.

The team also informed that reports of all clinical parameters were within the normal range. The medical board will meet again tomorrow to discuss Basu's condition.

A host of luminaries visited Basu in the hospital on Monday morning, including Urban Development Minister Asok Bhattcharya, State Transport Minister Subhas Chakraborty, his wife Ramala Chakraborty and Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi. "I spoke to him and doctors have informed me that his condition is stable," Gandhi said.

Heading: Red bandwagon out on an enlightening trip - Indian Express
Content:
After a gap of three years, the student elections of the Bengal Engineering and Science University (BESU) are expected to be held in October. The last elections were held in 2005, after which the university decided to suspend the elections owing to campus unrest.

BESU authorities have now formed a three-member committee for the implementation of the Lyngdoh Committee recommendations in the elections.

"The Committee submitted its report today. It has ascertained the practicality of the recommendations of Lyngdoh Committee that can be applied to our university," said Biman Bandopadhyay, registrar of the university.

The students of the university are keen on having elections as quickly as possible. The university is also employing extra security personnel on campus prior to the elections.

About 30 security personnel from a security agency will be deployed to beef up the security on campus.

Heading: 5-year-old girl raped, accused arrested - Indian Express
Content:
The Red Ribbon Express comprises a train of seven coaches. A caravan of bus and cycle will travel along with it

As part of its awareness campaign on HIV/AIDS, National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) along with the state government is implementing Red Ribbon Express Project in Gujarat.

Speaking to media about the project, Gujarat Minister of Health and Family Welfare Jainarayan Vyas said that while HIV/AIDS is fast becoming one of the biggest threats to people, awareness and prevention is the only way to deal with the menace. "The Red Ribbon Express will run across the state to create awareness about the syndrome and the modes of prevention," Vyas said, adding that prevention is the only way to deal with it. "Gujarat is a moderate state so far as HIV/AIDS is concerned. But, we need to spread awareness among people about the disease," he said.

"So far, we had been handling AIDS control programmes in the state through cluster based approach. But now, we are finding that the syndrome is spreading and is no more restricted to industrial clusters alone. It has spread across the region," said Gujarat Commissioner Health Dr Amarjit Singh. "Under such a situation, awareness about the disease becomes an absolute necessity," he said.

The Red Ribbon Express comprises a train of seven coaches. A caravan of bus and cycle will travel along with the train. It will enter Gujarat on September 11 from Maharashtra and travel across the state via Valsad, Surat, Vadodara, Anand, Nadiad, Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Viramgam, Dhrangadhra, Bhuj, Bhavnagar, Rajkot, Okha, Porbandar and Mehsana. It will move to Rajasthan on October 15.

The train will have three dedicated coaches for exhibition, an auditorium for interaction with select target groups, and for counselling and medical services. The bus and cycle caravans will move in villages to generate awareness.

Heading: Consumer disputes panel upholds forum’s decision against builders - Indian Express
Content:
In a shocking incident, three people allegedly raped a five-year old girl at Adarsh Nagar in Tarsali around 9 pm on Sunday.

The Makarpura police said the three accused, Mohd Sajim Pathan, Zuber Abdul Sheikh and Mohammad Naseem Kamaruddin are workers at the Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC).

According to the complaint filed by the girl's mother, it was Pathan who raped the girl, while the other two lured her to their house.

The police said the accused and the victim reside in the same neighbourhood. The police arrested the accused on Monday night.

Inspector H D Lashkari said the victim is now in the SSG Hospital.

"We will conduct medical tests on the girl," said Lashkari.

Heading: Nabbed Bangladeshis may provide lead to fake currency kingpin, hopes SOG - Indian Express
Content:
They were denying possession to a client despite full payment

Upholding a ruling of Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Ahmedabad, the Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has ordered builder Milan Barot of Mili Developers and chairman of Nirmit Bungalows S K Patel to hand over possession of a bungalow to one Mukesh Bhatt.

Bhatt had booked the bungalow, but the builder had denied him possession.

The Commission dismissed the appeal filed against the Forum's verdict in the case filed by Consumer Education and Research Society (CERS) and Bhatt. The Forum had ordered the respondents to hand over possession of the bungalow and the Building Use (BU) permission to Bhatt within three months from the date of the order. Failing this, the respondents were ordered to pay monthly damages of Rs 7,384 with nine per cent compound interest from the date of complaint till handing over possession. The Forum also ordered them to pay Bhatt Rs 10,000 for mental harassment and Rs 2,000 towards costs.

Bhatt had booked a bungalow at Satyasai Co-operative Housing Society and signed a contract with the builder. As per the contract, the builder had to hand over possession of the bungalow with all facilities mutually agreed, to Bhatt against a payment of Rs 8 lakh.

However, he ended up paying Rs 8.70 lakh and an additional Rs 50,090 to the builder. Bhatt spent Rs 2 lakh more on furniture and fixtures. But the builder demanded a total of Rs 9,52,750 from him. Since Bhatt did not get possession of the bungalow, he had to rent a house. Bhatt approached CERS and jointly filed a complaint with the Forum.

The builder submitted that as per Bhatt's instructions, he had done additional construction of Rs 2,69,550 on the premises, raising the cost to Rs 12,77,300, including Rs 20,000 maintenance deposit, Rs 43,000 legal and other charges. The builder said that Bhatt had paid Rs 8.25 lakh only and had still not paid Rs 6,07,300.

The builder contended that Bhatt had filed the "false" complaint just to avoid balance payment. He added that the BU permission had not been obtained as Bhatt had to obtain it by presenting documents on the additional construction. He had been lethargic in presenting the documents, leading to the delay.

The builder added that he would have to pay for the permission. The Commission comprised presiding member M G Gulabani and member Jatin P Vaid. H P Motiramani appeared for Bhatt and CERS, and S J Mehta for the appellants.

Heading: Tribals protest against development authority - Indian Express
Content:
The special operations Group (SOG) sleuths, interrogating three Bangladeshis arrested on Saturday, suspect involvement of a much bigger gang in circulating counterfeit currency in the market.

The trio — Mohammed Nazrul Sheikh (22), Abdul Majid Sheikh (32), and Mohammed Ikram Ali Sheikh — have been taken on a 10-day judicial remand for further questioning.

They were arrested at the Vadodara railway station with Rs 60,000 fake currency notes.

The SOG has sought the help of the Malda Police Superintendent in West Bengal in this regard.

Meanwhile, the SOG officials recovered 11 counterfeit notes from various shops in the walled city area from where the accused had purchased small items.

"These shopkeepers alerted us about the counterfeit currency. They are going to help us in the case by becoming the witness," said Inspector Karim Polra of the SOG.

"They are from a village near the Indo-Bangladesh border in Malda, where they were handed out the counterfeit notes and asked to circulate them across the country," he said.

The trio, in fact, are simple farmers who were lured by money to circulate the fake currency notes in Gujarat.

During interrogation, the SOG official added, it was found that small groups of people are spread across the country to carry out similar operations.

SOG hopes to get help from the West Bengal Police to track down the kingpin of this gang and solve the case.

Heading: Yankee doodle doo: American Corner bugles a new day for state on anniversary - Indian Express
Content:
KADA to devour over 1,000 hectares tribal land, says Satyagrahi Samiti

Protesting against the state government's decision to set up Kevadia Area Development Authority (KADA) on tribal land, people of 16 villages of Narmada district have decided to approach the Gujarati elite seeking their help.

On Sunday, members of Kevadia Colony-based Satyagrahi Samiti distributed a survey report written by Bangalore-based researchers Suparna Lahiri and Aditi Chanchani. The 48-page report is a study of the 16 villages that may have to give up 1,000 hectares of land in the name of tourism.

"KADA is trying to develop tourism in the agricultural land of tribal farmers. They intend to develop a water park, hotels, a golf course, gardens, camping, environment parks on the farmers' land," said Hari Tadvi spearheading the Satyagrahi Samiti formed to oppose KADA.

Speaking further he said: "KADA was formed in April this year. This incorrect step taken by the state government is being opposed by the samiti comprising 7,000 people from 16 villages".

Apart from this, Kevadia has a Scheduled Tribe status. No one can claim authority over tribal land, he said.

The report presented by the two researchers of Bangalore-based company, Equation, presents a gist of how the state government is doing injustice to the tribals settled on the banks of Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited (SSNNL).

It also speaks about how the people of 16 villages will get disturbed through the ambitious plans of KADA, Tadvi said.

This is the second protest against KADA, the first having been started by Medha Patkar in June.

The SSNNL authorities however, refused to comment on the issue.

Heading: Data centre to e-nable governance in Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
The American Corner at the Ahmedabad Management Association celebrated its fourth anniversary on Monday. The US Consulate General, Paul Folmsbee, was present on the occasion and related the success story of the American Corner in Gujarat and the US-Gujarat relations.

"Ahmedabad is a developing city. It has dynamism and cutting edge businesses. Gujarat is a wonderful state and is recommended by many for its progressive policies," said Folmsbee.

The sizeable Gujarati population in America has forged a bond between USA and Gujarat, said Folmsbee. "The synthesis of our two cultures has been wonderful. Indians are very warm and loving people," he said.
