A four-day programme is already underway as part of the celebration. Seminars on social entrepreneurship, higher education and talks on US elections have already been held.

An interactive session on US Visa application procedures will be held on Tuesday with the students.

A quiz competition titled 'Know USA' was also organised among the students. Aman Shah and Arjun Kapoor of Saint Xavier's College emerged champions. They said such quizzes must be encouraged for students to gain knowledge about a country and its culture.

Folmsbee said that Gujarat has always been a progressive state. The industries in Gujarat are doing a commendable job. The US companies are doing business in the state, as there are many lucrative options available. There are many small companies in Gujarat and US, which can be developed with a joint initiative, he said.

Many people from the state migrate to USA for higher studies and jobs.

They add to the American culture, said Folmsbee.

In the last four years, the American Corner has welcomed a steady inflow of hundreds of students, academics, researchers and professionals on a daily basis. The place serves as an information centre for many people in Ahmedabad who want to have an in-depth knowledge of the American culture. It has about 1,000 books, 46 periodicals and 200 DVDs and videos in its collection. It also screens videos and films, programmes by experts in USA and orientation sessions for students.

In India, American Corners exist in Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Goa.

Folmsbee plans to expand the reach of the centre all over Gujarat. He believes that India has a lot to offer to the world since it is the world's biggest democracy. He said future cooperation with India is essential on many fronts . Although India lacks good infrastructure, yet the opportunities here are plentiful, he said.

"I am going to visit many more companies in Gujarat. And I will meet Narendra Modi, too," Folmsbee added.

Heading: Gujarat’s mangroves get a gift from Geneva - Indian Express
Content:
The state government is coming up with a State Data Centre (SDC), which will be the core infrastructure component for supporting the e-governance initiatives of the National e-Governance Plan of the Government of India.

Neeta Shah, Director (e-Governance) of Gujarat Informatics Ltd. (GIL) told Newsline: "The tender process for purchasing the hardware components required for SDC is in progress. Once we acquire the hardware, the software implementation and streamlining will not take much time. We hope to make the SDC operational soon."

Once functional, the SDC will be a major breakthrough in taking governance in Gujarat to the next level. It will provide a centralised structure with hosting facilities to provide efficient electronic delivery of Government to Government (G2G), Government to Citizen (G2G) and Government to Business (G2B) services. The Gujarat State Wide Area Network (GSWAN) and Citizen Service Centre (CSC) will provide connectivity to ensure a seamless common delivery platform.

As per the Department of Information Technology guidelines , some of the key functionalities provided by the SDC will be: Central Repository of the State, Secure Data Storage, Online Delivery of Services, Citizen Information Services Portal, State Intranet Portal, Disaster Recovery, Remote Management and Service Integration.

Shah added: "The SDC will increase data security, streamline operational maintenance and reduce the cost incurred for e-Governance initiatives. It will be a single-window approach to all e-Governance measures for which the Centre will provide an assistance of Rs 55 crore over a five-year period. The state government will contribute the rest."

As to how GIL plans to transfer the existing e-applications and e-services to SDC once it is operational, she said: "The servers dealing with such applications will be shifted to the common server room of the SDC for integration into a common platform. We will make sure that the transition is smooth."

Neeta also explained the role played by consultancy firm Pricewaterhouse Coopers (PwC) in assisting the state government to set up the SDC. "PwC is helping GIL prepare the Detailed Project Report as well as the Request for Proposal. They will also assist us in implementing the project in the state," she said.

Heading: Nagori, other SIMI accused produced before metropolitan court - Indian Express
Content:
The Geneva-based International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN) has cleared the state government's proposal to seek financial assistance and carry out a research on biodiversity of mangroves along coastal south Gujarat.

C N Pandey, Director, Gujarat Ecological Education and Research Foundation (GEER), told Newsline on Monday that the funds sanctioned by IUCN under the "Mangroves for the Future" programme will be utilised on research.

The state Forest Department has taken up a large-scale mangrove plantation drive along the south Gujarat coast. The project cost is estimated at over Rs 10 lakh.

Pandey said that despite rapid industrialisation and urbanisation, the mangrove area along the state's coast has increased to 960 sq km. He said this is the second largest area under mangrove cover after West Bengal.

"The GEER officials have also launched a concerted effort to increase the mangrove area along the Kutch and the Saurashtra coast. Comprehensive research work on its biodiversity is already being carried out there," he added.

The officials said that though they have put in a lot of efforts to increase the area under mangrove cover along the Gujarat coast, the state still needs training and capacity building to protect and manage the coastal biodiversity.

"The foundation has also involved private stakeholders, including local industries and NGOs, for the conservation and management of mangroves," they said.

IUCN has selected four coastal states – West Bengal, Orissa, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat – for the restoration, conservation and management of mangroves.

The programme was first announced in 2006, and initially covered the six countries affected by the December 26, 2004 Tsunami.

An official said the state government can approach the IUCN again and seek more assistance for its mangrove conservation project.

During his visit to Gandhinagar early this year, Don Macintosh, who is attached to the IUCN Asia Regional Office at Bangkok, had expressed concern over the present status of mangroves and coastal environment in states like Gujarat.

He had said that rapid industrialisation and urbanisation along the shoreline was badly affecting the coastal environment.

Macintosh had then assured the state government that IUCN will provide financial as well as technical assistance for the management of the mangroves.

He said the international body was making an all-out effort to strike a balance between conservation and economic development for the sustainable use of natural resources in the coastal areas.

Heading: India’s first: Gujarat to go for ‘open book exams’ in schools - Indian Express
Content:
They will be produced in court again for further remand

Student's Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) general secretary Safdar Nagori and four other suspects in the Ahmedabad serial blasts – Aamil Pervez, Asif Hussain, Sibli Abdul and Qamaruddin Nagori – were produced before a metropolitan court here on Monday.

The five had completed their 14-day remand with the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) in connection with the July 26 Civil Hospital blast.

V R Toliya, Deputy Superintendent of Police, DCB, who produced the five SIMI men before Metropolitan Magistrate G M Patel, said they will be produced before the same court on Tuesday for further remand in connection with the blast at Maninagar on July 26.

The DCB had brought Nagori's brother, Qamruddin along with Aamil, Asif and Sibili to Ahmedabad from Madhya Pradesh on a transfer warrant on August 23. SIMI chief Nagori was brought to the city two days later. A day later, all the five were put in police remand till September 3. The metropolitan court later extended the remand period till September 8.

Heading: SCOPE brings hope: Learning English much easier now - Indian Express
Content:
New system to be implemented in Class VIII, IX and secondary exams this year; Class XI and Higher Secondary to follow from 2010

For the first time in the history of Secondary Education across the country, the Gujarat Higher Secondary Education Board (GHSEB) has introduced the concept of 'open book examination'.

It will be introduced in Class VIII, IX and the Secondary Board Examinations from the current year and in Class XI and the Higher Secondary (Class XII) Board Examinations from 2010. The plan was under consideration for the last one year and comes as a breather for students struggling with memory problems.

R K Pathak, Chairman, GHSEB said: "The marks-driven education system that we have has pushed students to mug up subjects in a major way. As a result even state toppers fail miserably when they appear in the competitive exams."

Chief Minister Narendra Modi had in his speech on the occasion of Teacher's Day also emphasised the need for an 'open book examination' and had assured the students to make it a reality. Pathak said: "A requirement to look into education in a more comprehensive way is being felt everywhere, but this is the first time that an initiative has been made at this level. It is the reasoning, analytical and understanding capacity that has to be developed in the students. We need to test their intelligence rather than their memory and that is precisely what we have attempted through this."

He added that with the introduction of this system, examinations are likely to become more challenging and competitive.

Education Minister Ramanlal Vora said the novel concept has been introduced for those schools which come under the GHSEB. Schools under other boards in the state will continue with the old fashioned system of examinations and assessments.

To make things more student-friendly, the GHSEB has also announced the clubbing of same group subjects for assessment.

Earlier, if a student scored extremely well in one subject and failed in another, he/she was compelled to repeat the examinations.

"Now that languages have been clubbed together into a group like science and arts subjects, a student can still pass if he/she scores an overall pass mark, while failing to score the pass mark individually in each subject," Pathak added.

Heading: This November, Europe will go bananas, the Jhagadia way - Indian Express
Content:
In an effort to make the average Gujarati youth adept at English, the state government has started the Society for Creation of Opportunities through Proficiency in English (SCOPE).

Scope was registered as a society to enable youths to make a place for themselves in the job market. It is working aggressively towards training 30,000 students every three months in the entire state.

The programme designed by the Cambridge University has been well received for its course content.

For efficient conduct of the programme, the state has been divided into five zones — Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot and Mehsana. Here, the partner agencies identified by the government opened five centres in each taluka. Each centre has three trained teachers who give lessons to the students.

Each centre is, however, facing one big problem. Getting qualified instructors so that the trainees can learn perfect English has become a Herculean task for the state government.

Scope Chief Executive Officer R K Pathak said: "We do not encourage government school teachers to become instructors at SCOPE. After teaching for six to eight hours in school, they are already an exhausted lot. We do not wish to exhaust them more."

He said so far 50,000 students have cleared the quarterly examinations. "We have a goal to train two lakh students by the year 2010. At the end of each quarter, 30,000 students pass out," he added.

Heading: Bomb threat letter lands at Udhna station - Indian Express
Content:
Two years ago, Jhagadia bananas entered the Middle East; by November this year, they are expected to make their European debut

Jhagadia is a taluka in Bharuch district. It is also the breeding ground of a particular variety of banana that is peculiar to the place.

Two years ago, Jhagadia bananas had entered the Middle East; by November this year, they are expected to make their European debut.

This has happened due to the efforts of the Jhagadia-based Desai Fruits and Vegetables Private Limited (DFVPL), which started a packhouse and cold storage facilities for banana harvested by 125 farmers of a club.

"The export of Jhagadia bananas has proved to be a lucrative trade. A banana farmer having just four hectares of land makes an annual profit of Rs 3 lakh today. Two years ago, he made a profit of Rs 1.5 lakh only," said Ajitsinh Parmar, Chairman, Jhagadia Farmers' Club.

He added: "Last year, around 80 containers, each with 20 tonnes of bananas, were exported to the Middle East. Harvesting is done throughout the year; it is going on even now."

There are more than 30 tribal farmers in the club who are benefiting by their association with the DFVPL, said Parmar.

Meanwhile, Ajit Desai of DFVPL said: "DFVPL has recently entered a contract to export bananas to Europe, which will materialise by November. The company is awaiting the UN quality standards certificate to begin business with Europe." The company is also getting offers from Japan, he added.

"Jhagadia bananas are in demand because of their unique size and sweetness. That is why DFVPL has not altered the traditional methods of harvesting, but has only made provisions for packaging and cold storage in Jhagadia," said Bakul Chaudhary, DFVPL Production Manager.

Heading: Nutty professors exchange blows in front of students - Indian Express
Content:
Frenzied activity was seen at Udhna Railway Station after stationmaster Deepak Mathai received a letter threatening bomb blast on Monday afternoon. The call turned out to be a hoax.

The letter, which was signed by 'Jehad group', warned that it was no joke and that they would avenge the arrest of 'their people'.

The dog squad of the Railway Protection Force (RPF) and Government Railway Police conducted a search operation at the station premises for two hours.

Policemen kept a close watch for any suspicious activity at the station.

Inspector Virendra Singh of Udhna RPF said, "We have taken the letter dated September 5 from the stationmaster. Written in Gujarati, it was delivered by a postman at the stationmaster's office on Monday afternoon. It could be a mischief, but we have taken a serious note of the matter."

Heading: It’s a fight for survival at Kandla port as labour unions threaten agitation - Indian Express
Content:
Both of them are in police custody after lodging cross-complaints

In an unexpected incident, two professors of Garda College in Navsari town exchanged fisticuffs and kicks in front of the students, while quarrelling over some trivial issue. The Navsari police arrested them after both lodged cross-complaints in the afternoon.

A quarrel erupted between Vice-Principal Ratilal Dhimmer and Junior Professor Ishwar Choudhary today morning.

The two teachers had levelled allegations against each other that they were taking money from the students for admission and other purposes.

What began as a heated argument soon turned violent with the two academicians freely exchanging blows in the presence of students and other staff members.

Principal of the college, B G Panchasra, tried to bring the situation under control, but the two brushed him aside and used foul language against him. Later, the two left the college premises.

Dhimmer and Choudhary went to the Navsari Town police station to lodge cross complaints, but there also they started to quarrel, following which the police arrested them and put them behind bars.

Panchasra said: "The issue behind the quarrel was an old one. The two professors would quarrel over minor issues regularly. I tried to sort things out."

He added: "We will take strict action against the two. I have reported the matter to the Veer Narmad South Gujarat University Vice-Chancellor, Babubhai Parajapati. We will also issue notices to both, as they have approached the police and sullied the reputation of the college."

Heading: Sexagenarian strips in HC, accuses architects of cheating him - Indian Express
Content:
Two main labour unions at Kandla port have decided to go on an agitation in the general interest of the port. For the last ten months, administration and development at the port have come to a standstill in absence of the chairman, deputy chairman, chief engineer, chief vigilance officer, and heads of key departments like Finance, Mechanical Engineering etc.

"All development projects have been pending for a year. No decision has been taken in any matter concerning administration or labour, in the absence of the top officials. Besides, there is a stiff competition from other ports in the vicinity in terms of facilities. We can't remain mute spectators to the gradual decline of the port when we earn our bread from it," Manohar Bellani, senior labour trustee and general secretary of the port's biggest labour union told Newsline on Monday.

Bellani further said that his union and the Kandla Port Workers' Union (KPWU), affiliated to AITUC, have sent a notice to the union shipping secretary to either fill up all the vacancies or face direct action including an indefinite strike any time on or after October 2.

He and Santosh Nair, general secretary of KPWU, said that work on development projects like the procurement of mobile cranes, four new dry cargo berths and a state-of-the-art satellite port at Tuna has not made much headway in the last 11 months.

Bellani said that though the Kandla Dock Labour Board had been merged with the Kandla Port Trust long ago, the employees of the merged board are facing many problems. Neither has there been a meeting of the newly constituted tripartite advisory committee, nor has statutory settlements under the Industrial Dispute Act been implemented, he said.

The copies of the notice have also been sent to the chief labour commissioner and the regional commissioner, which is required by law to begin agitation.

Hiralal Parekh, former president of Gandhidham Chamber of Commerce and the president of the All India Salt Manufacturers' Association termed the move as 'right' and 'timely action' on the part of the workers.

"I am happy that the labour unions are fighting for the very existence of the port," said Parekh, adding that he suspects some conspiracy to systematically kill the port. He said they would never allow this to happen, as the very existence of the port town depends on it.

Heading: ‘What is wrong in being a hardliner? One shouldn’t be a fanatic’ - Indian Express
Content:
A shocking scene was witnessed at the Gujarat High Court on Monday when an elderly man took off his clothes and began running around the premises, stark naked. Sexagenarian Rajesh Sheth, who is fighting a case with a city-based architect couple for the last 12 years, stripped to protest against the alleged corruption in the judiciary.

The incident took place around 1.30 pm, when the High Court premises on the S G Highway was abuzz with activity.

Sheth, a resident of Panchvati Society in Ahmedabad, removed his clothes near the parking lot in the court premises. The security man on duty could nab him only after a five-minute chase. "On being caught by the guards, Sheth began screaming at the top of his voice," said an eyewitness.

Sola police officers rushed to the court after being informed about the incident by the HC authorities. Sola Inspector M P Vasava said: "Sheth was detained and booked under Section 151 of the IPC." It deals with knowingly joining or continuing in an assembly of five or more persons even on being commanded to disperse.

On being asked about the reasons for such a protest, Sheth said that an architect couple had cheated him to the tune of Rs 20 lakh about 12 years ago. "They have used their connections to influence the judges to pass an order against me," he alleged.

According to Sheth, he had sold his house in Gulbai Tekra area of the city to an architect couple in 1996. They, however, never gave him the promised amount, and the cheques issued by them had bounced too. "If I do not get justice, I will immolate myself along with my family members," he threatened.

Heading: Advani refuses to comment on giving a Central role to Modi - Indian Express
Content:
Launch a people's movement to get GUJCOC: Modi
Chief minister exhorts people to write to PM telling him that Gujarat needs the Bill

It was vintage Narendra Modi at his best at the rally to welcome the Gujarat Swarnim Sankalp Yatra Rath on Monday. In the presence of Leader of the Opposition L K Advani, he reiterated the importance of the Gujarat Control of Organised Crime (GUJCOC) Bill and asked the 30,000-strong crowd to exert pressure on the UPA government to clear the same.

"Write a letter to the Prime Minister of India in any language and mention one thing — Clear the GUJCOC Bill," said Modi.

He added: "To protect Gujarat I am waging a war with the Centre and I want the support of the people of Gujarat to win it. Twice in two years the state has sent the GUJCOC Bill to the Centre, but to no avail. The Centre is neither saying yes, nor has it the guts to say no."

In his trademark rhetoric, Modi issued a warning to the Centre and said that Gujarat won't sit quite if the Centre continued to ignore the proposal for a strict law to fight terror, which is the need of the hour. "Aa Gandhi aur Patel Nu Gujarat Che. Ame Aatankwadiyo Ni Pug Champi Nahi Kariye (This is the Gujarat of Gandhi and Patel. It will not bow down to the feet of the terrorists," Modi said.

He also made an indirect reference to the Indo-US nuclear deal. "Recently Bush (US President) has released a letter that has exposed how the UPA government has the put nation's security at stake," he said.

Advani, who represents the Gandhinagar constituency, of which Sanand is a newly included block, remained visibly silent. In his 15-minute speech, he neither mentioned GUJCOC nor POTA. Rather, he focused on the fact that Sanand is a part of his constituency now. "I have been the Gandhinagar MP for 17 years. It is my good fortune that I have come here," he said.

He highlighted the important role played by the Jansangh during Emergency.

Advani also acknowledge Modi's contribution towards strengthening the party in the state. He added: "In all these years, if anyone has to give an example of good governance, there are only two choices; the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government at the Centre and the Modi government in Gujarat."

Modi too took the opportunity to indulge in some self praise. He spoke about how he auctioned all the gifts he had received as the Chief Minister to raise funds to promote the education of the girl child in the state.

"Rupees 15 crore was raised through the auction of all the gifts, which has now been spent on girls' education," he said. In a bid to underscore his generosity, Modi also asked the people, "Don't you like to keep gifts? Don't you like to decorate your homes? I too was tempted, but I decided to decorate my Gujarat."

He also described himself as a 'wise guardian' who always thinks about the future of the family. "Like parents, who start collecting valuables for their daughter's marriage as she enters adulthood, I decided to prepare for the golden jubilee celebrations of statehood which is in 2010." He said the Swarnim Jyot Sankalp Yatra, which kick started on May 1 from Amreli, will go to every nagarpalika in the state by 2010 and administer an oath to the people to make Gujarat a better place.

Heading: Man held for stealing co-passenger’s wallet - Indian Express
Content:
In an interview to Newsline on Monday, BJP prime-ministerial candidate LK Advani refused to commit on the question of taking Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi to the centrestage in New Delhi. He insisted it was not a question, but a 'suggestion for action'.

Recently we saw serial blasts in Ahmedabad and a series of bomb recoveries in Surat. Do you think there has been an intelligence failure?
Intelligence failure does happen in various cases in different governments.

But what is alarming is the failure on the terrorism front as such. Can someone explain why Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan or Gujarat cannot have anti-terror laws when it is in place in Maharashtra? This shows the complete lack of will to deal firmly with terrorism. The consequence of such laxity on part of the UPA government has put the internal security of the country at stake.

Other countries, where human rights are supreme, have special stringent anti-terror laws. Even the anti-terror law of the US is more stringent than our POTA. The first and the foremost need of the hour is that the authorities should convey the message of zero tolerance to the perpetrators of terror. The UPA government has failed abysmally in this regard.

You recently had a joint press conference with Narendra Modi in Delhi. What is the political implication of this?

We have already made a statement. The reason for calling him was that there had been a terror attack in Gujarat and the Gujarat government had attained remarkable success in the preliminary investigations. So we thought of calling him as well.

How do you rate Narendra Modi as a national leader?
No doubt, he is one of the best leaders. He is also a very good administrator. He is doing great work here.

To elaborate, do we see Mr Narendra Modi moving to Delhi once you come to power?
This is not a question, in parliamentary parlance; this is a suggestion for action.

LK Advani has always been viewed as the hardliner in the BJP. Is this image an asset or a liability now as the would-be PM?
These clichés are irrelevant. A hardliner is a person who decides and stands firm on the decisions. What is wrong in that? One should not be a fanatic.

In Gujarat, the SC/ST morchas are carrying out community-specific membership drives. Is there a paradigm shift in the party once viewed as a party of the higher castes?
There is no paradigm shift. From the beginning, the BJP tried to include everyone and maintained a holistic approach. That is why you will see that in most of the governments we have been party to, the tribal minister has been a BJP member..

Your observations on the NSG waiver?
No comments on the NSG. Our basic objection still stands and our apprehensions have been confirmed by the secret US document released in a newspaper recently.

Heading: Mumbai University may soon offer nine one-year PG courses - Indian Express
Content:
A man who stole a fellow passenger's wallet at the duty-free shop at Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport (CSIA) was arrested at Delhi Airport after a lookout notice was issued against him.

Rahul Bhatia landed in the city from NewYork along with Varsha Mehta (57), the complainant, on August 24. While Varsha was shopping at the duty-free shop, Bhatia stole her wallet that had $500 and Rs 10,000. According to Sudam Shinde, investigating officer, Varsha filed a complaint regarding her missing wallet at the Sahar Police Station after which a footage of Bhatia stealing her wallet was captured. A lookout notice was issued in his name. Bhatia was caught at Delhi Airport on Monday morning by the immigration authorities. Bhatia had gone to Delhi to attend a wedding. He was produced before a magistrate on Monday afternoon and was later released on bail.

Heading: Ticket scam: Supervisor, booking clerk arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai University (MU) will soon offer one-year post-graduate courses in nine subjects, based on the academic structure followed in educational institutions abroad.

In May this year, a delegation comprising MU's vice-chancellor Vijay Khole and 13 principals from other colleges around the city, including St. Xavier's College, K C College and Sophia College, had visited leading educational institutions in the United Kingdom.

The delegation, under H R College principal Indu Shahani, observed the structure of the post-graduate (PG) courses offered by the universities there, and studied various courses offered to see what improvements could be made to courses offered at the MU.

The delegation also met with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh to brief him about their observations.

The main idea is to offer a more intensive set of PG courses with one-year duration unlike the conventional two-year ones.

The two year system in India has around eight working months each year, while rest are used up in vacations. The new course, though, will have the same portion of working days and vacations, but will be more rigorous as it will be completed in a continuous stretch of one year. "In the universities abroad, especially in the UK, the cost of education is very high, so a lot of students opt for a one-year full time course. We hope that our students can be offered this option too," said principal of Ruia College, Suhas Pednekar, who was one of the members of the delegation. The one-year course is a success in developed countries due to the superior infrastructure, and the student-teacher ratio is much better abroad than in India.

The delegation also found that the courses offered by the universities abroad were more application oriented and there was more emphasis on developing skills to make it easier to get jobs. "The best universities offer tailor-made courses. People from the various industries come to share their needs with the universities, which allows the universities to design courses accordingly," said Pednekar.

With these concerns in mind, the delegation has decided to propose nine courses to the Mumbai University, which will be of a year's duration only. "The Prime Minister was happy about it when we told him. He said that by 2020, we would have surplus human resources and that the time had come to ensure a more vocation-based approach in education," said Pednekar, adding that some among the new proposed subjects are International Business, Taxation, Mass Media, Management and Economics. The courses will be exhaustive and will offer everything from the syllabus, within a year. The faculty would include experts from the field, along with professionals from the corporate world.

Heading: Chain snatching gang busted - Indian Express
Content:
The Government Railway Police (GRP) recently arrested a supervisor and a booking clerk at the reservation office of Virar station for their alleged involvement in a ticket scam. With the spotlight now on the possible nexus between booking clerks and chief booking supervisors, the Railways is now conducting a detailed check into systems. Two months ago, three persons, including one booking clerk from this centre, were also arrested by the railway police for issuing bogus season tickets. As reported by the Newsline, six booking clerks of Central Railway were suspended for pocketing money by selling high value ticket. The number of clerks involved in the scam has now gone up to eight. No supervisor has been suspended till now, but officials say it is only a matter of time before chief booking supervisors are also nabbed for being hand in glove with the booking clerks. According to police sources, the modus operandi of booking clerks of WR was that they issued a low value ticket of Rs 4 and scanned a high value figure on a blank paper on the computer. "On May 3, 2008, a woman complained at the booking office at Virar that she was issued a season ticket for 27 days instead of one month . After investigation it was found that the ticket was fake. The officials at Mumbai division lodged a police complaint. Season tickets worth Rs 5 lakh were also seized. On June 12, 2008, a booking clerk, Mohammad Iqbal Khan, was arrested with his two associates- Anil Devidas Karnik (supplier of blank paper) and Mayur Mohan Goregaonkar (a computer expert). When police conducted a detailed investigation, it was found that all this was going on with the help of chief booking supervisors- Rajaram Babulal Saroj (58) and Naresh Chandra Prabhu Narain Chobey (47). On September 6, 2008, they were arrested," said Namankit More, Senior Police Inspector, GRP.

But the modus operandi of the CR clerks is different. First a low value ticket is generated through the UTS but it is not printed on the ticket at all. A high value ticket is generated next to the low value ticket and is printed on the saved ticket, causing a mismatch in the Unreserved Ticketing System and the stock numbers of the tickets. The ticket on which a high value ticket should have been printed is kept blank, called "non issued" tickets. "But unlike CR, fake tickets in WR are not mismatched. But as these tickets are fake, lots of mistakes are found on the tickets as fonts are different or size may also be different," said a railway official on condition of anonymity.

Heading: Manyata’s former husband granted bail - Indian Express
Content:
The preferred mode of transport used in most chain snatching cases is usually a two-wheeler, however, the Mulund police recently arrested a gang of chain-snatchers that used an auto-rickshaw to flee from the scene of crime.

Last week, a patrolling police team nabbed four members of a gang red-handed.

Police sub-inspector and investigation officer Sanjay Sable, said, "Most of the chain-snatching incidents involve motorcylists who rob the victims and speed away, but this was the first time in Mulund when the accused used a hired autorickshaw to commit the crime." He added, "All the four are fresh offenders and the first case against them was registered in August. Three more cases followed and last week a motorcyclist spotted them while robbing a woman and noted down the rickshaw number. He informed a police patrol van that was passing by and after a chase the accused were nabbed." The police have recovered four gold chains worth Rs 60,000 from the accused.

"They would operate in the evening on jogging tracks or in the vicinity of temples and target middle-aged women. All the accused are slum-dwellers from the Mulund Colony area and have confessed to the crime," said Sable. The police are investigating whether any criminal case has been earlier registered against the gang.

Heading: Railway police arrest two for carrying weapons - Indian Express
Content:
After being sentenced to six months imprisonment for sending lewd messages to female actors, Mehraj ur Rehman, former husband of Manyata Dutt, was granted bail on Monday in connection with a case pertaining to his escape from custody.

Though Mehraj has three cases of obscenity lodged against him, he has been out on bail in all those cases. Last month, Mehraj was sentenced to six months' imprisonment in connection with one of the obscenity cases, but was granted bail soon after to appeal against the conviction before the sessions court.

Mehraj had allegedly escaped from custody of Hyderabad Police on July 1. The Hyderabad Police had come to Mumbai to take Mehraj to Hyderabad in connection with a criminal case registered against him there. However, Mehraj persuaded them to come along to a five star hotel in the city where he dined with the team and gave them the slip. He was however, re-arrested later.

With the bail granted on Monday, Mehraj can return to his hometown Hyderabad. "Mehraj has secured bail against a security bond of Rs 7,000. He will now go back home to Hyderabad," said defence advocate Taslim Khan.

Heading: ‘Increased accountability is true measure of RTI’s success’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Dadar railway police have arrested two men for carrying weapons- a country made revolver and five live cartridges.

According to Narendra Kulkarni, senior police inspector from Dadar railway police station, on September 6 around 4.30 am, the police apprehended Manoj Kanojia (26), a native of Uttar Pradesh, at platform number 6 of Dadar station.

A magazine and five live cartridges were recovered from him. However, in the melee, his accomplice, Nazim alias Chintu Khan, a resident of Dharavi, gave the police the slip. He was carrying a country made revolver with him.

"Our first priority was to arrest Khan since the weapons were with him. We arrested him on Sunday night from Kurla rail terminus from where he was planning to take a long distance train and flee the city," said Kulkarni.

Heading: State defends IGP for sending stalker to mental asylum - Indian Express
Content:
It is hard to believe that behind his five feet two and a half frame and humble face, is the man who has become a household name for fighting public causes and corruption. After winning the Nani Palkhiwala award for civil liberties in January this year, 61-year-old Shailesh Gandhi, a former IIT alumnus added another feather to his cap when he became the Chief Information Commissioner (CIC) on Friday. Newsline spoke to the man who started the RTI activism in the city about his journey and his future plans. Gandhi is expected to take the seat officially on the 18 th of this month.

Q. The RTI Act was formulated to motivate people to fight for more transparency. However, a large number of cases are pending. Will this not deter the common man from using this tool? What will you as the next CIC officer do to curb this problem?

There are 16, 600 cases pending in the State information commission and 8,500 pending cases with the Central information commission. On an average, around 15-200 appeals are disposed off every month. If these figures continue to rise, it will be the ultimate death of the RTI Act. The common man will loose faith in the Act, just as he has lost faith in the judiciary. This is a cause of worry for me; my idea is to reduce the pendency period to a minimum of three months.

I am taking this post to strengthen the RTI act. As an activist, I too have criticized the CIC officer for not taking his job seriously. However, now that I have got this opportunity, I'll try my best to bring in more transparency and reduce the backlog. If by any chance, I am not able to achieve the targeted results within 3-4 months, I'll call it quits.

Q. From taking up the Satyendra Dubey murder case in 2003 when the RTI Act did not even exist to other cases, which case was the most challenging for you as an activist?

I took up the Satyendra Dubey murder case by accident. When The Indian Express first broke the news, RTI Act did not even exist, but the case brought out angst in me. It was also challenging in the sense that without the Act, we tried to hold the officials answerable. After the RTI Act came into foray, the Chief Minister's relief fund case was the most challenging. We fought for almost two years to get a fair answer. The case taught me my first lesson, that though it is a powerful tool, it cannot be always successful keeping in mind the time lapse. This is an area we should carefully work on.

Q. After the RTI Act was introduced, what was your eureka moment. When did you realize this is an Act meant for a democracy like India?

As a youngster in IIT, I used to criticize the system. But twenty years down the line I became the system and still societal problems were the same. There was no particular moment for me, I was totally observed in my work. I found the true use of the Act by accident. In 2005 someone highlighted the case of political interference in police transfers. The case heightened my curiosity, and we filed a RTI. That was the beginning for me; I realized this is indeed a powerful tool. For me RTI is not a weapon, a weapon is used for destruction. I am not interested in destroying the government; all I want is an increased accountability. The RTI is indeed meant for a democracy like ours. In other countries, citizens can hold the officials accountable even with a phone call, sadly it is not the same here. Hence the RTI Act is tailor made for the country.

Q. You have also announced the plan of taking a salary of Re 1. Can you elaborate on that?

As a common man and as an activist, we always questioned a bureaucrat's attitude. I announced that I will take a salary of Re 1 as a token amount. I also have said no to the official car and bungalow. I have got everything from the society, a good education, a fruitful career and a happy family. Now is the time to give something back to the society.

Heading: Cops trace minor girl missing since last year, boyfriend held - Indian Express
Content:
The state government on Monday defended Special Inspector General of Police (IGP) Meeran Borwankar, who had sent a Powai resident to a mental asylum in Pune for allegedly stalking her and sending her disturbing SMSes, saying that her action was "justified".

This contradicts the government's stand nearly three weeks ago where it had agreed to lapse in following proper procedure of law. Advocate general Ravi Kadam informed the court that Borwankar had sent Asha Bajaj to a mental asylum after getting a judicial order obtained through a proper procedure of law.

However, the Bombay High Court has taken a serious note of the entire episode and said that they would be framing guidelines to be followed for conducting cases registered under the Mental Health Act.

On the last date of hearing on August 13, public prosecutor Satish Borulkar had informed the court that the concerned officers had failed to follow the proper procedure while sending the lady to the mental asylum. In June, Bajaj was sent to a mental hospital prison after she allegedly reached Borwankar's residence and made a wish to marry her son.

The Division Bench of Justice Bilal Nazki and Justice Ashutosh Kumbhkoni observed that the Pune Police also failed to inform Bajaj's mother, after she was sent to mental hospital. "We have strong belief that law was not followed in this case," observed Justice Nazki. However, Kadam said that Bajaj's mother was informed about the incident. He also justified Borwankar's action stating that on several occasion Bajaj had threatened to end her life.

The matter will come up for hearing on Tuesday.

Heading: ATM guard held for attempting robbery - Indian Express
Content:
Girl sent for medical examination; cops say the boy, with whom she eloped, may face rape charges

Following the Bombay High Court's directive to Mumbai Police Commissioner Hasan Gaffoor to file an affidavit regarding police efforts to trace a 16-year-girl who went missing from her residence in Malwani in May last year, the Mumbai Police Crime Branch on Monday traced the girl and arrested her 22-year-old boyfriend from a hotel in Kashimira.

While the girl, who is now 17, had been sent to a hospital for a medical examination to ascertain whether she was raped, her boyfriend identified as Feroze Abdul Khaleef Shaikh will be produced in court for police remand tomorrow.

According to the police, in May 2007, a missing person's complaint was registered after the girl went missing from her Malwani residence. However, after her parents learnt from their neighbours that she was seen leaving with Shaikh, a welder in the area, a kidnapping case was registered against him.

"The two had disappeared and could not be traced. In 2008, desperate to locate their daughter, the girl's parents filed a Habeas Corpus writ petition in the Bombay High Court stating that their daughter had not been traced by the police. Following this, a Bench comprising Justices Bilal Nazki and Ashutosh Arvind Kumbakoni directed the Mumbai Police Commissioner to file an affidavit in the matter. In his affidavit, the Commissioner stated that special efforts would be made to locate the girl and that the Crime Branch would be put on the job," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria.

On August 28, the case was handed over to the Crime Branch.

"This morning, Crime Branch Unit 6 located the girl and the accused at Yatri Hotel in Kashimira. Shaikh had told the girl that he loved her. He had saved Rs 15,000 and also sold his scooter. The two then fled to Madgaon in Goa, where he earned his living as a welder. When he got a whiff that the police were after him, the duo left Goa and kept shifting from place to place to evade the police," said Maria.

"We have sent the girl for a medical examination. If the two have had sex, the arrested accused will be booked for rape as the girl is a minor," he added.

Heading: Proposal to introduce Marathi as optional subject in CIE - Indian Express
Content:
Though he was unable to rob cash, he damaged the kiosk worth Rs 8 lakh, say police

A 22-year-old security guard posted at an ATM of Dena Bank near Jogeshwari station was arrested on Saturday for allegedly attempting to steal the cash. Though the arrested accused, Niranjan Yadav, was unable to rob the cash, the police say that he damaged the kiosk worth approximately Rs 8 lakh.

Police Inspector Datta Sankhe from the Oshiwara police said, "Yadav attempted to rob the ATM probably on the night of August 26 when he was on duty. However, the theft was discovered on the morning of August 30 when bank officials visited the ATM to deposit cash. The officials noticed that the back of the kiosk was completely damaged and concluded that someone had attempted a robbery. A complaint was registered with us the same day and we started our enquiries."

Yadav came under suspicion after the police noticed that he did not report to work since the day robbery attempt was made. "A safe within the ATM cabin which contains an 'admin card' used for gaining access to the machine was also opened with a duplicate key but access to the cash could not be gained as the accused did not know the code for opening the main box containing cash. Then, a disc-grinder had been used to cut away parts of the kiosk from the back. The fact that the lens of the CCTV camera had also been covered with a piece of paper helped us zero down on Yadav," said Sankhe.

After tracing the residential address of Yadav, the police kept a watch on his house in Goregaon. "Finally, on Saturday our officials saw him in the locality and recognized him from the description given to us. He was immediately picked up. During interrogation, he admitted that he had been planning the robbery for a month and had also managed to steal the key of the safe containing the admin card from a visiting bank official and had made duplicate of it," said Sankhe.

According to the police, after finishing his HSC, Yadav started working with a private security agency. His parents are from Uttar Pradesh and he stays alone at a rented flat in Goregaon. "Yadav has been charged with attempt to robbery and has been remanded to police custody till September 9," Sankhe said.

Heading: ED says Bhosale has not disclosed info on UAE bank accounts, opposes bail plea - Indian Express
Content:
Close on the heels of considering to make Marathi a compulsory subject for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (ICSE) and Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), there is a proposal to introduce Marathi as an optional subject in the University of Cambridge International Examinations (CIE) and International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) curriculum (for 14 to 16 year olds) in Maharashtra.

CIE is part of the Cambridge Assessment Group, a not-for-profit organization and part of the University of Cambridge. Dinesh Kamble, a member of the CIE's Higher Education Advisory Council, India, said that he would put forward the proposal to introduce Marathi as an optional subject at the Higher Education Advisory Council for India meet in Cambridge next month. Kamble who has been recently appointed as CIE India member is also the deputy registrar of the University of Mumbai.

"It has come to my notice that there are many Marathi students in IGCSE schools who wish to study Marathi. The idea is to offer Marathi as an optional subject. The level of difficulty- basic or higher- will be decided later," said Kamble.

CIE offers Marathi, Tamil, Telgu, Hindi at the Advanced (A) and Advanced Supplementary (AS) levels (16-18 years) and offers Hindi as second language at the IGCSE level.

Kamble said that he would discuss streamlining grades to marks conversion at the meet next month. "Students of CIE find it difficult to get in to colleges here after standards X and XII because there is ambiguity about the grades given by CIE. That is why a lot of students prefer to go abroad. If we are able to devise a way that will make it easy for colleges to recognise the CIE grades and evaluate students accordingly, we will be able to retain those students in India."

Heading: As terror spectre grips city, security device cos laugh all the way to bank - Indian Express
Content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Monday opposed the plea of Pune-based businessman, Avinash Bhosale, on grounds that he had not disclosed vital information regarding his personal bank accounts which are operational in United Arab Emirates (UAE) and in India to the agency, thereby, violating the conditions of the earlier High Court order for returning his passport.

Bhosale was arrested by the customs' officials last year for not declaring imported goods while returning from a trip abroad.

ED launched a probe into his dealings and confiscated his passport. In a nine page detailed affidavit filed by the Assistant Director of Directorate of Enforcement I Vikraman, he said that when senior ED officials went to Dubai last month, they found out that Bhosale has undisclosed accounts at ABN-AMRO and Standard Chartered Banks.

The Court had asked him to disclose his accounts, and provide authority letters to banks so that ED could access them, but he did not do so. The affidavit also says that at ABN-AMRO bank, Bhosale's personal account has four 'foreign currency' sub-accounts wherein big transactions have taken place, and the agency needs to probe the transactions,.

The affidavit also states that Bhosale had an account in the name of Bhosale Trading Company, at ABN Amro bank through which USD 8 lakh were transferred in 2003-2005. The affidavit alleges that it was a violation of law as Bhosale had NRI status during this period.

The affidavit also says that Bhosale has not disclosed before the agency any information regarding his accounts in Bank Of India's branches at Fergusson College and Koregaon Park in Pune, and at HDFC's Delhi branch. Considering the above aspects, the affidavit states that his passport should not be released till the probe is over. The matter will come up for hearing on September 10.

According to the plea filed by Bhosale, the high court had last month ordered E D to complete the probe within a week. However, stating that it was unjustifiable and that insufficient time was given, the ED had challenged the High Court's order in the Supreme court. Accordingly the apex court had referred the plea of ED to the high court again directing that the high court pass appropriate orders.

Heading: Motorman jumps signal at Belapur - Indian Express
Content:
Earlier: Private security used to be limited to a man in uniform and a firearmToday: Every establishment must have state-of-art electronic equipment

JThe spectre of terror attacks may have made paranoids out of everyone in the nation's commercial capital — from policemen to roadside pedestrians. But for those dealing with security apparatus, it has been a laugh all the way to the bank.

In a scenario where every establishment from colleges to temples, shopping malls to railway stations arms itself with security devices like metal detectors and CCTV cameras, the security equipment industry is booming with business.

Says Security Association of India President Gurcharan Singh: "In the past, private security was limited to the extent of a human presence with a uniform and a firearm. However, with the changing times and the nature of dangers, reliance on electronic security apparatus has become a must. Consumers of security services have realised that relying on mere man-power is not enough and that electronic security devices are much more effective — with lesser chances of error."

Asked about the size of the growing market for security services, Singh said, "With the present scenario of terror threats and the fact that a terrorist can strike anywhere without discrimination, the day has come when each and every establishment where people come together — like hospitals or municipal offices — has to be be equipped with state of the art surveillance systems."

Fire and Safety Association of India (FSAI) President and Zicom MD Pramoud Rao explained, "It was the attack on the twin World Trade Centre (WTC) towers at Manhattan that changed the whole scenario relating to private security. Post that incident, people across the world realised that any and every establishment can be a potential terror target, thus giving outfits dealing in security devices a boost. The 7/11 train blasts again reinforced the realisation that nothing is safe from hostile acts of terror."

Fame Group Assistant Vice-President Deepak Shinde said, "We have definitely tightened security over the past year and all our security personnel are equipped with hand-held metal detectors. Moreover, apart from door frame metal detectors at the main entry points, we have also installed such detectors at entrances of movie-halls within the premises."

Being the financial capital of India, Mumbai accounts for 30 per cent of the national market for security services, added Rao. "The private security business is increasing at a rate of 30-35 per cent a year and is expected to be a Rs 2,125 crore industry by 2012. The terror threats have created a city where everything from malls to railway stations to temples to even colleges is being equipped with security devices, specifically metal detectors (both door-frame and hand-held) and CCTV cameras. However, establishments are not the only places where such services are needed. A new range of security devices, specifically aimed at securing private residences, too have been introduced."

Latches and double-doors are a thing of the past, said Rao. "The present consumer has so much variety when it comes to residential security systems. There is also a new kind of electronic lock in the market which stores the finger-prints of the owner and other residents of the house — so that door can be opened only after the person puts his finger tips on the touch-screen," he said. "This is like something we have seen in Hollywood spy thrillers."

According to Rao, the CCTV cameras installed at railway stations are not sold to the Railways but are put there for a service charge. "The service charge for all the CCTV cameras installed with the Railways cost Rs 15 lakh per month. Our studies show that educational institutions and private residences are our next big market. We are getting communication from educational institutions in the city, asking for help in setting up surveillance systems in their premises with a view to prevent everything from eve-teasing to theft or damage of school property."

Heading: Man held for ‘licence-free’ driving after 4-day vigil - Indian Express
Content:
It was a close shave for a few hundred passengers of the Central Railway on Monday afternoon when a motorman jumped a signal just outside Belapur railway station, nearly causing a collision between two trains.

According to a railway official, a "signal at danger" alert was sounded after the Belapur-bound local on the Harbour Line from Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST) crossed the signal outside Belapur station at 1.03 pm. The train was scheduled to arrive at Platform No 2 at Belapur. It instead arrived on Platform No 1, from where the 12.57 pm CST-Panvel train had left barely a couple of minutes prior to that.

"The train was supposed to go to Platform No 2 and then return in the direction towards CST," said a railway official. "It instead went on Platform No 1, where there could have been a collision had the Panvel local been delayed by a couple of minutes."

As per sources at Central Railway, the motorman later said the signal had been clear and that was why he crossed it. Officials at the station refuted that claim. Central Railway Divisional Railway Manager J N Lal said an inquiry would be conducted immediately. "An inquiry is going on and if anybody is found guilty of negligence, stern action will be taken against him," said Lal.

A similar incident occurred last year on December 13 when a motorman hit an empty Thane local train from the rear, at Thane station. He was suspended immediately pending further inquiries.

Heading: CBI says two arrested from Nepal not linked to blasts, court orders their release - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai Police's message: Driving licence deserves same respect one gives to passport

In a move aimed at sending out a stern and unambiguous message to habitually delinquent drivers, Mumbai Police's Traffic Department today nabbed a 28-year-old Haji Ali resident for driving without a licence. At around 10.30 am, minutes after Keyur Rajendra Parikh had left his home, he was arrested.

Unlike any other arrest, however, this operation was "another milestone" for the Traffic Department, said Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Harish Baijal. This is the first time a "traffic offender's driving habits" had been under observation for four days, before the actual arrest.

According to Baijal, a crackdown was felt necessary as the Traffic Department had observed a tendency among those caught driving drunk to repeat the offence and those whose licences had been suspended to default during the prohibition period.

"The idea is to ensure that they treat the driving licence with the same respect that one gives to a passport. The message is very clear. If the law has told you not to drive and has suspended your licence, then you need to obey the law," Baijal pointed out.

Parikh had earlier been arrested on the night of July 14 when he was caught driving drunk after leaving a late night party at Hard Rock Café, Worli. He was produced at Bhoiwada Court on July 30, where he was given a punishment of one day's simple imprisonment and a Rs 2,000 fine.

Parikh's motor driving licence had also been suspended for six months. The traffic police then kept a watch on his driving habits, with a vigil outside his house and office.

The vehicle in which Parikh was caught driving on July 14 — a Santro with the vehicle number MH01-AE-3276 — had also been under traffic police scanner for four days. The photographs of the person driving the Santro matched that of Parikh from his July 14 arrest records.

The Traffic Department has got an entire background check done for all the 23,000 people booked for driving drunk. Details of the traffic offences, along with their photographs, are now part of a centralised data which is available to all traffic police posts.

The latest incident follows the case of Kumar Pujari Rao, a two-time traffic offender who was found driving drunk after his licence was suspended. Rao's licence had been revoked for life, making it illegal for him to drive a vehicle again.

After his arrest today, Parikh was booked under the Motor Vehicle Act for driving without an effective licence while leaving for work, a few kilometers from his house. According to Baijal, his only words to the Traffic cops at the time of the arrest were that "this will ruin my career as I have an assignment in a few days."

He was later produced in court where he had to deposit a Rs 5,000 fine and was sent to judicial custody. He has been told to appear for hearing on September 22.

When Newsline visited his residence, his mother Bhavna Parikh said that she was not aware of any arrest. "He is to go abroad for some business meeting and I'm sure that if it was serious, I would have been contacted by my son," she said. She added that her son is an event manager.

Heading: BMC plans multi-level parking lots with skywalks attached - Indian Express
Content:
The special TADA court on Monday directed the CBI to release two persons arrested from Nepal in connection with the 1993 Mumbai serial blasts case after the agency admitted that it was a case of "mistaken identity."

The CBI on Monday informed the court that the two persons, who were arrested by the Nepal police and then extradited to India under the pretext of them being two of the 127 accused in the 1993 blasts case, were indeed the wrong persons and it was a case of mistaken identity.

The CBI had produced the two before the TADA court saying that they were Salim Abdul Ghani Gazi and Riyaz Khatri, who had an Interpol Red Corner notice issued for their arrest in 1997. But the agency today took a U-turn and said the arrested persons had no connection with the blasts.

"We wanted Salim Gazi and Riyaz Khatri, instead the Nepal police deported Asfak Tak and Riyaz Lone. It's an honest error on the part of the Nepal police," said public prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam. Nikam said both the arrested have no past criminal background and hence should be released at the earliest.

Designated TADA judge D U Mulla ordered that both Tak and Lone be immediately released and directed the CBI to make their travel arrangements.

In its application, the CBI has also stated that both the persons would be flown back to Nepal and the cost would be borne by the agency.

Heading: Dry run, on the double - Indian Express
Content:
Seven mechanised parking lots to be constructed at Dadar, Borivali, Kurla, Powai, Matunga on PPP basis

Commuters can soon look forward to parking their four-wheelers inside mechanised multi-storey parking lots before walking across a spiffy skywalk connecting to the nearest railway station.

To cope with chaotic streetside parking and to manage traffic effectively in congested railway station areas, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) will construct seven multi-level parking lots in the city. According to 2007 estimates, there are already 14 lakh vehicles in the city, with 400 new vehicles being registered daily. This has caused unplanned parking along roadsides, which in turn reduces space on roads by more than 20 per cent.

"There is a need to create more parking spaces in the city. Accordingly, these spots have been selected which will be developed on a Public-Private Partnership model," said Additional Municipal Commissioner R A Rajeev. "There is no limit on the use of FSI for construction of parking spots and therefore multi-level lots will be constructed making maximum use of the space."

The locations of the proposed mechanised parking lots are Dadar (S K Bole Marg), Matunga (outside the railway station), two spots at Borivali (near the ward office and outside the station), two spots at Kurla (near the railway station) and three in Powai (along Adi Shankaracharya Marg). All these locations are close to railway stations and commuters can park their vehicles and take a local train to reach their destinations.

"We will also construct skywalks from these parking spots as it will be efficient for commuters to park and walk. The parking spot at S K Bole Marg can have a skywalk connecting it to Dadar station and to Siddhivinayak temple in Prabhadevi. Wherever possible, skywalks will be constructed," Rajeev said.

Each of these spots can accommodate 300 to 350 four-wheelers. Civic officials said that priority would be given to mechanised parking lots. "If a parking lot is multi-storeyed, then commuters cannot wait too long to park and then come down. Mechanised systems will just lift cars and owners can retrieve them in less than two minutes," said Chief Engineer (Roads) D L Shinde. The BMC has already constructed a multi-storeyed mechanised parking lot on a PPP basis at Bhulabhai Desai Road.

The civic administration will now invite tenders for contractors to develop these parking lots. Contractors will also be given 30 per cent of the space for commercial exploitation.

Underground parking: BMC yet to start work

* A year after floating the idea of setting up underground parking lots-cum-shopping complexes and shortlisting 21 sites in addition to Regal Junction and Crawford Market, the civic administration is struggling to start the project. After inviting tenders twice, the BMC will now again invite Expression of Interest from bidders with experience in underground parking construction and technology available to dig 20 metres underground.

* "We do not have the machinery to go so deep and create parking space as it is expensive and not readily available. It is therefore decided to let contractors suggest how to go ahead with the project," said a civic official. "Also, the other 21 sites are cancelled for now till these two sites are first developed."

* The project has also hit other hurdles like CRZ restrictions, besides security and heritage clearances.

Heading: No LPG cylinders for families, plenty for commercial users - Indian Express
Content:
Diesel on ration amid twin blocks

For the last three days, the city's civic bus undertaking Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML), which runs wholly on diesel, has had trouble with fuel supply. Of the seven tankers that it needs everyday, at least two are delayed.

"Bus schedules have not been affected, but it is true that some of our tankers are not coming, or are delayed. It is affecting our planning for the day," said a PMPML officer.

On Monday, to adjust for the delay in the arrival of one of the tankers, the company had to split the diesel supply meant for Nigdi with the Bhosari depot. On Sunday, around 600 kilolitres of diesel from Pune station were transferred to Narveer Tanaji Wadi for the stationed buses to refuel. "We are planning one day in advance now to make up for the delay," said the officer.

Supply hit another block on Saturday when the Loni terminal developed a snag in the server that lasted nearly a day, leading to slow supply. Although the authorities said things had normalised on Sunday, commuters struggled to procure diesel on Monday.

"There is no problem today, everything is normal," said Nitin Kankaria, general secretary, Petrol Pump Dealers Association.

But many petrol pumps turned away consumers. When business executive Jayant Karia went to Kasarwadi petrol pump, he was told the pump was out of stock.

At other places, pump owners rationed diesel to ensure that it was available through the day. "Earlier, we would take additional diesel on Saturdays to stock up for Sundays. Now, if a pump owner has a sale for 100 KL per month, it is divided for 26 working days and each day's supply is adhered to strictly," said a pump owner.

Travel agencies, which run on diesel, also had trouble getting diesel. "From Katraj to Navi Peth, there was no pump that was supplying diesel in the morning," said Deepak Jamdade, a driver with a travel agency.

Heading: Smaller, shallower, smarter, safer - Indian Express
Content:
Two workers with an LPG dealer in Bhosari were arrested on Sunday, yet another reminder of the corruption rampant in the process of distributing cylinders to Bhosari MIDC, Bhosari gaothan, Kasarwadi, Nashik Phata, Nehrunagar, Sant Tukaramnagar and Vallabhnagar.

While households struggle to get their quota of LPG cylinders, owners of businesses -hotels, canteens, and industries - continue to get their refills. They are being sold domestic cylinders at rates much lower than the industrial price of Rs 1,100. Yet, the district collectorate points out, not one case has been filed nor has anybody been caught black-marketing cylinders the area in eight months till Monday.

On Sunday, a group of citizens from Sant Tukaramnagar in Pimpri caught two employees of Gujar Enterprises while they were palming off two domestic cylinders to two of their alleged agents. Each domestic cylinder costs Rs 343 but these were being sold for Rs 500 — a fact the two employees confirmed to The Indian Express at the Bhosari police station. Police inspector Mohan Vidhate said the arrested would face charges under the Essential Commodities Act.

Rajesh Wable, president of the Hari Om Pratishtan, who along with 15 others caught the foursome, alleged hoteliers and household canteenwallahs are the most favoured. "They get as many cylinders as they want, for Rs 650 to Rs 800, while families struggle to get their quota," he said.

Gujar Enterprises owner Kunal Shah promised to investigate the allegations against his employees. He said employees on delivery duty are under pressure to hand over their cylinders to powerful people.

Foodgrains distribution officer Pradeep Patil said no cylinder misuse case has been filed in Pimpri-Chinchwad, though civic activists have been alleging a big racket. "I am short of staff but we will now inspect hotels and industries. Companies too should take action against errant dealers," he said.

J Vedagiri, territory manager of the Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd, said last year raids were conducted, but this year he was not sure.

Consumers attack LPG vehicle
In Dehu Road, angry residents on Sunday morning attacked a tempo carrying LPG cylinders. Consumers waiting for LPG cylinders at Kohli Gas agency stopped its vehicle and demanded that agency owner Mahendra Kohli address their problems.

Following the attack, officials of the district supply office cracked down on Ashok Sweets, Ashok Hotels and Ruchira Sweet Mart at Dehu Road. They seized 700 litres of kerosene and 12 LPG cylinders.

For weeks now, residents have been complaining about acute shortage of LPG cylinders, kerosene, petrol and diesel. "After the police intervened, 350 cylinders were distributed to customers," said inspector Mahesh Sawant. Kohli later urged consumers to cooperate as there was a genuine shortage of cylinders.

Heading: No room in city: Infy sends 3,000 executives south - Indian Express
Content:
In 15 days, sea change for swimming pools

Swimming pools run by the civic administration are set to don a new, safe look with the authorities promising to implement a series of guidelines within 15 days.

A restriction on depth will ensure some sort of protection against possible drowning. The draft safety guidelines propose that no pool should be deeper than 5 feet 6 inches, or 1.67 m, the depth having been calculated on the basis of a swimmer's average height. The administration, however, hopes to have this limit raised so that swimming can be promoted as a sport.

The guidelines include restrictions on pool size too. To reduce risks, the recommendations include a ban on diving boards at public pools, at least one trainer for every 20 swimmers, and a minimum area of 4 sq m per swimmer.

Several new features have been proposed to ensure safety - separate sections for children and amateurs; waterproofed walls and bottoms in the pools; anti-skid tiles at the sides; ladders to get in and out and more - with the pool surface and periphery under glare-free lighting, and under constant vigil from watchtowers at either end.

For swimmers' health, the proposals include enclosed shower booths and sanitary units, use of proper costume, medical check-ups and regular rehearsals for emergency services, installation of filtration and chlorination plants and tests on pool water by a government-run laboratory.

The guidelines had been pending with the Pune Municipal Corporation for six years but City Improvement Committee (CIC) has now pledged to get them approved with a few amendments. "The proposal seeking approval was tabled in May 2002, but was pending since. Now, the draft Development Control rules will be amended in such a way that swimming can be promoted as a sport," CIC chairman Ganesh Bidkar said.

The draft rules had been prepared after a series of accidents.

GUIDELINES
Depth: 1.67m proposed, but admin wants it raised to promote contests
Size: 25m × 9m maximum
Restrictions: No diving boards, one swimmer per 4 sq m
Staff: One trainer for 20 swimmers, guards at watchtowers
Safety features: Separate sections for children and amateurs, waterproofed walls and bottoms, 3m margin with anti-skid tiles; ladders to get in and out; medical teams, periodic tests on pool water

Heading: Guruji Talim is displaying Balaji Darshan this year - Indian Express
Content:
More than 3,000 information technology executives initially lined up to work at the Pune facility of Infosys Technologies Ltd have now been posted in Chennai because there is no office for them in the city.

Construction of Phase 2 of the Hinjewadi Project, where they would have worked, has been delayed, said T V Mohandas Pai, the company's human resources director. Pai, who is on the company board, was speaking with the media at the incomplete Phase 2 of the Infosys campus on Monday.

The project is running six months behind schedule and will require another 24 months to complete, he said. "The construction got delayed partly because of the MNS agitation earlier this year. But the construction industry is facing a shortage of manpower. We once had over 3,400 people working at Phase 2. The number fell to 1,400 at one point, though now it has risen slightly, 1,800," Pai said.

Pai said that this outflow of executives would continue. "There is no space here, where to they work? They had to be sent to Chennai," he said.

Pune is also home to the company's only legal process outsourcing facility, which started three months ago. "The market for the LPO opened up in the United States recently, with people asking why they should pay $150 an hour for documentation. At present the LPO industry is worth $200 million, but it could soon cross a billion dollars," Pai said.

After Mysore, the company is developing its Pune facility as another training centre. While the former is an entry-level training institute, the Pune facility, which will open shortly, will be a specialised training centre. With the completion of Phase 2, the company would have invested Rs 1,500 crore in its Pune set up, he said.

The second phase is spread over 114 acres and the company has already invested Rs 880 crore here. "In the last year, both phases have contributed to exports worth Rs 7,270 crore," he said.

Heading: Suicide on campus: Family to go on fast - Indian Express
Content:
Guruji Talim Ganpati, the third "Manache Ganpati" of the city, is unique for keeping its tradition of having volunteers across religions and castes for more than 120 years now. The mandal , also known for presenting new decorations every year, has on display "Balaji Darshan" as its decoration this year.

The roots of religious unity among volunteers of the mandal can be traced back to 1887, when the Ganpati idol was first installed. Nanasaheb Khasagiwale, Deepu Shinde, Sheikh Lalabhai and Sheikh Rustumbhai Nalband were among those who installed the Guruji Talim Ganapati . "The tradition still continues and we have volunteers from across various religions and castes," said Prithviraj Pardeshi, coordinator of the mandal's activities for this year.

According to researchers, being the biggest Talim, a place where wrestlers used to be trained, in those days, Guruji Talim Ganpati was allotted the third position in the immersion procession at a meeting held in 1894.

From then, the Guruji Talim Ganpati has been the third "Manacha Ganpati" of the city. The present idol of the Guruji Talim Ganpati, sitting on a mouse (the vehicle of Ganesha ), was created in 1972.

The mandal is well known for encouraging a new generation of artistes. This year too, Santosh Tak and Avinash Jindam, young artistes from Ahmednagar, have crafted the decoration.

Another unique feature of the mandal is that almost all the volunteers are from the trading community. "We have stopped taking donations for 22 years. The volunteers contribute for the activities," said Pardeshi.

"The mandal is always at the forefront when it comes to contributing for the national calamities. We raise funds for floods, famine and also help poor people who need medical help," he said. "The activities during the 10-day festival are, however, of a religious nature — like Mantra Jagar , Atharvasheersha Pathan and Ganesh Yaag ," he added.

Another feature of the mandal is its grand immersion procession. The Dhol Pathak of Shivgarjana and Chetak Sports Club, Darbar Brass Band and Nagara Vadan by Nagarkars are some of the other the highlights of this mandal .

Heading: Information on call for pensioners - Indian Express
Content:
The family of a man who had committed suicide seeking a college seat for his son has threatened to carry on the fight. The family says it will go on a hunger strike unless the college admits not only the boy but also his siblings.

Babu Saudagar, a watchman working with the Maharashtra Mitramandal Junior High School at Kalewadi, had stormed the campus of Marathwada Mitramandal College on August 29 demanding admission for his son. He assaulted college treasurer Bhausaheb Jadhav, drank pesticide and was rushed to Prayag Hospital, where he died on Sunday.

On Monday morning, his family along with members of the Maharashtra Muslim Front, the All India Consumer Committee and the All India Muslim OBC Organisation reached the college to meet board members. The college had beefed up security on the premises to prevent any possible backlash.

The chairman of the All India Consumer Committee, Sunil Mane said, "We have a set of prelisted demands that we would like to discuss with the board members. The deceased was the only earning member of the family, so we want them to appoint one of his sons in his place and admit his other three children to various courses. We also want the board to let them continue living in their room in Kalewadi."

Musa Ali, the son of the deceased said, "Till they give in to our demands we will continue our agitation."

College secretary S D Gange said, "The society has already paid for the hospital expenses and the education of the children of the deceased till now. This is all that we can do. They have put forth a set of ridiculous demands which cannot be considered."

Heading: MBM course in agriculture begins - Indian Express
Content:
The Defence Accounts Pensioners Association (DAPA) has volunteered to help the elderly with information on salaries of pensioners after the implementation of the Sixth Pay Commission.

DAPA members U.P. Kamble and Shailendra Mhaskar said that they would be open to calls between 2 pm to 8 pm for details on 24451319. If a person provides the old pension details, the association will help giving the revised pension figure, said Kamble.

The government accepted the Sixth Pay Commission on August 15 and issued a gazette on August 29 for implementation with retrospective effect from January 1, 2006. DAPA said in a release that banks maintaining the pension account will disburse the pension as well as arrears according to the new rates. The note carried details of the new rates and invited pensioners to call up.

Heading: TASMAC to start campus in London - Indian Express
Content:
State Agriculture Minister Balasaheb Thorat said today that marketing executives trained from the Agriculture College would transform agricultural marketing in the interest of farmers.

Inaugurating a post-graduate degree programme in agricultural business management at the College of Agriculture, he said, "Maharashtra is rich in agricultural produce and proper marketing would enable farmers to get appropriate prices for their produce."

The Master of Business Management (Agriculture) course has been launched by Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth at the century-old College of Agriculture from this academic year.
