Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Six injured in communal clashes during Ganesh immersion in Bharuch - Indian Express
Content:
To nominate or not to nominate was the question which went on in the minds of most student organisations today. Tuesday being the last day of filing nominations for the contesting candidates, confusion reigned in most colleges due to last minute alliances that were formed among different parties. Even as the time for the nomination drew to a close, major parties were still indecisive about the choice of their candidates.

With the aim to emerge victorious in the elections, parties got into last minute brainstorming to form the most fruitful alliance. Till yesterday, INSO party at DAV College, Sector 10, had denied any intentions of coalition with any other party and had also announced their panel. But Tuesday morning saw INSO entering into an alliance with SOPU. According to Juganpreet Singh, president, SOPU, "We have allied with INSO, ABVP and HPSU. While our presidential candidate will be from INSO, a SOPU member will fight for the post of vice-president."

Apart from uncertainty over the contesting candidates, there was also confusion about candidates who had been elected unanimously. While SOPU supporters at the DAV College claimed that their vice-presidential candidate had been elected unopposed, those of PUSU denied it. Said Simranjeet Singh, presidential candidate from PUSU, "SOPU members are spreading wrong information to mislead our voters. As our alliance has been formed with SOI, we have decided to field their member for vice-president. We will not withdraw her candidature."

The scene was no different in other colleges as well where consensus on candidates could not be reached till the filing of the nominations. "Since it was decided last minute that PUSU will join hands with SOI and SDHA, there were changes in the contesting candidates as well," says Ramandeep Singh of PUSU.

Nominations of various candidates were cancelled as well, the main reason being shortage of attendance. "Our nominations for joint secretary and general secretary were cancelled as the candidates were unable meet the attendance criteria," informs Juganpreet. Nomination for general secretary of the PUSU-SOI alliance was also revoked due to attendance shortage, according to Simranjeet.

In Government College, Sector 11, as many as 7 candidates had filed nominations for the post of president, out of which 4 were cancelled due to shortage of attendance.

As always, the girls' colleges wore a peaceful look as most of the candidates were elected unanimously. Independent candidate, Simran Bedi, B A final year student of Government College for Girls, Sector-11, was elected unopposed as the president as the nomination of the opposing candidate, Garima was cancelled.

Candidates for the other posts in GCG-11 too were elected unanimously. While Himani Walia of MCM DAV College was elected unanimously as the president, Chandrakanta of Government College for Girls, Sector 42, also was elected unopposed for the post of general secretary.

Heading: Visarjan passes off peacefully amid tight security in Vadodara - Indian Express
Content:
A dispute between two groups —one Hindu and one Muslim — resulted in stone pelting during the Ganesh visarjan (immersion) procession in Bharuch late on Monday evening. At least six persons were injured in the clash. The police lobbed tear gas shells to disperse the mob.

The incident occurred when a procession from Ghikhudia area in Bharuch was allegedly obstructed by a group of people from Bahar ni Undai area, who complained about loud music being played by the procession, police said. The situation turned ugly when some police officials were attacked and the mob started pelting stones. Apart from lobbing two teargas shells, the police also fired a round in the air to disperse the irate mob.

Inspector A S Shukla of Bharuch police (A division) said, "Around 18 people from both the communities have been arrested following the incident."

The incident occurred near a religious place in Bahar ni Undai area, said Shukla who is investigating the case. "Around four police constables and two civilians from Bharuch were injured. A police motorcycle was also damaged and the mob also tried to snatch away a rifle from a policeman."

Heading: How to get visa power? AMA session demystifies procedure - Indian Express
Content:
City police kept a strict vigil during the Ganesh visarjan ceremony on Tuesday.

Police control room officials told Newsline that the procession at Junigadhi passed off peacefully in the evening.

While security was stepped up well in advance, the Rapid Action Force (RAF) took out a flag march in the sensitive localities of the walled city area.

Over 50,000 people participated in the visarjan.

This year, over 12 police companies have been deployed, including RAF teams and 55 police personnel from outside the city. Army and paramilitary forces have also been pressed into service.

"We are taking extra caution this year to avoid the riot situation of last year," said Pravin Sinha, Joint Commissioner of Police.

"Over a thousand police personnel have been deployed across the city," he added.

The City Police, Wadi police, Panigate police, Navapura police, Rapopura police and Karelibaug police have been put on alert.

The walled city area has been kept under tight security with the passages sealed for the free mobility of the troops to guide the crowd.

Heading: Govt’s Rs 25 cr grant promises to quench thirst of parched Kalali, Bapod - Indian Express
Content:
American Centre expert takes questions from students, clears their doubts

A talk on how to procure US Visa was hosted by the Indo-American Education Society at the Ahmedabad Management Association on Tuesday. It was followed by an interactive session with the audiences to discuss visa-related issues.

The US is one of the major destinations for Indian students. There are 85, 000 Indian students studying in the US.

"Last year, we had 2, 25, 000 applications that recorded a growth of 80 per cent compared to the year preceding it. The American Center at Mumbai has 1,500 visitors everyday," said Christine Dal Bello, Media Officer at the American Center and the speaker of the session.

Dal Bello spoke about the critical factors one should keep in mind before selecting a university in the US. "Every year, a foreign student spends 16,000 to 46, 000 dollars for tuition and living. Therefore, sponsorship is equally vital and the credibility of the sponsors is essential to get a visa," she said.

During the interactive session, students asked Dal Bello about the issues they face while seeking a visa. On a question by a student who had failed to get a visa earlier, Dal Bello gave tips on how to perform at the interview. She said the candidate has to confidently convince the authorities about the purpose of his/her visa and his/her qualifications to obtain it.

In view of the terror threat after 9/11 attacks, the US has taken some additional security steps. A SEVIS (Student and Exchange Visitor Programme) fees is charged and also fingerprinting is carried out to record the backgrounds of the candidates.

The students were also keen to know about the safety situation in the US. To this, Dal Bello said: "The US is a safe place for students. The crime rate in every US city differs. All cities are not the same. A few incidents of crime cannot make a country unsafe. The same is the case with India. We cannot call it unsafe due to rising crimes in some cities."

When asked about the much-discussed debate over Gujaratis not being granted visas, Dal Bello disagreed that any discrimination was being observed against any candidate. She said the visa is a pass to the US and any qualified candidate can obtain it. There is no discrimination against any linguistic group or on regional or geographical origin, she said.

She further said that the fees charged for getting visas is not a profit-making business but is done on a cost recovery basis. The money is used to provide more facilities to the Indian candidates aspiring to go to the US.

Application process
Pay the application fees and the VFS service charge at the designated HDFC Bank. Schedule the appointment and complete the application.

Pay 100 dollars for the SEVIS (Student and Exchange Visitor Programme) fee.

Appear for the interview on the appointed date to give a brief on the family background, the purpose of application and the qualifications. Bring printed appointment letter, visa application form, SEVIS payment receipt, recent photographs, original HDFC Bank fee receipt and the bar code stickers. The VFS counter then couriers the visa.

Heading: Kalol police seize liquor consignment worth Rs 1.9 crore - Indian Express
Content:
Two overhead water tanks to be constructed in both the areas

Two areas of the city, Kalali and Bapod, which have been facing a water crisis since long, can now heave a sigh of relief as the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) has received a grant of Rs 25 crore from the state government for the construction of two overhead water tanks in these areas. The municipal body will receive the grant on Thursday under the state government's Swarnim Gujarat project.

With a population of over 30,000, rural areas in Kalali zone are dependant on community water posts and borewells for their daily water needs. The urban areas in this zone are supplied water from the neighbouring Tandalja area.

Bapod, which lies on the outskirts of the city, also gets its water supply from the neighbouring Nalanda water tank and Ajwa Dam. The low pressure of water supply further compounds their problem.

"These two areas have not been developed much and lie on the outskirts of the city, which is why they have to make do with low pressure water supply," said an official who did not wish to be named.

The new overhead water tanks promise regular water supply in the areas. "One of our major projects was the construction of water tanks in four areas. We will begin with two," said VMC Mayor Balu Shukla.

Each of the water tanks will have a capacity of 18 lakh litres, complete with a feeder line, pump house, water sump and transfer room. Tanks across the zone will be networked to benefit the neighbouring areas also.

Heading: MSU Board of Studies to hold meetings from Sept 15 - Indian Express
Content:
The Kalol police on Monday seized a huge liquor consignment worth Rs 1.9 crore outside Vrundavan Hotel near Kalali village in Vadodara.

The consignment containing 1, 85, 712 bottles of liquor came from Goa and was to be smuggled to Arunachal Pradesh via Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Orissa.

The police also arrested a guard working in the Central Excise Department for his alleged involvement in the racket.

Inspector K B Khant said: "Four trucks were issued permit. While we have seized three of them, we have been informed that the fourth one was diverted from Chhota Udepur. An excise guard from Mumbai has also been taken into custody."

Heading: Court sends Nagori and others to 14-day police remand - Indian Express
Content:
The M S University (MSU) Board of Studies has scheduled its meetings from September 15 onwards. The newly elected body will meet for the first time to discuss issues pertaining to routine examinations, new courses and subjects in the faculties.

The varsity authorities said that such a board is appointed at every faculty level to discuss or design any advancement in the course and then forward it to the Syndicate.

Prof Ramesh Goyal, MSU Vice Chancellor (VC) said, "The Board of Studies is an academic authority comprising of the experts elected at every faculty level who then decide on the academic syllabus and its structure."

AV Gupta, the MSU Registrar, said, "At least two experts are elected at every faculty level for the board. The present body has been elected this year. The elections are held after every three years."

The experts will make their suggestions to the Syndicate members and accordingly a decision regarding any change in the course or design in any subject will be taken, said Gupta. The meetings in each of the faculties will begin in September and continue till November.

Heading: Two killed, 13 injured in road accident - Indian Express
Content:
A city court on Tuesday sent Safdar Nagori, the ideologue of the banned Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI), Ameel Pervez, Shibly Peedical, Karimuddin Nagori and Mohammed Hafiz Hussain to a 14-day police remand.

On Tuesday, the five were produced before the court in connection with the blast in the LG Hospital compound in Maninagar area.

While producing the five before the court of Justice J M Patel, the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) officials said they suspect the five to be connected with some bigger terror outfit and involved in the bomb blasts reported in other states in the past.

To verify these, the DCB said, they might have to be taken to other states as well. They also said that the accused have to be questioned to find out the facts behind the email that was sent to some media organisations just before the serial blasts in Ahmedabad on July 26.

Heading: Cylinder blast in tea shop causes minor fire, but no one injured - Indian Express
Content:
Two persons were killed and 13 others injured in a road accident that occurred near Mahuvad Chowkdy about 12 km from Padra town. Police said the accident took place after a truck driver lost control over the vehicle and rammed a rickshaw coming from the opposite side.

According to officials at the Padra police station, there were more than 10 passengers in the rickshaw when the accident occurred. While two of them died on the spot, the truck driver managed to escape.

"The passengers were on their way to Sakarda village from Boj where they had been to attend a social function. At around 10.30 am, when the rickshaw reached the Mahuvad crossing, the truck collided with a rickshaw resulting in the fatal accident," said an official at Padra police station. The injured were rushed to Sir Sayajirao Gaekwad (SSG) Hospital for treatment.

Heading: DFS finds common link between two crimes -a pistol - Indian Express
Content:
Spark from refrigerator comes in contact with leaking gas

A minor leakage in an LPG cylinder caused an explosion and minor fire in a tea centre at Saroli village in Kapodara, early on Tuesday.

No causalities have been reported, as the shop was closed, police said. The losses were estimated to be around Rs. 15,000.

According to the police, there was a leakage in the gas cylinder, which was kept inside the shop. A minor spark in the shop's refrigerator caused the blast. The blast resulted in a mild fire, which was successfully extinguished later. However, the seating arrangements were damaged in the explosion.

The shop, Jalaram tea centre, situated near Royal Township in Saroli village, is run by one Rajendra Yadav, a resident of Laxminagar society in Puna Kumbharia, police said.

After the blast, several people staying in nearby areas gathered at the spot and informed the police and fire brigade officials about the incident. In addition, Forensic Science officials also rushed to the spot and collected some samples for further investigation.

Kapodara Police Inspector M V Chawda said: "Primary investigations have revealed that there was a minor leakage in the gas cylinder, which could have increased the pressure inside it. A spark in the shop's refrigerator may have caused the blast."

Heading: Uncharitably corrupt: Trust owner arrested for forgery - Indian Express
Content:
The Directorate of Forensic Science, Gandhinagar (DFS) has established the use of a pistol recovered by Mehsana police under the Arms Act in two serious cases of murder and attempt to robbery. The said crimes took place in Bhavnagar district and Ahmedabad.

S P Patriwala, Scientific Officer at the DFS told Newsline: "One Dilip Joshi was arrested by Mehsana police along with two pistols. The guns were then handed over to the DFS for testing with the newly acquired Integrated Ballistics Identification System (IBIS). It was found after the test that one of the pistols was used in two separate serious offences of robbery and murder in Bhavnagar district and Ahmedabad city."

He added: "We had the possession of the spent cartridges and bullets, which were recovered from the crime scenes. When all the data was fed into the IBIS, it showed that the same pistol was used in the two offences."

In February 2008, unidentified persons shot at an employee of a firm in Angadia in an unsuccessful bid to rob him of a bag containing valuables in Bharuch. The man had died during treatment at the VS Hospital in Ahmedabad. Again, in April, 2008 one Premji Dhandhaliya was shot dead by a notorious robber, Shailesh Dhandhaliya, in the Odhav area of Ahmedabad city, after a dispute.

The Local Crime Branch (LCB) of Bhavnagar district has arrested most of the accused in the case, including gang leader Shailesh Dhandhalia. The Odhav police is now planning to bring them to town on a transfer warrant in connection with the murder. Dilip Joshi is a member of the Shailesh Dhandhalia gang.

Investigation Officer, sub-Inspector Suresh Acharya of Bhavnagar LCB, said: "We had cracked the case, but it is the DFS input that has provided vital evidence and a common link between the offences."

Patriwala attributed their success to the IBIS, which has been acquired from Canada at a cost of Rs 4.5 crore. "The system is the only of its kind in the entire country and provides a very important 3D view of the cartridges and the bullets after their use. In fact, this is the first such case where the recovery of a pistol at one place has helped solve cases registered at another place," he added.

Heading: Relief train for Bihar to leave Surat on Sept 16 - Indian Express
Content:
Trivedi accused of siphoning off crores collected from unemployed youths

The Economic Offences Wing of CID (Crime) arrested the proprietor of Vadodara-based Blossom Charitable Trust, Haresh Rasiklal Trivedi, on charges of forgery to the tune of several crores. The CID arrested Trivedi on a transfer warrant from a jail in Navsari.

Trivedi is accused of cheating several unemployed youths across the state by luring them with a permanent job offer under his free computer education scheme for primary schools in Gujarat.

Trivedi, whose racket was spread in 11 districts of Gujarat, is also accused of siphoning off several crores, which he took as donations, from unemployed youths, by promising them a job with a monthly salary of Rs 3,500.

Trivedi's scheme proposed free computer education for students of class 6 to 8 in all district primary schools across the state. As this scheme required trained people, who could impart computer education to schoolchildren, Trivedi started appointing unemployed youths as computer instructors.

Interestingly, Trivedi also had written consents from the respective District Education Officers (DEOs), police said.

Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) MP Raol said: "He took a donation of Rs 52,000 from each candidate. The gullible youths didn't suspect anything, as they were assured a free computer printer and a job with a monthly salary of Rs 3,500. We think that Trivedi must have cheated at least 5,000 such unemployed youths."

Heading: Family seeks High Court help to return to the folds of community - Indian Express
Content:
Relief kit: plates, bowls, two sets of dresses for women, two-dozen candles

A special train carrying relief material for the flood-affected people of Bihar will leave Surat on September 16. Surat Municipal Commissioner S. Aparna and District Collector Dilip Rawal have requested the people, NGOs and other organisations in Surat to lend their full support in this regard.

Many areas in Bihar are still waterlogged. A large number of people have been displaced from their homes and are starving.

A meeting for coordination of the flood relief materials was organised by the South Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SGCCI) on Monday. Aparna, Rawal and representatives of several NGOs participated in the meeting.

It was unanimously decided that the relief package should comprise a kit containing plates, bowls, two dresses for women and two-dozen candles. The cost of a single kit comes to Rs 1,000.

Aparna, Rawal and SGCCI president Chetan Shah requested the NGOs and other organisations to take active part in the collection of the relief kits. They said people interested in donating cash or cheque towards the relief effort should donate the same at the SGCCI.

Shah said: "We have also requested the textile traders and factory owners to participate in the drive and asked them to invite their friends and relatives to help towards providing relief to the flood-hit people of Bihar. The NGOs and other organisations showed a positive response during the meeting."

Heading: Fatal fall: Passport Office employee jumps to death - Indian Express
Content:
Excommunicated, the four brothers find it hard to marry off their children

Sendha Sathwara is now looking for an intervention by the Gujarat High Court to get his children married off after community leaders excommunicated him and his four brothers five years ago.

The Sathwara community elders of Linch village of Mehsana district have decreed that anyone who marries into their family from the community, also risk being excommunicated.

"Every time we approach someone, the question we encounter is whether we have been re-inducted in the society, and we have no answer for that," said Sendha. He said finally he approached the city-based Yogakshem Foundation for help, which has now initiated legal proceedings against the community leaders.

"We had earlier tried to talk to the community elders in a bid to iron out the differences. We also sent a legal notice to them, but with the community leaders unrelenting, we had to file a petition of mandamus at the Gujarat High Court," said Rajendra Shukla from Yogakshem.

Sendha and his brothers were excommunicated in 2003. According to him, the real reason lies in a trivial incidence from 1980, when a young boy from his neighbourhood riding a bicycle had hit his niece. "The incidence was trivial. When my uncle went to protest against the incident, the matter took an ugly turn and both my uncle and I were attacked with swords. The family was influential," said Sendha.

He said matter reached the police station and the accused were put behind bars. "Later when members of the family became the community leaders in 2003, they excommunicated me and my brothers," he added.

Shukla said the case is a clear violation of the existing legal system. "Under the present legal system, the rights of marriage are protected under the Civil Marriage Act, but the constitution of the community forbids anyone from marrying outside the community and threatens them with excommunication," he said. He added that in several cases the constitution of the community violates the Indian Constitution. He said the community constitution not only enforces excommunication as has been in the case of Sendha, but also makes dowry a mandatory requirement for marriages.

"There are clear guidelines on the quantity of gold and silver to be given as dowry and the community members have to abide by the same," Shukla said.

Sendha said the brothers have 10 sons and two daughters among themselves, but cannot find a match. He said his two daughters Manisha and Chetna are in their twenties and they are unable to find grooms for them.

Heading: ‘Coal’lateral damage: Naroda residents - Indian Express
Content:
'Allegations' levelled against him by senior officials reason for committing suicide, says note

A 40-year-old man committed suicide by jumping from his sixth floor official residential-quarter in Navrangpura area on Tuesday morning.

The deceased, Bansi Modiya, from Itawadi village of Vijaynagar taluka of Sabarkantha district, worked as a driver at the Regional Passport Office in Ahmedabad.

According to a note left by Modiya, he committed suicide because of an allegation levelled against him by the passport officials. Gujarat University police have now registered a case of accidental death.

Regional Passport Officer M D Antani said: "Around 10:45 am I received a message that Modiya had jumped from his sixth floor residence next to the Passport Office. He sustained serious head injuries and was rushed to Shrey Hospital. From there he was taken to VS Hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival.

Antani added that Modiya was a very popular employee and a person par excellence. "I do not know why he took such an extreme step," he said.

Gujarat University Inspector B M Rajpara, said: "In his suicide note Modiya has stated that some allegation levelled against him by his colleagues was the reason why he was taking the extreme step. We have registered a case of accidental death and further investigations are on to find out the nature of allegation levelled against him in the office."

Modiya is survived by his wife, parents and four children.

Heading: A campus in northeast is NID director’s unfinished dream - Indian Express
Content:
Emission of coal dust from neighbouring textile processing units go unchecked

Every morning, the eastern suburb of Naroda finds itself enveloped in coal dust, thanks to the industrial units in the vicinity. The local authorities have taken no action against this and the populace is exposed to major health hazards.

Pleas and protests by the public as well as their representatives have failed to move the authorities at various levels: right from the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation to the Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB). The most affected areas include Premnagar, Ambedkarnagar, Shaktinagar and Nadianagar with a population of nearly thirty thousand people.

There are over a dozen textile processing units in the vicinity of Saijpur Bogha ward that use lignite and cause large-scale air pollution. Their chimneys emit loads of coal dust, especially at night.

Local municipal councillors Dr Krishna Thakar, Dr Ganpat Parmar and Deepak Makwana say they have pointed out this problem in the past, but suspect that civic officials are routinely bribed into inaction because of which the problem persists.

Thakar and others have demanded the early closure of the polluting units or changes in their functioning. They have threatened to organise public protests and demonstrations outside the AMC zonal office on Naroda Road if no action is taken within a week.

Thakar, who is a medical practitioner, said that due to the coal dust settling atop houses, people living within a 10 sq km radius are exposed to serious diseases like asthma, tuberculosis, rheumatism and stomach ulcers.

"The factory owners bribe not only the civic officials but even the local politicians regularly and this is the root cause of inaction. Only cosmetic action has been taken all these years," said Thakar. He added: "I don't care about political implications. This problem has to be solved for the sake of the local residents who have been suffering for several years now."

Champaben Jayantibhai Parmar, a housewife who lives in Ambedkarnagar locality, said: "We cannot sleep in the open out of fear of inhaling the coal dust that also blackens mattresses. My neighbours feel breathless at night."

Suresh Nadiya, a government employee living in Shaktinagar says that burning coal particles flying in the air often land up on clothes causing small fires. "We have complained to the health officials in the ward several times, but to no effect," he said. Another local resident, Rekhaben Jayantibhai Mewada, is quite sceptical about the issue. She said, "Some action follow after a lot of complaints, but the effect lasts only for a few days."

Contrary to the councillors' statements, Deputy Municipal Commissioner U C Padia said that no one has complained to him about the matter so far. "If any comes up even now, I will have the matter investigated and solve the problem," he said.

K C Mistry, regional officer at Ahmedabad said: "We have carried out preliminary investigations in the Naroda-Saijpur belt, from where there have been many complaints regarding industrial pollution in the past also. We have taken samples of the pollutants and have sent them to Gandhinagar for a detailed analysis, on the basis of which we will take corrective action."

(With inputs from GauravSharma)

Heading: Thermos bomb hoax sends Khadia police into a tizzy - Indian Express
Content:
Darlie Koshy decides not to go for a third term after 2010

Bringing an end to all speculations, Darlie Koshy has announced that there will be no third consecutive term for him as director of the National Institute of Design (NID), Ahmedabad, after his tenure comes to an end in June 2010.

Having made his decision not to continue for a third term, Koshy is now busy giving shape to many of his plans in the last two years of his term at the premier institute.

"When I took over as the director, NID had a single campus. During my tenure, it set up several campuses. But, I feel uneasy that despite a lot of effort, we have not been able to set up an NID in the northeast. I spoke to the vice-chancellor (VC) of the North-Eastern Hill University (NEHU) at Shillong for starting at least some under-graduate programme at their institute, but unfortunately that thing is also not working out," said Koshy.

He said the establishment of Exchange Programmes through MoUs with 32 best-in-class institutions in the world was one of the major achievements during his tenure.

He said when he joined the institute in 2000 it had around Rs 2 crore as bank balance, which has now reached about Rs 21.8 crore. "The 11th Five-Year Financial Plan for NID will get over in 2012, and I managed to get Rs 139 crore allotted in the budget for NID. This is the first time such a thing has happened for any institute in the country. I am confident that under my guidance and leadership, the financial turnaround of NID has come about, through enhanced government support, institutional funding, strengthening of consultancy activities, outreach project programmes and corporate contributions," he said.

Koshy said he was also happy that during his tenure, NID became the first and the only institute in the country with eight research chairs. He added: "Besides, we also introduced 15 postgraduate programmes, including eight migrated programmes and seven new programmes in emergent areas like New Media, Toy Design & Development, Graphic Design, Software User Interface Design, Information & Digital Design, Transportation and Automobile Design and Strategic Design Management.

He further said that he was happy that the seeds of future leadership had already been planted in the institute. "I can leave it happily. As of now, I just want to shift back to New Delhi and spend some time with my family," Koshy told Newsline.

He also put to rest speculations that he was joining the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT). He said his future plans are not yet final, but he is definitely not joining NIFT.

Hunt for Koshy's successor begins
By mid-September, a committee, which is already been formed by the NID's governing council, will start work on finding a replacement for Darlie Koshy, who is due to retire as the institute's director in June 2010. Koshy said the decision to not continue as the director for a third term was not sudden. "It has come after a lot of thought process. I think I informed the governing council about my future plans at the right time, as it not so easy to get a new man on the job for such a creative and world recognised institute," Koshy added.

Heading: PU turns a blind eye as rules go for a toss - Indian Express
Content:
The recovery of a thermos flask, filled with fire-cracker powder, iron nails and iron-pills, near the residence of Ashok Bhatt, the Speaker of the Gujarat Legislative Assembly, sent the Khadia police into a tizzy on Tuesday morning.

The police have registered the case and further investigations are on. According to the police, the incident occurred around 9 am near Aka Kuva Sheth ni Pol in Khadia area.

One Sidhir Patel spotted the thermos flask on the footpath and immediately informed the Police Control Room. The Khadia police rushed to the spot and informed the officials of the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL).

Khadia Inspector S M Parmar said: "The thermos flask was filled with fire-cracker powder, iron nails and iron pills. It seems someone placed it there just to play prank. But we are taking the issue very seriously and investigations are on to find out the person responsible for this. The material has been sent to the FSL for further investigation."

Out of the total 23 blasts that rocked Ahmedabad city on July 26, two had exploded in the Khadia area.

Heading: Girl power missing from election scene, as usual - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the campaigning drew to a close today, colleges in the city, which would otherwise have been buzzing with activity, largely wore a deserted look. Barring a handful of colleges, the euphoria surrounding the elections was missing in most of them.

Till a few years ago, campaigning often took a feverish pitch as the day of polling approached but with the strict guidelines of the Lyngdoh Committee in place, students feel that the enthusiasm surrounding elections has fizzled out.

With bans on posters, banners and door-to-door campaigning, students seem to be missing the 'once festive look' colleges used to sport during elections. Says Karanbir Singh of SD College, "The Lyngdoh Committee has taken the entire charm out of the elections. It has become a drab and colourless affair now. We can no longer have the kind of fun we used to have during elections."

As the rules insist on curtailing the amount of money spent during elections, students feel this too has adversely affected the campaigning process.

"We can no longer organise parties for potential voters which was a big platform to interact with students. Also we are finding it difficult to woo hostellers as door-to-door campaigning is not allowed," feels Harman Brar of PUSU.

Student leaders feel that with the use of printed manifestos being prohibited, it is difficult to make students aware of the party's agenda. "These rules have limited our activity and because of this, not many students are enthusiastic to be part of the election campaign. Moreover, our agenda too is not known to many students as there are no manifestos to distribute," says Simranjeet Singh, presidential candidate from PUSU. He adds that he plans to improve the infrastructure of the college and the hostel on priority basis but not many students are aware of this.

The students' opinion, though, seems to be divided about the implementation of the Lyngdoh rules. Some students feel that the guidelines have helped streamline the election procedure. Kiranpreet Kaur of Government College, Sector 11, says, "Instances of violence were very common during elections. Parties often resorted to unlawful means to win the elections. All this has been curbed with the coming of the Lyngdoh Committee."

Heading: Parents say a big no to ‘open book’ exam system - Indian Express
Content:
Women in the city may not be lagging behind in any field, but when it comes to student politics, girl power simply vanishes from the scene. While the girls feel they should be given an opportunity to contest, boys think otherwise. They say politics is not the place for girls.

Continuing with the trend, parties have fielded few girl candidates in this year's elections. Though some colleges have girls contesting the elections, boys seem to be the unanimous choice of most parties for the key posts.

The girls, however, don't like the bias.

"We need to come forward and break this trend. People generally act on their pre-conceived notion that girls are 'soft' and that is why they are a misfit in politics," said Simran Bedi, who is contesting for the post of president at the Government College for Girls, Sector 11.

Her views found support from the other girls in the college who said they were not at all misfit in politics. "We can be as successful as boys. The only reason we do not participate actively in the elections is that boys are too insecure to let us be a part of it," says Rajpreet Kaur Lalli, the vice-presidential candidate of the college.

Simran added that if given an opportunity, she would contest elections in the university too. Some girls, however, stay away from politics deliberately. "Keeping in view all the violence surrounding politics, my parents will never allow me to be a part of the elections. Students' polls hardly pass off peacefully and girls do not want to be part of any controversy," said Geetanjali of MCM DAV College.

"We refrain ourselves from elections due to the violence attached to it. Another reason is that there is pressure from the boys who don't want us to participate in the polls," said Garima of DAV College, Sector 10.

The boys, however, are of the view that politics is an odd place for girls as it is a male bastion.

"It has always been the norm that men have contested and won the students' elections. This is proof enough that everybody wants a male leader. Girls should steer clear of this field," said Ravinder Singh of DAV College, Sector 10.

"Politics is not as easy as it sounds. Girls being delicate cannot sustain themselves for long," said Rohit Khanna of Government College, Sector 11.

Heading: Primary teachers choose Ambaji excursion for giving clarion call against state’s apathy - Indian Express
Content:
It will dilute the value of SSC certificate, jeopardise future of the students

The Gujarat Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board's (GSHSEB) decision to announce an 'open book' examination format for the SSC exams, has drawn flak from the parents' association and the Opposition.

The parents association has termed it as a hasty decision, which will render the SSC certificate of little value, even as the teachers' association has welcomed the move.

Chiman Vyas, General Secretary of the Vali Mandal – Gujarat (Parents Association), said: "The decision has been made without taking into confidence the parents, experienced professionals and teachers. Students will face problems while applying for further studies in other states or countries. We are hurt by the GSHSEB chairman's decision. A mere reference by the Chief Minister on September 5 has been immediately put into action by the board. I feel this is just an appeasement of the Chief Minister's sentiments without understanding the repercussions."

The Gujarat Congress has also described the decision as a threat to the future of the students. "This is a conspiracy to help the private schools and colleges in the state. The students will be discouraged from learning anything new or putting in more effort for studies," said Kunwarji Bavadia, acting GPCC president.

Elsewhere, Ramesh Patel, the General Secretary of the Secondary Teachers Association has said that while introducing the concept will be difficult, it will, nevertheless, inspire a competitive spirit among the teachers and the students.

Shyam Sundar, a teacher of the H B Kapadia High School said: "Though the teachers' community has had a mixed reaction to the news, it has largely been welcomed. There are some doubts about whether the system will click or not. Some teachers do believe that the 'open book' system will make examinations relatively easier. A major hurdle in its application will, however, be the fact that the students are not familiar with the system and may take time to adapt to it."

Heading: New age Nazis? Indians are racially pure, claims Vibrant Gujarat website - Indian Express
Content:
Every year during the much-hyped three-day state-wide enrolment drive in primary schools, the Narendra Modi government pronounces its resolve to promote and improve quality education. But the ground reality suggests pathetic conditions of both teachers and students in these schools.

In a bid to highlight these problems, the Gujarat State Primary Teachers' Federation has now called a meeting of senior office-bearers of its district units at the famous pilgrim place of Ambaji in north Gujarat on September 27.

"At the Ambaji meet, we will deliberate on the various problems being faced by the teachers and the students in about 33,000 government-run primary schools across the state. We will also chalk out the agitations we plan to launch against the government, which has remained apathetic to our long-pending demands," said Federation president Dilipsinh Gohil.

Gohil told Newsline on Tuesday that the government was exploiting the primary teachers, mainly the para-teachers, who have been recruited as Vidhya Sahayaks on a monthly ad-hoc remuneration of Rs 2,500.

He said as compared to other states in India, the Vidhya Sahayaks recruited by the Education Department in Gujarat received a very low monthly remuneration. The monthly salary of para teachers in Delhi is as high as Rs 9,500, while in Uttarakhand it is around Rs 6,000, he said.

He said according to a recent report by the All India Primary Teachers' Federation, even poor states like Bihar and Jharkhand were paying Rs 5,000 and Rs 4,500 to their para-teachers.

He said it was also unfair on the part of the state government to fix a five-year tenure of Vidhya Sahayaks – the longest among all the states. "The tenure of para-teachers ranges between only 10 and 12 months in Andhra Praresh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Orissa, Uttarakhand and West Bengal, while it is only 59 days in Meghalaya. It is three years in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh each," he added.

A senior Federation leader said: "Our Vidhya Sahayaks are made to wait for five long years before their services are regularised. Parents spend over Rs one lakh on their ward for undergoing the two-year PTC training after passing HSC Board examination – the eligibility criteria for appointment as a Vidhya Sahayak. But what they receive after appointment is a meagre pay."

Since its launch in 1998, the Gujarat government has recruited about 85,000 Vidhya Sahayaks in primary schools across the state. The services of about 45,000 of them have been regularised in the pay scale of Rs 4,000-6,000, which is also lower compared to states like Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. There are over 40,000 PTC passed candidates who are still waiting to be recruited as Vidhya Sahayaks.

Gohil also criticised the government for not amending the hackneyed rules related to the erratic teacher-student ratio framed way back in 1980.

"In Gujarat, there are about 430 PTC colleges, most of them self-financed, which churn out at least 35,000 teachers every year. Against this, the government recruits only 5,000 of them, leaving behind a backlog of 30,000. This has resulted in mounting unemployment of PTC teachers in the state. If the government amends its age-old teacher-student ratio rules and allot teachers on the basis of classrooms and not on pupils' strength, nearly 20,000 PTC pass-outs could be recruited as Vidhya Sahayaks every year," said a Federation official.

Heading: VMC to switch on streetlights with the click of a mouse - Indian Express
Content:
Reason: Less number of inter-caste marriages, says the website on global investor summit

The website of the Vibrant Gujarat Global Investor Summit 2009 has stunned everyone with its explanation for the boom in the Clinical Research industry in Gujarat—the racial purity of Indians.

The website reads as follows: "Following the outsourcing of Clinical Research work from the West, India is becoming a choice destination for the CRO sector. Ahmedabad's SG Highway will house about a dozen such Clinical Research Organisations. Pharma companies choose India as the destination for the reason that Indians are of a pure race, mainly because of lesser number of inter-caste marriages…."

The CR industry in Gujarat, that registered a turnover of Rs 500 crore last year, is all set to make a giant leap in the coming years. According to the state government-run website, more than infrastructure, labour pool, education system, cost effectiveness and excellent process quality that India and Gujarat offer, it is the pure genetic make up of Indians that is drawing the multinationals to the state.

The statement has come as a shock for the industry experts, even as a site promoter maintained that the content was uploaded only after a series of meetings with the concerned departments. Interestingly, the concerned departments, including the Gujarat State Biotechnology Mission (GSBTM) and the Information Department could not explain the logic.

"There is nothing like a pure race. That was Adolf Hitler's concept," said Akshaykumar Saxena, Director, GSBTM, a nodal agency established in the state for the promotion of biotechnology. About the website content, Saxena said, "It is not on our department's site. I do not know about Vibrant Gujarat."

Dr Bhagirath Patel, Director, Shivrath Centre of Excellence in Clinical Research, said: "The Clinical Research industry is on a boom. But the state government's reason for this has come as a shock. It seems unbelievable."

At present, there are nine CR centres in Ahmedabad including giants like Quintiles Research India Private Limited, Lambda Therapeutic Research Limited, BA Research India Limited, Accutest, Intas Biopharmaceuticals Limited, and Zydus BSV Pharma Private Limited among others who have set up their facilities on the Sarkhej-Gandhinagar highway near Ahmedabad. Reliance Lifescience, Claris Lifesciences, Nicolas Piramal and Veeda Clinical Research are soon to come up.

Of a total 242 trial-projects, more than 80 are being conducted in Ahmedabad. Patel said, at present, the industry generates 15,000 jobs every year, which is expected to swell to 2.5 lakhs by 2012. That would make Gujarat home to nearly 40 per cent of the CR industry.

Bhagyesh Jha, the promotion in-charge of VGGIS and director of the State Information Bureau, expressed ignorance about any such content on the official website. "I will have to check it," he said.

Heading: Hot wheels: Vintage cars from Gondal to elegantly parade in Mumbai - Indian Express
Content:
In a first of its kind in the country, the Vadodara Municipal Corporation has adopted the Global System for Mobile Communication (GSM) Control for the city's streetlights. Once implemented, the officials at the Street Light Department will be in a position to monitor the complete picture on their computer screens rather than go for a personal verification.

The new system is also expected to result in energy saving by up to 52.50 per cent, say VMC officials involved in the project. With the single click of a mouse, the Executive Engineer (Electrical) will be able to switch on and off, streetlights of any given unit (the number of poles fixed in one km of a road) in the city.

Subodh Shah, Executive Engineer, VMC, told Newsline: "The streetlights on Baroda Productivity Road, Vasna Road and in a couple of other areas have already been put under the new project. The estimated cost of the project is Rs 11 crore. Nearly 60 units are linked to this new technology and the project will soon cover the entire city."

He added: "This is the first ever project in India, made indigenously with an aim towards efficient energy consumption. The streetlights will switch onto the energy saving mode in accordance with the timings set by us. The traffic minimises after 11 pm and that is when the system will automatically go into that mode."

According to Shah, the programming of the streetlight timings will also take care of the seasonal variations. This will contribute to about 7 percent saving as compared to conventional operating methods.

To ensure that the streetlights have a long life, luminaries with Ingress Protection will prevent the entry of dust and insect and maintain the optimum luminescence.

The new initiative is also expected to detect the unauthorised pilferage of electricity from the streetlights. "Pilferage occurs more during the festive season, especially from poles in the internal roads," Shah said.

Heading: An adventurous educationist - Indian Express
Content:
Gondal in Rajkot district is famous all over the world for the vintage car collection of its erstwhile rulers. On Monday, Mark Shand of Cartier International (who is also the brother-in-law of Prince Charles) and the organiser of Concours d'Elegance, the famed international exhibition of automobiles, visited Gondal and selected three classic vintage cars from the regal collection for a display at the exhibition.

Concours d'Elegance means "parade of elegance," and is an exhibition of automobile design, craftsmanship and history.

Vintage cars with the Indian royalty and private collectors have never been exhibited on an international stage before. India has also never hosted an edition of the Concours d'Elegance. But this time, the Royal Western India Turf Club in Mumbai will host the Cartier 'Travel With Style' Concours from October 31 to November 2.

In Mumbai, an international jury will select the best vintage car, which will receive an award. The Gondal royal family is known to be automobile aficionados across generations and have retained more than 34 vintage cars in their collection. Some of the cars belong to the early 20th century. All these cars are on display in a garage in one of the palaces in Gondal. Visitors from far and wide come to visit this museum.

The three cars selected today were: Chrysler CI Rumble Seat Coupe, Packard 120 (1935 model), Mercedes 300 SL (1968 model) and Delage D8 (1969 model).

Durgesh Jadeja, a family friend of Maharaja Saheb Jyotindrasinhji and Prince Himanshusinhji: "Surprisingly, all these cars are in working condition, as Mahrajasaheb of Gondal and his son are taking personal care of the cars. The Prince drives all the cars from time to time and several attendants take care of the vehicles regularly."

He added: "On Monday, Mark Shand and Ms. Aline Conquelle, a journalist with the Paris Match magazine, and Manvendra Singh, Maharaja Saheb of Bafwa, Madhya Pradesh, visited the palace and selected the three cars."

Jadeja further said that the collection with the Gondal royal family is different from the ones with other collectors. All the cars here are factory purchased models, which are very costly and original spares are used to keep them running.

Heading: End of conflict: no extension in working hours of High Court - Indian Express
Content:
The first time he sailed into the sky, Mitul Dikshit was in school. "It was my first experience of paragliding and I can still feel the moment," says the director of Dikshant International School.

The adventure sports enthusiast has done it all since then — from paragliding to white-water rafting, to scuba diving in the Andamans.

Once he stepped out of the Scindia School in Gwalior, where he spent his growing up years, Dikshit took home memories and a passion for adventure.

"I studied there from Class III to XII. It was compulsory to participate in adventure sports and I am glad it was that way," says the academician who has made it mandatory in his school in Panchkula.

"I have introduced adventure sports at Dikshant International. We plan occasional trips with the students and it's a much looked-forward-to event on the calendar," says Dikshit who took along a group of boys from the school to the Andamans recently for his scuba diving adventure trip.

"It was the second time that I was doing it and once again it was an out of the world experience," he says.

While he has his hands full during the academic session, such trips, packed with fun and thrills, work as a de-stressing exercise for Dikshit. "I was lucky to be introduced to adventure sports at a young age and which is why I think it's important to start adventure activities during school years," he adds.

"Such activities are seasonal and you have to make sure you work a plan out in time," says Dikshit, who has already zeroed in on his next big thrill.

This time he's going to try skiing, something he hasn't done before. "We are all looking forward to our Auli trip in December," says Dikshit. For someone who spends most of his time behind the desk, it's such "seasonal" breaks that give him a chance to show his "active" side. "It's not just thrilling but a wonderful way to stay fit too," he sums up.

— Jagmeeta Thind Joy

Heading: Annual day celebrated at GMCH-32 - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Justice conveys decision to Bar; assures strict working hours, no undue breaks

The much-debated conflict over the extension in the working hours of the Punjab and Haryana High Court by 45 minutes has finally been resolved.

Keeping in mind the sentiments of the High Court Bar Association, Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur and other judges of the HC unanimously decided on Tuesday that the working hours of the court will remain the same as laid down in the HC rules.

The working hours of the High Court will remain 10 am to 4 pm. The Chief Justice conveyed the decision to Bar President Rupinder S Khosla on Tuesday.

The lunch break, too, will not be reduced by 5 minutes, as suggested by the General House of the Bar Association on Monday.

On Tuesday, the resolution passed by the General House was circulated between all High Court judges during the lunch break, after which it was unanimously decided that there will be no extension of court timings by 45 minutes, as previously decided by the Full Court.

It may be recalled that the HC Bar had strongly opposed the decision. Advocates had expressed their resentment, saying the Full Court had not taken the Bar into confidence before taking such a significant decision.

On the other hand, the judges had held that the decision was implemented according to the directions laid down in the Malimath Committee report.

Reacting to this, the advocates had said the Malimath Committee report also suggested changes in the functioning of courts and judges and that it should be implemented in totality.

The General House, in its resolution, had also demanded that the judges should stop taking long tea breaks, which ranged from 15 to 30 minutes.

"It is a welcome decision and we strongly appreciate and thank the timely action taken by the Chief Justice. It is due to his endeavour that the problem has been resolved and the sentiments of the Bar respected. He has also assured us that the Bar will be consulted whenever a decision is to be taken with regard to its administrative functioning," said Khosla.

He added that the Chief Justice had assured that strict working hours would be observed and no undue breaks of any kind would be taken.

Heading: Smart cards to make vehicle registration easy - Indian Express
Content:
Bhupinder Singh Hooda, Haryana Chief Minister, on Tuesday expressed concern over the rising incidents of female foeticide and urged the medical fraternity to boycott the doctors who indulge in this evil practice.

He was speaking at the annual day celebration of the Government Medical College and Hospital (GMCH), Sector 32, on Tuesday. Hooda said that if social evils like female foeticide were not checked in time, it could lead to serious consequences.

On this occasion, Hooda urged the Director Principal of GMCH, Prof Raj Bahadur to run a refresher course from time to time to update the knowledge of doctors serving in adjoining rural areas.

He also announced that a sum of Rs five lakh be kept at the disposal of the Director Principal of the medical college and hospital, out of the Chief Minister's relief fund, saying that many patients from Haryana visit the hospital for treatment.

He also gave away prizes to outstanding students for their achievements in various fields and also released the college magazine entitled as Glimpse 2008.

Prof Raj Bahadur read out the annual report of the college and hospital and enlisted future plans of the institute. Principal secretary to the chief minister, ML Tayal,

Mayor Pardeep Chhabra, former director principals of the college as well as parents of students were present on the occasion.

Heading: New deadline for PET Scan Centre - Indian Express
Content:
Residents of Panchkula will no longer have to stand in long queues for the registration and licensing of their vehicles. Replicating the system at Chandigarh, citizens can now avail of the smart card system, which will enable the authorities to issue the registration cards on the same day. Also, residents will be able to get their vehicles registered without being physically present.

"Till now, the district was following the system of access-based software, where only one counter was enabled to collect the registration and license fee of vehicles. It was also compulsory that the vehicle owner be physically present. We are now shifting to the sarthi-vahan software. While sarthi stands for the making of the license, vahan stands for the registration of vehicles. The smart cards will now be introduced on the pattern of Chandigarh, the metallic chip of which will contain all details of the vehicle owner," said an official at the SDM office, on condition of anonymity.

"Besides, the system will have inbuilt digital signatures of the SDM, so that the overall work does not suffer in his absence," he said.

The number of counters at E Disha, Sector 1, will also be doubled from six to twelve, to facilitate the smooth functioning.

"Previously, there were only six counters: three for registration and three for license. Cash could only be deposited at one counter, due to which, people had to wait for hours for their turn. Unlike the previous system, the number of counters have been doubled with the collection of cash facility now available at all the twelve counters," he added.

Heading: Former chief architect writes to PM against Admn proposal - Indian Express
Content:
With frequent delays marring most of the ongoing projects at the Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), the PET Scan centre, being set up to determine the exact diagnosis of cancer cells, too, is hanging fire.

While the August deadline has already lapsed, construction work on the project is still on. The authorities have now extended the deadline and claim the project will be complete by October.

Talking to Newsline, A K Gupta, deputy director, administration said: "The work has been going on at a fast pace and we expect that the construction to be over the end of next month. The construction process has taken time, due to which, the starting of the facility has been delayed."

With plans of the PET Scan facility in the pipeline, machinery worth Rs 8 crore is lying unused at the hospital. This under utilisation of resources has come under a sharp scanner, especially when most of the ongoing projects at the institute are way behind schedule. The completion of the Rs 46 crore project, Advanced Cardiac Centre, meanwhile, is behind schedule too.

The authorities, meanwhile, say it will be functional by the end of this year. As in the case earlier, equipment worth several crores is not being put to use here too, as the infrastructure is not ready to house the same.

The project has been pending for several years, with the earlier deadline being 2004.

"The Advanced Cardiac Centre is a big project and work for the same is taking place at a fast pace. We should be able to complete the project by the end of this year," Gupta said.

Heading: HC issues contempt notice to Haryana DIG for filing false affidavit - Indian Express
Content:
Former UT chief architect M N Sharma has written to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh against the Administration's proposal to install Gothic lamp posts on prominent roads of the city. He says it will damage the special character of Chandigarh.

In his letter, Sharma has stated that the distinctive character and the works of Le Corbusier, for which Chandigarh is known, need to be preserved while accommodating changes necessitated with the passage of time.

"The city needs to be protected from the unmindful acts of the Administration that continue to tarnish the fabric of the city," the letter states.

A copy of the letter has also been sent to the Union Minister of State for Finance, Pawan Kumar Bansal, and the Foundation Le Corbusier president Jean Pierre Duport.

The Administration is set to spend around Rs 15 lakh on the project. Gothic lamp posts have already been installed along the road facing Punjab Raj Bhavan. Nearly 40 more are to be installed on the road leading to the Golf Club.

The move has been opposed by architects and planners in the city.

Sharma had recently sent another letter to Jean Pierre Duport asking him to send a team of experts from the Foundation to take a look at the developments across the city.

Heading: Sahara India to cough up Rs 2.5 lakh as compensation - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has issued a contempt notice to Deputy Inspector General of Police (Telecommunications) Haryana, Balbir Singh, for filing a false affidavit.

A few years ago, several Haryana Police constables (drivers) had moved court demanding parity of pay with the drivers employed in civil departments.

The Haryana government's stand was that the constables were offered promotion avenues which were not open to other drivers.

Balbir Singh, the then Superintendent of Police (Telecommunications), had filed an affidavit in court stating that a proposal had been sent for consideration to the Haryana government for promoting driver constables to head constables.

The High Court ruled in favour of the petitioners and directed the Haryana government to grant equal pay to the drivers.

Challenging the order, Haryana government moved the Supreme Court, which set aside the HC order.

The drivers, however, moved court again submitting that the Haryana government had not fulfilled any of its promises. Later, it was discovered that the affidavit was incorrect and no such proposal was sent to the Haryana government for consideration.

Heading: NHAI chief to be present in court on next hearing: HC - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has imposed a fine of Rs 2.5 lakh on Sahara India for deficiency in services and been asked to refund Rs 2,91,7502, which was deposited for the allotment of a land.

Ranvir Singh, a resident of Sector 35, availed of the Sahara City Home Township (Swaran/rajat yojna), floated in 2005. He deposited Rs 2,01,750 for the allotment of a three-bedroom flat, which was pegged at Rs 27.07 lakh. He was told that its construction was to be completed by December 31, 2007.

The company then requested him to deposit Rs 2.7 lakh but the complainant did not deposit the amount as the builders didn't gave a satisfactory reply regarding when the flat would be completed.

He alleged that neither the construction of the flat was completed nor did the company refund his amount.

In its reply, Sahara India asserted that no commitment was given to the complainant regarding the handing over the house by December 31, 2007.

It was pleaded that the complainant failed to deposit the amount of Rs 2.7 lakh, which was 10 per cent of the total price of the accommodation. The allotment of the first phase was done on "first come first served basis", the company said.

The forum found that the company had not produced any document suggesting "how many persons/applicants applied along with the complainant for the allotment of this type of flat and on which dates".

The forum ruled: "They have not produced the list of the applicants along with allotment letters issued by them to suggest if they had applied on the criteria of "first come, first serve" basis". It is evident that the company has been guilty of deficiency in service."

The company has also been directed to pay Rs 10,000 as litigation costs.

Heading: Abdul Hamid’s memory to stand tall - Indian Express
Content:
Taking a strong note of the absence of any representative on behalf of the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) in the ongoing case of completion of National Highway (NH-22), the Punjab and Haryana High Court today directed the NHAI Chairman to be present in the Court on the next date of hearing.

The directions were passed after the court took exception to the fact that nobody was representing the NHAI for the last two hearings.

The directions were passed in the wake of a petition filed by Harish Kumar Puri. The HC had then directed the NHAI to furnish a detailed plan of the Pinjore-Kalka-Parwanoo bypass.

Though the NHAI had submitted a plan, the High Court has directed it to furnish a plan again, as the one submitted earlier was not clear.

The authority had also been directed to remove the encroachments on the Pinjore and Kalka road. It had also been directed to file the progress reports of the various projects being constructed by the same.

Heading: Punjab to have three new jails soon - Indian Express
Content:
Army plans pillar depicting life of Paramvir Chakra awardee

The Army proposes to construct a pillar in the memory of Havildar Abdul Hamid of 4 Grenadiers, who died fighting the enemy in Khem Karan sector on September 9, 1965, during the Indo-Pak war and was awarded the Paramvir Chakra posthumously. The pillar will come up at his memorial in Assal Uttar, near Khem Karan in Tarn Taran.

The Golden Arrow Division organised a two-day event on the occasion of 43rd Assal Uttar Day, which included setting up food stalls, medical camp, sports events, a musical evening and canteen services for ex-servicemen in the memory of Hamid.

The celebrations concluded with a wreath-laying ceremony, a guard of honour, sounding the last post and two minutes' silence at Hamid's resting place.

Brigadier Vinod Kumar of the Golden Arrow Division said Hamid's bravado was unparalleled in history, for which he was awarded the highest gallantry award. "Not many people are aware of the glorious history associated with the place, while only a few people know who Abdul Hamid was," he said.

He added that with this aim in mind, the Army proposes to construct a pillar bearing scenes from the 1965 war and the story of Abdul Hamid. "The scenes would be engraved on metal and the pillar would be placed where it can attract the public," he said.

On September 8 and 9, 1965, Pakistani forces launched a major offensive led by a regiment of Patton tanks on the location held by 4 Grenadiers. Though under intense artillery shelling and tank fire, Abdul Hamid moved from one firing position to another and pulverised three Patton tanks of the

enemy. He was fatally wounded by an enemy shell while aggressively engaging the fourth tank.

Ironically, the place has failed to interest successive governments and all maintenance of the memorial

has been solely the Army's

efforts so far.

Heading: Striking PepsiCo staff block highway for 4 hrs - Indian Express
Content:
Work at Nabha jail on; to start at Kapurthala, Faridkot by this year-end

The problem of overcrowding in jails in Punjab would soon be a thing of the past, as the state plans to add more capacity in its existing jails and set up three new jails at Nabha, Kapurthala and Faridkot.

Sources say a sum of Rs 201 crore has been earmarked for setting up new jails and for adding infrastructure facilities and new barracks in some existing jails in the state.

Of this, while a sum of about Rs 170 crore is required for new jails, the rest of the money would be spent on adding new barracks and infrastructure in the existing jails.

Confirming this, Punjab Minister for Jails and Tourism Hira Singh Gabria told The Indian Express that while work on the Nabha jail is already on and its boundary wall is complete, work on Kapurthala and Faridkot jails would start by the end of this year, when the foundation stones of these jails are laid.

The new jails are expected to be complete within a year and the government is in the process of inviting tenders for allotment of construction work.

The total capacity of jails in the state would rise by 10,000 with new jails contributing a capacity of 6,000.

Sources say Punjab has a total capacity of about 12,000 inmates at present, while there are about 16,000 prisoners and undertrials lodged in jails.

Admitting to the problem of overcrowding, Gabria said though the state has only 5,000 prisoners, there are over 11,000 undertrials lodged in various jails. "We are trying to upgrade facilities inside jails and add more capacity," he said.

The Minister said already Ludhiana and Amritsar Central Jails had been upgraded and new barracks had been added in them. He hoped to add some new features in existing and new jails soon.

Gabria claimed that the new jails would have shops and other facilities, where prisoners and undertrials could buy vegetables, sweets and other amenities.

"The new jails would also have the provision of accommodating family members of prisoners serving long sentences. Such families can stay for three-four days in the jail with their kin lodged inside the jail," the Minister added.

The state has seven central jails at Patiala, Bathinda, Ferozepur, Amritsar, Gurdaspur, Jalandhar and Ludhiana; five district jails at Nabha, Sangrur, Faridkot, Kapurthala, Hoshiarpur; two open-air jails at Nabha and Kapurthala; one women's jail at Ludhiana; one borstal jail at Ludhiana and 10 sub-jails at Fazilka, Moga, Muktsar, Patti, Ropar, Barnala, Malerkotla, Phagwara, Dasuya and Pathankot.

Heading: Cong MLAs slam report indicting Capt - Indian Express
Content:
Buoyed with the support of a number of employee and farmer organisations, the striking employees of PepsiCo's FritoLays unit here today blocked traffic on the busy Sangrur-Patiala highway for over four hours.

Commuters were a harried lot as the striking employees held a rally outside the PepsiCo's unit on the state highway in the morning.

While elaborate arrangements were made by the police to avoid any untoward incident, the dharna passed off peacefully without any violence. Traffic had to be diverted through the villages in the area to avoid inconvenience to commuters.

The striking employees were supported by members of BKU (Ekta), Ugrahan group, BKU (Punjab), Dakonda group, All-India Trade Union Congress, Khet Mazdoor Sabha, Punjab Kisan Sabha, PSEB Employees' Federation, Technical Services' Union and Dehati Mazdoor Sabha, besides some other farmers and employee organisations.

Though talks have been on to resolve the dispute between the management and workers, they have failed as the striking staff has been seeking reinstatement of its terminated president and 12 suspended employees.

The district authorities and Sangrur MP Sukhdev Singh Dhindsa have also joined the negotiations. The unit, meanwhile, has been closed since August 19.

Heading: PM has failed Amritsar, says Sidhu - Indian Express
Content:
Say decisions of the House committee were biased and politically motivated

The controversy over a report indicting former CM Capt Amarinder Singh in the Armritsar land scam refuses to die down. Ahead of the last day of the Assembly session tomorrow, a confrontation between the treasury benches and the opposition Congress MLAs seems inevitable on the issue.

As many as 30 Congress MLAs, in a statement released to the media today, said the policy under which the Congress government exempted the land in Amritsar from acquisition was only a continuation of what was laid down by the previous Akali government led by Parkash Singh Badal.

Reacting to assertions by Harish Rai Dhanda, MLA and chairman of the House committee that prepared the report, Congress MLA Jeet Mohinder Singh said the Akali government had exempted 87 acres in Amritsar much before the Congress exempted 32.5 acres. The MLAs alleged that even though Leader of Opposition Rajinder Kaur Bhattal gave names of the three Congress MLAs to be a part of the committee, they withdrew and expressed dissent after they felt that there was an "ulterior" motive in the committee's functioning, intended to indict the former CM and others regardless of the evidence they gathered.

Jeet Mohinder said, "Harish Dhanda needs to go back to law school. The five Judge SC judgment of 2002 in the Gujarat Assembly case, clearly stating that 'any issue of the previous House cannot be taken up or discussed by the next House' is all that Dhanda needs to study."

The Congress MLAs alleged that the decisions of the committee were biased and politically motivated keeping in mind the standing of Captain Amarinder Singh and the ensuing Lok Sabha elections. The MLAs who signed the statement include O.P. Soni, Darshan Singh Brar, Gurpreet Kangar, Ajaib Singh Bhatti, Sukhpal Singh Khaira, Balbir Singh Sidhu, Makhan Singh, Luv Kumar Goldy, Rana KP Singh, Sukh Sarkaria, Mangat Rai Bansal, Sher Singh Gaggowal, Sadhu Singh Dharamsot, Sunil Jakhar, Ajitinder Singh Moffar, Surjit Singh Dhiman, Ajit Singh Shant, Ishar Singh, JP Jain, Joginder Singh Panjgrain, Harmohinder Singh Pradhan,Sunny Brar, Nirmal Singh, Harchand Kaur, Avtar Singh Brar, Naresh Kataria and Jeetmohinder Singh Sidhu.

Heading: Congress leader killed; Akali held - Indian Express
Content:
AMID invitations from the Punjab Congress for the Prime Minister to contest the ensuing Lok Sabha elections from Amritsar, cricketer-turned-politician Navjot Singh Sidhu, a sitting MP from Amritsar, today said the PM has "failed" to keep the promises he made to the people of Amritsar. Sidhu said the PM was to give a special package of Rs 5,000 crore, a special economic zone and a lot more, but nothing had happened. "The PM is welcome to contest from my constituency, but will have to answer a lot of questions from the people," he said.

In city for the screening of his film, "Mera Pind My Home", Sidhu said, "The popular saying is 'Jack of all trades but master of none'. I have changed this. I am not a jack of all trades; I am the master of all."

Heading: Demand for separate SGPC a conspiracy: Sikh high priests - Indian Express
Content:
In a spillover of the Congress and Akali rivalry during the panch elections, 32-year-old Jagsir Singh, a Congress worker and claimant to the post of sarpanch of this village, was murdered last evening, allegedly by his Akali rivals.

Police said Jagsir Singh was shot dead by his Akali rival, Balraj Singh, and four of his accomplices. Barnala SSP Shive Kumar Gupta said while Balraj Singh has been arrested, the police are looking for the other four.

Meanwhile, Congress workers staged a protest over Jagsir Singh's death and blocked traffic at Court Chowk in Barnala. Congress leaders Kewal Singh Dhillon, Harchand Kaur and Vijeyinder Singla also reached the spot and persuaded the workers to end the protest after the police announced the arrest of Balraj Singh.

Dhillon told ENS, "Jagsir had won the panch elections and had a backing of four panches, while Balraj Singh was backed by just three panches. As per the law, Jagsir should have been appointed sarpanch, but the local administration sidelined him and made Balraj the sarpanch, triggering a rivalry between the two groups." Dhillon added, "There are nearly 1,500 cases where appointment of sarpanch has been done wrongly. I plan to raise this issue tomorrow in the Vidhan Sabha."

It is learnt that Jagsir Singh took the matter to the Punjab and Haryana High Court and was directed by the court to meet the DC on the issue.

Heading: Inebriated man strangles daughter to death - Indian Express
Content:
The Sikh high priests, who met today at Akal Takht for the first time after the appointment of Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Gurbachan Singh, today termed the demand for a separate SGPC in Haryana as a "political conspiracy to weaken Sikh power". The high priests, instead, sought implementation of the Gurdwara Act.

Jathedar Gurbachan Singh said there were no division between the Takhts on the issue of the Nanakshahi Calendar and it could be amended in consultation with experts if any change is required. The meeting was held to discuss issues pertaining to the centenary celebrations of the Sikh holy scriptures.

Addressing mediapersons after the meeting, Giani Gurbachan Singh said the Sikh community should not be swayed by the demand for a separate SGPC for Haryana.

"This demand is politically motivated and aimed at weakening the Sikh community," he said. He added that parties having any kind of grudge related to gurdwara management could consult the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee for redressal of their complaints.

Meanwhile, SGPC secretary Dilmegh Singh has been appointed in charge of the centenary celebrations in place of Harbeant Singh, secretary, who is abroad at the moment, while Manjit Singh has been appointed PA to SGPC chief Avtar Singh Makkar in place of Angrez Singh, who is now assistant secretary of the Dharam Prachar Committee.

The meeting was attended by Giani Balwant Singh Nandgarh of Takht Damdama Sahib, Giani Tarlochan Singh of Takht Kesgarh Sahib and two granthis — Jaswinder Singh and Mall Singh.

Heading: EC orders transfer of DSP, SHO in Moga - Indian Express
Content:
A Dalit man, under the influence of liquor, strangled his 17-year-old daughter to death on Monday night when she tried to intervene in a quarrel between her parents. It was alleged that the deceased, Gurpreet, was raped by her father, Salinderpal, alias Shinda, but this could not be established as the body was cremated in a hurry before the police could reach the spot.

Shinda has been arrested under Sections 302 and 201 of the IPC .

The episode took place in Daduwal Colony of Daduwal village in Jalandhar district. "Last night Shinda was beating me when Gurpreet tried to save me. Shinda then started beating Gurpreet and strangled her," said Shakuntala, Shinda's wife.

"When the girl's body was bathed by the village women, it was clear that she had been raped," said Veena, a neighbour. It is learnt that Shinda, an alcoholic, had tried to kill his another daughter about two years back, but the girl had a narrow escape. At that time, Shinda had pledged not to indulge in any such act in future. Shinda is unemployed and has seven children.

Heading: Dropouts find their way back to school - Indian Express
Content:
Acting on an inquiry report submitted by the SSP, Ferozepur, the state Election Commission had ordered the transfer of DSP (City), Moga, Balwinder Singh Sandhu and SHO (City) Satnam Singh. While Sandhu has been sent to PAP, Jalandhar, SHO Satnam Singh has been transferred to Ferozepur. The Election Commission has also asked Inspector Pushpinder Singh, posted at Nihalsinghwala, not to interfere in the Moga MC election process. Moga MC goes to the polls on September 14.
