Moga SSP Ashok Baath confirmed the transfers, which were done after complaints against these officials were lodged by Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee president Mohinder Singh Kaypee and MLA Joginderpal Jain. The EC has sought a report on the complaint from Ferozepur SSP Dinesh Partap Singh. Reacting to the transfers, Jain said, "This is a job half done. We also SSP Ashok Baath to be transferred as he and his staff openly admit allegiance to SAD president Sukhbir Badal."

Heading: New Pradesh Congress Committee appeases all - Indian Express
Content:
Kamlesh is 16 and has never been to a school. She comes from a remote village in Sirmour district and has been working as a domestic help. Till recently she feared the very concept of going to school. But this was before she went to a village summer camp- a unique brain child of Pratham, an NGO working in the field of elementary education. As the month long summer school concluded, it changed her perception. "Abhi bhi der nahin hui ," ( Its not too late yet) she says. Kamlesh is just one of the success stories from several such summer camps that were organised in remote villages of the state by Pratham under its "Read India" campaign. As several of these month-long camps concluded, the results were encouraging. "The number of children in the state, who can read, has increased now," says Vivek Sharma, head of the North India initiatives of Pratham.

The Indian Express visited some of these summer camps in villages of Sirmour. Enthusiasm among the children at Jogiban village near Nahan could be seen as despite heavy rains, they made their way to attend the "special tuition", as many called it. Books and blackboards made way for colourful learning kits, games, rhymes and play-grounds. This pedagogic approach helped to attract and retain students like Kamlesh. "On the first day I saw the kids playing interesting games and the teacher didi explained to me that the kids are learning to read. This made me join the classes," she says.

"The children are engrossed in special games that help them identify numbers, alphabets and words as well as the story-telling and paragraph reading sessions," said Nisha, a shiksha sarthi at one such camp in Bankala.

The comparison of pre and post summer camp results of 1.6 lakh students in 8,874 villages, show an improvement of 15 per cent in overall reading capability of children. Learning capability in terms of numbers and letters has seen an improvement of 13 per cent.

In Bakhras block of Sirmour where number of school dropouts is the highest, 65 kids attended these camps and found a reason to go back to school. Devinder Sharma, coordinator of the summer camps in Bakhras, says, "I personally talked to 20 of such dropouts and their families. They wanted the shiksha saarthis to continue to teach them."

Heading: Pre-feasibility survey for Leh rail line project gets NOC - Indian Express
Content:
The new Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) reconstituted after Kaul Singh Thakur took over as state PCC president has turned out to be an "appease all" body, with former chief minister Virbhadra Singh's supporters in majority.

The PCC has given fairly good representation to women and sitting MLAs, while ex-MLAs and former ministers have also been adjusted to balance the 88 names cleared by the All India Congress Committee (AICC).

The list of eight vice presidents includes G.R. Musafir, Ram Lal Thakur, Sujan Singh Pathania, A.N. Vidyarthi, Anil Sharma, Kunjana Singh, Harbhajan Singh Bhajji and Anita Verma.

General Secretary of All Indian Congress Committee (AICC), Janardan Dwivedi, released the list of the reconstituted body that takes care of all districts, groups, region and cast considerations.

Name of formertransport minister G.S. Bali failed to figure in any of the five categories into which the body is divided though his supporters have got representation of nearly seven per cent among the total posts of office bearers of PCC.

General secretariesinclude Asha Kumari, Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, Mukesh Agnihotri, Ajay Mahajan, Sudhir Sharma, Kuldeep Singh Rathaur, Satya Prakash Thakur and B.D. Chaudhary.

The list of 26 secretaries is dotted with some important names such as Dr Kailash Prashar, Manhari Devi, MPS Rana, ex-MLA Rohit Thakur, MLA Yog Raj, Sohan Lal, Adarsh Sood, Aishwarya Katoch. Ram Vijay Singh Negi has been appointed as the treasurer.

Senior leaders including Virbhadra Singh, Vidya Stokes, Sat Mahajan, Anand Sharma, Viplove Thakur, Sukh Ram, Raj Kishan Gaur and Chadresh Kumari have been made members of the executive, besides 44 others.

Of these nearly 22 are ex-MLAs. All MPs, MLAs and heads of the frontalrganisations are ex-officio members of the executive. Earlier there was speculation on inclusion of MLAs but the reconstituted PCC has included the eight MLAs.

Heading: FIR against retired tourism official; senior IAS officer also named - Indian Express
Content:
The Trans-Himalayan Railway Private Limited has been issued a no objection certificate(NOC) by the Himachal Pradesh government to undertake the groundwork for conducting pre-feasibility survey (PFR) of the Pathankot-Leh railway project.

As per the terms and conditions of the agreement, the PFR for the Rs 65,000 crore-Leh rail line project is expected to be completed within next three months. The company would study the feasibility of the rail line project for a broad-gauge two-way electrified track and the proposed route would be finalised in the PFR.

Trans-Himalayan Railway is a promoter company of ICC Holdings, a private infrastructure and engineering company. The rail line to Leh would be constructed from Jogindernagar, passing through Patlikuhl, Manali and Keylong, in Lahaul and Spiti and Pangi.

Since the state had expressed the desire to link the proposed Bhanupalli-Bilaspur railway section with the Leh rail line, the company has also offered to construct the rail link connecting Jogindernagar with Bilaspur, that would further complete the circuit till Bhanupalli in Una. Managing Director of Trans-Himalayan Railway, Rakesh Saran Mathur, said the NOC was signed by secretary, Planning, Himachal Pradesh government and was handed over to him in presence of Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal.

"Before the difficult and tribal areas are cut-off due to snowfall in November, we intend to complete the ground work for collection of geographical data and reports such as soil and terrain suitability, prospective course of the rail line and technological support required for theproject," said Mathur.

Heading: N-deal fame Karnal MP demands inquiry by HC judge - Indian Express
Content:
An FIR has been registered against a retired general manager of Himachal Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation (HPTDC), Ramesh Kapoor, who had allegedly tampered his service records to show his age four years less than the actual.

The FIR registered at Sadar police station in Shimla also includes the name of a senior IAS officer, Tarun Shridhar, who was the managing director of HPTDC when Kapoor was working under him.

The police have booked Kapoor for forgery and hence causing loss of lakhs of rupees to the government in terms of salary, emoluments and post retirements benefits. According to sources, the police is investigating the role of Shridhar, for not taking any action in the case.

The principal secretary of Tourism had directed realisation of excess salary of two years, amounting to nearly Rs 8 lakh, paid to Kapoor and in case he failed to do so and did not submit the proof of his date of birth, a case be registered against him within a month.

The action in the case has been taken nearly two and half years after allegations were raised by an employee, which was followed by preliminary inquiries into the incident by three agencies including CID, Vigilance Bureau and finally the police, but no case was registered.

According to preliminary inquiry of the police, Kapoor's date of birth in his school records was February 2, 1944 which was overwritten by year 1948 in his service records. The officials in-charge of keeping the service book of the employees in HPTDC would be also be questioned.

Heading: RTI: NGO’s efforts pay, officers asked to pay up - Indian Express
Content:
The Lok Sabha MP from Karnal, Arvind Sharma, who was recently in the news for his flip-flop during the trust vote in the Lok Sabha, has once again raised a finger against the Bhupinder Singh Hooda-led Congress government in Haryana.

Talking to the media after visiting the injured at a hospital here today, he alleged that there was no proper arrangement of medical facilities for the guest teachers injured in police firing on September 7.

He demanded an inquiry by a High Court judge, saying that it was the only way the truth behind the incident could be found.

Seeking registration of an FIR, Sharma said the police personnel involved in the firing must be booked.

Sharma further said there was no way in which one could differentiate the functioning of the present Congress government from that of the previous INLD government, "which was thrown out of power in the state by people because of such excesses."

Heading: Religious leaders fume as Governor refuses to meet them - Indian Express
Content:
The Suprabhat Seva Samiti had asked for information which the PIO failed to provide, resulting in a fine of Rs 40,000 for 3 BDO-cum-PIOs

One man's tireless efforts have resulted in getting justice for an entire community in a Sonepat village recently under the Right to Information (RTI) Act.

As a result, three Block Development Officers (BDOs)-cum-Public Information Officers (PIOs) have been fined Rs 40,000 each by the RTI Commissioner, Haryana, for not providing proper information asked for under the RTI, in a clear violation of the provisions of the act.

Refusing to bow down to the tremendous pressure from the government officials "who tried many tricks in the book to browbeat and dissuade me not to pursue the case," Ved Prakash, a social activist from Sonepat, has set an example for others to follow.

Ved Prakash, head of the NGO Suprabhat Seva Samiti of Fazilpur, Sonepat, had to struggle for one and a half years to make the BDOs see reason. "They even put false and baseless charges against me," said Ved Prakash.

Ved Prakash said one and a half years ago, he had filed an application to the BDO, Sonepat, who is the PIO, Department of Development and Panchayat, to get information about the developmental activities in the Fazilpur gram panchyat. The information related to construction of village lanes and the expenses incurred on them. Information regarding encroachment of some village lanes, number of water taps, incomplete water schemes had also been sought.

When Ved Prakash did not receive any information within the stipulated period of 30 days, he sent a complaint to the Chief Information Commissioner, Haryana, following which, the NGO and the BDO received notices to appear for hearing in Chandigarh. The notice reportedly angered the BDO-cum-PIO who allegedly began harassing Ved Prakash by levelling false charges of misuse of panchayat funds against him. The BDO even summoned Ved Prakash to his office to explain his position.

"The idea was to browbeat our NGO into submission so that I withdraw the complaint," said Ved Prakash.

Interestingly, just two days before the hearing by the CIC in the case, the Fazilpur panchayat secretary visited Ved Prakash's house to offer 74 pages containing a part of the information and asked for Rs 940.

Later, during the hearing, CIC G Madhavan strongly objected to the demand of money for information, since under the RTI Act, information is to be provided free of cost after the expiry of the 30-day-period .The CIC also rebuked the officer for putting false charges against Ved Prakash and asked him to pay for the information.

But the saga lingered on. "In between, three BDOs took charge, but none failed to provide the relevant complete information. They also failed to appear before the CIC despite notices sent to them in this regard," Said Ved Prakash.

Taking note of defiance of the RTI Act, State Information Commissioner M R Ranga recently imposed a fine of Rs 40,000 on the three BDOs which has to be paid by them from their salaries.

"Ved Prakash's courage is an example of what can be achieved under the RTI Act," said Krishna Tyagi, Haryana State Coordinator of PRIA, a national-level NGO, that provide support to Ved Prakash.

Heading: Health dept to fill 5,943 posts - Indian Express
Content:
A group of religious leaders, who had come from all over the state to hand over a memorandum to Haryana Governor Dr A R Kidwai, left in disgust today when they were refused audience. The Governor did not meet them despite the fact that the religious leaders had been given an appointment by the Governor's office for today evening at 4 pm.

The memorandum related to the protest against the recent brutal murder of Swami Laxmananad Saraswati by some miscreants at Orissa and the continuous pollution of the river Ganges.

The religious leaders, who gathered outside the gate of Haryana Raj Bhawan before the scheduled time of the appointment, were not allowed inside despite waiting for two hours. By 6 pm, the ADC of the Governor informed them that they could hand over the memorandum to him as Dr Kidwai would not be able to meet them.

Feeling humiliated, the religious leaders refused to hand over the memorandum and left. Talking to The Indian Express, Swami Ram Sunder Sathi from Hindu Kendriya Marg Darshan Mandal from Kaithal said it was a great insult of the Hindu religious leader by the Governor. "In India, the guest is considered as God, but we don't know why the Governor refused to see us for even a few minutes," he said.

VHP leader Vijay Bhardwaj said the Governor's behaviour was "strange".

Heading: Girl on the move - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana Government has decided to fill up 5943 posts of various ranks in the Health Department. Health Minister Kartar Devi said that out of these, 2306 would be filled up by restoration of the posts abolished by the previous government.

She said that it has been decided to fill up 637 additional posts, which include 359 posts of medical officers, six posts of senior dental surgeons, 30 of dental surgeons, 60 pharmacists, 66 radiographers, 51 ECG technicians and 65 senior medical officers.

Apart from this, 3000 posts of nurses would also be filled up in a phased manner. The action is a part of the process to reorganise the Health Department according to the requirements of the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM).

Heading: Behind the Scene - Indian Express
Content: In the filmi grading system, the girl's moved from Grade B to Grade A. After starting out with the new Jani Dushman and the very sidey Ladies Tailor, actress Prity Bhutani is now looking forward to a kitty of hot stuff including Khalbali Hai Khalbali, Vikalp, and Ajay Devgan starrer Golmaal Hai -2 and Ek - The Power of One. In a free wheelin' conversation, Prity shares how she never imagined joining films. "I come from a very conservative Sikh family, and the thought of being an actress never crossed my mind," she chose commerce and limited her potential to college dramas. "Somehow theatre continued post college too and it was after I started getting modelling offers that the road to Bollywood opened." It was two short films with Tanuja Chandra, who is quite a hard task master, ad films, kathak lessons from Sitara Devi's daughter, Jayanti Mala, till she got a break opposite Sharad Kapoor in Jani Dushman. "Well, work just rolled in, there was Ladies Tailor, Tamil and Kannad projects, and now, there's Ek - The Power of One, produced by K.Sera and Sangeet Sivan, Ajay Chandok's Khalbali Hai Khalbali, a dance number in Vikalp..." she reels sticking to the glitz and glamour.

Heading: House of Fashion - Indian Express
Content:
Elections as per the Lyngdoh Committee involve limited money and big strategies

Till the Lyngdoh Committee put a check on the Panjab University (PU) elections, September was considered as the loud, extravagant and festive month of PU. Now, it's different — subdued, peaceful and low on controversies. But what it is high on instead are the managerial skills. This, particularly when they have to do all the planning, marketing and implementation in a mere Rs 5,000 and in limited ways. "One tent and the fluorescent sheets and the money is gone," says Pardeep Singh, party president of SOI.

The road-shows that were considered as a show-of-strength too have seen a set back this session. "The extra expenditure is unexplainable, so we have to plan the minimalistic rallies in a fashion that they get maximum viewers," Pardeep tells us that Sarabjit Singh, the party president, has formed a full-fledged planning team and has Amit Brar and her group of girls making the posters.

Tejpal Cheema, PUSU party president, holds meetings with party members Parminder Jaswal, Gagandeep Kaur, Navjot Sahni, among others every evening to decide the classes they have to visit the next day. "With n-number of restrictions on campaigning, including ban on printing material, that's the only way to reach the students," he tells us that with him asked to step down from the post of contesting president for want of attendance, promoting the new president needs new strategies. For SOPU the plans were made and conveyed at the start of the campaign. "A round of classes to be made in the morning with academic related issues and of the hostels with problems which concern them," chips in Saurabh Gupta, spokesperson of SOPU. While students tell us that what still rules is unofficial hostel parties and free movie tickets, "The extent of it cannot be made public," chirps a PU hosteller.

But it's INSO that takes the round of applause for sending four groups to cover all the departments in two days. "With this new way of elections, we the contenders and the voters, both have to do a little thinking. While we have to strategize, the voters have to hear us out to decide on their own," says Vikas Rathee of INSO, who has seen elections progress in the last four years, "from pomp and show to something more intelligent." Here's to a fresh start.

Heading: Foot loose - Indian Express
Content:
Atul & Ramesh Kapoor tell us their success story

What makes a businessman successful is his ability to visualize the demand of the future and need of today. Something Ramesh Kapoor did perfectly well 24 years back. "There were no good garment stores and that's the reason I opened Trendsetter," says Ramesh, as he tells us that Sector 17 seemed like an obvious choice then, as he saw it as a booming market. "A few initial hitches, some challenges and the store was done," he tells as he takes us around and introduces us to his next venture — Catwalk, one which his son Atul Kapoor is managing. Having joined his father in 1996 after his BCom, "I chose my business over MBA because that's what I like. Besides, I wanted to build my future with it," Atul tells us that ever since there has been no looking back. "Catwalk, Sector 17, came up in 1998 and Catwalk, Manimajra, in 2006," he recalls the time when their expansion plans materialized.

From bridging the gap in demand and supply of quality garments to that of sourcing the present trends, Kapoors moved on. "While, earlier we only sourced finished products from companies, now we have started designing our own knitwear," Atul tells us that for the purpose they either take a factory on lease or outsource it, while the designing is done by them and an NIFD pass out designer. As for the fabrics and yarns, they travel for 10 days in a month to procure them and get the best possible deals.

"We believe in getting and giving value for money and work for it," Atul says that their variety in women and kids wear is unmatched. "We will also soon come up with the men's section where we will have garments of Louis Phillips, Van Heusen, Levi's and Wills among others. Also, we will soon start the manufacturing of trendy ladies coats, for they too are not available in the city," this time round Atul visualizes the future course...

Heading: Grand Finale - Indian Express
Content:
Get Connected
Taking their services a notch higher, Virgin Mobile, announced that customers will now be able to purchase Virgin Mobile branded products and services online by visiting its website, www.virginmobile.in. Apart from the convenience of buying from home, customers will be rewarded with additional talk time, extra messages as well as other freebies. For example, the Bak Bak offer will provide online customers Rs. 100 worth of free talktime, 500 free SMSs, lifetime validity and a free prepaid connection on purchase of every handset. M. A. Madhusudan, Chief Executive Officer, Virgin Mobile India, said, "With 44 per cent of the total internet population in India falling within the age group of 19-24 years, this medium has become an integral part of youth's lifestyle. It is therefore logical for us to extend our presence on the virtual space and offer our connection at the click of a button."

Rising Sun

Inaugurated by Chief Minister of Himachal, Prem Kumar Dhumal, the hill top retreat is situated 60 km from Shimla, and spreads over a 15 acre estate. "Our motto is to make Suryavilas a niche destination and put it on the global tourism map," says Gaytri Bajaj, Director, Suryavilas, Resort and Spa.

The newly launched resort is a five-star property designed to co-exist in perfect harmony with the natural landscape. It houses 57 luxurious bedrooms and suites with outdoor jacuzzi and barbecue and 24 hour 'in room' dining! There's a multi-cuisine restaurant with a fine wine list. "It's a perfect place to unwind, refresh and re-charge," adds Gaytri as she informs the services of internationally renowned spa company "Thalgo" on board.

Rock da Party
Hip hop is what ruled the freshers party of Flying Cats held at Vodoo on Tuesday, whether it was the music or the attire. Accessorized with chunky chains, colourful caps and cool bandanas, the students also participated in Mr and Ms Flying Cats and Best Dressed Man and Best Dressed Lady contest. Judged by Priyanka Khosla, Managing Director, Flying Cats, and Tishaa Khosla, a debutant author, Ms. Flying Cats award was given to Sakoon Dhaliwal, Mr Flying Cats to Ankit Anand, Best Dressed Girl to Anmol Sandhu, Best Dressed Man to Amit Kumar and Best Dancing Couple to Amit and Babita.

Heading: Eye on MC polls: Sukhbir assures water supply, sewage facilities - Indian Express
Content:
Get your gyan, ask your queries

Getting Dali and Dada mixed up is a criminal mistake. However, there was a phase when many Surrealists crossed over to become Dadaists. Salvadore Dali was a painter who remained committed to the aesthetics of beauty and his fevered imagination continued to conjure up images that were often considered the ravings of a mad man.

He did, however, admit to being influenced by the Dadaist movement, but many aesthetes are of the opening that Dali's work was too painterly to be anti-establishment. Dali was born in Catalonia, Spain, in 1904. His early life was marked by two tragic events, the loss of his identical twin brother and later his mother, whom he 'worshipped'.

His talents surfaced early. Dali's father, Salvadore Dali Cusi, held an exhibition of his charcoal drawings in 1916 and subsequent trips to Paris were instrumental in forming his decision to become an artist. Always an eccentric, Dali stood out with his long sideburns and hair and his get-up as an English dandy. Later, his handlebar moustache became a trademark.

Early influences of Cubism marked Dali's student life but he went on to evolve a style that was entirely his own. Where clocks melted (The Persistence of Time), trees morphed into elephants and the demarcation of dream and reality melted into one. The Surrealists were heavily influenced by Freudian theory and one of Dali's paintings The Enigma of William Tell is dedicated to the Oedipus complex. Dali was also influenced by Luis Bunuel who he later made a path-breaking experimental film with.

The hallmark of Dali was not just his eccentricities but his vision combined with impeccable skill. His command over the brush could conjure up images that were hyper-real and yet he would employ distortions and fantasy landscapes to transform reality. Many Indian artists till date still pay tribute to Dali by quoting his images and in some instances imitating his eccentricities.

Demystify art, e-mail georgina.maddox@expressindia.com

Heading: Punjabi University goes eco-friendly - Indian Express
Content:
Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Badal made an appeal to the residents of Kharar to elect members of his party to the Kharar Municipal Council (MC). Civic polls are slated for September 14.

Addressing a huge gathering at the Ramlila Ground on Tuesday, Sukhbir assured the residents to bring the entire area under water supply and sewerage facilities. "Our topmost priority will be to provide clean and safe potable water to each and every household and provide them with sewerage facility," said Sukhbir.

Listing the policies and programmes of the present regime, Badal said the SAD-BJP combine had taken Punjab to such heights that were not even dreamt of during the Congress regime. "We are bound to make Punjab a power surplus state with the provision of a 24-hour power supply for all, besides selling out surplus power to other states," he said.

He appealed to the residents to vote for the "Rising Sun" for an all-round development of the town.

"We are investing Rs 2,000 crore on the development of infrastructure of the Greater Mohali Area," he said.

Other leaders who addressed the gathering were Punjab Tourism Minister Hira Singh Gabria, Chief Parliamentary Secretary (Revenue) Sukhpal Singh Nannu, MLAs Ujjagar Singh Badali (Morinda), Charanjit Singh (Chamkaur Sahib) and BJP Mohali District president Khushwant Rai Geega.

Tight security arrangement virtually turned the area into a khaki garrison. With all roads leading to the Ramlila Ground sealed hours before Sukhbir's arrival and extensive frisking of the visitors, the public complained of harassment.

Heading: SC-certificate rule awaits nod from Centre: Buta Singh - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjabi University Environment Society (PUES) in Patiala took out a march on Tuesday to create awareness about the environment in the campus.

More than 500 teachers, students, staff members, NSS volunteers, children, deans of various faculties and heads of departments, led by Vice-Chancellor Dr Jaspal Singh, took part in the procession.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr Jaspal Singh said: "Given the level of pollution, we are heading towards a catastrophe. We need to be proactive and extra vigilant to save our planet from further degradation. The campus will be smoke and polythene free in the next two months. Additional dustbins are being placed at vantage points for dumping the polythene carry bags being used by campus residents to avoid their recycling. More than 2,500 trees have already been planted."

Dr Jagbir Singh, convener of the PUES, said all shopkeepers on the campus had been persuaded not to use polybags.

They will be supplied with environment-friendly alternatives for packing purposes. Special dumping pits are also being created to dispose other waste material which could be used as manure.

Heading: Abandoned 10-month-old finds a home - Indian Express
Content:
Buta Singh, Chairman of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, has in principle agreed to implement the SC-Certificate rule in Chandigarh. Addressing mediapersons here on Tuesday, he said he would get the rule passed in the Cabinet to bring relief to those belonging to the reserved categories.

He added that the Administration had also agreed to the rule, but was awaiting a nod from the Ministry of Home Affairs. "All those who possessed an SC/ST certificate when Chandigarh was made a union territory will be acknowledged by the Administration after this is passed in the Cabinet. As the UT Administration is governed by the Ministry of Home Affairs, it is waiting for an official direction," he said.

"We have held a series of meetings and even discussed the matter in the inter-ministerial meetings. We have also read the Supreme Court rulings. The matter was put forward before the Ministry of Social Justice, which has now referred it to the Law Ministry. In case the Law Ministry takes long to vet the rule, we will take it to the Cabinet and get it approved by the Prime Minister," he said.

He also announced that the Commission would try to get the 85th Amendment implemented in the UT. "We are working on the modalities and shall definitely get the 85th Amendment implemented in UT too, which would enable SC/ST employees to get better promotion avenues, at par with the general category candidates," he said.

The amendment, if implemented, will pave the way for faster promotions of those belonging to the scheduled castes and tribes. This will also facilitate a separate promotion roster for the SC/ST employees, who will be segregated from those belonging to the general category.

Heading: Parties protest ‘insufficient’ time for campaigning - Indian Express
Content:
After spending around 10 months at an orphanage, an abandoned baby girl found a permanent home on Tuesday.

An issueless couple from Kharar adopted her from the Universal Disabled Caretakers Social Welfare Society, a non-government organisation, at Padiala village near Kharar.

She was just a day-old when Navjeewan, the name given to her at the Society, was dropped in a cradle placed outside the NGO's centre on the busy Kharar-Ropar stretch of the National Highway-21 on November 2, 2007.

The NGO has long been taking care of abandoned children.

Society president Shamsher Singh and spokesperson Rajinder Kaur said a couple (who did not wanted to be named) had approached them with a request to adopt the abandoned girl.

"After completing all the requisite legal formalities and verifying the antecedents of the couple, we handed over the baby to them," said a member of the Society.

In its fight against female foeticide, the Society has appealed to the public at large not to kill the unborn girl child. It also appealed to people that instead of dumping the unwanted newborns at unsafe places, they should place them at the Society's cradle. The Society said it was open to adopting any child without any query.

Heading: Don’t the poor have a right to clean environment, asks NCSC chief - Indian Express
Content:
It was a chaotic day for different student bodies that remained busy filing nominations and clarifying the errors in them.

The final panels will be announced after the cancellation and withdrawal procedures are over.

As the deadline for campaigning, as announced by the university earlier, ended on Tuesday, the campus saw frayed tempers. Protesting against the "insufficient" time given to them for canvassing, the students said the university was confused on the matter. According to the forms issued by PU, they said, campaigning was to end a day before the elections, while the Lyngdoh Committee, too, had said campaigning had to end 48 hours before the elections.

Talking to Newsline, SOPU member Barinder Dhillon said: "None of us is clear about the last date for campaigning. We do not know what the authorities are up to."

The candidates of other contesting parties, too, think the time given to them for campaigning was too less. The tents of different parties were removed by the evening, as different parties together approached the Dean, Students' Welfare, to seek more time.

Till late evening, the DSW had not responded to the representations. Students said they would protest if they were not given more time to campaign for the polls

As far as the panels are concerned, nothing seemed in order, with different parties remaining indecisive till late. With the Lyngdoh Committee recommendations barring students with criminal cases registered against them from contesting the polls, the parties found it difficult to select candidates. As a result, they remained busy forming alliances.

Three days before the D-Day, the National Students' Union of India (NSUI) sprang the biggest surprise by withdrawing its alliance with the Students' Organisation of Panjab University (SOPU) and tying up with the Panjab University Students' Union (PUSU). The u-turn evoked criticism, as the move made the NSUI lose trust among the voters.

Later in the day, the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) declared its alliance with SOPU. It already had a tie-up with the Haryana Students' Association (HSA).

The parties that will now contest the students' elections are SOPU-HSA-ABVP, PUSU-NSUI and INSO-SOI.

NSUI u-turn invites criticism

The u-turn taken by the NSUI has come as a surprise. To add to the chaos, party members are blaming each other for the move. Talking to Newsline, Avneesh Pande of the NSUI said: "The party has no knowledge of any alliance. Three members from our party — Manu Madan, Sukhjit Brar and Naveen Chahal — took the decision on their own. We never announced any alliance with SOPU." Other members, however, said it was Pande who declared the panel on Monday along with SOPU.

Heading: Project for cardiac patients needs resuscitation - Indian Express
Content:
"How would you like it if a garbage dump comes up in front of your official bungalow," an angry Buta Singh, Chairman of National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), asked Municipal Commissioner Roshan Sunkaria on Tuesday.

At a meeting with Chandigarh Administration officials, Buta Singh reprimanded the "indifferent" attitude adopted by the bureaucrats towards minority groups in the city.

Questioning the location of the Solid Waste Management plant in Dadumajra, Singh said: "These poor people, who work in filth throughout the day, have been pushed to sleep with the same filth around at night, all because of the Administration's garbage dump. Don't they have a right to a clean environment, as you bureaucrats have?"

When the entire NCSC panel started shooting queries — about the 1,000 safai karamcharis (sweepers) who were laid off recently or the increasing dropout rate of students from the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe categories — officials were seen literally ducking for cover.

"The sweepers have been shifted under the control of a private contractor, who pays them only one-third of their previous salary. Why haven't you, at least, bothered to ensure that the workers are paid in accordance to the Minimum Wages Act?" asked Singh.

While UT Adviser Pardeep Mehra passed on the query to UT Home-cum-Finance Secretary Sanjay Kumar, the latter passed the buck to MC Commissioner Roshan Sunkaria, who failed to come up with a satisfactory answer.

UT Inspector General of Police S K Jain was also not spared. Singh enquired about the status of investigations in the case of alleged suicide by a student of the GMCH-32. Jain told him that the police had submitted the chargesheet in the court after receiving the forensic report. "Why haven't the police arrested anyone yet? What are your officers doing?" Singh thundered.

Charging the UT Administration with not implementing the reservation policy in its true spirit, Singh said: "Seats reserved under the SC/ST category are being transferred to the general pool. Why can't the Administration let other reserved category students claim the seats?

Also, SC/ST schoolchildren are not being provided textbooks."

BUTA SPEAKS OUT
* On UT Home Secy post"The three officers, whose names have been sent to the Ministry of Home Affairs for being appointed as UT Home Secretary, must be considered by the Administration. Reserved category officers should not be victimised by depriving them of such a post."
* On PEC controversy "Two professors of the Punjab Engineering College, who are facing a second inquiry after being given a clean chit earlier, are being victimised as they belong to the reserved category."
* On judoka's case "Rajesh Kumar, a national-level judo player, was granted his certificate only after the court's intervention. In a country which clearly needs such good sportsmen, our Administration was a mute spectator when Kumar was chucked out of college."

Heading: Car dealer told to pay Rs 1 lakh for withholding papers - Indian Express
Content:
It has been 10 months since the much-hyped telemedicine project for cardiac patients has stopped functioning at the Kharar Civil Hospital (KCH). The pilot project under the Rural Punjab Heart Attack Tele-Access Project was launched in 2004 by the PGI, Chandigarh, in collaboration with the Punjab Health Systems Corporation (PHSC).

End came for the project when Dr Anil Grover, Additional Professor, Department of Cardiology, PGI, left in November 2007. Dr Grover took away the equipment attached with the project, rendering it non-functional, Senior Medical Officer (SMO) Dr Jai Singh told Newsline.

"Following his resignation, Dr Grover came to us and took away the ECG, fax machine, modem, computer, printer and other allied systems that linked KCH with the PGI under the project," claimed Dr Singh.

He added that Dr Grover had reasoned that the equipment had been allotted on his name and he had to deposit it back with the PGI to get his 'no dues certificate'.

The SMO said Dr Grover had assured them that the equipment would be installed back shortly, but it was not done despite repeated requests.

"We repeatedly approached the head of PGI's cardiology department, Dr Yash Paul, but to no avail," added Dr Singh.

On February 15, 2004, the then Kharar MLA Bir Devinder Singh had inaugurated the project. From May to July 2005, the KCH could not use the service due to a fault in the fax machine at the cardiac care unit of PGI.

Under the project, the ECG of a patient with chest pain was done at the KCH and faxed to the PGI for an expert opinion. Accordingly, the patient was prescribed medication or referred to the premier institute for further treatment.

At the time of the launch, it was announced that the project would soon be upgraded and made online. Besides, administering injection Streptokinase, required within six hours of a heart attack, to acute pain cases was to be allowed at the KCH at subsidised rates or even free. None of these saw the light of day.

Talking to Newsline, Dr Anil Grover said: "The project was lying defunct before my resignation. PGI Director Dr K K Talwar had no faith in it while cardiology department head Dr Yash Paul was not confident about its success. After talking to the then PHSC managing director, Dr Roshan Sunkaria, I returned the fax machine to the Indian Journal of Cardiology, which had funded it. The other equipment were returned to the PGI, which required it for issuing a 'no-dues certificate' to me."

Dr Yash Paul said: "The project stopped with Dr Grover's resignation, but I am yet to investigate the reasons behind it as the project had also remained under Dr K K Talwar for some time."

Heading: Five dengue cases reported from adjoining areas of city - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum directed Ashwini Automobiles in Industrial Area to pay Rs 1 lakh as compensation for deficiency in services.

The car dealers have also been asked to refund Rs 7,500 and Rs 8,148, which was taken from the complainant on the pretext of late payment and insurance charges respectively.

The complainant, Amit Jolly, had approached an auto credit establishment in Sector 8 for financing a new Santro XL in 2007.

After completing all formalities, he was assured that the loan would be approved as soon as possible.

Later, Jolly was informed that the loan has been rejected by the ICICI Bank

but was approved by GE Money.

After the vehicle was delivered in August 2007, he got it insured from Reliance Insurance.

As downpayment for the car, Rs 34,753 was paid to Ashwini Automobiles, along with 36 cheques of Rs 9,700 each. He also gave 35 advance cheques to GE money.

Jolly alleged that despite paying regular monthly

installments, the documents of the vehicle were not given to him.

In its reply, GE Money stated that as the ICICI Bank had rejected the complainant's request for loan, he had to file another set of documents with them which he did not.

Subsequently, the loan was disbursed by the GE Money to Ashwini Automobiles.

Ashwini Automobiles, in its reply, stated that it had received only Rs 2,88,800 from the complainant — leaving Rs.11,200 and Rs 7,500 (late charges) outstanding against Jolly.

The forum said the dealer was under no compulsion to deliver the vehicle if the full payment had not been received. "But if the vehicle was delivered, the company should have issued the sale certificate and other documents, which they did not," ruled the forum.

Insurance company to settle claim by paying Rs 1.3 lakh

Chandigarh: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal forum has directed the National Insurance Company to pay Rs 1.3 lakh as claimed by the chief account officer of the Haryana Electricity department.

The chief account officer of the Uttari Haryana Bijali Vitran Nigam, in his complaint, stated that they had obtained an insurance policy against a premium of Rs 1,77,908.

In November 2003, a robbery took place in the office of SDO in Gohana, where Rs 2,85,473 went missing. During the investigation, the police recovered Rs 1,53,500.

The complainant averred that the insurance company raised an additional premium claim amounting to Rs 58,085, which was later on changed to Rs 34,381 on account of increase of cash in transit (from Rs 550 crore to Rs 659.47 crore) as the "policy was adjustable".

Alleging that the company was not releasing the claim on one pretext or the other despite repeated reminders, the complainant moved the consumer forum seeking a refund of Rs 1,31,973.

The insurance company asserted that the limit of cash in transit with a single carrying limit was Rs 5 lakh and cash in safe for Rs 6 crore as per the detailed list attached for maximum single location cash money.

The company pleaded that due to non-cooperation and non-submissions of the documents and information, besides non-payment of the adjustable legitimate premiums demanded by them, they closed the file of the claim.

The forum found that the insurance company is liable to pay the complainant the claim of Rs 1,31,573 as assessed by the surveyor. —ENS

Heading: ‘Among the 14 cops who raped me, 2 are seniors’ - Indian Express
Content:
More than five cases of dengue have been reported from the neighbouring cities of Chandigarh.

Officials said patients have been coming to the PGI and Government Multi-Specialty Hospital (GMSH), Sector 16, from the areas around Mohali and Panchkula. No fresh case from Chandigarh, however, has been reported.

"After the monsoons retreat, cases of vector-borne diseases like dengue and malaria begin to rise. The situation in Chandigarh is under control with the number of dengue cases few and far between," said a senior health official. Two cases of dengue fever were reported in August at the PGI.

Last year, Chandigarh alone had seen 76 cases of dengue. In 2006, 121 cases of were reported.

Even as dengue cases keep coming in with regularity, officials said the number of malaria cases in the city has gone down as compared to last year.

Around 60 cases of malaria have already been treated at various dispensaries of the city this season, said officials.

Heading: LPG racket flourishes while officials pass the buck - Indian Express
Content:
The 17-year-old from Hyderabad, who on Friday had alleged that 14 policemen had raped her in 2005, on Tuesday alleged that the police officials raped her at the Faraskhana police station.

At a press conference in Patrakar Bhawan, she said, "There are two senior officials involved. I have already given the names to the investigating officers. However, they are trying to ignore the issue."

Parshuram Wadekar, president Pune City, Republican Party of India, said, "The cops are trying to bring other minor issues like the fact that her lawyer is already wanted for crimes and is absconding. If the lawyer is a criminal, what has that got to do with this case? They are trying to divert attention from the main issue. For the last three days, they are taking the girl for identification of various places where she was kept. However, they are not ready to take her for identification of the policemen who raped her."

The girl also alleged that her statement was recorded in Marathi, when she asked for a translator she was refused permission to get one. Amanullah Khan of the Republican Party of India said, "It was after a lot of efforts that she was assigned a translator. The police are being slack in handling the case. They are trying to confuse the girl. Not only this they are also reluctant to take up the case against the policemen from the Faraskhana police station."

"We will wait for another two days. If no action is taken against the policemen and the two senior officers, we will make all the names public," she said.

Heading: Divest the powers of PF appellate tribunal to dists: Labour lawyers body - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after the black-marketing of LPG cylinders came to light, the officials still refuse to show any sense of urgency that could ease travails of domestic consumers, especially in the twin industrial town of Pimpri-Chinchwad, where it is suspected that a huge racket is flourishing. In fact, the district collectorate and officials of the Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd are busy passing the buck as to who should first initiate action in the matter.

While J Vedagiri, territory manager of BPCL, says that conducting raids and inspection was the duty of the district collectorate, Pradeep Patil, foodgrain distribution officer, is emphatic that fuel company has to act decisively in the matter.

"The FDO should conduct surprise raids and inspection from time to time. It is their responsibility to find out whether domestic cylinders are going to the right hands or are being misused," Vedagiri said.

"Our job is to verify the authenticity of customers and check whether the LPG cylinders are being used legally," he said. Vedagiri said their job also involves taking custody of the cylinders seized during raids. "Over the last two-three years, we have seized 300 cylinders which are still lying with us," he said.

On the other hand, an angry Patil says, "We are not the licensing authority for LPG. The company has to take action when they come across black-marketing cases or illegal use of cylinders." Patil said the FDO will act if there are malpractices concerning kerosene or ration as the FDO is the licensing authority in such cases. "The company officials can't throw their hands up. They should act strongly when a black-marketing case comes to light. In such cases, they should act against the dealer."

Stating that the FDO will not shrug off responsibilities, Patil said, "We will send a team to Pimpri-Chinchwad to find out the actual position. But finally, BPCL has to take the necessary action."

Vedagiri, however, says that he has only one officer for Pune area and another one for areas from Pimpri-Chinchwad to Lonavla. "We are short-staffed, hence FDO should take the initiative," he says.

The fallout of the buck passing, which apparently is going on for quite sometime, is that no raids have been conducted in Pimpri-Chinchwad in last eight months. "One raid was conducted last year in Pimpri, but the FDO staff was beaten up by workers of the hotel. In Pune area, 17 raids were conducted last year. This year, so far, two raids have been conducted," Vedagiri says.

"The misuse of domestic cylinder is due to the vast difference between the price of domestic cylinder and commercial ones. One domestic cylinder cost Rs 343 while a commercial one is for Rs 1,100, says Vedagiri.

The story so far
On Sunday, a clutch of citizens had caught two employees of Gujar Enterprises, an LGP dealer in Bhosari, and two alleged agents while selling domestic cylinders for Rs 500 instead of its original price of Rs 343. All the four were arrested and charged under the Essential Commodities Act. Activist Rajesh Wable had alleged that black-marketing of cylinders was common in the area what with industrialists, hoteliers, roadside canteens and food mess being favoured while domestic consumers are made to struggle to get their refills. Even Gujar Enterprises owner Kunal Shah acknowledged that his employees are being made to part with cylinders by powerful people in the area.

Heading: Conductor hangs himself in State bus - Indian Express
Content:
The Federation of Labour Law Practitioners Association of Maharashtra has written to Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Oscar Fernandes, to divest the powers of the sole provident fund appellate tribunal in Delhi to the district courts across the country. The logic: after a company is fined by the regional Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), they will have to go to the only appellate tribunal in Delhi to challenge the decision. Often, the logistical costs of travelling to Delhi and hiring a lawyer override the benefits of a reversed order.

"Only one or two out of every ten orders passed by the Pune region EPFO are challenged in Delhi," said Jayant Shaligram, a city-based lawyer who has been handling provident fund cases for the last 15 years. "The orders generally require that the recovery of the fine amount be made within 15 days failing which the bank accounts of the company are seized. One can post an appeal to the tribunal in Delhi, but to procure a stay a counsel has to be in Delhi to argue the case. Very often, companies feel that it is not worth the effort to go to Delhi," Shaligram said.

The Federation also suggests to extend the powers of the appellate tribunals to the industrial tribunals as well. In the letter, president of the federation, Ashok Gupte states, "Due to the heavy expenditure involved in travelling and the cost of litigations, many parties are unable to file appeals. Under these circumstances, it would be in the interest of litigants to provide Appellate Tribunals where the Industrial Tribunals are already established."

Commissioner of Pune region EPFO Francy Joseph has welcomed the move. "It is a good suggestion as it reduces the expenditure."

However, a lawyer, on condition of anonymity, said that divesting powers to all district courts in the country will only benefit the defaulting companies. "At present, the EPFO commission is expediting matters promptly. If the tribunal powers were to be divested to district courts, the cases will drag for years. The EPF Act, which has been benefiting the weaker sections, will cease to do so," he said.

Heading: This Dassera gold buyers likely to get green ‘toppings’ - Indian Express
Content:
A conductor of the Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) was found hanging in the Amalner-Pune bus at Shivajinagar depot on Tuesday morning. The deceased has been identified as Sharad Rangraon Patil (40), a resident of Hanuman Nagar area of Amalner in Jalgaon district.

After primary investigation, the police suspect that Patil may have committed suicide following a dispute with his family over a piece of land in his native place.

According to the police, after parking the bus at Shivajinagar depot at 8 pm on Monday, driver Manohar Shamrao Patil and conductor Patil went for dinner. The driver went to the rest room of the depot to at 10.30 pm, while Patil returned to the bus . Next day at 7.30 am, he went inside the bus to meet the conductor and found him hanging from the roof of the bus, the police said.

The Shivajinagar police took Patil's body to Sassoon hospital where a post-mortem was conducted.

Senior police inspector Rahulkumar Yewle said that the deceased is survived by parents, wife, two daughters and a son. Patil was working with the corporation for 20 years.

His brother Bhaiyyasaheb Patil, who works in a private company, said, "There was no dispute between Sharad and family members. We all had gathered at our native village for a religious ceremony. Everything was fine. We never thought he will take this extreme step." No suicide note was found.

Heading: Tulshibaug Ganpati - Indian Express
Content:
The latest to join the green brigade in the city, the jewellers may gift every customer, who purchase gold from them on Dassera (buying gold on Dassera is considered auspicious), a Shami tree sapling.

The Department of Social Forestry has proposed to distribute about one lakh saplings of Shami tree to the Pune Jewellers Association, which is considering gifting the saplings to those who buy gold from them on Dassera which will fall on October 9. The idea is to urge people to plant more trees and save the dwindling Shami trees from vanishing.

The state Social Forestry department has sent a letter in this regard to the president of Pune Jewellers' Association, Fatechand Ranka requesting him to consider the proposal of distributing Shami saplings to consumers.

"The premise is certainly good and we are keen to implement it this year. But before we move in that direction, we need to hold a joint meeting with the Social Forestry and Association panel,"said Ranka.

Director of Department of Social Forestry, Prakash Thosre said, "We have created a bank of about four lakh Shami seedlings. Out of this, we have plans to sell about one lakh saplings to the jewellers, who can gift them to their consumers. We will rope in the volunteers of National Green Corps (Rashtriya Harit Sena), which has school students among them, for help." "Apart from jewellers, we are also considering banks and establishments where there will be a flow of customers on Dassera," Thosre said.

Meanwhile, the Association has sent around 600 circulars about the initiative to its members. "Once we finalise on the implementation of the plan, we might gift the saplings to the consumers on the spot or give them a token and ask them to collect the saplings from the stalls set up by the Social Forestry department," said Ranka.

Heading: Students show the environment-friendly way - Indian Express
Content:
The Tulshibaug Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav Mandal, the fourth Manacha Ganpati of the city, has provided its 20 volunteers to the city police to help them in patrolling during Ganeshotsav in the backdrop of the recent acts of terrorism in the country.

The mandal placed in the heart of the main market of the city had also appealed to hawkers in the area to vacate the market at 5 pm every day during Ganeshotsav to avoid overcrowding and all the 240 hawkers had responded to the appeal. "We are taking precautions as we feel it is also our responsibility to help the police in such situations," said Nitin Pandit, treasurer of Tulshibaug Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav Mandal.

The mandal is famous for its imposing decorations and this year, it has presented a moving tableau on the story of Rishi Vishwamitra. The mandal is keeping alive the tradition of presenting such decorations from 1952.

The Tulshibaug Ganpati was installed in 1901. Being the biggest market area in the city, mandal was allotted the fourth position in the city after Guruji Talim Ganpati. "As Tulshibaug was the biggest market at that time, traders from various places used to come here. It was thought that during Ganeshotsav, the message of Independence movement could be spread to places by word of mouth through these traders ," said Pandit, who is associated with the mandal for the last 23 years.

The tradition of presenting imposing and moving tableau goes back to 1952 when famous sculptor D S Khatavkar initiated the process. "The scenes are mainly based on mythological stories. This time, the theme is 'Tapasyabhang of Vishwamitra by Menaka'. There are four moving figures in the scene conceptualised and created by sculptor Vivek Khatavkar," said Pandit. The mandal is also involved in various social activities like providing grocery to the poor and needy people. "This year cutting down the spending on loud speakers, we have given grocery to five NGOs in the city," said Pandit.

Heading: All eyes on V-C's chair? - Indian Express
Content:
For a change, the usual loudspeaker noises at the Ganesh mandals were replaced by environment-friendly slogans. And the ones to bring about this revolutionary change were the students of four schools in the city.

These young volunteers of National Harita Sena were from Ahilyadevi High School, Hujurpage High School, Renuka Swaroop English School and Bharat English School, who organised a rally last Saturday to send across the message of environment friendliness to the Ganesh Mandals in the city. "We gathered at Shaniwar wada at 8.30 am and visited the five most important Ganesh Mandals in the city," said Amruta Joglekar, teacher, Hujurpaga Highschool.

According to Subhash Badve, Deputy Director, Social Forestry Department, Pune, "Our attempt was to send across the message of environment friendliness through school children. We have tied up with over 250 schools in Pune and made them a part of Harita Sena, a national movement to save the environment."

The students presented a street play that depicted issues related to sound and air pollution using Ganesha as the narrator. The play involved an interview of lord Ganesh by the students in which the god unveiled the story of how man has made the Earth a polluted place. "From Shaniwar wada, we went to Kasba Ganpati, Tambdi Jogeshwari, guruji Talim, Tulsi baug and Kesri wada and performed an environment-based aarti in front of the Ganesh idols. The aarti was to pray to lord Ganesha to grant his devotees the wisdom to plant more and more trees to conserve the environment," added Joglekar. Students of Renuka Swaroop performed a play on air, water and sound pollution that received a positive response from the viewers. The students also gifted the Ganesh mandals a copy of the prayer and s hamee plants. " Shamee is a rare plant. It is said that in the entire Pune city, there are only two trees of Shamee . The historical importance of Shamee tree is that in Mahabharath, Pandavas had hidden their weapons on these trees. Further, it is lord Ganesha's favourite tree. So, taking this opportunity we gifted Shamee plants to all the mandals and advised them to plant the trees," she said. With over 9000 schools from across the state becoming a part of the Harit Sena, the future not only seems to be bright, but green and clean as well.

Heading: At Ranjangaon plant, Cummins races ahead in green initiatives - Indian Express
Content:
Narendra Jadhav likely to join RBI, race begins for his post

Even as speculation grows over the possibility of University of Pune Vice-Chancellor Narendra Jadhav joining Reserve Bank of India as deputy governor, the long-time aspirants for the post of vice-chancellor have stepped up their efforts to grab the coveted post, at least this time.

Jadhav is reportedly in the race for the deputy governor's post of the Reserve Bank. Recently, D Subbarao has been appointed as the RBI governor. As he is junior to the present deputy governor Rakesh Mohan, it is said that Mohan would be posted on the World Bank in November. In that case, the deputy governor post will become vacant, where Jadhav is a very strong candidate along with other two. According to sources, Jadhav is pressing hard for the the post of deputy governor if it becomes vacant.

In view of the likely changing scenario, the aspirants in the University of Pune have renewed their efforts for the post of the vice-chancellor.

A candidate from the Pune district is vying for the post and has sent feelers in the university circle for support. The candidate has worked on all the important posts in the university and has a huge experience in academics as well as administration.

According to sources, one of the aspirants even met the vice-chancellor on Tuesday and spoke to him for a while about the recent developments. The candidate is trying for the post from last two terms.

Besides a few regular names that become a point of discussion in the race for V-C's post, according to the sources, a well-known personality in the university who is presently in Bangalore has also been informed about the latest developments.

Heading: Ganesh mandal  presidents arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Green initiatives and the profit motive are incompatible-that has been an unwritten law of the corporate world. However, city-based Cummins Generator Technologies' (CGT) have turned this common wisdom on its head.

CGT's new plant at Ranjangaon, incorporates a range of environment-friendly features, right from the construction materials to waste disposal. What is unique about the initiative is that while many other companies have 'gone green' on a piece-meal basis, such as the disposal of waste, or in the selection of construction material for their buildings, CGT's is the first plant to have gone the whole hog.

"For us, in corporate life, 'green' is a societal obligation" said Pradip Bhargava, MD, CGT, " If long-term sustainability is a question mark in the context of environmental and climate changes, it has to be addressed by industry as a key member of civic society." So the plant on the 11-acre plot has a 25 square metre wind tower, that provides natural ventilation and cooling for the 50,000 sq feet shop floor. Use of glasswool to construct the roof makes sure that maximum use is made of the available daylight. In fact, artificial lights are not used during daytime on the shop floor. And when employees forget and leave lights on, the automated building management system switches them off after a certain period. Even the taps, if left turned on, are turned off by this system. Some of the machinery runs not on electricity, but on alternate energy sources like compressed air.

Vinay Mahajan, of SN Pingle consultants who designed the eco-friendly plant, said, " We used a by-product of thermal power plants, fly-ash for building the bricks."

The company has also gone for rain-water harvesting--rain water runoff is collected, filtered and allowed to percolate recharging ground water levels. Shantanu Suvaranapathaki, a senior employee, said that about 300 kgs of compost will be generated from the plant's waste every year and about five lakh litres of rain water will be harvested. For the record, the plant, inaugurated in January 2008, produces 80 alternators a day, a figure which company officials point out, will go upto about 150 by December this year. Three thousand trees have been planted, and 35 per cent of the plot is dedicated to green cultivation.

Bhargav says that along with "doing the right thing", the initiatives also make great business sense. "Apart from the wind tunnel, which cost a little over a crore, we did not incur any other extra costs. In fact, our electricity bill has come down by 25-30 per cent."

Over the first ten years the facility is expected to save over 14 million KW of electricity and avoid over 14,500 tons of carbon-dioxide emissions. That is the equivalent of removing 274 cars from the roads, stated the company release.

Heading: Hike SMP for cane: Farmers - Indian Express
Content:
In a significant action, the Chatuhshrungi police arrested as many as 16 presidents of various Ganesh mandals for allegedly installing pandals on roads without seeking permission. Judicial magistrate (first class) A K Mandavgade released them on a fine of Rs 500 each.

Those arrested were identified as Vikas Patole (23) of Somnath Mitra Mandal, Ghokhalenagar, Shankar Pawar (28) of Ajinkya Mitra Mandal, Durga Nagar, Vithhal Banda Rajput (55) of Baba Balaknath Mitra Mandal, Wadarwadi, Vitthal Manohar Mangavad (22) of Janseva Janata Vasahat Rahivashi Sangh, Janvadi, Raj Atmaram Nihman (28) of Navjivan Mitra Mandal, president, Sus Road, Lokesh Meghavat (30) of Sevalal Mira Mandal, Pashan, Uttam Orase (55) of Jay Mitra Mandal, Wadarwadi, Vikram Shinde (35) of Ganesh Mitra Mandal, Pashan, Deepal Gade (23) of Jaybhawani Mitra Mandal, Janwadi, Suresh Takale (38) of Navyug Mitra Mandal president, Aundhgaon, Sandip Salunke (36) of Shree Krushna Mitra Mandal, Aundhgaon, Ashish Pawar (23) of Akhil Maharashtra Mitra mandal, Aundhgaon, Dnyaneshwar Gunjal (26) of Azad Mitra Mandal, Koliwada, Prahlad Hemade (29) of Koliwada Mitra Mandal, Aundhgaon and Sujit Pawar (29) of Satej Mitra Mandal, Aundhgao. All were booked under section 33 (131), 36/134 and 120 of Mumbai Police Act.

Heading: Boy dies in wall collapse - Indian Express
Content:
Various farmers organisation have geared up to take on the government if it fails to increase the statutory minimum price (SMP) for sugarcane for the forthcoming crushing season starting next month.

"The state government has announced the SMP of Rs 811.80 per ton and it is not acceptable as it was decided six months ago," Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana MLA Raju Shetty told The Indian Express on Tuesday.

The SMP for the year is same as that was decided last year, he said adding,"the government has not considered the increase in diesel and fertiliser prices while deciding SMP. The government is working in favour of the sugar mills and ignoring the farmers."

The sugarcane production is estimated to be less this season, he said, point out that the sugar mills will have to pay the SMP sought by farmers or the agitation launched last year would be intensified this year.

The Pune Zilla Shetkari Sanghatana threatened not to allow the operations of sugar mills in the coming crushing season if the government fails to increase the SMP for sugarcane.

Sanghatana president Shiajirao Nandkhile urged the Maharashtra Sugar Mill Federation to justify their acceptance of SMP by giving details of calculating the production cost within 15 days.

The government should accept the supplementary report of the Agriculture Price Commission on revision of SMP for various agriculture produce, he said adding, "The interest of the farmers should be given priority instead of making politics out of it." On the possibility of sugar mills in the state getting sugarcane from neighbouring state, Nandkhile said the sanghatana would intensify its agitation and would not allow sugarcane from other states.

The agitation of farmers had turned violent last year with the farmers burning their crops in protest.

Heading: Killer in disguise - Indian Express
Content:
A boy who celebrated his third birthday a couple of days back had a tragic death in his sleep, when a wall of his house adjoining the railway line in Juna Bazaar area, Mangalwar Peth collapsed in the early morning on Tuesday. His parents were also injured in the incident.

Police identified the deceased as Harsal Sheikh, son of father Nasir an auto-rickshaw driver and Reshma. According to the police, the wall collapsed because of the heavy rains during the last few days. When the incident took place around 6 am the boy was sleeping, while all others including his aunty Amreen (20) and grandmother Noorjehan had woke up for having their meals early due to Roza .

Police said that the wall fell right on the boy and he was caught in the debris. His father and mother escaped with minor injuries. Faraskhana police and firemen reached the spot and rushed the boy to hospital but was pronounced dead.

Heading: Striking the right chord - Indian Express
Content:
Among 175 million victims of HCV, 12.5 million are Indians, making it a major threat for the coutntry

Its asymptomatic nature makes it a killer in disguise and high number of victims, makes Hepatitis C (HCV) the deadliest virus. Talking about India, the figures have revealed that almost 12.5 million people are affected from HCV across the country; in another words, every 15th carrier of HCV is an Indian. However, on positive note, timely treatment may help in complete eradication of the virus.

"Hepatitis C is a viral infection that affects as many as 175 million people across the world. It can become life threatening if it remains undetected for long," says Dr Parimal Lawate, gastroenterologist at Jehangir Hospital.

Worldwide, an estimated three to four million people are infected with the virus each year. In India alone, the death rates of Hepatitis C patients exceed over a hundred thousand per year. HCV kills people four times more than HIV every year (WHO estimate).

What is Hepatitis C?
Hepatitis is an inflammation of the liver that is caused by various viruses. Over the time, hepatitis seriously damages the liver and can eventually lead to liver cancer, the need for liver transplantation or even death. HCV accounts for one-fourth of all cases of chronic liver disease in India.

There are at least six different strains of the hepatitis virus, including hepatitis A, B, and C. Hepatitis B and C are considered the most serious strains and affect the greatest number of people.

Who is at risk?
The most common risk factor for Hepatitis C infection today is intravenous drug use, especially through sharing of contaminated needles. In fact, 60 per cent to 80 per cent of all IV-drug users are infected with the HCV.

Other risk factors include tattooing and body piercing if the tattoo/body piercing needles are not properly sterilised.

Although Hepatitis does not spread easily through sexual intercourse, a high-risk behavior such as multiple sexual partners, is associated with an increased risk of HCV. Blood transfusions are another leading cause of HCV where unsuspecting patients are given blood, affected by Hepatitis C virus.

HCV is Curable
Unlike HIV, Hepatitis C can be cured. There are proven treatments that enable people to eradicate the hepatitis C virus from their bodies for good. Without effective treatment however, hepatitis C can progress to cirrhosis, liver cancer or liver failure. The disease is responsible for a majority of hepatocellular carcinoma cases, of all cases of liver 50 to 75 per cent are caused by HCV. In about 60 per cent of all liver transplants, the transplants are carried out on people with HCV.

The Symptoms
There may be no symptoms in the first six months of infection. Nearly 20 per cent of those infected clear the virus from their body naturally and experience no long-term effects of the infection.

However, for the remaining 80 per cent a chronic or long-term infection is likely to develop. The course of a chronic hepatitis C infection is extremely varied and unpredictable. Because of the common absence of symptoms, many people are unaware that they have a hepatitis C infection until sometime after infection.

Another reason so many people with hepatitis C remain undiagnosed is that many of the symptoms are subjective, at least in severity, and easy to put down to something else. So, for example, depression, fatigue, skins problems, insomnia, pain and digestive disorders could all have other causes as well. Nine out of 10 people, who have Hepatitis C, are not even aware of it. For these reasons Hepatitis C is often referred to as — a silent killer.

Drug treatment to eradicate the virus has advanced greatly in the last few years. With effective treatment, 80 to 90 per cent of people with genotype 2 or 3 of HCV can be cured and about 40 to 50 per cent of people with genotype 1 HCV can be treated effectively.

Preventing HCV
Currently, there is no vaccine for HCV. The best way to prevent HCV is to avoid high-risk activities.

Is there a test for HCV?
Four categories of HCV laboratory tests are available -- (1) liver enzyme tests, (2) tests to detect antibodies to HCV, (3) tests to detect the virus, and (4) HCV genotyping.

Is there a treatment for Hepatitis C?
Pegylated Interferon Alfa 2b or 2a with Ribavirin Capsules is the recommended by doctors during the course of treatment for chronic Hepatitis C. Conventional Interferon is also prescribed with Ribavirin for treating Hepatitis C.

* One in every five with chronic HCV develop irreversible liver damage (cirrhosis)
* About one in every four with cirrhosis due to HCV, progress to liver failure and die
* HCV is responsible for as many as one in every four cases of liver cancer
* Two out of every three liver transplants are carried out on people with HCV
* At least one in every three people with HIV also have HCV
* About 175 million people worldwide suffer from HCV

Heading: Pandal panorama - Indian Express
Content:
The sarod performance at Pune festival by father-son duo, Pandit Rajan and Sarang Kulkarni was a perfect portrayal of harmony of thoughts and style

Heavenly tunes, exciting jugalbandi and spontaneous applause from the audience were the highlights of sarod performance at the Pune festival by father-son duo — Pandit Rajan Kulkarni and Sarang Kulkarni. Tabla maestro Ramdas Palsule who accompanied them added to the mood and moment with his distinct style.

"This is the second time that I have performed at Pune festival. Not many people know what sarod is and I feel it is such programmes get people to know more about Indian classical music, especially instrumental music," says Pandit Rajan Kulkarni.

Kulkarni, a disciple of Pandit Ratnakar Vyas carries the legacy of his uncle, a disciple of Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar. "My father was the principal of Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, Amritsar. My music is a combination of Gwalior Gharana and Meher Gharana," says Pandit Rajan Kulkarni, expressing satisfaction over the fact that music today is becoming universal and the ego clashes between Gharanas are disappearing. "There was a time when disciples of one Gharana were not allowed to even listen to singers of the other Gharana. But today, the scene is changing. Gurus in fact advice their disciples to go to other masters and take the best of their practices," adds he.

Having returned recently from a Europe tour, Pandit Rajan Kulkarni feels, "Indian classical music is the origin of all kinds of music. The kind of response that I received from the audiences in Germany, Italy and France was amazing. They not only appreciate our music but are also astonished about the fact that Indian musicians can play for hours without having the written notes in front of them. And this, I feel is our victory because, that's what raagdari is about."

This spontaneity and improvising ability of an ideal classical music performer was on display at the programme. Expressing satisfaction over the concert Kulkarni adds, "A concert is a two-way process. The music first reaches the heart of the performer and then the listeners. Unless every musician performs for himself, the music cannot appeal to masses. I feel today's programme was one such magical amalgamation."

His son and disciple Sarang Kulkarni, who gives the credit of his musical abilities to his father, accompanied Kulkarni says, "I initially played the tabla, and that knowledge today helped me learn sarod." Sarang incidentally is also an ardent fan of rock music. "It is all about the seven swaras and how one presents it," he smiles.

Marked by respect for each other and a universal musical approach, the duo with their magical performances also portray a perfect example of guru-shishya parampara in Indian classical music.

Heading: 6 minors rescued from Budhwar Peth, one is from Bibvewadi - Indian Express
Content:
From fun themes to issues of social concern, the mandals leave no stone unturned in adding that unusual touch to the Ganeshotsav this year.

From building 26 feet statues to bringing forth the issue of farmers' suicides, the mandals this Ganeshotsav have made the most out of the creative inclinations they posses, making Puneites indulge in the experience of a lifetime. The remarkable themes for pandals this Ganeshotsav encompass an array of activities that set ablaze the current scenario in the city. Where the tableau at Shivshakti Kabbadi Sangh Mandal at Dattawadi depicts farmers' suicides, Sakhali Pir Talim Rashtriya Maruti Mandir very vividly exhibits the theme of CYG this utsav. "This issue has been troubling our state since long and we wanted to bring this issue to the notice of as many people as we can and what else could have served as a better medium than Ganeshotsav, when people just flock in to visit various pandals all across the city," says Mane, Shivshakti Kabbadi Sangh Mandal. Issues of social concern did receive their due share of importance this year and also this year are showcased some of the activities that will hit the city in near future, one being the CYG theme depicted by Sakhali Pir Talim Rashtriya Maruti Mandir.

Also an unusual sight meets the eye when one visits Jai Hind Mitra Mandal at Shaniwar Peth. The theme - Alien vividly comes across in the tableau they have come up with. With unidentified flying objects levitating mid-air and also astronauts treading a moon like surface, provide kids with a visual treat. "So many kids come here just to have a look at the aliens. We chose it because we wanted the kids to come around. After all Lord Ganesha himself was very child like," says Parag Pethekar, Jai Hind Mitra Mandal.

When the current scenario carves its way to the pandals, the mythical characters who till now have reigned the theme of every festivity continue to enthrall their ardent lovers. The Hatti Ganpati Mandal that is drawing a large number of people to witness a dynamic 26-feet Kumbhakaran statue that picks up laddoos and stuffs it in its mouth. "This is the third time we are erecting a Kumbhakaran because larger than life image of mythical characters often attract people," says Sham Mankar, Hatt Ganpati Mandal.

Also, Akhil Bharatiya Mandai Mandal has once again established the 115-year- old statue of Ganesha and Sharda, which again is making people flock to the Pandal for darshan. The mandal has also designed the pandal keeping in mind the attributes of both the Gods. "Everywhere there is only one pratima of Ganpati that is established but we have Maa Sharda and Lord Ganesha together and the pandal too has been designed depicting the qualities that they provide you with," says Bhola Wanjare.

Heading: Lucknow temple gets first woman mahant - Indian Express
Content:
Days after a 17-year-old girl from Hyderabad alleged that 14 city policemen raped her at a lodge in Nana Peth in February 2005 and that any girl sold at the brothel is first brought before the police, a team of Faraskhana police on Monday rescued seven girls, including six minors, from a brothel in Budhwar Peth. Among the six is a 15-year-old girl from Bibvewadi area who was sold to the brothel by her friends about four months ago.

Several cases have been reported where girls from poor families in other parts of the state and country were lured to Pune by agents on the promise of a job and then sold to brothel keepers. With the rescue of a Bibvewadi girl, the police suspect the existence of a racket eyeing poor girls in the city.

"The girl was working as a housemaid in Camp and Hadapsar when she developed friendship with some persons. They assured to give her a good job but forced her into prostitution," said police sub-inspector Vimal Bidwe, who rescued the girls. Bidwe said that the girl was not able to give details about her family. She also could not provide details of the persons who brought her to brothel.

Another 16-year-old girl, who hails from a poor family in Nanded, was similarly sold by some unknown persons to the brothel in Budhwar Peth. "The girl, who had appeared for SSC examination, happened to meet the agents who lured her to Pune on assurance of a good job. They, however, sold her to the brothel," Bidwe said, adding, "even this girl could not provide the names of persons who forced her into prostitution.
