Bidwe said, "We have communicated with the parents of this girl. They are extremely poor and don't have money for travelling to Pune. So our team will be going to Nanded for handing over the girl to her parents."Five more girls, between the ages 17 and 22 years hailing from West Bengal, Hyderabad and Uttar Pradesh, have been rescued. The police have arrested the brothel keeper Gita Kancha Tamang (38) from Budhwar Peth. Primary investigations revealed that Tamang has paid Rs 10,000 per girl to the agents. Tamang has been remanded to police custody till September 18.

When asked whether there existed a racket of local agents pushing local minor girls into the city brothels, senior police inspector V T Pawar said, "Investigations are on and it will be too early to draw a conclusion."

"We have sent the victims to a rescue centre. The victims were not able to reveal the details of people who sold them at brothel," he said.

Meanwhile, the crime branch is verifying the allegations of rape against the city policemen by the Hyderabad-based minor girl. Assistant Commissioner of Police (Faraskhana division) Suresh Pote had termed allegations as false. He said the girl and her lawyer Khalid, who is wanted in several offences in Hyderabad, are trying to damage the reputation of the city police.

The social security cell of crime branch has, however, initiated investigations into the matter. The police have recorded the statements of the girl. The police teams have visited the places where the girl alleged she was raped. When contacted, Additional Commissioner (crime) Rajender Singh said, "We are busy investigating the case and nothing can be disclosed as of now."

Heading: Housing scheme for urban poor yet to take off... - Indian Express
Content:
Call it the changing tides. Arunima Singh (25) took over as the first woman mahant of renowned Mankameshwar Temple in Lucknow on Tuesday. Christened as mahant Devaigya Puri, she has succeeded her guru mahant Keshav Giri, who breathed last on August 24. A native of Barabanki, she holds a diploma in pathology from Indian Institute of Paramedics Delhi. Mahant Meera Puri, a woman mahant of Shree Guru Dattatreya Yog Ashram in Sirmour district of Himachal Pradesh, supervised her coronation as the successor of mahant Giri.

Did she face any opposition on grounds of gender? "Tough opposition was expected at the election of a woman as mahant of the Mankameshwar Temple but it turned out to be a smooth affair. I had the blessings of my guruji and support of people," said a beaming mahant Devagiya Puri, facing a rush of disciples eager to touch her feet and seek her blessings.

"A divine soul has no gender. Guru parampara is an ancient tradition and anybody can be a mahant, " said mahant Meera Puri, who represents the Shree Panch Dasnaam Junagadh Akhara. President of Dasnaami Akhara mahant Gyan Das said several women disciples have been elevated to the office of mahant in the past. "Anyone can be a mahant if she fulfills the qualifications," he said.

The chief of Ganga Sena, Anand Giri said if a woman disciple has been baptised by a guru and is unmarried, she can hold the office of mahant at any akhara. But if she does not meet any of the two criteria, her appointment as mahant is illegal, he added.  

Gender issues apart, how was mahant Devaigya Puri initiated to the spiritual world? "I was pursuing my studies at the Indian Institute of Paramedics in Delhi. In 2000, I visited the Mankameshwar Temple, stayed there for a week and took part in a yajna. Since then I am associated with the temple," said the religious leader. "My guru mahant Keshav Giriji wanted me to be his successor and become the next mahant of the temple. He baptised me on January 10, 2001. Subsequently, I renounced the worldly life, " she said, adding that she faced no resistance from her family when she opted for this path.

Asked about her priorities, the newly-elected mahant said, "I have no agenda except to fulfill the aspirations of my guruji and ensure development of the temple and spiritual and moral uplift of its disciples."

Heading: ...Health scheme for poor suffers same fate - Indian Express
Content:
Manyawar Shree Kanshiramji Shahari Gareeb Awaas Yojna, a scheme of the state government to provide free houses to the urban poor, is yet to take off.

While in 24 districts, land is yet to be identified, in others, though land has been identified, development agencies have been unable to start construction because they have not yet received possession of the land.

Under the scheme, two-room set houses will be allotted free of cost to people living below poverty line, destitute widows and the differently-abled.

A total of 1.1 lakh houses are to come up in three-storeyed buildings in the 71 districts of the state. Over 1,500 houses are to be developed in each of the 60 districts, which have maximum urban population. In each of the remaining 11 districts, 1,000 houses will be developed. The construction cost of each house has been estimated at Rs 1.75 lakh.

The state government has set a deadline of March 2009 for the completion of construction in all districts. On July 24, it had issued a work order. But even after over two months, construction work has not started in any district.

"The scheme has already been delayed by almost two months. The land acquisition process will take at least 15 more days. With such pace, development agencies will be able to construct only the ground floor of the multi-storeyed apartments within the stipulated time," said an official.

In a meeting with Urban Development Minister Nakul Dubey and other officials on Tuesday, Housing Minister Naseemuddin Siddiqui directed officials to complete land acquisition process by September 15 in all the districts.

Siddiqui has also directed the development agencies to complete all formalities at the earliest and float tenders for the construction by October 6.

Joint Secretary Ashtbhuja Tiwari (Housing and Urban Planning) said: "The delay in the scheme is due to some confusion regarding the type of land needed for the project. Within the next 10 days, all the development agencies will float tenders to start construction."

While in 27 districts, the development authorities are to construct the houses, in other districts, Uttar Pradesh Housing and Development Board is to take up the task.

District magistrates and divisional commissioners have been given the responsibility to provide land to the development agencies.

"In 27 districts, where development authorities will operate, land has been identified. Among the 44 districts where Housing Board will work, land has been identified in only 20 districts," said a Housing Board official.

The official added that in Lucknow, though the municipal corporation has identified 16.18 acres in Para village near Sarojini Nagar, the Lucknow Development Authority is yet to get possession of the land.

Similarly, 10 acres in Kanpur (Rural), 6 acres in Kanshiram Nagar and 10 acres in Unnao district have been identified, but no development work has begun.

Heading: Sugar mills: govt extends date for filing financial bids - Indian Express
Content:
Even two months after the deadline to implement the Rastriya Swastha Bima Yojna (National Health Insurance Scheme), the project remains a non-starter in the state. Reason: delay in the preparation of the list of people living below the poverty line (BPL).

While the scheme has successfully started in Haryana, Rajasthan and New Delhi, Uttar Pradesh has failed to initiate it till date. This, after the process began in April. In June, ICICI Lombard was chosen to provide "smart cards" to BPL families. In the first stage, the card, assuring cashless access to health services, was to be distributed by the first week of July in 15 districts.

The Department of Rural Development, which has been given the responsibility to start the scheme, has decided to use the 2002 BPL survey as the base for the project. The state government has called a high-level meeting along with the representatives of ICICI Lombard on Wednesday in this connection.

Sources in the department, however, said that even if the 2002 list was used to provide health insurance cards, the scheme will take at least another month to begin. "It is true the scheme has been affected following a delay in the formulation of the present BPL list. Thus, the government is considering other options," said Manoj Kumar Singh, Commissioner (Rural Development).

He added, "ICICI Lombard has promised to rearrange the 2002 BPL list as per the required format free of cost within a month. Since the process has already been delayed, we plan to launch it at least in one or two districts in 15 days. The final decision in this regard will be taken on Wednesday."

The new BPL survey is expected to take at least another one-and-a-half month to be completed. The final list of around 99 lakh BPL families is yet to be made public at the Gram Panchayat level.

Heading: Two arrested with revolver from LU - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has extended the date for filing of financial bids by private investors till 2 pm on September 16 in connection with the divestment of 31 sugar mills of the public sector UP State Sugar Corporation.

In July, five companies — Gammon India, Dalmia, Era, Chaddha and Noida-based Uflex — had submitted expressions of interests (EoIs) in accordance with the modified terms and conditions. On Monday, among the five companies, only Gammon India filed the financial bid.

Gammon India has emerged as the frontrunner to acquire the public sector unit. According to a senior government official: "If the other four companies fail to file

financial bids by September 16, the government will consider the price quoted by Gammon India."

The official added that on September 6, Gammon India had sought permission to allow one of its 100 per cent-owned subsidiary to take part in the bidding process, which the government had accepted. He, however, claimed that the price quoted by Gammon India should not be lower than the reserve price worked out by the valuation experts hired by the government.

"Even if the price quoted by Gammon India is lower than the reserve price, the government may offer to the company if it was willing to quote the price higher than the reserve price," the official said. "If the single bidder, Gammon India, is willing to quote a higher price than the reserve price, then the government may consider its bids," he added.

Heading: Eye surgeon eyes a place in Guinness record book - Indian Express
Content:
A licenced 0.32 bore revolver was recovered

Two youths, including a local student leader, were arrested with a licenced revolver from Lucknow University campus on Tuesday.

"Since carrying arms inside the university campus is banned, Mohd Faiz and Mohd Shahid were arrested," said Lucknow University police outpost in-charge, Satish Singh.

The incident took place during a routine checking of students when the police noticed over half a dozen youths sitting inside a Tata Sumo near Shaheed Chowk inside the university campus.

When the police asked them about their identities, two of them failed to produce their I-cards.

Shahid, a student leader, claimed that he was a student of second year MA in the university.

Faiz, however, told police that he was not a student of the university.

Singh said that when both the youths were frisked, a licenced 0.32 bore revolver was recovered from Faiz who claimed that it was for the protection of Shahid.

Chief Proctor Dr A N Singh said, "In the wake of arrival of President Pratibha Patil here for a special convocation on September 23, security in the campus has been strengthened."

He said that as a part of the security exercise, entry of outsiders in the campus has been banned. The police and proctorial board members are regularly checking the I-cards of students.

Heading: Maya govt asks court to withdraw cases against ministers - Indian Express
Content:
After conducting 150 eye operations free of cost within 14-and-a-half-hours in 2006, Dr S P Singh, Director of the Regional Institute of Ophthalmology, is eyeing the Guinness Book of World Records. He now plans to conduct 200 free operations in 15 hours in November to register his name in the record book.

So far, all his bulk operations have been free of cost. In March 5, 2001, Singh had set a record in the Limca Book of Records by performing 81 operations — Intra Ocular Lense (IOL) — in 11 hours at one go. The Regional Institute of Ophthalmology, a state government affiliated eye hospital in Allahabad, is among the 15 institutes in the country and the only one in the state that trains eye surgeons in super specialty treatment.

"I have already written to the Guinness Book of World Records. They have appreciated my work. In November, I will invite them to watch me operate on 200 patients in 15 hours," Singh said.

A recent government directive has given an eye surgeon a target to carry out 700 operations annually. This, according to Singh, inspired him to launch a drive against cataract. "I also drew inspiration from late Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi who had pledged to donate his eyes," he said. "If the Prime Minister of our country can donate his eyes, why can't the eye surgeons perform free surgeries for the welfare of the poor?" he added.

In a span of 18 years, Singh has performed nearly 50,000 surgeries. In 2000, for the first time, he had operated upon 50 patients at a stretch. "Performing bulk operations the first time was a little difficult. I single-handedly performed the operations in a span of 11 hours," he said.

After 2001, he had broken his own records by conducting 90 operations in 2002, 102 in January 2003, 120 in February 2003, 130 in 2005 and 150 in 2006.

He has also set a record of performing maximum number of eye operations in the state. The director general of health in Lucknow had awarded him with an appreciation letter for his valuable service to the society.

Heading: Dead youth at MLA’s house: family refutes police claims - Indian Express
Content:
The Mayawati government has started the groundwork to protect its tainted ministers from the clutches of law. Last week, the state home department had sent an application to the Faizabad district court requesting it to withdraw criminal cases against its two ministers.

Transport Minister Ram Achal Rajbhar and Fisheries Minister Dharam Raj Nishad were charged with cases of arsoning and rioting at Gosaiganj police station in Faizabad nearly 10 years ago, when the state was under BJP rule.

During the hearing of the case on Tuesday, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Gyan Prakash summoned the then officer in-charge of the Gosaiganj police station, Vinod Kumar Singh and both the BSP ministers to record their statements before the court on September 19.

According to Rakesh Ved, an advocate at the Faizabad court, on April 15 1998, the BSP leaders had led a protest against the administration and blocked the Faizabad-Azamgarh highway. When the police tried to disperse the mob, BSP supporters became violent and damaged public property. Subsequently, Singh had lodged cases against 16 BSP members.

Heading: Kanpur blast: Bajrang Dal men undergo narco test - Indian Express
Content:
The police are still groping in the dark over death of one Amit Mishra whose body was found hanging at the official residence of BSP legislator Sushil Kumar Singh in Lucknow on Sunday.

After the police recovered a "suicide note" from the deceased, it had jumped to the conclusion that Mishra had killed himself. But now they are in a fix. The police have been unable to verify Mishra's handwriting since they have no specimen of it in their possession.

This comes after the victim's relatives refused to believe the police's theory that Mishra had taken his life.

"I want to know what forced my nephew to take this step. His personal diary and cellphone are still missing," said Mishra's uncle Ram Kumar.

The family members have now decided to request the administration to get the case probed by an investigative agency. On Wednesday, they will meet top police officers in this connection.

"My only question is why Amit's hands were tied, when his body was found hanging. The answer I had got till now is unsatisfactory. The police say Amit had tied his hands to ensure that there was no chance of his survival, which I find ridiculous," Kumar said.

He also said that the family doubts police's claim that Mishra was employed at the MLA's residence.

The police maintained that Singh had employed Mishra a month ago.

"The police say that another servant of the house Santosh Mishra had helped him to get the job. Amit had never mentioned Santosh to us," he added.

Mishra's cousin Vipul Mishra wondered if he could write properly as he had dropped out from the school when he was either in Class III or IV.

"The suicide note produced by the police shows that Amit wrote Sitapur as his residence while we live in Lakhimpur Kheri," Vipul said.

The neighbours of the MLA, meanwhile, remained tight-lipped about the incident. Vivek Bajpai, one the MLA's neighbour, however, said: "We never saw Amit. I know only about Santosh."

In the midst of all these claims and speculations, Superintendent of Police (East) Harish Kumar said investigations are still on.

"It is true that we are investigating the case and are looking for a specimen to verify the suicide note. We have not found any diary or any mobile phone from the house," Kumar said.

Heading: Azamgarh case accused may undergo narco analysis tests - Indian Express
Content:
Two Kanpur-based Bajrang Dal activists underwent narco analysis test at a Mumbai laboratory on Tuesday. The brother duo — Sunil and Subodh Dixit — was allegedly close to two other members of Bajrang Dal, who were killed in a mysterious blast, in a house at Kanpur's Kalyanpur area on August 24.

Senior Superintendent of Police Kanpur, Ashok Kumar Singh said: "We expect to receive the test report after a week. Depending on the report we will decide our future course of action."

The police had picked up the brothers after going through the call details of Rajiv Mishra and Bhupinder Singh, who were killed in the August 24 blast at Rajiv Nagar locality. The call details had revealed that Rajiv had called up Subodh a few minutes before the blast. There was also frequent exchange of calls between Bhupinder and Sunil. The Anti-Terror Squad and the local police are conducting a joint probe into the case.

Heading: Madhumita case: witness escapes bullet attack - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh Police could go for narco analysis tests on those involved in the attack on BJP parliamentarian Yogi Aditya Nath on Sunday in Azamgarh that led to fresh communal tension in the area.

The police till date have arrested 15 people of which two have been accused of murder and there is a strong possibility of more arrests.

The option to conduct the psychoanalysis tests was given by Principal Secretary (Home) Kunwar Fateh Bahadur and DGP of the state Vikram Singh who visited the district on Tuesday. "The test could reveal if the attack was planned," said V K Garg, the outgoing SSP of Azamgarh.

"The principal secretary (Home) and the DGP issued directives to maintain law and order and check riots in the area," he added.

Later in the day, the visiting officials held a meeting of police officers at Reserve Police Lines where outgoing DIG of Azamgarh Range Abhimanyu Tripathi and SSP Garg were also present. Vijay Kumar and Ramit Sharma, meanwhile, who had replaced the outgoings officers respectively, had not taken charge till Tuesday evening.

Outgoing DIG Tripathi said the DGP and the principal secretary have instructed the police to review the role of some of the police officers who were assigned with the job to keep a watch on visit of BJP MP. The officers were also asked to hold meetings with religious leaders and senior citizens from both the communities.

The top officials later left for Gorakhpur from where they will visit Varanasi.

Meanwhile, clashes erupted at Kaptanganj Township in rural area of Azamgarh causing panic among locals.

SP (Rural) Sarvesh Kumar Rana, however, said: "The clash between two groups was not a sequel to the Sunday's clash, but an altercation over procuring kerosene from a ration shop. Heavy police deployment avoided the situation from becoming worse. Five persons each from both the groups were arrested."

In an another related development, the brother duo of Piyush Singh and Dhiraj Singh of Mukeriganj locality in Kotwali area were sent to jail today for murdering a man during Sunday's violence.

Circle Officer (City) Azamgarh S K Srivastava said the brother duo had no political affiliation. They were arrested red handed and .30 bore pistols and cartridges were recovered from them.

Heading: 300 acres must come from project area, says Mamata - Indian Express
Content:
The key witness in high-profile Madhumita murder case, Deshraj, escaped a near fatal attack after his neighbour's sons shot at him in Kaiserganj area of Bahraich district on Monday.

Acting on an FIR lodged by Deshraj against five relatives of his neighbour, the police arrested Babloo and Ajit on Tuesday.

The accused have been booked under the attempt to murder and SC/ST Act.

"The attack had no connection with the Madhumita murder case and the incident was sequel to an altercation between Deshraj and members of a family on Sunday," said Ram Kewal, Circle Officer (CO) Kaiserganj.

According to Kewal, Deshraj, a resident of Godhaiya village, had gone to purchase fish from a weekly market near Ghaghra river where he entered into an altercation with Ramendra Singh and his sons —Sujan Singh, Babloo and Ajit — over getting the contract of the fish market. But the policemen escorting Deshraj intervened and managed to bring him back home.

In the FIR, Deshraj stated that when he had gone to relieve himself in field, Ramendra and his sons arrived there and opened fire at him. The bullet missed Deshraj and he escaped unhurt.

The escorting policemen who were standing at a few yards away rushed to the spot after hearing gunshot, but by that time the assailants had escaped.

Heading: New protest, Naxalite party holds rally - Indian Express
Content:
A day after Tatas said that the agreement reached over the Singur issue was vague, Trinamool Congress hit back saying that there was no confusion about the modalities of the agreement signed between Commerce Minister Nirupam Sen and leader of Opposition Partha Chatterjee.

"The agreement is clear," she told mediapersons in Kolkata on Tuesday. She also took the opportunity to confront state Sen's latest statement that the Tatas had been assured that no land from the project area would be given to farmers.

"Three hundred acres will be returned from within the project area and remaining hundred acres will be given from the adjacent areas. We respect the agreement and urge the state government to implement it," the Trinamool chief said.

Taking an apparent dig at the commerce minister, she said, "We have a one-point programme now — to implement the agreement reached at Raj Bhavan on Sunday and we are not bothered about a few comments made by some individuals."

The Trinamool chief added, "At the meeting that I held with Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee it was decided that a four-member committee would be set up to determine the modalities for obtaining maximum land from within the project site and the rest from the adjacent areas."

The policy to return the land to the farmers has been framed and only the procedural requirements needed to be worked out now, added the Trinamoool chief.

Trinamool chief visits Basu in hospital
Two days after CPM patriarch Jyoti Basu was admitted to AMRI Hospitals in Kolkata, he had an unexpected visitor on Tuesday.

Around 6.30 in the evening, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata

Banerjee paid a visit to the veteran Marxist leader and stayed on for about 10 minutes. Accompanying her were leader of the Opposition Partha Chatterjee and Trinamool member Shobhan Chatterjee. Samir Putatunda, a former CPM member and a former disciple of Basu was also present there.

"I spoke to him and he is doing fine," said Banerjee after meeting him.

On Tuesday doctors confirmed that his condition continued to remainstable. "He had a normal breakfast and lunch on Tuesday," the medical board said.

The team also informed that a CT scan had been conducted on Monday evening under radiologist Sukalyan Purkayastha and no appreciable change in the blood clot was noticed. The medical board will meet again on Wednesday to discuss Basu's condition.

Throughout the day a host of luminaries visited Basu at the south Kolkata nursing home. Among them were Meera Bhattacharjee, wife ofBuddhadeb Bhattcharjee, CPM MP Sujan Chakraborty and ICC president Sanjay Budhia.

Veteran CPM leader Jyoti Basu was admitted to AMRI Hospitals around 11.35 am on Sunday after a CT scan conducted on Saturday revealed a blood clot in his brain. On Friday, Basu had injured himself when he fell down in the bathroom of his Indira Bhavan residence in Salt Lake.

Heading: Autumn shocker for IPL summer: CAB spent over Rs 20 lakh only on VIP chairs - Indian Express
Content:
The worries of Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee over Singur issue are far from over. Landless agricultural labourers and sharecroppers of Singur, who lost their jobs after the land was acquired for the Tata Motors factory, have decided to launch a fresh movement demanding compensation from the state government.

The people are being organised under the banner of Communist Party of India Marxist Leninist (Liberation), a Naxalite political party. Over 1,000 agricultural labourers and 1,200 sharecroppers of Singur will participate in the rally to be held in the Barohatkalitala area of Singur on Wednesday. The rally will be addressed by senior state committee members of CPIML (L).

The sharecroppers alleged that their interests were not taken care of during the discussions held between the representatives of the state government and Opposition parties at Raj Bhavan on Sunday. Sajal Adhikari, a CPIML (L) state committee member, said the state government has not announced any compensation for the agricultural labourers of Singur. "The state government has said that only 25 per cent of the land value would be given to the registered sharecroppers, though they deserve the similar compensation that was given to the land owners," he added.

"These marginal farmers, who were beaten up on several occasions by Singur police for resisting the state government's forceful land acquisition, would assemble at Singur tomorrow demanding withdrawal of criminal cases filed against them by the police," Adhikari said.

Farmers have also demanded that the details of the agreement between the state government and Tatas be published immediately. "Only a part of the agreement was published that did not provide all the details," said Adhikari.

Villagers of Singur, meanwhile, held a rally supporting the Tata's Nano plant on Tuesday, even as the work at the small car factory remained suspended.

More than a thousand people including farmers, CPM leaders, members of various syndicates, who supplied construction material to the Nano factory and unemployed youths participated in the rally. They raised pro-Tata slogans and stated that if Tata factory leaves Singur, it will spell a doom for the area.

"This is a non-political rally. People from all walks of life are present here. After the construction of the Nano factory, the area has seen rapid development. If Tata's move out, people will lose their jobs which they got at the factory," said Dibakar Das, local CPM leader.

Heading: Ex-councillor from Rishra gunned down - Indian Express
Content:
Jagmohan Dalmiya to 'summon' Prasun Mukherjee

Over Rs 20 lakh spent just on cushioned chairs for VIP guests during the Indian Premier League (IPL)! Well, in what could snowball into the biggest controversy over Prasun Mukherjee's reign at the Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB), it has been revealed that cricketing body overspent big time during this year's Twenty20 extravaganza.

When Shah Rukh Khan's much-hyped Kolkata Knight Riders took the city by storm in April-May during the 45-day Twenty20 carnival, little did he and the Indian cricket board realise that the CAB administration would bungle badly and overshoot their IPL budget by almost Rs five crore.

In what is now being seen as a major blot on Mukherjee's stint at the helm of the Eden office, the CAB is learnt to have spent Rs 8.26 crore for organising the seven matches of the IPL at the Eden Gardens.

The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) had categorically promised to each of the 8 hosting state bodies that they will be reimbursed for expenses incurred for hosting IPL by Rs 3.5 crore each. The CAB, however, ended up as the only host to overspend by Rs 4.76 crore. All these figures came to light after the IPL accounts were audited two weeks ago and CAB treasurer Bablu Ganguly went on record with the figures.

Jagmohan Dalmiya-led faction stormed back to power at the CAB, defeating Prasun Mukherjee at the annual elections that were held in July end.

Interestingly, the current CAB treasurer Ganguly, who of course wasn't around during the IPL days, also confirmed to The Indian Express on Tuesday that the previous CAB administration had spent a whopping sum of money just on buying and setting up chairs for the VIP guests at Eden's Club House.

It was revealed that for the IPL, the CAB had bought 96 specially made cushioned chairs for hi-profile guests for the IPL matches - at a whopping cost of Rs 16,000 each. That apart, the CAB had shelled out another Rs 4.8 lakh just for getting the chairs installed at Eden's BC Roy Club House. The total amount spent on the chairs comes to Rs 20,16,000.

Understandably, the Dalmiya-led administration has decided to "summon" the former Kolkata Police Commissioner to the Eden Gardens office to clear the smoke.

"After taking into account all the aspects of IPL accounts, Dalmiya will want to discuss these matters with the former president and he is planning to ask him to come down to this office here sometime soon," Ganguly said. He, however, was balanced in his views when asked about why the previous administration ended up overspending for the IPL.

"That's not the issue. Yes, the CAB did overshoot the Rs 3.5 crore budget by a massive margin. But again, Eden Gardens is a huge stadium, and it is only natural for the hosts to overspend. Having said that, it's only to the benefit of Bengal cricket if we look forward to ensure this doesn't happen again, instead of harping on what went wrong," the CAB treasurer said.

Heading: Muchipara case: Accused produced in court - Indian Express
Content:
Party supporters beat up murder accused in police custody

Four unidentified youths gunned down Anant Srivastava, former Congress councillor of Rishra municipality, near Hastings Jute Mill in Hooghly on Monday night.

Following the incident, his party had called a 24-hour bandh in Rishra on Tuesday. During the bandh, angry Congress supporters pulled out the murder accused from a police van and thrashed them while they were being taken to the Serampore Walsh Hospital for a medical check-up. The incidents took place near the Rishra police station. The mob also torched the police vehicle.

A senior district police officer said that no one has been arrested in connection with the incident.

According to the police, Srivastava, a labour officer of the Hastings Jute Mill, was inside the Congress office near the mill when four unidentified youths stormed the office and fired at him around 7 pm, killing him instantly.

One of his party colleagues was also seriously injured after the assailants threw bombs at the office.

Srtivastava was rushed to the Serampore Walsh Hospital where he was declared dead on arrival.

As the news of the Congress leader's murder spread to neighbouring areas, several Congress supporters staged a demonstration in the area demanding immediate arrests of the guilty.

They said Srivastava had to pay with his life for protesting against growing criminal activities in the area. A large number of police personnel were deployed in the area and a hunt was launched to nab the culprits.

Later, the police arrested Krishna Chakraborty, who had an old rivalry with Srivastava, and another man in connection with the murder.

Heading: Marriage proposal rejected, woman attempts suicide at reality show venue - Indian Express
Content:
Woman accused of poisoning her five-and-a-half year old child

Sangeeta Das, who allegedly poisoned her child four years ago, was produced in the Bankshal court on Tuesday.

Sangeeta had admitted her five-and-a-half-year-old child Tanmoy Das to the Calcutta Medical College and Hospital on January 29, 2004, but the next day he was declared dead by the hospital authorities. The postmortem revealed that the death was caused by poisoning.

Married to Kartik Das in 1997, Sangeeta left her husband's Chunapukur house due to frequent fights between them and took the child to her parent's house on Premchand Baral Street. Although the couple did not file for divorce, they were living separately since then.

"After a few months of our marriage, we started having problems. In March 2003, Sangeeta left my house with my son and never allowed me to meet my own child," Kartik said.

Recalling the past events, Kartik said that when he heard about his son's illness, he rushed to the hospital but authorities informed him that the child was already dead.

"I called my wife. But she did not inform me about the cause death. I did not suspect anything at the time. I also approached the family court asking her to come back, but the case got dismissed," Kartik said.

Later, when he grew suspicious, he applied for the postmortem report at Lalbazar and filed a case under Section 156 in the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court in 2007, he added.

According to Kartik's lawyer, on the basis of the complaint, the court ordered the officer-in-charge of the Muchipara police station to investigate the death of the child.

After investigation, the police filed a chargesheet under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code against Sangeeta.

The court issued a warrant on Monday and the police arrested Sangeeta from her parent's house.

The Bankshal court has refused to grant her bail and has fixed September 23 for the next hearing.

Heading: Partially recovered, Shinjini returns home - Indian Express
Content:
Tanua Saha, a resident of Biplabi Barin Ghosh Sarani, who attempted suicide at the Nehru Children's Museum where auditions for a reality show were being organised on Monday, has been put on ventilator in a south Kolkata nursing home.

According to the police, she was neither a participant nor related to the organisers of the show. Tanua, an employee of TATA AIG, consumed poison after her boyfriend, Rajshekhar Roychoudhury, refused to marry her.

Roychaudhury is a resident of Hind Motor in the city's suburbs.

According to Tanua's cousin Sourav Saha, she had attempted suicide twice earlier.

"These instances were also related to her affairs," Sourav added.

"She started seeing Roychoudhury around two months ago. But problems started cropping up between the two," Saurabh said. The police said it seemed that she had already planned to commit suicide before she left home on Monday.

According to the police, she was carrying the poison with her and consumed it inside a toilet of the museum.

"The guardians of the participants raised an alarm after Tanua lost consciousness. A police team reached the museum immediately and she was rushed to the Sambhunath Pandit Hospital, but due to non-availability of bed there, she was taken to a private nursing home," said Ashok Banerjee, O-C of the Hastings police station.

"We have collected the vomit samples for testing and are also looking for Roychoudhury, who has gone missing after the incident," Banerjee added. Hospital sources said that Tanua has started responding to the treatment and will be kept in the Intensive Care Unit until her condition becomes stable.

Heading: Music therapy invigorates differently-abled in Kolkata - Indian Express
Content:
Two months ago a paralysed Shinjini Sengupta left the city in a stretcher for Bangalore to get treated at NIMHANS. Her condition brought into light the adverse affect of reality television. Late Monday night, the 16-year-old schoolgirl returned home "70 per cent recovered" but her near and dear ones are far from being happy.

"We are glad that she has come back to us in a much better state, but she is emotionally scarred. Moreover, we feel that not enough steps have been taken to avoid such cases," Sankar Ghosh, Shinjini's maternal uncle, said.

Shinjini was one of the many teenaged participants of a dance competition aired on a private Bengali channel, ETV Bangla. During the shooting of one of the episodes, she was rebuked by the judges of the show for an "uninspired" performance. The public humiliation upset the teenager so much that she could not recover from the shock. "The trauma coupled with ailments such as thyroid fluctuation and blood sugar, rendered her paralysed. She is still undergoing treatment,"Ghosh said.

Shinjini might be in a stable condition now, but a career in television is something her family "can't think of now". "She is not mentally prepared to face the media yet,"Ghosh said. The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights had stepped in to fight for Shinjini's cause and the commission sought an explanation from the producers of the dance contest and Shinjini's parents on the entire issue.

Though her parents had blamed the judges for their daughter's condition, fingers have been pointed at them too.

"Even if parents nudge their children to perform better, shouldn't there be guidelines to protect the rights of the children. How can they be subjected to such harsh behaviour?" Ghosh questioned. The authorities of the private channel, claimed Ghosh, offered very little help to her family.

Heading: Housewife dead, city in  enteric grip - Indian Express
Content:
Ramkrishna Biswas, extends a friendly hand towards you when you meet him, followed by a warm smile.

It is, however, evident that his attention is elsewhere. The 32-year-old suffers from autism but is keen to play the notes on a synthesizer.

The moment Pt Tarun Bhattacharya starts strumming his Santoor, Biswas loses no time in making a place for himself beside him and trying his hand at the synthesizer.

The music therapy session at Depot at the E-Mall, turned out to be quite exhilarating for its enthusiastic participants and curious onlookers. The session organised by the Rotary Club of Calcutta Metro City for a handful of students from Divine Smiles, a school for autistic and differently-abled people, was a test-drive.

"I have tried music therapy on patients of depression, stress with successful results. I want to see how this works with these children," says Bhattacharya. Indian classical music, especially the raagas, have a curious ability to forge a balance between the mind and the body, said the musician. "I have been trying to use the power of music for healing," offers Bhattacharya.

From violent drug addicts to suicidal NRI's, Bhattacharya has seen music therapy deal with the bitterest difficulties in this world. "Raaga Bageshree has amazing results on blood pressure. It has a mellowing effect almost instantaneously," says Bhattacharya.

So, during the therapy session, he used raagas like Bageshree to first arrest the attention of his special guests and then tried to get them to play along with him as he belted out raagas like Bhairavi and Kirwani.

Heading: Google, police take cyber crime lessons to schools - Indian Express
Content:
The city is in the grip of enteric disease once again, with at least 173 cases being reported from south Kolkata — Rabindra Pally and Purba Phulbagan areas of Baghajatin in Jadavpur being the worst affected. The disease has also claimed one life in the area.

The victim has been identified as Lakshmi Chakraborty (28), a housewife, residing at Purba Phulbagan.

Although the local councillor and the health officials of the civic body refused to accept the fact that the death was caused due to enteric disease, MR Bangur hospital authorities have confirmed the disease as the cause of her death.

"A leak was caused during the drainage upgradation work by the Kolkata Municipal Corporation. But the leak took some time to be detected, which resulted in water contamination in the area. We have taken prompt steps to prevent the disease from spreading to other areas," said Chandana Ghosh Dastidar, local councillor.

According to Dastidar, not more than 35 people have been affected by the disease, although, in reality, the number of victims is about 200.

Heading: Party time, but George win heart - Indian Express
Content:
With youngsters becoming Internet savvy in the rapidly emerging world of computer technology, cyber crimes and misuse of Internet have also taken an upward curve.

To help put a check on this, Google India, as a part of their BeNetSmart awareness initiative, carried out an awareness campaign in nine schools in Kolkata on Tuesday.

"We decided to start a campaign to help students know how to avoid misuse of the internet and inculcate in them the best cyber practices," said Rishi S Jaitly, policy analyst, Google India Pvt Ltd. The team interacted with 5,000 students in the city, added Jaitly.

The nationwide programme first took off from Mumbai and Chennai after which it came to Kolkata. In this campaign, Kolkata Police assisted Google India in educating school students about proper internet usage.

According to Jaitly, the Internet and Mobile Association of India, along with the police, are a part of this campaign.

The students were given tips to never disclose personal information like name, phone number, passwords or birth date online to anyone whom they do not know, to never reply to mails or chat with unknown people, to make sure that the names included in their contact list are known to them, not to meet anyone known through Internet outside without an elder's presence and never to fill out any forwarded questionnaires, even if they were from friends.

"I use the Internet for research and chatting. Today I learnt some rules to check its misuse," said Soumya Bhowmick, class XI student of Ballygunge Government High School.

Students were asked to be careful about what they post on the net and explained that nothing stays private on the internet because there are hackers present in the cyber space. Both Google and police warned students against downloading anything from the internet without consulting their parents, as many sites have spyware that might damage their computers.

Students were also advised against sending pictures of other people and forwarding embarrassing pictures of someone else.

"When Google approached us, we agreed to render assistance to help spread the message against cyber crime among students. We hope that in future such campaigns will be extended to university and college students too. An initiative to fight the menace of internet crimes requires efforts from the government, the police as well as the private sectors," said joint commissioner of Kolkata police, Debashish Roy.

"Teenagers and youngsters often get involved in an increasing number of internet crimes. There is an increasing amount of internet crimes that the teenagers and youngsters get involved with Such awareness campaigns are good for them," said Rupak Hom Roy, principal of the Ballygunge Government High School, one of the schools visited by team.

Heading: Barreto capitalises on a defensive lapse to secure full points - Indian Express
Content:
Mohun Bagan virtually clinch Premier Division title after hard-earned 1-0 win over George Telegraph at home

They set the stage, invited the players and expected a party. The players almost let them down.

For Mohun Bagan fans, all roads led to the club ground today. They were up against George Telegraph in what had been billed as the championship match for the big team. Bagan won the match 1-0, and with that, effectively won the Calcutta Football League (CFL) Premier Division title. But it was George who won the heart.

It was around 2pm and a chock-a-block Metro compartment gave the impression of a rush hour.

Rush hour indeed it was, for those who swear by green-and-maroon. Outside the ground, the party started early. It kept the mounted police busy.

Inside, however, George were in fine fettle. The capacity turnout was getting edgy by the moment. Suddenly they erupted when PC Lalawmpuia scored in the 27th minute. Referee Rathin Mukherjee played spoilsport as he called off-side.

"Who appoint these morons?" — the supporters were angry. Old warhorse Jose Barreto calmed their nerves two minutes later. For the rest of the match, Bagan's fate hung on that slender margin.

Baichung Bhutia, who preferred to cool his heels due to an injury, was stumped by a scribe as the latter asked him to comment on Singur. "Aare yaar match dekhne do. Mohun Bagan title jeet raha hai aur tum Singur ka baat kar rahe ho (please let me concentrate on the match. Bagan are winning the title and you are asking me about Singur!)," — the skipper appeared tense. The fans too were living on tenterhooks as the Geroge players were making a mockery of the Bagan midfield and defence. Ultimately, they breathed a sigh of relief, thanks to the support from referee Rathin Mukherjee and his assistants. Mukherjee's reward, a blow from Bagan's Isfaq Ahmed.

Maybe these were the reasons why celebrations were a little guarded after the match. There were firecrackers, paper-boats and loud cheers. But deep inside, even the ardent Bagan fans might have felt that George were the better team today.

So, they gradually turned the heat on East Bengal who would face Bagan on Friday. A draw that day will make the champions tag official and plans are already afoot for a bigger celebration.

All the while, Kolkata Police stood as a spectator and seemed to be enjoying the show. Fans thronged into the ground after the match and the players' safety was at stake. By Fifa parlance, this is a serious offence. Here, the DC Ist Battalion Biswarup Ghosh, who was in charge, stunned everybody with his comments. "I don't know how this has happened. Maybe they have gate-crashed into the ground."

Heading: Kitschy Kitschy bang bang - Indian Express
Content:
A brilliant show by George Telegraph went in vain. Mohun Bagan now effectively are the Calcutta Football League (CFL) Premier Division champions after their 1-0 victory over George at home today.

George's experienced central defender Deb Kumar Sasmol was pretty solid throughout except on one occasion, when he let slip Jose Barreto past him in the 29th minute. It made the difference. Barreto tapped home a S. James through pass and took his side to 30 points from 13 matches. With a better goal difference, they are now almost home and dry. Even a defeat in the last match against East Bengal on Friday will not matter unless Mohammedan Sporting, their nearest rival with 24 points, win both their remaining matches by big margins.

A 20,000-strong Bagan crowd today partied hard in the stands and then inside the ground after the long whistle. But George stole the show with their creative style of play.

Except for first 10 minutes, they controlled the show.

They created moves from defensive-third, enjoyed a greater ball possession, controlled the midfield and put pressure on their more fancied rival with some brilliant off-the-ball play. Coach Raghu Nandy told his boys to play free football. The George players, led by Man of the Match Subho Kumar responded very well.

Still they returned empty-handed because their strikers, Pradip Roy and Francis Maduako were wayward. They had a couple of sitters, in the 46th minute and then 10 minutes later. The strikers hit wide.

Poor refereeing didn't help their cause either. Referee Rathin Mukherjee and his assistant Kashinath Sen often deprived them of justice. Also, the Bagan centrebacks Peter Odafe and Dipak Mondal kept a tight vigil on the play-maker Free Bourne to ensure safety.

George, however, are certain to finish fourth, which will allow them to play in the I-League qualifiers.

Meanwhile, Bagan midfielder Isfaq Ahmed, who came as a substitute, was red-carded for hitting the referee.

Heading: Blast into the Past - Indian Express
Content:
This one was a fashion show with a difference, where the clothes and the models almost played second fiddle to something far more stylish — the Formula One Vodafone Mclaren Mercedes MP4/22. Last weekend the city played host both to the Formula One car and designer Manish Arora who showcased his latest collection inspired by the race tracks and the high glamour associated with it. The Johnnie Walker F1 show that was kick-started in Kolkata will travel to other cities like Jaipur, Chandigarh, Ludhiana, Luknow and Pune.

The designer who is busy putting together a collection for the upcoming Paris Fashion Week made it clear that his inspiration for the collection was simple — sport meets high fashion. "F1 combines the best of both the worlds — fashion and sport. This is perhaps one of the most high profile and glamourous event in the world, a place which excites both lovers of high fashion and adrenaline junkies," says Arora. His line-up predictably included plenty of checks in blacks and reds — in the shirts, skirts, tights and jackets. And to make sure the audience did not forget the reason for the fashion show, the F1 and Johnnie Walker logos were there in every design — from the oversized jackets to the tights. His latest collection reflected exactly what Arora is famous for — bright, colourful kitsch.

Heading: Home Body - Indian Express
Content:
A film recalls a trip to a lost continent — Gondwanaland

Two years ago, 10 travellers set out on a journey of 16,000 miles — through a continent that no longer exists. They were across what was once Gondwanaland, a land mass that split around 170 million years ago into the Indian subcontinent, Arabia, Africa, Australia, Antarctica and South America. "We wanted to bring together some of these countries at least on our roadmap," says Akhil Bakshi, who led the Gondwanaland expedition.

A 40-minute film, called Back to Gondwanaland, documents their three-month-long trip to Cape Agulhus, the southernmost tip of Africa. Huddled in three SUVs, they passed through 17 countries, many affected by political instability, civil wars, terrorism, banditry and famine, not to mention the bird flu. Bakshi recalls how in the Kaisut Desert of Kenya, the group came across majestic processions of the spectacular Rendille tribe walking with their saddled donkeys at a swinging trot. "Bright as lamps, they threw stones and spears at us when we pointed our lenses at them. Thankfully, their aim was not as good as their looks," says Bakshi.

The film throws up fascinating images — burqa-covered Iranian women celebrating Navroz with gusto, the vast expanse of African game reserves dotted with antelopes and wildebeest. And what the film does not say, Bakshi's travelogue will. "Like the so-called orthodox Syrian women dressed in hot pants that could shame a Parisian model," chuckles Bakshi. His 550-page book is in its final draft and is scheduled to release by the end of the year.

The trip wasn't entirely about unwinding. The group comprised anthropologists, botanists, geologists and zoologists, among others. "The Gondwanaland expedition gave the scientists an opportunity to conduct exploratory research as well as review and synthesise existing knowledge, while observing geological features," says Bakshi. He recalls Turkey, where they came across a rare species of iris that otherwise grows only in the Himalayas. "Egyptians look so much like us, their houses look like those in Haryana and they even have a monkey god similar to our Hanuman," says Bakshi.

Heading: Unplugged - Indian Express
Content:
Manju Kapur's new book The Immigrant deals with the experiences of home in an alien land

Considering her home is an imposing Lutyens bungalow on Akbar Road, author Manju Kapur's vivid descriptions of middle class Indians and joint families are clearly far removed from her life. But home, and by extension family, Kapur insists, is what she knows best and she says the problems remain the same irrespective of the address. "My imagination works best in families. I think they are largely underrated in Indian novels, but if you look at it closely, much of the works of writers like Vikram Seth and Amitav Ghosh too deal with the family in the microcosm. Home is where we live our lives and there are so many economic, social and gender issues that are played out," she says.

Her latest book, The Immigrant (Rs 395, Random House), like her previous novels, Difficult Daughters and A Married Woman and Home, delves on the familiar terrain. The story of Nina, a 30-year-old lecturer of English at Miranda House, who immigrates to Canada after her marriage to Ananda, a dentist in Halifax, is set against the Emergency in India. It is also a tale about home, and the absence of it, in the face of the trials she faces in her life. "I usually begin writing on an issue that bothers me. The characters come later, and finally the story. In A Married Woman it was the demolition of the Babri Masjid and here it is the Emergency. I grew up during the period and if you had an opportunity to leave, you went, hoping never to return again, leaving all that was familiar, all that you thought was yours for good," says the 50-something, who returned to India despite a brief stint at Halifax in the early 1970s.

Kapur, who teaches English at Miranda House, is on an indefinite sabbatical at the moment, using the time to pen her next novel that centers around custody. "Teaching has helped me a fair bit. But what has been crucial to me is my extensive reading habit. In order to be a good writer, it is important to broaden your literary consciousness. Just the awareness of what language can do and how you are constantly challenged to do something different is important," she says, remarking that most of her novels go through multiple drafts and that her laptop is peppered with various versions of her manuscripts. "I made 14 drafts for The Immigrant," she says wryly.

Her book had an unconventional pre-launch at a Gurgaon-based call centre, but for an author who is so nuanced in the intricacies of public life, Kapur has never been one to frequent book launches or parties. "I like being left to myself. It's probably why I find travel very stressful and overrated. I do not have a hugely exciting life. I keep myself busy doing little things at home. I can't bring myself to attend these dos. Writing can never be a social stepping stone," she says. She'd rather distill the experiences of her everyday life into the next bestseller.

Heading: Dance with Me - Indian Express
Content:
The Rock On team left Kolkata wanting more

We were hoping that that a date with the Rock On team at the city nightclub Someplace Else this Sunday, would translate to an impromptu concert. No such luck. What we got instead was an interaction session with the cast of the film, minus the lead man, Farhan Akhtar. The director-turned-actor was unwell and couldn't leave his hotel room. Luke Kenny, Purab Kohli and Arjun Rampal discussed their rock influences. "Some of my favourite bands are U2, Radiohead and Indian Ocean," said Purab Kohli. "I adore Elvis," gushed Arjun Rampal who played the temperamental guitarist Joe Mascarenhas in the film. They also seemed quite excited about the kind of response the film has received. "I hope Rock On manages to stir interest in rock music in this country," said Kohli.

But they were unanimous about their choice of the rockstar of the film. "It has to be Gattu (Abhishek Kapoor, the director of the film). It was his vision. Though his last film, Aryan, flopped, he wasn't bogged down. He was determined to see Rock On through," summed up Rampal.

Heading: Bengal tells Tatas: Nano plant won’t be touched - Indian Express
Content:
The calendar has conspired against Australian Foreign Minister Stephen Smith. He is in India this week amid renewed calls for his government to sell uranium now that the Nuclear Suppliers' Group has approved the US-India deal. If Smith had wanted to focus solely on the good news in Australia-India relations, his timing could hardly have been worse. But his trip was planned months before anyone would have dared guess the date or the outcome of the nuclear deal endgame.

Still, Australia-India diplomacy has weathered awkward coincidences before. Prime Minister John Howard landed in New Delhi in March 2006, right after George W. Bush had been in town to advance the nuclear accord. So Howard, whose government then had a policy of exporting uranium only to Non-Proliferation Treaty signatory states, was greeted by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh with a smiling request for uranium sales.

Within 16 months, the conservative Howard government had radically changed policy, announcing an intent to sell yellowcake to India subject to safeguards and the NSG's approval.

That was then. Howard promptly lost an election. Today's Labour government in Canberra, under Kevin Rudd, has restored the NPT-members-only policy on uranium sales. Yet it also has a strong commitment to ties with India.

And Stephen Smith is from minerals-rich Western Australia, so both resource economics and geographic proximity make India a natural partner in his worldview.

Some fair winds are helping his bilateral endeavour. After initial bumps — notably Australia's distancing itself from the quadrilateral dialogue with the United States, Japan and India — the relationship is shaping up well. Australian exports to India, notably in gold, copper, coal and education services, are booming with growth of 30 per cent a year.

India is Australia's fastest-growing export destination and source of migrants. A thickening web of interaction has reinforced the respect each society has for the other's democratic (not to mention cricketing) qualities, despite the odd controversy. Indian students and skilled workers are welcome additions to Australia's economic and social fabric. Not that the deal is one-sided: as an education destination for Indians seeking opportunity, Australia is second only to the United States.

The agenda of common interests is long. On the strategic plane, these include: ensuring continued US engagement in an Asian system which can accommodate a rising but not destabilisingly dominant China; protecting sealanes for trade and energy security; improving and coordinating responses to natural disasters and climate change; and countering terrorism and jihadist ideology in Pakistan, Afghanistan and Southeast Asia. Engagement looks set to deepen across these fronts, including in candid dialogue among defence and security agencies. Australia has troops fighting and dying in Afghanistan. Their foes are India's too. At sea, operationally-focused talks and exercises take place between navies that see each other as partners of choice.

So the future is bright — except for the nuclear issue. Yet Indian observers should reflect on how far Australia has come. A decade ago, Canberra saw India as part of the global nuclear proliferation problem. Australia's support for India's waiver at the NSG shows that Canberra's foreign and security policy establishment now sees India as part of the proliferation solution.

Indian observers are perplexed at the contradiction between Australia's backing for the US-India deal and its refusal to countenance uranium exports under that deal. But Indians should be used to political compromise. Australia's position on nuclear ties with India is more about balance than consistency.

Most Australians are genuinely concerned about nuclear dangers. They worry about nuclear proliferation, to states and to terrorists; they fear the potential for nuclear weapons to be brandished or used in a conflict. And they are troubled by the risk of nuclear accidents, military or civilian. Their sentiment is hardly just aimed at India. France's nuclear testing in 1995 drew a far more visceral public reaction than India's in 1998.

Australia, like India, is a democracy, and Australian governments are deeply mindful of opinion within political parties and the population.

John Howard's decision to allow uranium sales to India was premature because it lacked bipartisan support. The Labour party opposed such sales partly as a result of its own internal nuclear deal. Under this, the party's right wing secured consent from the left to allow uranium mining to expand. In return, a show of resolve was offered on non-proliferation, including reiterating a ban on uranium sales to non-NPT countries. India fell foul of this.

Through its NSG stance, the Rudd government has done what it can to help India within the spirit of its own non-proliferation views and the strict letter of Labour party policy.

In the long run, an Australian uranium supply relationship with India is likely. But Rudd won't risk domestic contention on this. Australia will watch to see if the US-India deal is politically durable in India and whether a hyper-democratic India, with its restive coalitions, can be a reliable partner.

India could help itself by helping its friends in Australia to convince the Labour left and other doubters that New Delhi really can be a leader in disarmament — that it is serious, for instance, about fulfilling the undertakings in Pranab Mukherjee's statement on September 5.

Australia and India could explore a creative partnership on nuclear security. This could involve a combined push for a verifiable global treaty to stop making fissile material for weapons, practical collaboration on export controls, and advocacy of a restrained and diminishing role for nuclear arms in Asia and globally. Credible Indian participation in the nuclear disarmament commission set up by Australia and Japan would be another step.

This is not about diplomatic blackmail. There is no direct link between Australia-India cooperation on arms control and possible future uranium sales. The challenge, rather, is to finish changing the context so that Australia and India can fully recognise each other as partners in nuclear security.

And anyway, since both Canberra and New Delhi worry about nuclear dangers, working together to reduce them can only be in both countries' interest.

The writer directs the international security program at the Lowy Institute, Sydney. He has served as an Australian diplomat in India and on arms control

express@expressindia.com

Heading: Dip in suspected gastro cases in the city - Indian Express
Content:
Publishes pamphlets asking people to use artificial ponds; 'No religion says you have to immerse idols only in the sea, religion has nothing to do with environment'

Even after being snubbed by her party members and leader Uddhav Thackeray, mayor Shubha Raul has silently and strongly kept alive her ideals of eco-friendly Ganeshotsav this year. After successfully kickstarting the green immersion of Ganapati idols at her official residence, she has published pamphlets urging devotees to use artificial ponds instead of the sea for immersion of idols.

"Religion has got nothing to do with the environment. No religion says that you have to immerse your idols only in the sea," said Raul. "My idea was to immerse home idols in artificial ponds, and prevent marine pollution. Although we cannot make this compulsory for the sarvajanik mandals, there has been a positive response from individual families and we want more such families to adopt to artificial ponds," she told Newsline.

The pamphlet — published by the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) with an appeal from the mayor — says, "While celebrating this festival, devotees pray to lord Ganesha with great faith. If the same emphasis is also laid on the environment, our future generations will be able to celebrate the festival with double joy."

Raul has appealed to all households to immerse the idols in artificial ponds instead of going to the sea. Citing example of Pune, which already faces the problem of immersion in its two polluted rivers, she pointed out that large idols are used in mandals only for puja while small clay idols are actually immersed.

Around 1,60,000 home idols are immersed in the sea each year and the number is expected to increase by another 20,000 idols this year. The mayor had sparked off controversy after she spoke in favour of the environment and suggested that Ganpati idols should not be immersed in the sea as Plaster of Paris (PoP) idols are hard to dissolve and result in marine pollution.

She had also recommended that the height of idols from mandals be reduced and that they be made of natural soil. Despite protests from various quarters for "hurting the religious sentiments of people" by telling them to take a green turn, Raul has been silently going ahead with her plans.

She now hopes that by next year, even the sarvajanik mandals too would take the eco-friendly route by reducing the idol height, and more and more households take the green route. "On Thursday, around 278 idols came to my place for immersion. This figure itself shows that people are supporting the move. I am against hurting anyone's religious sentiments; all I want is a hygienic and environmentally safe way to celebrate the festival."

Heading: Keen to keep order, cops issue warning to MNS men - Indian Express
Content:
For the first time in the last seven days, the number of suspected cases of gastroenteritis being reported from affected areas of Prem Nagar and Ishwar Colony in Dhandari has dipped to less than 15 cases on a single day.

Only five cases of mild diarrhoea were reported today in the medical camp held in the affected area. A Health department official said the situation was better in comparison to 60, 70 and 20 and 15 cases registered in the last four days from the same area. The disease had also claimed two lives.

While the Health department said that the situation was improving in the affected areas as the residents were learning to take care about harmful effects of unsanitary conditions, it feared that in the wake of unhygienic condition prevailing due to overflowing sewerage water into the streets, nothing could be predicted.

District Health Officer Dr SS Dhir said antibiotic medicines have been distributed to prevent the onslaught of the disease.

On the other hand, in order to prevent further outbreaks in the city, the Health department has categorically mentioned the names of the places which run the risk of disease outbreaks due to lack of sanitation.

Most of the areas seen as risk prone areas by the Health department fall in Dhandari, Giaspura or Sherpur colonies.

The disease outbreaks were witnessed last year too in these three industrial areas inhabited by migrant workers and the families residing in the vehras.

Dr Dhir, however, said the areas now required to be covered by the fogging machines thoroughly and the sewerage cleared from the streets to provide a long term solution to the outbreak of diseases in such areas.

Heading: MMRDA to launch rental housing project at Borivali - Indian Express
Content:
But party unmoved, demands public apology from Jaya; producers say Big B's The Last Lear to release on Friday as scheduled

A day after a fiery speech by Raj Thackeray addressed to a gathering of mediapersons and a consequent gag order served by the police, at least 1,000 Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) workers across the state were served prohibitory orders under Section 144 of the Criminal Procedure Code even as hundreds were detained in Mumbai by policemen keen to avert the anticipated trouble.

In a flurry of preventive detentions, 350 MNS workers across the city were picked up on Tuesday. In South Mumbai, 10 MNS activists were detained even as a search continued for four other active members who were dodging the policemen. In Dadar, 37 party workers were detained right after Raj's statement to the press on Monday.

The official MNS line remained unchanged. "Our stance will remain the same and the agitation will continue till she (Jaya Bachchan) renders a public apology," said Nitin Sardesai, the party's spokesperson . "The police have detained several party workers — at least five to seven persons at each police station," he added.

While Jaya did apologise to a local tabloid in an interview published on Tuesday morning, the MNS said that would not suffice, and demanded that she apologise publicly, on television if necessary.

On Monday, the MNS chief had demanded that all films and promotional campaigns featuring Amitabh Bachchan and his family members be banned after Rajya Sabha MP Jaya Bachchan made an apparent light-hearted remark that she would speak in Hindi as she belonged to Uttar Pradesh.

Meanwhile, through Sunday and Monday, banners appeared in several parts of the city commenting on Jaya Bachchan's statements on speaking in Hindi. Posters of films starring Abhishek Bachchan were also torn and blackened.

"It seems like the democracy of this government is of the people, by the people and for UP and Bihar. The police are using any excuse to detain our workers. They are hunting and searching out our workers. Lokmanya Tilak had said that the politics should not be used, for people are sovereign," said Shirish Parkar, another MNS spokesperson.

Raj has said that no film of any Bachchan family member would be allowed to be released in Mumbai till Jaya rendered an unconditional apology.

However, Shubho Shekhar Bhattacharjee, CEO of Planman Motion Pictures, who are the producers of The Last Lear, told Newsline that there will be no change in the release date of the film. "We're going ahead for September 12. Our promotional campaign is on. We've got the go ahead from the Censor Board and other important film bodies to release the film. Beyond this, we don't think any outside party can dictate terms to us. The Last Lear will release this Friday."

Directed by the acclaimed Bengali director Rituparno Ghosh, The Last Lear is the English adaptation of Utpal Dutt's play, Ajker Shahjahan. The film also topline actors Arjun Rampal, Preity Zinta and Shefali Shah.

As for the lead actor of the film, Amitabh Bachchan, he has expressed his concern about the film's release. Bhattacharjee claims that his office has been exchanging emails with the superstar. Bachchan, who is currently in London, is slated to arrive in Mumbai early Wednesday morning after which he is expected to leave on a multicity promotional spree for The Last Lear.

Heading: MSRDC invites EoI for construction of MTHL - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Metropolitan and Region Development Authority (MMRDA) is all set to launch its second rental housing project at Borivali. On Monday, the Collector, on instructions from the state government, handed over 16 hectare of land near the Western Express Highway to the MMRDA. This plot is part a of MMRDA's share of the surplus land acquired under the now repealed Urban Land Ceiling Act.

Additional metropolitan commissioner, Milind Mhaiskar said, "Usually our target is to have 1000 rental housing tenements per hectare. But in this case, since the land parcel is huge, we plan to have a holistic approach. We will be having a separate plan for the project in which along with residential complexes there would also be public amenities like hospitals and schools."

Over the next five years, the MMRDA plans to construct five lakh homes; each with an area of 160 sq ft in the whole of Mumbai Metropolitan Region. The MMRDA plans to accomplish this either independently or in collaboration with developers and landowners who can offer a minimum of 500 sq metre of land for the project. Of this officials state that as many as two lakh homes will be constructed over the next one year. As part of phase one of the rental housing scheme, the MMRDA has already tied up with Dhanashree Developers to construct 35,000 houses on 100 acre of land at Vasai. The homes would be allotted to families that do not own a house in the metropolitan region and have a minimum family income of Rs 5000.

The Borivali project would be the first rental housing project which the MMRDA would be executing on its own. AR Wankhede, estate manager for MMRDA said, "The land, which is a part of the abandoned Khatau mills, is in a prime location and is completely unencumbered except for scarp machinery. With a Floor Space Index of 4, we will be potentially having about 160 acres of land at our disposal." He added that 4000 sq metre of land in Thane is another location for creation of tenements under the projects.

"Besides these, we are also scrutinising several proposals that we received from interested developers willing to construct rental homes in return of Transfer of Development Right," said Wankhede.

Heading: Mulund blast accused bail plea rejected - Indian Express
Content:
The much-delayed Mumbai Trans Harbour Link (MTHL) has finally moved a step further after series of flip-flops by the State government as Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) on Tuesday invited Expressions of Interest from contractors to design and construct the sea link on a turnkey basis.

The 22.5 km sea link is proposed to commence from Messant Road on eastern side of Sewri Railway Station on Harbour Line and traverses through the creek waters meeting the main land near Shivaji Nagar and terminating on National Highway 4B at Chirle in Navi Mumbai. The EoI has invited interested parties to design and construct an approach road on Sewri side, bridge across intertidal zone on both sides, deep sea zone, via duct and embankments. According to sources in the MSRDC, like the Bandra-Worli Sea Link that is being constructed on contract basis too, the proposed MTHL could also be a cable-stayed bridge.

The proposed sea link offers to cut the distance between the two locations by 15 km and reduce travelling time from more than two hours to about 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), which was asked to fund the project by the cabinet sub-committee on infrastructure, is set to present the financial model to the Authority on Wednesday on the estimated Rs 6,000-crore sea link.

In July, the cabinet sub-committee on infrastructure had rejected the "unrealistic" bids of the Ambani brothers who were in the fray to construct the sea link on a public-private partnership model. Instead, the sub-committee allowed the MMRDA to own and take care of the financial aspects of the bridge and asked the MSRDC to carry out the work.

"The eight lane bridge is estimated to cost around Rs 6,000 crore. The funding is proposed to be in three phases—initially Rs 2,000 crore has to be pumped in, while later, through assistance of financial institutions, another Rs 2,000 crore would be raised by a long-term loan. We are hoping to get a sizable amount through securitisation of the bridge which would fetch MMRDA upfront money that could be invested in the construction," a senior bureaucrat said requesting anonymity.

The bureaucrat added that betterment fees and grant of development rights would be used to upgrade the infrastructure in the "impact region" which is approximately 1,000 sq meters which includes areas like Panvel, Uran, Khopta and the Uran sub-region would stand to benefit the most once the project is completed. The development rights at the Nhava end of the bridge would also be taken by the MMRDA.

Heading: Asha Bhosale’s daughter in hospital after medicine overdose - Indian Express
Content:
Court said 'prima facie evidence was available against the accused and releasing him on bail would prove risky'

The Special Prevention of Terrorism Activities court on Tuesday rejected the bail application filed by 2002 Mulund blast accused Adnan Mulla. Special POTA Judge M R Puranik rejected the bail on the grounds that "prima facie evidence was available against the accused and releasing him on bail would prove risky."

In its order, the court observed that keeping in mind the prosecution's claim that there are evidences to prove that Mulla was a part of the conspiracy,his custody was essential.

Mulla in his bail application had stated that he has been falsely implicated in the case and that the prosecution is relying on the confessional statement of a co-accused and the same cannot be used against him since it does not have any legal value.

According to the prosecution, Mulla was driving the vehicle that was used by some of the accused to commission the blasts. The blast took place on March 13, 2003, in a train at Mulund station and claimed over 16 lives.

Heading: Traced minor girl tells court: don’t want to stay with parents - Indian Express
Content:
A day after melody queen Asha Bhosale celebrated 75th birthday, her daughter was admitted to Jaslok Hospital Intensive Care Unit (ICU) after alleged overdose of medicine early on Tuesday morning.

A family member rushed 52- year-old Varsha to the hospital at half past four in the morning in an unconscious state. According to the doctors, she was critical in the morning but was reported stable later in the day. "According to the doctors, there was an overdose medication. We have not registered any case since she is still unconscious but will do so after recording her statements. Prima facia, it does not look like a case of suicide as doctors have denied any poison in the body," said Ramrao Pawar, DCP (zone II.)

Though hospital authorities deny to give any information on Varsha's condition, Col M Masand, CEO of Jaslok Hospital, issued an official statement saying: "We confirm that Varsha Bhosle has been admitted to Jaslok Hospital and is under Dr J D Sunavala's care. We are committed to providing the patient with the best possible medical attention. Since we value our patients' privacy, we are unable to comment further at this juncture."

A former columnist with Rediff and with magazines and newspapers, Varsha had also worked as a playback singer in Hindi and Marathi movies, and appeared in concerts with her mother.

Heading: High Court reserves order in stalking case - Indian Express
Content:
16-year-old says I am married, would want to stay with 'my husband'; father says she is still 'welcome'

The 16-year-old girl, who was traced by the police on Monday after she went missing last May, was produced in the Bombay High Court on Tuesday where she said that she is married and would want to stay with her husband.

The Mumbai Police Crime Branch located the girl in a hotel in suburban Kashimira on Monday, along with her 22-year-old boyfriend whom they arrested. The girl's parents had alleged that she had been kidnapped by her boyfriend.

A division bench of Justice Bilal Nazki and Justice A A Kumbhakoni asked the minor girl whether she would like to stay with her parents to which she denied. She told the court that she was married and would like to stay with her husband. Since the girl is a minor and a case of kidnapping and missing is registered against her boyfriend (the accused), the girl was sent to the Deonar remand home. The court has now adjourned the matter till September 12.
