Speaking to Newsline, the girl's father said: "She is my daughter and I would accept her at any point of time. Though she is refusing to stay with us now, but she is welcome to my house."

In May 2007, a missing person's complaint was registered after the girl went missing from her Malwani residence. However, after her parents learnt from their neighbours that she was seen leaving with the accused, a welder in the area, a kidnapping case was registered against him. After the duo could not be traced by the police, the girl's father filed a Habeas Corpus writ petition in the high court earlier this year, following which the Bench has directed the Mumbai Police Commissioner file an affidavit regarding police efforts to trace the girl.

"In his affidavit, the Commissioner had stated that special efforts would be made to locate the girl and that the Crime Branch would be put on the job," Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria said on Monday.

Subsequently, the case was transferred from the Malwani Police to the Crime Branch on August 28.

According to police, the couple had initially fled to Madgaon in Goa, where he earned his living as a welder. When he got a whiff that the police were after him, the duo left Goa and kept shifting from place to place to evade the police, and finally landed at a hotel in Mira Road, Thane.

Heading: MSBSHSE holds workshop to study other boards - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Tuesday reserved the order on a petition filed by Powai resident Asha Bajaj who has reportedly been sent to a mental hospital in Pune by Inspector General of Police (IGP) Meeran Borwankar for allegedly stalking and sending marriage proposal for the officer's elder son.

Advocate General Ravi Kadam while arguing before division bench of Justice Bilal Nazki and Justice A A Kumbhakoni said: "There is no legal framework existing in India which deals with stalkers. While in countries like Australia, England, New Zealand and South Africa, there is a legal setup for dealing with stalkers." According to Kadam the petitioner Bajaj was sent to the hospital following proper procedures under the law.

Kadam further added that in the developed countries a stalker's civil liberties are either restrained or punishment of up to five years is handed out to him. Citing the example of famous musician John Lennon who was killed by a stalker, Kadam said, "Borwankar is a victim and the court wants to take action against her. If life and liberty under the constitution is applicable to Bajaj, Borwankar's right to a life free of harrasment should also be looked into."

According to the petition filed by Bajaj, she was sent to a mental hospital prison after she allegedly reached Borwankar's residence and expressed wish to marry her son. The court had earlier observed that the Pune Police also had failed to inform Bajaj's mother, after she was sent to mental hospital. "We have strong belief that law was not followed in this case," the court had observed.

Heading: Enquiry against motorman for jumping signal at Belapur station - Indian Express
Content:
The Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education (MSBSHSE) is holding a two day workshop in Mumbai to familiarize its board officials with the syllabi, textbooks and examination systems of other boards of education in India.

The boards that will be looked at are- the Indian School Certificate Examination (ICSE), Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) and International Baccalaureate (IB).

On Tuesday which was the first day of the workshop, officials and principals from ICSE, CBSE, IB, IGCSE schools including Secondary School Certificate (SSC) schools discussed issues like the curriculum, evaluation system, administration and textbooks among others. Basanti Roy, divisional secretary, MSBSHSE said, "This is the first time that we have conducted such a workshop. The workshop will enable people from the education field to interact with each other and keep themselves updated with and understand the latest developments in boards other than their own." Roy added, "The Mumbai office decided to take the initiative because different types of schools are coming up in Mumbai.The workshop will serve as a common platform for the all boards of education to examine each other."

On Wednesday, principals and officials of all the boards will make presentations on their particular styles of functioning.

Heading: As Ganesh utsav draws to an end, Mumbai gears up for cleanliness drive - Indian Express
Content:
After a motorman jumped a signal just outside Belapur railway station on Monday afternoon, Central Railway authorities have suspended him and initiated departmental enquiry against him.

According to sources, Brahmchari, the motorman of Belapur-bound CST train, crossed the 'Home red signal' near the Belapur station. After crossing the signal, the train, which was supposed to arrive at platform no 2, arrived at platform no 1. Just a couple of minutes earlier, a Panvel-bound train had left platform no 1. According to railway authorities, there could have been a major collision had the Panvel-bound train left the platform couple of minutes later.

S Mudgerikar, CPRO of CR, said, "Motorman was suspended yesterday and departmental enquiry has been initiated against him."

"But motorman clarified his position saying that the signal was not red. So following the signal he moved towards platform no 1 instead of 2. But the railway officials have a different story to tell. The truth will come out after the investigation," said an official from CR.

Meanwhile, railway records reveal that this incident is not an isolated one. Every year several such incidents occur but most of them go unreported. Crossing a signal is an offence that can result in the motorman being discharged from services.

According to railway sources, a minimum of five cases of signal at danger occur every year but due to the monopoly of motormen's unions, the administration is forced to turn a blind eye to them.

CR records show that there was one case of signal at danger in 2001-02 and the number had risen to three in 2002-03. In the year 2003-04, there were two cases while 2004-05 registered four such cases. In 2006 -07, two cases, have been recorded. And in 2007 -2008, again number had risen to three. In 2008-2009, this is the second such case.

But, according to sources, the CR administration had taken action against eight motormen in 2001-02, removing three from service. "Every signal at danger does not mean that there has been an accident. In some cases, there is a collision and sometimes nothing happens at all. But to cross the signal is an offence in itself," said an official from the CR on condition of anonymity.

Other similar incidents
* A similar incident of a motorman crossing the signal had occurred in 2003 when, on August 28, the Matsya Gandha Express hit an empty engine near Diva railway station. The case came to light after 59-year-old BR Hegde —one of the passengers of the train—narrated the incident to The Indian Express. Hegde was travelling with his family to Honavar district. According to railway sources, no entries of the incident had been made in the record books. Hegde, who returned to Mumbai a month later, brought the incident to light. Following which the action was initiated and the motorman and guard of the Matsaya Gandha Express were suspended.
* In another incident in 2003, an outstation train standing at signal near the platform at the Lokmanya Tilak Terminus hit an engine pulling five coaches for shunting, as the motorman did not see the shunt-signal. There were no casualties.

Heading: Colleges fail to respond to RTI application filed by students union leader last year - Indian Express
Content:
As the date for the final immersion of Ganpati idols draws closer, various groups around the city are planning to clean up after remnants of the idols wash ashore on September 15.

On Tuesday, five schools from around the city, in association with the Children's Movement for Civic Awareness (CMCA), participated in a beach clean-up drive in order to spread awareness about the eco-friendly methods that need to be followed during immersion.

Students from Hiranandani Foundation, Gopal Sharma Memorial School, Beacon High School, Navy Children School, and Utpal Shanghvi School participated in the clean-up drive. Students from each school donned green aprons and white gloves to pick up the litter and the leftover debris from the previous day's immersion. "Earlier, we never thought much of this, but then after we joined CMCA, we are careful not to throw anything outside and litter our surroundings," says Reetu, a seventh grade student from Utpal Shangvi. A similar drive is planned for September 15.

As part of the CMCA initiative, civic clubs have been instituted in schools around the city. Students from the sixth, seventh or eighth grade are chosen to be a part of the club. They participate in various eco-friendly drives around the city. Reena Gupta, a volunteer with the CMCA says, "We are around 50 volunteers and we have around 45 civic clubs in schools around the city."

The CMCA, which is tied with the Sophia College Ex-Students Association, has been carrying out the drive for the past three years. Students from the CMCA civic clubs have in the past participated in campaigns to spread awareness on issues relating to use of plastics and firecrackers. The organization is now planning a campaign to ensure a pollution-free Diwali, a 'Thank You to Traffic Police' and Conservancy workers. The initiative has been taken to sensitize people of their civic responsibilities.

The Rotaract Club of NM College is also planning to do a clean-up drive around the Tulip Star area near Juhu Beach on September 15."We are expecting around 60 people and maybe more. We're hoping to spread awareness about some eco-friendly measures and this is the fifth year we are doing this," says Bhaumik Sanghvi, a student of NM College, also adding that they hope their numbers will increase in the coming years. The Club consists of college students in the 16-21 years age group, though others are also expected to take part.

Fropper.com is another group that plans to continue its cleanliness drive from last year, when a small group of Fropper employees got together to clean the city. Navin Mittal, Business Head, Fropper.com says, "Last year, we got a huge response so this time we decided to tie up with colleges and youth who want to do something similar. And since Ruia college already had some eco-friendly movements happening, we thought we would give them a platform."

This year, there will be three groups when the clean-up drive happens at Girgaum chowpatty on September 15- Fropper employees, Fropper members and Ruia College students.

Heading: Man arrested for murdering his brother-in-law - Indian Express
Content:
State Chief Information Commissioner summons college authorities to appear for a hearing today

RA Poddar College of Commerce and Economics at Matunga, Elphinstone College at Fort and Maharshi Dayanand (MD) college at Parel have been summoned for a hearing on September 10 by the Maharashtra State Chief Information Commissioner Dr Suresh Joshi after these colleges failed to respond to the queries filed under the Right To Information Act (RTI), 2005.

Gajanan Kale, president, Samtawadi Chhatrabharti, a students' union, had forwarded RTI applications to 20-25 colleges in Mumbai to find out the number of students belonging to backward categories admitted in the first year junior and senior sections of the Arts, Science and Commerce departments, the amount of money collected by the colleges as library deposit, laboratory deposit and caution money. He also sought information about the amount of money reimbursed to the students, the balance amount, if any, with the colleges, the fees collected from girl students in junior sections, the donation collected from students, the number of students admitted in the management quota, the fees collected from students belonging to Other Backward Class (OBC), Scheduled Caste(SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST), and the number of filled and vacant posts allotted for professors belonging to backward class category between 2000-2006.

The college authorities have been asked to submit their replies to the queries filed by Kale on September 10 during the hearing. Kale had earlier filed applications in January 2007. Since he failed to receive the replies to the queries, Kale again filed applications in February. Still, the concerned authorities didn't provide the replies to his queries. However, a disappointed Kale filed a second appeal on July 17 under section 19 (3) of the RTI Act, 2005.

When contacted, Kale said, "Many colleges relpied to most of the queries. We found out that a number of colleges were charging additional fees from students belonging to backward category and girl students. Many colleges never returned library deposits and other deposits collected from the students."

"We have complained about the issue to the vice-chancellor. We're awaiting action from the university," he added.

Quizzed on the issue, Lakshmi Vyas, principal, Eplphinstone college said, "We did not receive any RTI queries. If he (Gajanan Kale) is claiming that he had sent the application to us last year, why did he not get back to us then itself? Anyway, our information officer will attend the hearing on September 10."

Heading: Civic body to start a Mother and Child hospital in Borivali - Indian Express
Content:
The Sewri police on Monday fished out decomposed body of a 19-year-old youth from a gutter near the Sewri railway station and arrested his brother-in-law on charge of murder. According to the police, Salim Abdul Rayani and his brother-in-law Mohammed Adil Mohammed Salim Khan went to see the Gokulashtami celebrations in their neighbourhood. However, only Khan returned to his rented room in Sewri. After receiving a missing person's complaint, the police grilled Khan who later confessed to having murdered Rayani.

"According to Khan, Rayani's refusal to return Rs 2000 he had borrowed from him led to former's murder. But, we suspect that it was an ego problem between them which led to Rayani's murder. Their families live in a village in Uttar Pradesh and Rayani used to speak unflatteringly of Khan whenever he visited his hometown. Khan came to Mumbai a few years ago and was working as fish merchant. Rayani had joined him a couple of months ago. However, since Rayani's behaviour remained unchanged, Khan decided to kill him," said Police Sub Inspector Arjun Gaikwad of the Sewri police station who is investigating the case.

"When the duo were returning home on the evening of August 24, Khan attacked Rayani and stoned him to death. He, then, disposed of his body in the gutter near the railway station. After reaching home, he called up Rayani's family and said that he was missing. Following this, Rayani's brother filed a missing person's complaint " said Gaikwad.

"An injury — identified as a bite mark— on one of Khan's middle fingers intensified our suspicion that he had killed Rayani. Later, Khan confessed to having murdered his brother-in-law and disclosed the location where he had disposed of Rayani's body," said the police.

Heading: Right under BMC nose - Indian Express
Content:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has decided to start a dedicated Mother and Child hospital in Borivali soon to cater to the medical needs of women and children.

Currently, the Mumbaikars depend on the Parel-based Wadia hospital and other 27 maternity homes dedicated for healthcare services to women and children.

However, the civic administration has now approved a four-storey hospital which will meet the increasing demand of medical needs in the suburbs.

"Women and children requiring medical attention have to travel to three main hospitals in the city. This hospital will be able to cater to their needs," said health committee chairperson Shubhada Gudekar.

"The BMC is in a process of appointing medical and paramedical staff for the upcoming hospital. The four-storey building which was built three years ago and handed over to the corporation will be used for this hospital. It will be operated completely by the BMC,"said the sources.

"A building has been already constructed in Borivali. This hospital will cater to the special needs of mothers and children in the suburbs. Entire cost of the project is Rs 10 crore," Additional Municipal Commissioner Kishor Gajbhiye said.

Heading: RPF wants hoax calls to be treated as ‘acts of terror’ - Indian Express
Content:
A stretch of DN Road, right in front of the BMC headquarters, makes a mockery of the civic body's promise to rid the city of potholes. Rains over the last two days has left the stretch, recently repaired, pockmarked with potholes. Following complaints from commuters of bumpy ride due to missing paver blocks, the stretch was repaired two days back using the imported Carboncor technology.

"The material has been washed off due to rainfall in the last two days and resulted in potholes. The excess water will be removed and the road will be relaid before Ganpati immersion. We are just waiting for a dry spell," said a contractor.

However, civic officials feigned ignorance about the potholes. "I don't know about this potholed patch," said chief engineer D L Shinde. "There might be hardly any pothole in the city. We have repaired all the potholes and bad patches before the Ganpati festival." But the proof is to the contrary and right under the BMC's nose. In fact, had the civic body accepted Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh's jestful suggestion that it announce Rs 1000 reward for anybody who spots a pothole, the citizens would have a field day on this road.

This year, the civic body has been struggling to repair potholes, after a new technology — called Carboncor — imported from South Africa was introduced, which many contractors refused to use, alleging monopoly by the supplier of the material.

Heading: BMC teams at rly stations to keep check on influx from flood-hit Bihar - Indian Express
Content:
Proposal was first floated by RPF Chief Security Commissioner (Central Railway) and is now with Railway Ministry

The Railway Protection Force (RPF) has submitted a proposal to the Railway Ministry that hoax phone calls be treated as 'acts of terror'. The idea was originally floated with the RPF Director General by its Chief Security Commissioner (Central Railway) B S Sidhu.

Sources said that the issue is currently being discussed by the Railway Ministry. If the Ministry is 'thoroughly' convinced by it, then the issue would be forwarded to the Home Ministry, which can place it before Parliament.

The proposal speaks of treating hoax calls as 'acts of terror' and calls for offenders to be prosecuted under the laws meant to tackle terror activities. In the USA, hoax calls are treated as 'acts of terror' and the proposal speaks of application of similar stringent means to curb such activities ideas.

According to Sidhu, the RPF studied hoax calls patterns for a 50-day period (July 9-August 28). During this time, it received 13 'threat' calls, all of which were found to be hoax calls.

Because of the hoax calls, 12 trains had to be halted and there was a major delay in the running of these train services. Over 12,000 work force hours were wasted in checking and frisking.

However, the police could arrest only three people, who had made the hoax calls just for fun. Any one resorting to such kind of activities is liable to a fine with six months of imprisonment under the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and the Indian Railways Act.

"We have received a proposal from Chief Security Commissioner (Central Railway) in this regard. But as of now, no decision has been taken on this as this requires thorough brain storming and it is also a matter of legislation," said RPF Additional Director General Rajiv Mathur.

"Hoax calls spread panic and most of the time they are pranks. The entire security force has to be in action and there are chances of anti-national elements checking our 'reaction' time. So hoax calls can be termed 'anti-national'. But till now, the instructions are that offenders who make hoax calls should treated under the existing laws," Mathur added.

"First of all, it is difficult to trace hoax calls. Secondly, even if the person is arrested, it all depends on what the content of the call is and that has to be proved in the court which is very difficult," pointed out Special Public Prosecutor Rohini Salian, who is currently handling the 2003 Mulund blasts case.

Heading: Despite party snub, Mayor keeps her eco-friendly Ganpati idea going - Indian Express
Content:
Expecting some of the exodus from the flood-ravaged Bihar to reach Mumbai and to prevent a possible entry of epidemics, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's (BMC) health department has decided to post teams at three railway terminuses in the city to keep a check on the people coming in.

With lakhs of people affected in the ravaging Kosi floods and left homeless, Mumbai's civic administration expects that many may head to Mumbai.

"There are eight trains coming to Mumbai from Bihar every day. Teams of doctors will be posted at Kurla, CST and Bandra railway stations from tomorrow to check the incoming passengers," said executive health officer Jairaj Thanekar. They will be provided with medical tests and medication, he said.

Earlier, the BMC had blamed spread of polio and kala ajar in Mumbai on migrants from Bihar. As a preventive measure, the health department is swinging into action this time.

Heading: Crime graph soars: 4 murders in four days - Indian Express
Content:
For the first time in the last seven days, the number of suspected cases of gastroenteritis being reported from affected areas of Prem Nagar and Ishwar Colony in Dhandari has dipped to less than 15 cases on a single day.

Only five cases of mild diarrhoea were reported today in the medical camp held in the affected area. A Health department official said the situation was better in comparison to 60, 70 and 20 and 15 cases registered in the last four days from the same area. The disease had also claimed two lives.

While the Health department said that the situation was improving in the affected areas as the residents were learning to take care about harmful effects of unsanitary conditions, it feared that in the wake of unhygienic condition prevailing due to overflowing sewerage water into the streets, nothing could be predicted.

District Health Officer Dr SS Dhir said antibiotic medicines have been distributed to prevent the onslaught of the disease.

On the other hand, in order to prevent further outbreaks in the city, the Health department has categorically mentioned the names of the places which run the risk of disease outbreaks due to lack of sanitation.

Most of the areas seen as risk prone areas by the Health department fall in Dhandari, Giaspura or Sherpur colonies.

The disease outbreaks were witnessed last year too in these three industrial areas inhabited by migrant workers and the families residing in the vehras.

Dr Dhir, however, said the areas now required to be covered by the fogging machines thoroughly and the sewerage cleared from the streets to provide a long term solution to the outbreak of diseases in such areas.

Heading: Cash-starved PAU to convince farmers to pay cess for research purposes - Indian Express
Content:
With four murders in the last four consecutive days, the crime graph has suddenly shot up in the city. From Friday to Monday, the city recorded one murder every day. What causes panic among people is that in all these cases no arrest has been made so far.

It was on Friday night that a taxi driver Kamaljit Singh alias Sonu was allegedly shot dead by Shiv Sena (Bal Thackerey) students' wing president Suraj Ahluwalia along with others. The leader was reportedly in an inebriated condition when he allegedly shot the driver over some monetary dispute. The Division number 8 police had booked Ahluwalia, his one gunman Shammi Kumar and another persons Happy. No arrest has been made in the case.

The next day, another murder was reported from the Tyre Market where a 50-year-old rickshawpuller Angrej Singh was found dead. His body was found from the shop where he used to work. A resident of Apara village near Phillaur, Angrej Singh, used to work in a shop selling spare parts of diesel engine, opposite the railway station. He used to ferry goods of the shop and used to sleep in the same shop during the night. This case is yet to be solved.

On Sunday, another 50-year-old rickshawpuller Om Parkash found dead on the Sua road under the Focal Point police station. The case has not been solved.

And again on Monday, for the fourth consecutive day fourth murder was reported from the city when the Basti Jodhewal police registered a murder case in connection with the killing of a migrant labourer, who was bludgeoned to death by three persons. The police have booked three migrant labourers namely Sunil, Bhanu and Ram Karan. The trio is on the run.

However, SP (Detective) Gurpreet Singh Toor denied that there was a rise in the crime graph in the city. "Of the four murders, two have been solved and we hope to solve the remaining two soon. The police are trying their best to solve these cases and nab the accused," SP Toor added.

Heading: No mid-day meals as officials, schools play the blame game - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Agricultural University Teachers' Association (PAUTA) will initiate a campaign to convince farmers to pay 50 paise as cess for every Rs 100 earned by a farmer. The money, thus, collected will be used by the university for research purposes.

Pauta spokesperson Dr Mukesh Saig said, "Our first Kissan Mela begins at Ballowal Saunkri tomorrow. We will distribute pamphlets among farmers to convince them to pay the cess. As farmers have objected to levying of the cess, the state government has aborted the scheme."

Dr Siag added, "We will also start a signature campaign to be submitted to Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal on the last Kissan Mela in Bathinda on September 25."

The plan of levying 50p cess on every bag of wheat and paddy sold in Punjab was proposed by well-known economist Dr S S Johl, who heads a fund-generation committee constituted by PAU V-C Dr Manjit Singh Kang. As per the plan, the cess will help generate Rs 150 crore per annum.

Experts feel that this will help the university to tide over perennial fund crisis and pump in more funds for research. The experts claim that by agreeing to this cess, the state government will also be relieved of its burden to pay Rs 100 crore as the annual budget to PAU.

This move, however, has been strongly apposed by kissan unions across the state.

Dr Siag said, "Kissan unions may have their viewpoints but we as faculty of the PAU will directly go to farmers and explain our situation to them. We are sure that no farmer will object to the cess if a clear picture is projected to him. We will convince him that this money will only be used for the benefit of the farmers, just like the Green Revolution did wonders for farmers in the state."

Heading: To settle personal scores, priest denies burial - Indian Express
Content:
Though the government schools in the city have closed down for autumn break till September 14, the issue of serving midday meals to students who come to attend remedial coaching has taken a centre stage.

Under the Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan, students from Class VI to Class VIII who are weak in studies are given two-hour training in various subjects in their schools everyday. While the schools have been ordered to serve midday meals even during the autumn break, some schools are shying away from doing any extra work. These schools allege that they have not received any instructions from DEO (Elementary) or the Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan District Coordinator regarding serving meals in schools but SSA district coordinator denied this and said that verbal instructions were issued to all city schools.

A government school headmistress rued: "I have to depute a teacher every day to serve midday meals to students as there are 95 students in my schools who come for remedial coaching. So holidays are full of stress."

But children love to attend school courtesy the Midday Meal Scheme. Bachan Kaur, whose son studies in Class VII, said, "We are poor and cannot afford sweet dish everyday. My son enjoys going to school as along with food, sweet dish is also served."

But there are schools which are shying away from the idea of serving meals in schools. Requesting anonymity a government teacher said, "Why should we serve a meal to a student who comes only for two hours in a day? Moreover, we did not receiveany orders from the higher authorities. We do not mark the attendance of these students. So there is no question of midday meal during holidays? Moreover, who is going to cook the meal?"

Amarjit Kaur, District Education Officer (Elementary), Ludhiana, said, "We gave verbal instructions to all the schools through telephones to serve midday meals to the students who come for remedial coaching. The students who come without breakfast and are too poor to afford it need a meal in the school. During the seven holidays, a teacher in a school is supposed to serve the meal under her supervision. The meals are prepared by cooks but teachers unnecessarily make an issue out of it. I will depute my staff tomorrow to get it rectified."

Heading: Traffic awareness drive kicks off - Indian Express
Content:
The general secretary of the Brown Memorial Hospital Employees' Union and an employee of the Christian Medical College and Hospital (CMCH), BM Fredrick, has alleged that the priest in charge of Kalvari Church had issued an order prohibiting his mother's burial in the graveyard in order to settle personal scores with him. Fredrick was actively involved in the campaign that effected the resignation of the former chairman of the CMCH Society

However, Kalvari Church priest in -charge Warris K Masih said that it was a unanimous decision of the Church of North India (CNI) not to entertain anybody who was against the wishes of the church.

He added that though the committee had decided not consider anybody who was against the church, they later decided to oblige them on compassionate grounds.

Fredrick had alleged earlier that since he is the secretary of UCNI (United Church of Northern India) - which has land issues with CNI — he was prohibited to use the graveyard land for the burial. Though my mother was a member of the CNI Kalvari Church, her body was not being allowed to be buried in the graveyard, he said.

"All this is being done to settle personal grudges that the top functionaries of the CNI have been harbouring against me since I have played a key role in lodging complaints against CNI and also in the ouster of former chairman of the CMCH Society," he alleged. Fredrick's 92-year-old mother Neomi Massey died this morning following a protracted illness.

Fredrick said that when he approached Masih, he was told that no land would be given for his mother's burial as she had lived in the USA for over 10 years. "However, I contended that she had been living in the city since 1989 and was a member of the church," he said.

He further alleged that though the land was being given for the burial now, they were still not allowed to pay the last respects to the body at the church.

Heading: N-deal is Bofors scam’s sequel, says Grewal - Indian Express
Content:
An traffic awareness campaign kicked off from Bhai Bala Chowk today as a part of the Jaycees Week celebrations. Rupinder Singh, SP (Traffic), flagged off the campaign.

Under this programme, the Jaycees of Ludhiana is holding camps at important intersections of the city and making residents aware of various rules and regulations of traffic.

The SP (Traffic) lauded the efforts of Jaycees. While presidents of different chapters of Jaycees stressed on the need to streamline traffic to ease the pressure of the roads.

Heading: Students apprised of educational avenues abroad - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharatiya Janta Party (BJP) Investor Cell, Punjab State Chief Sukhminderpal Singh Grewal termed the Indo-Nuclear deal as Bofors scam sequel and expected it to be bigger than its predecessor. He alleged that US Secretary of State Condoleeza Rice and Pranab Mukherjee, Minister of External Affairs is understood to have brokered a secret deal wherein the Congress party have promised a "lion share" of over Rs 4,00,000 crores nuclear trade to support the withering US economy.

In a statement issued here today, Grewal reiterated that the National Security Advisor's statement that US "interests" would be protected as a barter to US support to clinch the IAEA approval and NSG waiver followed by External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee's response that the UPA government will wait for ratification of the 123 agreement between India before executing bilateral agreements with more competent countries viz. France, Russia etc corroborates his claim that the Congress is bent to favour US-based companies.

Grewal said that he suspected enrichment and reprocessing technologies transfer have been removed from the NSG waiver to strategically favour US in the guise of clean waiver as US had not build any nuclear reactor for last 30 years and the nuclear reactor technology marketed by US did not support re-processing. The absence of enrichment and reprocessing technologies from the NSG waiver will further vindicate his stand. US have supported India only to spur indigenous Nuclear Reactor Construction by pushing a three-decade old Nuclear Reactor outdated technology, revive their own Industry and most important, open the doors to the sale of US defence, space equipment and technology to India.

Grewal cautioned External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee to restrain from brokering such anti-national deals at the behest of Congress President Sonia Gandhi.

Heading: Exhibition at Fab India - Indian Express
Content:
Desh Bhagat Institute of Hotel Management and Catering Technology, Mandi Gobindgarh, today organised a seminar on "Academia interface" with a view to bring the students face to face with educational facilities in foreign countries.

Attended by the faculty and students of the institute, the seminar was presided over by John Norton, head of the Hospitality Department, Waiariki Institute of Technology, New Zealand. In his address, John discussed with the students many important points like immigration process to his country, courses available in his institute, qualifications required, accommodation facilities available, cultural experiences, need for IELTS, working conditions, study format for theory and practicals, geographical location etc. He also answered various queries of the students who wanted to know more about his country. Nortan who took a round of the campus praised the infrastructural facilities available there.

In his message to the students, Dr Zora Singh, chairman of Desh Bhagat Group of Institutes, said that in the present age of liberalisation and globalisation, they cannot keep themselves confined to a particular region or state. They will have to adopt a cosmopolitan outlook and learn all the skills required for success in their respective fields. Earlier, Prof Shalini Gupta, Director General of Desh Bhagat Group, welcomed the distinguished speaker and exhorted the students to update their knowledge and skills by exposing themselves to all types of academic and industrial opportunities.

Heading: Forum directs LIT to allot a plot at rate prevailing 35 years ago - Indian Express
Content:
Fab India, a handloom clothing store, has put up an exhibition of a festive collection of block-printed Chanderi silk kurtas and dupattas at its city outlet.

Fab India's Chanderi silk range is the result of traditional methods of sizing and hand-weaving the fabric that have been perfected over centuries, and have passed down the generations, said Pooja Khurana, the store manager.

She said, "Fab India has made an effort to sustain the Chanderi craft by using the traditional weaving skills of craftsmen to develop a contemporary range of garments for the people of Ludhiana. Our brand has something for everyone, and this exclusive exhibition is sure to catch the attention of those who are always on the lookout for clothes that are unique, chic and comfortable to wear."

Today, Fab India has its presence in cities like Chandigarh, Panchkula, Mohali, Amritsar, Jalandhar and Ludhiana., she said. Fab India will launch many new outlets across the country, she added.

Heading: Harmeet, Parasmani win inter-bank declamation contest - Indian Express
Content:
District Consumer Dispute Redressal Forum directed the Ludhiana Improvement of Trust (LIT) to allot a plot of 200 sq yd to the consumer at the rate prevailing 35 years ago and also pay Rs 10,000 as compensation for harassment and mental tension to the consumer.

The president of the forum, T.N. Vaidya and member D.S. Bakshi Jagjit Kaur Mander said if the plot of the size 200 sq yds was not available in Model Town Extension Part-II Development scheme, then LIT should allot a plot of same size in any equally developed scheme at old rates.

Dr Vishwanath Sood, Jatinder Sood and Surinder Nath Sood of New Lajpat Nagar, Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana, had filed a complaint and had stated that the Trust had acquired a plot belonging to Pran Nath Sood, father of the present complainants, for Model Town Extension Part-II scheme in 1973.

As per the trust policy, Pran Nath applied for allotment of a plot against the locally-displaced persons category by depositing the requisite fee in January, 1975.

However, he was not allotted any plot. He kept reminding the officials in writing, but to no avail. He died in 1980.

On the other hand, the LIT officials opposed the allotment of any plot to the complainant family.

After hearing the arguments, the forum president, T.N. Vaidya and member, D.S.Bakshi and Jagjit Kaur Mander held that it had come to light that several persons had been allotted plots under the LDP category ignoring the complainant family claim for over 30 years.

The forum also observed that the application for allotment of plot was filed with the trust way back in 1975. Since then, the application has never been declined or rejected. Even the record of the trust showed that Pran Nath was eligible for getting a plot against his acquired plot and as such his legal heirs were also entitled to the same.

Heading: Grandparents Day celebrated - Indian Express
Content:
State Bank of India organised an inter-bank declamation contest for the different banks of the city on Tuesday. Various employees of different branch offices of the banks in the city took part in the contest.

Among the judges were Pramod Sharma of Income Tax Department and Surinderveer Singh Sethi besides others.

The contest was won by Harmeet Singh of Punjab National Bank and Dr Parasmani of LIC, India.

Heading: Life’s rocking - Indian Express
Content:
To celebrate the Grandparents's Day, a declamation contest was held in the primary wing of Sacred Heart Senior Secondary School, Bhai Randhir Singh Nagar, where grandparents of the students were invited as judges.

Children participated with much zeal and enthusiasm, and it was a treat to watch the young orators. The main topics were "Laughter is the best medicine", "Are malls-a-hindrance or an asset to the society," "Internet is more a cause of laziness or facilitator of knowledge etc." A game for grandparents was also organised on the occasion. Sister Sobel, the principal, and Father John, the director of the school, honoured the guests and referred to grandparents as mentors whose guidance and affection could nurture the young minds of children.

Heading: Singh is King - Indian Express
Content:
After Arjun Rampal in Rock On, watch Shahana Goswami nag Randeep Hooda in Ru Ba Ru

A walk from the Raghuvanshi Mills compound to Phoenix Mills with newbie actor Shahana Goswami seems longer than usual. Every second glance from a passer-by speaks volumes of her popularity and her newly-acquired celebrity status. Post Rock On, this versatile actress is a runaway success. "With the success of Rock On, my life has taken a U-turn. Today, wherever I go my character Debbie goes with me," she smiles, clearly loving the adulation.

Dressed in blue denims, a white top and beads around her neck, she is your typical collegian with oodles of ardour and zest. And for this 22-year-old, her success story has only begun.

After doing minuscule roles in Yun Hota To Kya Hota and Honeymoon Travels Pvt Ltd she is now looking forward to her next big release, Ru Ba Ru with actor Randeep Hooda, on Friday. "This one is a romantic story, about a live-in couple's relationship and the ups and downs they go through. I nag quite a bit in this movie too," she says, afraid of the fact that after two 'nagging wife' roles she might be stereotyped as one.

A Delhiite by birth, Mumbai has been her home for the last four years. "I have lived here through my graduation years and I have been a part of Jaimini Pathak's theatre group, Working Title, which initially helped me get into films," she says, looking around for some shade to escape the city's humid weather. But she has never been trained in acting. "It is in my genes," she proudly states, giving instances of her parents' involvement in theatre and dance.

For Goswami, Ru Ba Ru happened while she was still in college completing her graduation. She gave her first shot for Ru Ba Ru in Bangkok, much before she was signed on for Rock On. But ironically enough the latter has turned out to be her first big release. "It is all good. What I fear is with the success of Rock On, expectations are sky high. Everyone around me expects me to give a brilliant performance in Ru Ba Ru as well," she says, as we pass by a magazine stall with posters of Rock On.

Success has kept her grounded. This, we can see in the little things that make her happy. As we walk around Phoenix Mills, she stumbles upon a host of white and mauve periwinkle flowers along the periphery of the compound which she admires, something that is typical of her character in her forthcoming movie as well. However, she refuses to look at any of the restaurants around. "I am on a strict diet; I can only have juice right now. This profession makes you do all sorts of things. But I make sure I binge once a week at least," she says, while climbing the stairs that lead to The Bowling Company.

Heading: Wine baroness - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi-based composer Gaurav Dayal has struck gold with his album Play Groove Punjab

It's not everyday that Wyclef Jean drops a line saying that he liked your music. And when Gaurav Dayal woke up to one of those days, he was over the moon. The Delhi-based music arranger, sound designer and composer for some of the most popular Punjabi pop albums in the late 90s, Gaurav Dayal decided to put all his music education into an album that he hoped would change the way people looked at Punjabi music. The result is Play Groove Punjab (BIG Music, Rs 125), the highest selling and most downloaded non-Bollywood album out of India this year.

Tired of hip-hop remixes and hearing staple beats in every Bollywood soundtrack and pop album, Dayal chose to compile a multi-artist album in late 2007. "All the tracks that I was composing or designing before catered to the artist only. I'm not Punjabi and I wanted to compose my own tribute album to a genre that gave me my first break," says Dayal who hit the big league in Indi-pop circles with Jassi's hit single Dil Le gayi Kudi in 1999. Working in between other commercial sessions, tentatively arranging loops, hook lines, and choosing artists wasn't easy but Dayal wanted the album to sound international.

"With the best equipment and arrangement, Punjabi music can appeal to people who like other genres as well. I wanted to arrange the sound in a truly international way but with brand new compositions, merge the traditional instruments in a completely different format," says Dayal who even went to New York City's renowned recording studio Masterdisk that boasts of artists such as Jay-Z and Beyonce.

Industry observer Jasmine Malik who works with record label HMV isn't surprised that the album has done so well. "Compared to solo artist albums, a multi-artist compilation does better because it gives it's buyers a choice. I've known Dayal's work and he's not been afraid to try different things, to challenge the way we listen to popular music," she says.

The album is a collection of ten richly layered songs replete with guitar solos, strings, hand claps and liberally sprinkled with infectious beats. Dayal invited some of Punjab's most prolific singers and amongst them, Husna Di Sarkare and Sohna Yaar Mera by Rana and Ishq Tere Ne by Shubha Mudgal stand out. Rocker chick Aditi Singh Sharma of Crimson and Level 9 has even sung the English hook line in Husna Di Sarkare which has become the most downloaded Punjabi track since the release of the album.

A Google search belies the popularity of the album as listeners from across North America, Canada, Germany and Australia have posted favourable comments along with praise for the album. "There hasn't been great publicity for the album in television channels, and the video isn't path breaking. But the album is a testimony to the fact that if you can engineer a clean but dynamic sound for your music, there will be listeners," asserts Dayal. And Wyclef Jean just might be one of them.

Heading: Asha forever - Indian Express
Content:
From the heart of a French chateau come the perfect wines to accompany Indian food

Three years ago, when Melanie Tesseron (inset) was asked by her uncle to take over the family owned Chateau of Pontet-Canet in France, she knew almost nothing about wines. "It was an interesting learning graph," says the 30-year-old who conducted a wine and cognac tasting session of her Pontet-Canet vintages at Ricks, the buzzing lounge of Delhi's Taj Mahal Hotel.

"I sacrificed my career as a graphic designer to enter the world of enology. The transition was not natural. Although I had tasted and enjoyed drinking wine, I never cared for the tasting notes. I undertook a year-long course in deciphering wine language just to survive," she laughs. Today, she is firmly in control of affairs of the 81 hectare vineyards of Chateau Pontet-Canet.

On her first official visit to Delhi, she describes the deep red 2001 Pontet-Canet as a "hidden treasure" which pairs perfectly with north Indian dishes like mutton or lentils. "Most of our wines go well with Indian food," she says. Tesserron has been a lover of spicy Indian curries since her brother worked as a chef in Goa for three years. "At home, my brother would often make a mutton curry and we would pair it with Pontet-Canets of various vintages to check out which paired the best. During Christmas, the family gets together and gorges on Indian curries, washing it down with wines," she continues. With a price tag Rs 15,000 upwards, these wines are available only in select hotels across the city.

Heading: Criminal Botch-up of Investigation - Indian Express
Content:
In her 75th year, the songstress is going as strong as ever

Singing legend Asha Bhonsle celebrated her 75th birthday in great style by releasing a new album, Precious Platinum. The new album is a collection of songs composed and arranged by composer Nitin Ramesh Shankar. Bhonsle said that in an age obsessed with rhythm, she wanted to cut an album that was different. "People can't sing item songs when they just want to sing to themselves or to others. There should be some songs which, for instance, a lady sitting at home can just sing, so I told Nitin Shankar to make an album with songs like that," she said.

The video of one of the tracks from the album, Tum Jo Mile, was also screened for the audience. Regarding the shooting of the video, which is set amidst waterfalls on the Western Ghats, Bhonsle joked, "I was standing on a precipice and I was afraid that it would be my last song. We shot for three days in rainy and windy weather and at the end of it, I fell ill." The diminutive diva, who's been singing since she was 16, is the world's most recorded artist. She's also the only Indian artist to be nominated twice for the Grammy awards.

Age has dealt lightly with Bhonsle as was evident when she entered the venue, and held court with the grace and élan that comes from years of being the reigning queen of Indian airwaves. She was in a reminiscent mood as she talked about her long association with the music industry. "I have been singing for 65 years. Now you sing happy birthday to me."

Heading: Rajkumar bail plea rejected - Indian Express
Content:
117 days after twin murder; 102 days since getting probe; 90-odd days after nabbing accused; 40 days since then CBI chief said the case is cracked...

The CBI finally admitted on Tuesday that it does not have sufficient evidence against the domestic helps accused in the murder of teenager Arushi Talwar and household help Hemraj.

The investigating agency said in a press conference today that it has been unable to file chargesheet against Krishna, Rajkumar and Vijay Mandal within the stipulated 90-day period. With Mandal already out on bail, the other two also look set to get bail.

Officials, however, said they were "actively" working on the missing pieces of evidence, and that a "consolidated" chargesheet would be filed "as soon as possible".

On August 31, Newsline had first reported that the CBI might miss the deadline for filing chargesheet since it was yet to locate Arushi and Hemraj's cellphones and the murder weapon, believed to be a 'khukri'. CBI director Ashwani Kumar had confirmed this development.

On Tuesday, 102 days after it took over the probe, CBI attempted to give fresh impetus by announcing a reward of Rs 1 lakh for any information about the whereabouts of the phones and the murder weapon. On the domain of "public hunt" now are Arushi's phone (Nokia N72 make; number 9910520630) and Hemraj's Tata Indicom handset (9213515485), besides the missing 'khukri'.

The CBI also says it is in the process of sending a formal request — a Letter Rogatory — to authorities in Nepal to help locate the missing pieces of evidence. Reason: the agency believes Krishna and Rajkumar, both belonging to Nepal, hid the phones and murder weapon there.

The agency also said it would file a progress report in court under Section 173 of CrPC about its investigations till date. Sources said the agency would soon submit details of brain mapping, narco-analysis, polygraph tests, and forensic reports in court.

The agency had earlier allegedly tried to turn Mandal into an approver, the help had told Newsline after getting out of jail on Saturday. "They asked me to help them and inform the court about all that happened that night," he had said. "How could I tell the court anything when I don't know anything?"

He also said Krishna and Rajkumar are "innocent".

But on Tuesday, CBI joint-director Arun Kumar, a UP cadre IPS officer who is heading the probe, gave the media briefing a miss. Instead, two relatively junior officers — Neerja Gotru (DIG, Interpol) and Asha Shrivastav (HoD, Lie Detection Unit, CFSL) — told the media about status of the case. While Gotru has not been among the core probe team in the double-murder case, Shrivastav gave a verbal presentation on narco-analysis, brain-mapping, finger-printing and lie-detection tests. They did not, however, reveal details of final results of these tests conducted on the accused.

On July 11, the day CBI gave Arushi's father Rajesh Talwar a clean chit, then joint-director Arun Kumar had said, "Vijay Mandal, Krishna and Rajkumar had killed Arushi and Hemraj." Subsequently, then CBI director Vijay Shankar had said a day before leaving office on July 31 that the case stands "solved". "We have evidence which we will present in court," he had said.

But barely a month later his successor Ashwani Kumar told Newsline on August 30, "We have not found the mobile phones and murder weapon till now."

Kumar had indicated that CBI would not be able to file the chargesheet in 90 days: "Our investigation is still on but it is not necessary that we have to file chargesheet within 90 days. The law says if chargesheet is not filed within 90 days, then the accused can get bail."

Agency probing: Some unanswered questions
If CBI does not have any evidence against the three accused — Krishna, Rajkumar and Vijay Mandal — how would the agency prove its case in court?

CBI today said it would contact authorities in Nepal to help locate evidence (mobile phones and murder weapon) since Krishna and Rajkumar come from Nepal. But Noida police had detained Krishna the day after the murders; Rajkumar, too, was in Noida at the time. Is it possible for the duo to go to Nepal and hide evidence?

CBI today announced Rs 1 lakh reward on information about Arushi and Hemraj's cellphones and the murder weapon. After the police and the CBI's top investigators, with all access to technology, could not find them, how far will it be possible for a lay citizen to trace them?

Why was CBI joint-director Arun Kumar, who as good as held fort on the case for the past three months, missing from Tuesday's media conference?

Having failed to move an inch in its investigations in 102 days, what would CBI report to the court under CrPC Section 173?

Heading: On family front, ‘distress’ vs ‘relief’ - Indian Express
Content:
Vijay Mandal may have been lucky in securing bail, but Rajkumar has to wait for some more days to walk out of Dasna prison where he and Krishna are lodged. Special magistrate Sapna Mishra Tripathi rejected the bail plea of Rajkumar on Tuesday after CBI counsel R K Saini argued there were serious allegations like destruction of evidence against Rajkumar.

However, defence counsel Naresh Yadav argued that CBI has no evidence against the domestic help of the Duranis, the Talwar couple's friends. "We have told the court since the beginning of the case that the domestic helps are innocent and they have been falsely implicated in the murder case. Rajkumar should be released as there is no evidence against him," Yadav submitted before the court. The defence later filed

Rajkumar's bail application in the court of sessions judge Rama Jain who will hear the application on September 19.

Heading: 6 days after teen crushed, parents try to correct Blueline registration in FIR - Indian Express
Content:
With CBI deciding to "delay" filing a chargesheet against the three accused in the Arushi-Hemraj murder case, the Talwar family on Tuesday expressed surprise that the investigative agency did not find anything substantial to nail the alleged murderers more than 100 days after taking over the probe.

Dinesh Talwar, Arushi's uncle, said the family had "trusted" CBI in getting to the bottom of the case. But, "the delay in filing a chargesheet is CBI's failure," he said. "They were unable to find evidence against any of the accused even after so many months of investigations. The agency should not end the case on a dead note."

Talwar's lawyer Satish Tamta said the family feels "there is still hope that the agency would be able to file the chargesheet soon".

Meanwhile, co-accused Krishna's family expressed relief at the day's development. "Relieved" and "happy", his niece Sunita said: "We always believed my uncle is innocent. He was home, sleeping, with the family on May 15 (night of murders). We have never lied, and this has been proved since CBI could find no evidence against him."

Krishna's lawyer Fateh Chand Sharma said his client is likely to secure bail. "The last day to file the chargesheet is September 11," Sharma said. "We will file Krishna's bail application on September 11 and he should walk out of jail soon."

'Want justice for Arushi'
* Rajesh Talwar: We were hopeful that CBI would file chargesheet on time.
* CBI had done the investigation, I believed them... if they (Krishna, Rajkumar, Mandal) are guilty, they should not be allowed to walk free.
* It is extremely distressing for us today. We don't know if a chargesheet will be filed; we don't even know if the accused did it.
* Nupur Talwar: I cannot rest in peace till I know what happened to my daughter.

(As told to NDTV)

Heading: Kanth to head new child rights panel for Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
It has been six days since 14-year-old Sanchit Gupta was crushed to death by a reckless Blueline driver in New Usmanpur.

But his family has not had the time to mourn. They are familiar faces today at the Seelampur police station, reminding officers of their need for justice.

The police have not only failed to note down the correct registration number of the bus in the FIR, they have not written down the driver's name either, the Gupta family said.

Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) Jaspal Singh, however, refused to accept there was anything wrong with the FIR.

FIR number 362/08, registered on September 3 — the day Sanchit Gupta was killed on his way to school — bears an incomplete registration number: DL 1 PB 103. The correct number is DL 1 PB 0103.

Noticing the mistake, Sanchit's family approached Investigating Officer Gaje Singh, but he would not hear them out. The boy's father Pankaj Gupta said, "I called him the moment I realised the number was incorrect but the officer kept on delaying our meeting. The FIR also does not have the name of the offending driver. Is the police trying to weaken our case?"

Sanchit's mother, Sangeeta added, "We have lost our son. But what hurts more is that the police is trying to hush up the case." A teacher by profession, Sangeeta said, "The FIR states that the driver and owner of the bus Karam Singh was taken to the GTB Hospital after the incident. If the police knew where to find the driver, why have they not put his name down in the records?"

Family members also accused the cops of painting over the number plate on the rear of the bus. An emotional grandfather Anand Prakash Agarwal broke down while speaking about the family's struggle with the police. He said: "After officers here failed to satisfy our queries, we approached the deputy commissioner of police's office on Tuesday. He has assured us of help."

However, the DCP concerned of the northeast district, Jaspal Singh, told Newsline: "If the number of the vehicle is 0103, we can still write 103. We just need to insert a '0' as its prefix once we transfer the details on the computerised form."

Singh was also asked why driver Karam Singh's name was not on the FIR. "There is nothing wrong in that either," he said, adding: "At that moment, it was more important for us to manage the victim's family and complete other formalities."

Heading: At the cool new TERI campus, air-conditioners have gone underground - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi government will set up a new Commission for Protection of Child Rights, likely to be headed by former IPS officer Amod Kanth.

The government's Social Welfare Department will issue a notification to set up the commission on Wednesday. "It will be an advocacy and advisory panel on all issues related to children's rights — from education to child labour," Secretary (Social Welfare) Devashree Mukerjee said.

"I have been told that I would be heading the organisation and I am looking forward to it," Kanth told Newsline from Patna.

The commission will be on lines of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights, formed last March. Delhi is one of the first states to set up the commission at the state level.

The commission will be allowed to take suo motu cognisance of any case related to child rights.

Kanth's role in the Jessica Lal murder case investigations came under the scanner after a lower court released all the accused. But the 1974-batch IPS officer, who runs the child welfare NGO Prayas, got a clean chit when Manu Sharma and other co-accused were convicted by the High Court. He retired from service last year.

He founded Prayas in 1988, and the NGO at present supports 50,000 children in Delhi, Gujarat and Bihar. Kanth was a member of the high-powered committee supervising 47 custodial homes in Delhi and the supervisory committee of the Directorate of Social Welfare.

The chairperson's term will not exceed three years.

Heading: DDA’s slum-to-plum housing story - Indian Express
Content:
The seasons don't exist four metres below the scorched earth on which we stand — where the temperature always hovers at a cool 25 degrees Celsius, whether it is a hot summer day or a bone-chilling night.

This knowledge was enough for architect Sanjay Mohe to innovate, and he discovered the benefits of a natural air-conditioning system.

Given a brief to construct an energy-efficient campus for the TERI University in Vasant Kunj, Mohe ordered a tunnel to be dug at this depth. He then set up a network of suction devices and ducts that channelled the cool underground air into the institute's hostel rooms. The result — a hostel that does not need air-conditioners or even fans.

This is the city's first green campus, a pale-brown, exposed brick structure built on two acres of rocky land the university got from the Delhi Development Authority in 2003. Registrar Rajiv Seth said, "This is the first campus that has a coherent environment-friendly structure."

The university has been operating out of TERI's office at the India Habitat Centre since 1999 but will shift on Thursday to the new campus with 300 students and the 50-odd faculty. President Pratibha Patil and environmental scientist R K Pachauri will be present at the building's opening.

Green buildings don't come cheap and this took Rs 25 crore to construct. But Seth said: "The cooling systems have brought down energy use by 40 per cent. We will recover the cost in six years."

The building has a few other environment-friendly aces worked into its blueprint. The orientation, for one, allows glare-free daylight in all occupied areas. It blocks direct sunlight during the hottest hours. Windows and walls are completely shaded during summer and thick walls are encased by another jacket of sandstone to provide complete insulation.

But the striking features are the three types of cooling systems, which includes the earth air tunnel. The first, used in the office block, six laboratories and dining areas, is the variable refrigerant volume system, which is an efficient version of a split air-conditioner. "It's intelligent too. It senses the number of people in a particular area and adjusts the flow of cool air," said Mohe, a Bangalore-based architect. There's also the thermal storage system, which is basically your desert cooler, with the padding of khus replaced by a lattice of stones. "The stones are cooled at night with water and the honeycomb brickwork ensures it stores cool energy. In the day, the air outside circulates through it and cools the classrooms too," Mohe said.

A university that focuses on research initiatives for a better environment had to show the way towards green architecture. But why did the elegant sandstone have to go with the moss-green glass that has mauled the landscape of urban India? "It doesn't trap heat like the others," assured Gurwinder Singh, supervisor of constructions at the site. "We have used high insulation glass from Belgium that only lets in the light and not the heat."

Heading: Ground Zero: sceptics hope - Indian Express
Content:
Put on fast track, 'in-situ slum rehabilitation project' works on a 50-50 model: half the area of redeveloped shanties for slum-dwellers, the other for multi-stories. Newsline digs in

Asked by the Union Urban Development Ministry to "immediately" start work on its project to rehabilitate slums at the same site, DDA is at present studying various models for the 21 slum clusters it has identified as part of the development scheme.

The project on a public-private partnership (PPP) mode would use 50 per cent land of the slums to raise multi-storey buildings for the slum dwellers. Of the rest, "one-fourth land would be used as commercial component," said Ruchi Jain of Gian P Mathur and Associates, the DDA-appointed consultants preparing detailed technical and economical viability reports for five colonies. "This area is meant for small shops and other community-oriented activities.

"Another one-fourth of the land would be a remunerative component for the builder — the promoter would be allowed to raise high-category multi-storey complexes on this."

A novel project proposed by DDA, the "in-situ" rehabilitation scheme moves away from the agency's previous model of shifting slum dwellers to the city's fringes as part of rehabilitation package till date.

A senior DDA official said the agency has received plans for the first four colonies to be redeveloped as part of the project.

The consultants have also prepared preliminary building plans, as also plans for each dwelling unit. DDA officials said estimated an budget has been prepared for each one. "Chances are the project will finally apply for some sort of subsidy under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM)," an official said. "And in order to do so, it needs to live up to certain stipulations — most notably in the size and structure of proposed dwelling units."

"Therefore, plans prepared for the dwelling units (should) fulfil requirements under JNNURM."

Newsline looks at details and plans for three of the first four colonies zeroed in for rehabilitation first — the fourth colony is proposed at Jailorwala Bagh, near Ashok Vihar in Northwest Delhi

KATHPUTLI COLONY
Site area: 5.22 hectare
Number of dwelling units proposed: 2,800

One of the largest and most dense clusters, Kathputli Colony (near Shadipur depot in North Delhi) is expected to see rehab work start by this year-end. Mitu Mathur, an architect with consultants Gian P Mathur and Associates, said a detailed report has been submitted to DDA.

Under the plans, "high-category" residential units would be built next to slum-dwelling units, with different approach roads. As per the report, 2,800 dwelling units are proposed to be built here, with over half the 5.2 hectare set aside for building 10 towers with 10 floors each. Mathur said, "About 2.1 acre will be set aside as the commercial component, and another 2.4 acre as remunerative component, to be developed later."

The consultant's report anticipates that the slum-dwellers would need to be relocated to a transit camp during construction work. Land has been identified for this purpose at Swatantra Bharat Mills, some 2 km from the colony.

KESHOPUR
Site area: 0.785 hectare
Number of dwelling units proposed: 489

The proposed plans do not mention remunerative component due to the small size of this site. In its report to DDA, consultants Gian Mathur and Associates have suggested that each dwelling unit should be priced at Rs 1 lakh, and Rs 2 lakh per unit be applied for under JNNURM to generate revenue. Total investment here is estimated at Rs 38.64 crore.

BLOCK E & F, SECTOR 18, ROHINI
Site area: 3.08 hectare
Number of dwelling units proposed: 1,254

The plan for this colony, submitted to DDA by consultants Kapoor & Kapoor Associates, involves building 29 nine- and ten-storey towers with a total of 1,254 housing units. "The remunerative component has been divided into two making space for 126 High Income Group (HIG) houses and 170 Low Income Group (LIG) houses," an official said.

The report says there is no need to relocate residents during construction. "There is a vacant DDA land next to the slum cluster, and the towers would be constructed on this land," the official said. Estimated investment for this site is Rs 118 crore, with estimated revenue generation pegged at Rs 130 crore. The net profit, thereby, comes to Rs 12 crore, the plan estimates.

The Cost Factor
Building of houses: 17,434.12 lakh
Remunerative component: 3,300 lakh
Commercial component: 4,018.56 lakh
Transit camp: 675 lakh
Total investment: Rs 254.27 crore

REVENUE GENERATION
Commercial Profit: 12,727 lakh
Remunerative component: 17,000 lakh
Total revenue: Rs 339.69 crore
NET PROFIT: Total Revenue - Total Investment = Rs 85.42 crore

Heading: NRI picked up for possessing drugs - Indian Express
Content:
"I have performed for George and Laura Bush, Kapil Dev..." 10-year-old Kiran rattles off the illustrious list. A folk dancer and one of the many talented artistes living in Kathputli colony, she is clearly oblivious to the open drains and rats running amok as she performs her routine for Newsline. She is also oblivious to the fact that Kathputli Colony has been selected as one of the Jhuggi Jhopri clusters that will undergo redevelopment under Delhi Development Authority's in-situ slum rehabilitation project.

A couple of weeks back, the Delhi Development Authority had announced that it has identified 21 clusters in the Capital where multi-storey buildings will come up in the place of the jhuggis in an effort to rehabilitate slum-dwellers.

Kathputli Colony, located under the Shadipur Depot bridge, will be one of the first colonies to benefit from this project, with construction slated to begin by December.

"You had best ask Begum Aunty about it," is the standard response received from almost anyone in the colony when asked about their take on the DDA project. "Begum Aunty" as it turns out, is 43-year-old Sultana Begum, the local area representative of Kathputli Colony.

Her response to Newsline's queries on the project, is however, cautious. "I am aware of the slum rehabilitation project — I read the details in today's papers. Sheila Dikshit had come to the Colony six months ago and had announced that something of this sort was being planned. Let's see what comes of it," says Begum.

In 2002, the government had rehabilitated a few families from the colony to Vikas Puri. Within a matter of few days, however, they were back. With the memory of the earlier fiasco still in their minds, the colony residents who are aware of the project are choosing not to get too excited about it.

"There are close to 10,000 families who live here. Most are artistes who come from Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. Many NGOs have set up shop close by and help these artists in finding work. All prior efforts to rehabilitate the colony residents, since it was set up after Independence, has failed. This project might work, but where are they going to send the residents during construction?" asks K L Gupta, who runs a small kiosk in the Colony.

Heading: Cable operators asked to pay up - Indian Express
Content:
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has arrested an NRI for reportedly possessing contraband drugs.

According to sources, Harish Joshi was picked up by the DRI team on Monday night from DLF Phase V in Gurgaon. It was initially believed that he had been abducted. Joshi, vice president of Grimus Group of Companies, had just reached the entrance of his office in DLF Phase V, when six persons in a Toyota Qualis forced him into their car. They then drove away with him, sources said.

"The watchman at Grimus informed us that some unknown persons had abducted Joshi. We reached the spot and also launched an investigation. Later, we got to know that a central agency team had detained him on the charges of possessing heroin," said a senior police officer on condition of anonymity. "It was confirmed on Tuesday morning that the DRI had arrested him," the officer added.

Joshi's wife was in Kerala at the time of his arrest. His son lives in Canada. Officials of DRI, Delhi Zone, were not available for comments.

Heading: New course on Indian culture at DU - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Consumer Commission sounded a note of warning to cable operators who provide connections to subscribers without checking the quality of wires. The Commission has asked a cable and network operator to pay compensation of Rs 50,000 to the widow of a man who was electrocuted after he touched an uninsulated cable wire.

The Commission, presided by Justice J D Kapoor, took to task Prem Kapoor, a cable operator in Shahdara, and Mukesh Yadav, in-charge of Transex Cable Network.

Sher Singh died on May 28, 2004 when he tried to reconnect the cable connection to his television set after cleaning his house. Wife Kiran Devi then moved the consumer court against the cable operator and Transex Cable Network, claiming her husband died due to gross negligence of safety on their part. The cable operator, though, denied the charges.

Prem Kapoor and Yadav denied they had given cable TV connection to the family. Singh's wife gave the consumer panel evidence in the form of various documents to establish that the two had approached her husband for installing a cable connection, and charged them Rs 250 per month for the services. She also produced before the Commission a copy of the FIR lodged against Kapoor and Yadav under the penal provision of causing death due to rash and negligent acts.

Lending credence to the records, Justice Kapoor held the duo guilty of "deficiency in service" for not ensuring safety of their subscriber.

Heading: NCP legislator breaks away from fold, could form new party for Gurjjars - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi University is all set to launch a new certificate course for students on appreciation of Indian art and culture.

The university has roped in five of the most famous names in the present Indian art scenario — photographer Raghu Rai, Kathak exponent Pandit Birju Maharaj, sitar maestro Ustad Asad Ali Khan, painter Anjolie Ela Menon and renowned puppeteer Dadi Pudumjee to introduce students to their individual field of expertise.

The course will have 10 lectures of two hours' duration each, from September to December, at the university's Viceregal Lodge.

Heading: ‘Govt in Delhi will not be formed without BSP’ - Indian Express
Content:
With the Assembly elections in Delhi creating new political equations, another faction emerged on Tuesday as Ram Vir Singh Bidhuri, Nationalist Congress Party legislator from Badarpur, resigned along with two councillors of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi belonging to the party.

He is now planning a national meet of the Gurjjar Mahasangh that had pushed for reservations for Gurjjars in Rajasthan and could declare the formation of a new political party of the Gurjjar community in Delhi, sources close to the legislator said.

Sources in the Gurjjar Mahasangh say the Gurjjars, along with a small faction of rebels from the Nationalist Congress Party's Maharashtra division, could join hands to form a new party.

"We're preparing the ground for a way to handle the anti-secular parties like the BJP in Delhi," he said.

The meeting has been scheduled for September 13 in Delhi, and Gurjjar leader Colonel Kirori Singh Bainsla, who had led the Gurjjars in Rajasthan, could also attend the meeting, sources told Newsline. Gurjjar leaders from Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Delhi would be participating in the meeting. Speaking to Newsline from Pilupura, a source close to Colonel Bainsla said, "He (Bainsla) has been holding meetings of (Gurjjar) leaders and will take a decision soon."

Bidhuri was the president of the NCP's north India division and part of the five-member All India Working Committee of the party. He sent his resignation to party president Sharad Pawar along with Mahesh Awana and Mamta Sharma, MCD councillors from Mithapur and Jaitpur respectively, on Tuesday.

He had been a part of the 25-member delegation that had held talks with representatives of BJP government in Rajasthan in June and got the nod for a special status — Extremely Backward Caste —approved for the Gurjjar community. "We are now looking to unite the north India division of the NCP and the Gurjjars of all states to form a new front," he told Newsline.

However, he refused to divulge whether the Gurjjars and the rebel NCP members would be declaring the formation of a political party but did not deny the possibility.

Heading: Sisters mowed down by chartered bus in Seelampur - Indian Express
Content:
In the run-up to the Delhi Vidhan Sabha polls, the Bahujan Samaj Party has been busy trying to establish itself in a city that has been dominated by just two parties so far. The party was the first to announce the list of candidates.

Newsline spoke to the General Secretary of the Delhi Unit Kanwar Singh Tanwar.

You are said to be the man behind the final list of candidates and the selection process. How were those done and what are the preparations of the party like?
We are a new entrant in Delhi and the party needed to kick off its campaign earlier to build a strong base. I have been in social service for many years now and understand the issues of the common man. Mayawatiji trusted me due to my work at the grassroots level. The selection was done strictly on the basis of the amount of social work every candidate was involved in. We have a good list of candidates who have been working on the ground longer than those of the BJP or the Congress and there are 17 councillors from our party in the Municipal Corporation of Delhi. We believe the government in Delhi will not be formed without BSP this time.

How many seats do you think you will be able to win in these elections?
There are at least six seats in which we are very strong. Some other seats where we are somewhat strong need some work and it is being done. We think we will win at least 12 seats in the upcoming elections.

How do you think the BSP will be a part of the government in Delhi?
The BJP and Congress governments have focused only on city-centric issues during their rules. Poor people from the outskirts and unauthorised colonies have been neglected. Migrants from other states are treated as second grade citizens. Even now the two parties are fighting over mundane issues and holding rallies where hardly any people from these sections turn up. Mayawati has announced that we will complete the process of regularisation of colonies within two months if we are a part of the government. The neglected sections, fighting for their rights will win us the elections.

Who comprise these 'neglected sections' ?
Look at the Valmikis — the sweepers who keep the city clean. There are at least 1.1 lakh of them working in pathetic conditions. Gurjjars of outer Delhi have been neglected in all constituencies and there is no water, electricity or employment for them in these areas. Migrants from Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and other states live in pathetic conditions and the government does nothing about them. People from many other communities have been neglected in various constituencies in Delhi and we will address their issues. We will get them their rights and they will win us the elections.

Delhi has tradionally not voted along caste lines unlike other states. What are these 'communities' that you think will help you win the elections?
We have candidates from all communities depending on the composition of the constituencies. Jats, Gurjjars, Yadavs, Vaishyas, Baniyas, Muslims and Punjabis have all been given tickets to address the issues of the neglected communities. Look at any policies framed by the governments in Delhi, whether it the BJP or the Congress — none have touched the issues of the common man; price rise or power woes.
