With film, TV and advertising crews on constant prowl for new ways of exciting audiences, provincial settings and people living in them have become popular tools in providing an attractive edginess for audiences tired of glamorous escapism. So presumably Vogue India did not think it was doing anything exceptionally sensational or out of the ordinary when it decided to plan a photo shoot in Jodhpur using local residents to model a range of branded luxury accessories. Certainly nothing to warrant the violent response it has sparked off across the world from the Indian media, the western press including venerable dailies such as The New York Times and The Independent to anonymous observers in the blogosphere.

What the fuss is all about is a 16 page photo-feature that shows, among other things, middle class families on two wheelers with the woman carrying handbags said to be costing upwards of $ 1000 apiece; a local man sipping tea with his pals, sporting a leather D&G hat, a baby with a 100 dollar bib, a farmer holding up a Burberry umbrella and young Rajasthani women adorned in traditional finery with Miu Miu and Alexander McQueen on their feet.

Social commentator Kanika Gahlaut called the feature vulgar. Pavan K. Varma, author of The Great Indian Middle Class maintained that "These people (the 'models') have been used as commodities to sell fashion". The New York Times pointed meaningfully to a recent World Bank figure that has half of India's population living on less than $1.25 a day. All these are valid criticisms. Yet, there is something baffling about the sharpness of the response. Commoditisation and conspicuous consumption are trends we have lived with for a long time now. And an awareness of India's poverty has not prevented the western press from wholeheartedly supporting India's moves towards liberalisation. What, then accounts for the sudden negative reaction?

To some extent, it is the nature of the provocation. Unlike similar photo features shot in provincial settings, the Vogue India feature has used locals to actually model the goods rather than merely swell a crowd which gives the impression that the goods are for their use. In doing so the feature has revealed not just a lack of sensitivity about the blatant disconnect between means and affordability but also, unintentionally perhaps, brought into focus, the gulf between one India and another.

The very introduction to the feature conveys to the reader that she is being taken out of her natural habitat into what it calls 'authentic India'; as if it were something removed and even possibly exotic. The models, if described objectively would be people of simple means, engaged and content, if not exceedingly happy. Many of them are beautiful; some of them are adorned in the colourful and widely reputed finery of the region. But the magazine's intervention, which is not to discover but rather to locate its range of pricey boutique goods in this vivid terrain come across like early missionaries, carrying the civilisational tools of Hermes and Miu Miu. That the cost of even the cheapest of these trifles is equal to the monthly household budget of a family just deepens the sense of displacement.

To be fair to Vogue India, the feature appears to have been a well-intentioned addition to its special India feature -- an experiment with edge gone wrong, as can happen. What is of concern is that the feature reflects a relationship between the über-metropolitan and the non-metropolitan India that cannot be left unaddressed.

Mumbai-based Shah is the author of 'Hype, Hypocrisy and Television in Urban India'

Heading: UP Govt’s bid to drop case against BSP leaders - Indian Express
Content:
The Prime Minister's proposal to set up 16 central universities in states which do not have one already has encountered a roadblock. While the Human Resource Development (HRD) Ministry is in a hurry to push the Bill through during the next session of Parliament, the Finance Ministry has insisted that a clearance of the Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) be sought first. A high-level meeting will be held this week to resolve the issue and expedite the passage of the Bill through the next Parliament session.

Getting an EFC clearance for the proposal, already approved by the Cabinet, would mean a detailed expense assessment. The HRD Ministry is also worried that this could take up to a year, not a good prospect considering that elections are due in a few months.

"Last week, the Finance Department asked the HRD Ministry to get the EFC nod for setting up the central universities. The ministry, however, feels it is too early to go through the committee as the modalities have not yet been worked out," a senior official said. The EFC clearance is mandatory for projects estimated to cost over Rs 100 crore — the 16 new universities are expected to cost well above Rs 5,000 crore.

"It could take up to a year for the Finance Ministry to work out the modalities. This is unacceptable as the Government will soon face elections and the model code of conduct would come into force," added the official.

It is learnt that the HRD Ministry tried to push for an ordinance, but the Cabinet Secretariat said this could not be done as no prorogation notice had been issued by the President, and technically the House was still in session.

Earlier this year, the HRD Ministry had hurriedly pushed through six new IITs and drawn flak from no less than the Science Advisor to the PM, Prof C N R Rao. Now, the Prime Minister's Office too wants to focus on the quality of education that will be imparted from these new institutes.

THE NEW VARSITIES

• The 16 states which will get a Central University in the 11th Plan: Bihar, Jharkhand, Orissa, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu & Kashmir, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Goa.

• In three states, existing universities will be converted into central universities. These are Dr Hari Singh Gaur University at Sagar in Madhya Pradesh, Guru Ghasidas University at Bilaspur in Chhattisgarh and Goa University.

Heading: Now, JMM to remind Sonia of Cabinet berths - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh Government has written to the Faizabad district court to withdraw criminal cases against its two tainted ministers.

The two BSP ministers — Ram Achal Rajbhar (transport) and Dharam Raj Nishad (fisheries) — have criminal cases pending against them. Criminal cases of arson and riot were filed against them about 10 years ago at Gosaiganj police station of the district during the BJP rule in the state.

According to sources, a letter from the state Government's Home Department reached the Faizabad district court last week, stating the Government's intention to withdraw cases against Rajbhar and Nishad.

Hearing the case on Tuesday, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Gyan Prakash issued notices to the then in-charge of Gosaiganj police station Vinod Kumar Singh, and both the ministers, asking them to record their statements on September 19.

On April 15, 1998, the BSP leaders had started an agitation against the administration by jamming the Faizabad-Azamgarh Highway regarding some local problems and damaged public property, including some roadways buses.

Heading: Cong rath yatras in Gujarat from Sept 14 - Indian Express
Content:
After securing the Chief Minister's chair in Jharkhand, the Shibu Soren-led Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) has now set its eyes on its "share" of two berths in the Union Ministry.

Aspiring party MPs Teklal Mahto and Hemlal Murmu are camping here for the past couple of days to meet UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and inquire as to when the Cabinet expansion would take place to accommodate them. Soren is also likely to reach here on Wednesday to meet Sonia.

"Our quota of two berths, one Cabinet and the other Minister of State, is due. The Congress leadership has assured us that we will get our due. Today Soniaji was busy, so we are likely to meet her along with Guruji (Shibu Soren) tomorrow and hope a decision would be taken soon," JMM MP Teklal Mahto said.

By raising the demand for the berths in the Union Ministry, the JMM has clearly signaled that it was not satisfied with Jharkhand's top post.

Heading: Clear stand on CBI probe into PF scam: SC to UP - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress will hold rath yatras in all Lok Sabha constituencies of Gujarat to highlight the achievements of the UPA Government, especially the flagship programmes, and to dispel misgivings, caused by the Opposition BJP and the Left, about the Indo-US nuclear deal. The nuke deal will also be packaged as a proof of the UPA's commitment to providing electricity.

Similar publicity exercises relating to the n-deal are likely to be launched across the country after the Extended Congress Working Committee meeting on September 13, which will discuss the party's strategy for the next Assembly and general elections. The CWC meeting is also likely to endorse the state's as also the central government's stance on Amarnath land row, according to party sources.

As for the Gujarat publicity exercise, the idea is to involve top state leaders in each Lok Sabha constituency in this mass mobilisation programme in the state. The proposed rath yatras, scheduled from September 14 to October 9, will cover almost 9,000 villages. Around 104 large public meetings and 1,300 small ones are planned across the state during this period.

At present, the Congress holds 12 out of 26 Lok Sabha seats in the state. Although the ruling party at the Centre had got a drubbing in the last Assembly elections, party leaders believe the defeat was more a reflection of wrong selection of candidates and over-dependence on BJP rebels who turned out to be a liability, rather than a verdict on the Congress' mass appeal. Congress leaders also believe that the cult status of Chief Minister Narendra Modi may not have the same electoral appeal in the Lok Sabha elections as it had in the Assembly election.

The Congress hopes to improve its tally in the next general elections and, therefore, plans to be first off the block to hit the campaign trail.

Heading: SC issues notice to MP Govt on mining activities - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Tuesday asked the Uttar Pradesh Government if it agreed to a CBI inquiry into the multi-crore Ghaziabad District Court Provident Fund (PF) scam, in which 36 judges, including a sitting Supreme Court judge, have been named as beneficiaries. The UP Government has two weeks to make its stand clear before the apex court.

Earlier, it was brought to the court's notice that an SSP-level officer of the state police, who was involved in the probe, had hinted that there was pressure on investigators. In an official letter, which was produced in the court on Tuesday, the Ghaziabad SSP had told his seniors that it was "impossible" for the local police to investigate the case freely.

However, after its notice was drawn to the letter by the counsel for one of the petitioners, the Bench came down heavily on the UP Government for not bringing the letter to its notice on its own.

"Why did you not bring it to our notice all these days. The Chief Justice's Bench and another senior-most judge heard the matter. The Solicitor General appeared in the case, but it was never brought to our notice," the Bench said. It also took exception to the fact that the Government had concealed the contents of the letter from the court.

"You did not disclose it to the Supreme Court...We are extremely sorry with your approach," the Bench told the state's counsel. Thereafter, the Bench headed by Justice Arijit Pasayat decided to seek the response of the state government, as the consent of the state is necessary for ordering a CBI probe.

The Bench was hearing the petitions filed by the Ghaziabad District Courts Bar Association and Transparency International (TI), which are seeking a CBI probe into the scandal in which crores of rupees were fraudulently siphoned off from the PF fund between 2002 and 2007. Previous hearings in the matter have witnessed tension between the Bench and the counsel for the petitioners.

Hearing in the matter will resume on October 22.

Heading: Hazare warns HRD Ministry of NCTE graft - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Tuesday sought a reply from the Madhya Pradesh Government on why it should not restrain mining activity in the state.

Taking up the plea of Ajay Dubey, secretary of Prayatna, an NGO working on environment-related issues, the Bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan issued a notice on the petition challenging the Madhya Pradesh High Court's order that allowed mining activities to continue across the state.

In his petition, Dubey has pointed out that a large number of mining leases were functioning illegally across the state.

Dubey's counsel told the Bench that the State Pollution Board had also admitted that out of the total 5,069 mining leases across the state, 3,874 were operational and only 2,162 had necessary environmental clearances.

"The High Court overlooked that the whole procedure of grant of consent for operation of any mine of mineral leases of more than five hectares has to be cleared and passed through detailed processes as mining activity of minerals is presumed to have hazardous consequences on the overall environment and lives of thousands of people," the petition said.

Heading: Malaria parasite may be behind Kanpur deaths - Indian Express
Content:
The National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) is under fire again and this time it is social activist Anna Hazare who has shot off letters to the Human Resource Development (HRD) Ministry, Prime Minister's Office and to Sonia Gandhi alleging "largescale corruption in NCTE". The HRD Ministry has now been asked why no substantive action has been taken against NCTE and on Hazare's complaint, say top government officials.

Hazare has alleged that the body's western regional centre at Bhopal is steeped in corruption and is allowing dubious private institutions to proliferate. Officials also believe that the NCTE — a statutory body that regulates teachers' education — has resulted in unnecessary control and centralisation of affiliation/recognition of educational institutes that has brought in the associated problem of corruption.

"There is massive corruption in NCTE and I wrote about this to HRD Minister Arjun Singh, the PM and Sonia Gandhi last month, substantiating it with document-based evidence. The Bhopal regional centre of NCTE handles teacher-training institutes in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. All these states have a surplus of D Ed/B Ed teachers, yet more and more such private institutes, even with very poor facilities, are being constantly permitted by NCTE," Anna Hazare told The Indian Express.

"When I first complained on the issue some six months ago to the HRD Minister, the Bhopal centre was closed on his directions for a while. However, it's back to business now and so I wrote to the PM this time. If no action is taken against NCTE, which by engaging in corruption is weakening the very foundation of education in the country, we will bring a movement straight to the capital in protest," Hazare added.

In addition to Hazare, complaints against NCTE's alleged corrupt ways have also come from former Rajya Sabha Congress MP Ram Niwas Mirdha. HRD Ministry officials also confirmed that there were several complaints against the body.

Incidentally, the HRD Ministry had constituted a committee led by former education secretary Sudeep Banerjee to examine the relevance of NCTE. Suggesting that the body be repealed, the committee had recommended that Diploma in Education (D Ed) and Bachelor of Education (B Ed) courses could easily be conducted by universities and there was no need for an additional body like NCTE. The HRD Ministry had even circulated a Cabinet note on the same in May 2007 but then the matter was suddenly buried. With Hazare's complaint, the NCTE repeal issue has been revived and even the PMO is said to have asked the HRD Ministry to re-examine the issue.

Heading: 4 held with stolen uranium - Indian Express
Content:
Plasmodium vivax, one of the parasites causing malaria, which till date was thought to be merely causing infections, is believed to have turned fatal and could be behind the "mysterious fever" causing deaths in Kanpur.

About 50 people have died so far due to the fever in Kanpur. It has spread across 150 villages, mainly in four blocks — Amraudha, Malasa, Dherapur and Sarvankheda — home to 3 lakh people. Attributing the cause of deaths to malaria, experts in the National Institute of Communicable Diseases (NICD) are investigating if this strain, which otherwise is less virulent and doesn't cause deaths, has started killing people or if any new strain has emerged in the area.

"Generally, plasmodium vivax which is widely present in Kanpur doesn't cause mortality. If investigations show that this is the only strain circulating in the area, then it is a cause of concern," said Dr Shiv Lal, Director of NICD.

Preliminary investigations had pointed out that Hepatitis E, a form of liver disease, may be behind the deaths. According to experts in NICD, while Hepatitis E could partly be responsible for the deaths, the major cause is malaria. Last month, a team of experts from the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBCP) and NICD had visited the affected area.

"Preliminary results from Sanjay Gandhi Post Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences in Lucknow had confirmed that the deaths were due to Hepatitis E. But now, more samples have been brought for investigation," said an official. Experts from Delhi had also visited the spot and collected sera samples of the people down with fever, which will be investigated at NICD.

"Usually, P Falciparum is a deadly virus which kills people. But it will be strange if vivax is behind the deaths. We will investigate the matter with the help of National Institute of Malaria. A team from the institute is already in Kanpur," another expert said.

Heading: In villages, it’s up to old guard - Indian Express
Content:
The West Khasi police have arrested four persons for trying to sell a kilogram of uranium that was reportedly stolen from the Atomic Mineral Division (AMD). The packet had the seal of the AMD and Government of India. Those arrested include the headman of Lumkya village in Ri-Bhoi district, Samuel Nongmalieh. This is the second time this year that the police have arrested people trying to sell "yellow cake" in a packet with seals of the AMD and GoI.

Speaking to The Indian Express on Tuesday, West Khasi Hills district Superintendent of Police M Kharkhrang said the other three arrested have been identified as Jiington Starwell Kharjahrin from Nongstoin, Dispillar Lawphniaw from Wahkaji and Starwell Kurbah of Mairang. He said the police are looking for John Khongmin and had gone to his village on Sunday, but found him absconding.

Kharkhrang said Khongmin, who is the son of an employee working for the AMD, had supplied the packet. He said: "We will send a team to the AMD in Shillong to investigate how the packet was smuggled out." The packet will be sent to the AMD to verify whether it contains radioactive uranium.

Kharkhrang said the investigation will not only centre on this particular case but will try to unravel whether such packets, with seals of AMD and GoI, are freely available in the market. He said the probe would try to link this particular case with an earlier case when five persons were arrested by Shillong police in May for trying to sell a kilogram of "yellow cake" for Rs 26 lakh.

Heading: A day in a relief camp - Indian Express
Content:
As the rescue boats carrying food packets approach the flooded Laxmipur village in Purnea district, the young commander calls out to the three old men standing on the bank, asking them to assemble everyone in the village to collect their share of food.

Within minutes, a crowd of over 100 rush to the boats with outstretched hands. These are the people who have been refusing to leave their village in order to take care of their cattle and guard their homes and property from thugs roaming around freely during the night.

Besides a few women and children, most people who have braved the waters for the last 20 days and stayed back in their flooded villages are old men in their 70s, 80s and some even in their 90s. From Laxmipur to Balua Bazaar in Supaul, to Hanuman Chakla in Purnea, it's the same story.

"My son and his family left the village about a week back. If I leave too, who is going to look after the cattle? Besides, the moment the thieves know that there is no one left in our house, they will empty it," said a frail-looking 70-year-old Ghiasuddin.

In Balua Bazaar, Neelam Devi, aboard a rescue boat on her way to a safer destination, is sad that her father-in-law has been left alone.

"The old man did not want me to go. He said who will cook for him. But how could I have stayed back? My son would have died under these circumstances," she said. "The young men have left so that they can look for work. They are staying and eating in relief camps and at the same time also trying to hunt for opportunities to earn. Some of them, who have money, have brought food and other essential goods from the market," reasoned Sudhir Paswan, in his mid-40s, from Balua Bazaar.

However, the commander of the rescue boats in Laxmipur was not quite impressed. He made every effort to convince the old men to shift to relief camps. "Do you all want to die here? Come to the relief camps. You will get food, clothes and medical aid," he appealed.

Heading: Left, allies meet Patil, seek early monsoon session - Indian Express
Content:
With 125 well-ventilated tents, 50 toilets, a 24-hour medical team, a 28-member kitchen team, five hand-pumps, two big common tents and 20 permanent sheds, the Baidyanathpur paper mill mega relief camp along the Saharsa-Vaidyapur Road can possibly be termed as a model relief distribution centre in this flood-ravaged region. The camp started functioning on September 3 and accommodates 800 people from Gwalpara, Bihariganj, Murliganj, Triveniganj and Kumarkhand blocks of Madhepura, Sonbarsa Raj, Patarghat and Saur Bazar of Saharsa. The Indian Express spent a day at the camp.

7 am: Officials and volunteers distribute chewda (rice flakes) for breakfast — a 2 kg packet for each tent. Families huddle together for breakfast; some of them grumble that they have got less than others.

7.30 am: Nine-year-old Sukhiya from Gwalpara tells everyone that they will also get biscuits. Children along with their mothers crowd near the store. They are told that biscuits would be distributed around 11 am. The kids are excited; Rani from Kumarkhand announces that she is going to keep some for her grandmother. A baby girl was born the other day in tent number 13. Everyone is talking about the little one.

11 am: Children sit in rows, waiting for their share of biscuits. Camp in-charge Rakesh Mishra and his team ensure that there's proper distribution of food items. Over 300 children get biscuit packets.

11.20 am: On his daily inspection, District Magistrate R Laxman calls Mishra to find out if foodstuff is being distributed properly or not. Mishra gives a compliance report. The DM comes here for inspection once a day. Mishra is worried as children from neighbouring villages also queue up for foodstuff. "It's difficult to check people from neighbouring village who sneak in during meal time," he says, as around 50 boys can be seen crossing over to the neighbouring village with biscuit packets in their hands.

11.30 am: Baidyanathpur outpost in-charge Sub-Inspector Bhola Prasad Singh says he needs more policemen to distribute clothes. Mishra insists clothes should be distributed at night when villagers can't sneak in.

11.35 am: Special ADM M P Singh comes to inspect the camp kitchen where rice, pulses, potato and peas are being cooked for lunch. He is satisfied with the arrangement.

12.30 pm: Some people start assembling for lunch. There are others who prefer to wait.

1.30 pm: Nand Kishore from Saur Bazar says: "Food was tasty." A camp official remarks: "The Government will make them lazy by providing free lunch." He is immediately reprimanded by a senior officer, who says, "Ours is a welfare state and it is only a Rs 1,000 crore package for these people".

4.30 pm: People have just woken up from their afternoon siesta. Dr Akhilesh Prasad is busy attending to people complaining of body ache, fever, and so on. He has already gives medicines to 247 patients. Dr Prasad calls up other doctors on duty during the second and third shifts. Outside the medical camp, UNICEF distributes a plastic bucket, a mug and a soap to every tent.

5 pm: Children play kabbadi. One of the residents has his radio on and waits for a news-update on the flood situation in the state.

5.30 pm: Head cook Bhanu Bhattacharya gives instructions to his staff. Pulses like arhar and gram, potato, peas, soyabeans are being cooked for dinner. Bhattacharya says 200 kg of rice, 100 kg of potato and 40 kg of pulses is being cooked in each shift.

6.30 pm: Some 40 people who had observed Ramzan fast are served chewda. Some non-Muslims also join them. But the cooks are quick to identify them and ask if they have converted for food. Embarrassed, they leave.

7.30 pm: People go back to their respective tents. They are told that after dinner, children would be given clothes.

10.30 pm: Dinner is served.

1 am: It's finally time for Mishra to retire for the day.

Heading: Reality show participant fails to clear audition, attempts suicide - Indian Express
Content:
Accusing the UPA Government of jettisoning the monsoon session of Parliament, leaders of the Left, BSP, TDP and JD(S) on Tuesday knocked on the doors of President Pratibha Patil seeking her intervention for immediate convening of Parliament to discuss issues like the Indo-US nuclear deal.

However, leaders of Om Prakash Chautala's INLD, Ajit Singh's RLD and other UNPA constituents like AGP and Babulal Marandi's JVM stayed away from the delegation, once again bringing to the fore cracks in the coalition.

While the INLD is seriously engaged in talks with the BJP to sew up an alliance in Haryana for the next Lok Sabha and Assembly elections, AGP has almost tied up with the saffron party in Assam. Ajit Singh, agitated over Mayawati's decision to contest all the seats in UP, is undecided on his future course of action.

The leaders submitted a memorandum to the President saying the government's decision to jettison the monsoon session is a deliberate manipulation of established traditions concerning the sessions of Parliament. "A series of reports have appeared suggesting that the assurances made by the PM to Parliament and the country on the nuclear deal have been violated. Worse, there are reports that crucial information on the deal was concealed. These are serious matters concerning the sovereignty and security of India and its independent foreign policy. Parliament, therefore the people, are being deprived of their fundamental right to make the government accountable and answerable on these matters," they said.

Heading: Pepsi unit loses fizz in Punjab - Indian Express
Content:
A month after the mysterious death of Prasun Adhikary, a participant of a Bengali television reality show, another controversy rocked the same programme on Monday, when a 21-year-old participant consumed poison and collapsed at the audition venue.

According to sources, Tania Saha from Shyambazar, failed to clear the programme's audition and consumed poison from a bottle she had carried to the venue, Nehru Children's Museum, with her. She collapsed in the middle of the proceedings and the organisers rushed her to a city nursing home, where she is undergoing treatment.

Shortly after Tania was admitted, a police team from Hastings Police Station visited the Nehru Children's Museum and later the nursing home. The cops are now waiting for Tania's version of the story before deciding on a course of action. No FIR has been lodged in the case so far.

The organisers of the programme, Fatafati, meanwhile, maintained that Tania was not a participant and that they had nothing to do with her suicide attempt. However, sources disclosed that the girl had gone for auditions along with her boyfriend. She failed to make a mark in the audition, and maybe, in a fit of depression, attempted suicide.

The episode brings back memories of the August 9 incident when 23-year-old hotel caretaker Prasun Adhikary mysteriously fell to death from the fifth floor of a hotel in a Medinipur town after an alleged wrangle with organisers and participants of the same reality show.

Heading: Tourists stranded as CPM men abduct houseboat crew - Indian Express
Content:
Troubled with labour problems for the past four months, FritoLay India, a unit of PepsiCo India Holdings Ltd, is now planning to shift its production base from Punjab to its other locations in Kolkata and Pune. It had shut down its industrial production earlier this month.

While the company management has denied shifting out from Punjab, it has already shifted its production base from the state and moved out all its employees from the factory premises, which is locked since August 20. The current stand-off took a violent turn when on August 23 a few workers agitating outside the unit sustained injuries following a clash with the local truck union workers.

On Tuesday, the workers along with the Bharatiya Kisan Union, blocked for four hours vehicular traffic on the busy Sangrur-Patiala state highway. They were demanding the withdrawal of termination order of their union president Sanjeev Kumar and suspension of 12 fellow workers.

Set up in 1989 and producing 'Kurkure' and 'Lays' chips, the shifting of the production base has also come as a major blow to potato growers in the state. The unit utilised over 120 tonnes of potatoes every day and over 1,500 farmers from neaby areas benefited from the unit.

The indefinite lock-out at the unit has also hit industrial sentiment in the state, which is down across the country in the backdrop of problems Tatas are facing at their Singur plant.

The problem at Channo, however, is different. FritoLay India management alleges that the workers have been on a go-slow approach and production line has been on the decline by 70 to 80 per cent during the past four months, when labour trouble first brewed in the plant.

In May this year, the workers planned a strong workers' union and its new president, Kumar, claims to have asked for some hygienic uniform for the 250-odd casual workers in the factory, besides some other amenities. This, he alleges, led to his suspension in May this year and later his termination.

The management instead charges him of being the trouble-maker and is not in any mood to accept him back, though Sangrur MP Sukhdev Singh Dhindsa and the Sangrur district administration are working overtime to bring about a settlement at the unit.

With the workers at the unit not ready to budge till Kumar is also taken back, the talks between the management and the workers have failed.

MP Dhindsa on his part says, "Efforts are on to bring about a settlement and we are hopeful it will soon be reached. We are not wanting the company to move out of Punjab anyway. We are in talks with both parties and the management has agreed to revoke suspensions of all 12 employees. I am also pushing for taking back the terminated employee, which can happen only after some time."

Heading: Speculation over Sabari’s link with sons of ministers - Indian Express
Content:
The CPI(M) has disgorged trade union militancy into the backwaters of Kerala even as the Tourism Department, managed by Politburo member Kodiyeri Balakrishnan, has been campaigning for responsible tourism in God's Own Country.

On Saturday, CPI(M) men 'abducted' the crew of a houseboat, in which two UK couples were enjoying the backwaters. That day, the House Boats and Resorts Workers' Union, affiliated to CPI(M)'s trade union wing CITU, launched an agitation seeking a better pay package. The tourists were left stranded mid-lake for more than six hours with no one to take care of them, denting the tourist-friendly face of the state.

Some speed boat-borne union leaders, while patrolling the backwaters to ensure the success of the stir, spotted the houseboat carrying the UK couples. Soon, after a movie-style chase, the gang hopped on to the houseboat and forcefully took away the crew as well as the key of the boat. The agitators gave scant concern to the tourists' plea that their boat should be spared as the cruise had begun a day before the agitation.

Leaving four foreigners in the middle of the lake, the agitators sped past to their union office, where the boat workers were detained. Learning about the incident, the boat owner got his crew released with the support of the police. The crew could return to the boat only late in the evening.

The aggrieved tourists have filed a complaint with Minister Kodiyeri Balakrishnan. "...we booked three days and two nights on the backwaters of Kerala. We were enjoying the cruising until some communists took away our crew, leaving us stranded. My wife was ill and we might have needed medicine. But we were stuck without facilities, help or any explanation. If we report the matter in the UK, many tourists would drop their Kerala plans," said Krish Merresel, a UK tourist, in his complaint.

Heading: On everybody’s mind, Justice Sen remains out of sight - Indian Express
Content:
The mystery surrounding the business empire of Sabarinath, the young swindler who was arrested by the Thiruvananthapuram police last week, deepened further with allegations that sons of two CPM ministers supported his business dealings.

Quizzed by the media, CPM Central Committee member and state Health Minister P K Sreemathi said on Tuesday that she was not aware whether her son had links with the swindler.

Meanwhile, BJP youth outfit Yuva Morcha on Tuesday said a central agency should investigate the murky business dealings of Sabarinath. Morcha state president K Surendran said CPM Politburo member and Home Minister Kodiyeri Balakrishnan should reveal his family's connection with the owner of a Maruti Swift car bearing KL-01 AK 55 number plate. He said the car seized from Sabarinath's premises was later taken to a secret place to cover up his connection with a minister's son. Though a BMW car has been confiscated, the police have not revealed anything about the Swift, he said. Surendran's demand came after allegations of the police torpedoing the probe into charges against the young swindler after they stumbled upon his connections with the ministers' sons.

Heading: What Yedyurappa’s report card misses: Christians under siege - Indian Express
Content:
With Union Minister for Law H R Bhardwaj having stated that the impeachment motion against Calcutta High Court judge Soumitra Sen would be brought before Parliament, following a letter to the effect from the Chief Justice of India to the Prime Minister, Justice Sen preferred to stay incommunicado, at least for the media, on Tuesday.

At his residence at CL-117, Sector-II in Salt Lake, both cars were parked in the driveway. Two male household helps, who answered the door, said Sen was not at home and that his wife, too, was away at work. A woman who answered the residence phone said she had been instructed to tell all media that "no comments or interviews would be given by Sen".

The turn of events that has forced Sen to stay indoors and threatens to taint his career, even terminate it, has little reflection in his rise in the profession. Born in Guwahati on January 22, 1958 to a lawyer father, Sen came to Kolkata after completing his commerce degree and joined Calcutta University for his LLB.

Upon completing the law course, Sen enrolled as an advocate with the Calcutta High Court in February 1984, specialising in constitutional matters. In HC circles, he was known as a jaat lawyer — one who comes from a family of lawyers. He was member of the elite Bar Library Club, before being elevated to judge status in December 2003.

When contacted, his lawyer Subhash Bhattacharjee said Sen's wife Anuradha worked with Helpage India, while his daughter and son study in Class X and VIII, respectively. "He has an ailing mother, aged 80, who recently broke her kneecap following a fall. She is also being treated following an eye operation. The tension has been intense, he has not slept all night. His children are facing stigma and taunts at school," Bhattacharjee said.

The possibility of impeachment has evoked strong responses from the Kolkata lawyer community. A section of the Bar Association here said Sen had a flourishing practice in the High Court, and a keen understanding of law.

Bhattacharjee added that following a court directive ordering him to return the money he is alleged to have misappropriated as a Court Receiver, Sen did so with the interest included.

"Both SAIL and Shipping Corporation of India have stated in court that they have no interest in pursuing the matter. The order passed by an HC Division Bench headed by Justice P Chatterjee on the order of a single-judge Bench comprising Justice Kalyanjyoti Sengupta clearly states that Sengupta's order was 'without jurisdiction'. This order has not been challenged by anyone, and is the protection that Sen is enjoying right now," Bhattacharjee said.

Arunava Ghosh, senior advocate of the Calcutta HC, said all charges levelled by the single-judge Bench were set aside by the Division Bench later.

Heading: Valley IG who called Hurriyat leader ‘martyr’ shunted out - Indian Express
Content:
As he marked 100 days of his government on Tuesday, Karnataka Chief Minister B S Yeddyurappa fanned out across the state with his ministers presenting self-congratulatory report cards at every district headquarters.

However, among the "fulfilled" election promises and the budget pronouncements he highlighted, the one thing the BJP Chief Minister made no mention of was the spate of communally tinged incidents of recent weeks where Christians have seemingly been at the receiving end.

This included an unprecedented decision by the Davangere district administration to order the closure of three churches in the town, which are facing allegations of illegal conversions by outfits like the Hindu Jagarana Vedike. In his order sealing the three churches in the KTJ Nagar area, the Davangere Deputy Commissioner labelled them unauthorised.

Over the past two successive Sundays, police cases have been registered in Bangalore against nearly 25 people, leading to the arrest of as many as 12, including an American, on charges of "promoting enmity between different religious groups" and "insulting religious feelings", under Sections 153 A and 295 A of the Indian Penal Code.

Local police officers at the Frazer Town and Ulsoor police stations where cases have been registered said they had received complaints from members of Hindu groups alleging forcible conversions and use of inducements against the arrested persons.

Last Sunday, September 7, a mob of over 200 people attacked a church in the Bada village of the Davangere district over alleged forcible conversions.

"Over the last eight months to one year there have been allegations of forced conversions in Davangere district. Cases and counter cases have been registered. On Sunday some 200 villagers provoked by a handful of people attacked a church. We have arrested 17 people on charges of instigating the attack," Davangere Superintendent of Police Sandeep Patil said. According to the police in Davangere, they have identified 75 churches across villages in the district and have enhanced security in the face of the recent attack.

The incidents come on the back of the state Education Ministry issuing show-cause notices to over 2,000 Christian schools for staying shut on August 29 to protest the violence against Christians in Orissa.

Some leaders of the Christian community, including BJP MP and former police officer H T Sangliana, have staged protests in Bangalore over the alleged targeting of Christians and will submit a memorandum to the Chief Minister seeking better protection.

Speaking at the celebration of 100 days of his regime, Chief Minister Yeddyurappa said his government "wants to provide a peaceful, secure life for all citizens". "If any minority community person says we have done them any injustice I will resign immediately. We have attempted to look at everyone equally," he said.

Some police officers associated with the registration of cases of alleged proselytisation said there was nothing new about them, and that these were frequently registered but never highlighted. "Maybe because the BJP is in power they are getting highlighted," an assistant commissioner of police said.

Heading: Painting a storm - Indian Express
Content:
The recent high-level reshuffle in J-K Police in which the Government replaced Inspector General of Police (Kashmir range) S M Sahai has been prompted by the controversy surrounding the killing of Hurriyat leader Sheikh Abdul Aziz in police firing.

Sources say Sahai was shifted out to the Crime Branch as he had suggested that Aziz was a martyr and hoped his "sacrifice" would finally calm down the situation. Sahai had admitted that the police top brass had made a miscalculation when they allowed a procession to march along Muzaffarabad road on August 12. The Muzaffarabad road march was, however, directly handled by Inspector General of Police (north Kashmir) B Srinivas who along with a small contingent of police and CRPF men confronted the procession at Chahal — 21 km ahead of Baramulla — and opened fire, killing four protestors, including Hurriyat leader Sheikh Aziz, and wounding several others.

However, sources say, the Centre, especially National Security Advisor M K Narayanan, was given a different input, suggesting that Aziz had been shot from behind and he was killed because of a group clash and not in police firing.

Though Srinivas had categorically stated that the police had not even begun investigation when Narayanan made a statement — that a police bullet did not kill Aziz — he had termed the police firing at Chahal a bonafide act because otherwise "the protestors would have been confronted by the Army's Rampur brigade, (2 km ahead of Chahal)".

Sources say the axe fell on Sahai for another reason as well. He had been advocating that law enforcement agencies must not confront the protestors and allow the cathartic outburst as the public was constantly comparing the intensity of police action in Kashmir with Jammu where the police had exhibited more restraint even when police posts were attacked by mobs. However, the statement about Aziz's "martyrdom", sources add, became the final nail.

However, there is a growing criticism of the recent Government reshuffle of the police top brass. The highest level decision-making body in Governor Vohra's dispensation, the Administrative Council, comprises three advisors — S S Bloeria from Jammu city, C Phuntsok from Leh and H H Tayabji, a retired IAS officer from Mumbai. The council, however, does not have any representation from the majority community of Kashmir.

Heading: RTI champion is now a ‘victim’ - Indian Express
Content:
His international fame can be guessed by the fact that Forbes magazine called him the 'Picasso Of India'. He is one of the best-known artists from India. In early 2008, his painting Battle of Ganga and Jamuna: Mahabharata 12, fetched him $1.6 million, setting a world record at Christie's South Asian Modern and Contemporary Art sale. But back home, the 93-year-old Maqbool Fida Husain remains caught in controversies. On Monday, the Supreme Court refused to initiate proceedings against him for hurting sentiments with 'obscene' paintings. Here's a list of his brush with controversies:

• In the 1990s, some of Husain's works became controversial because of their portrayal of Hindu deities in the nude. The paintings in question were created in 1970, but become an issue only in 1996 when they were printed in Vichar Mimansa, a Hindi magazine. The controversy escalated to the extent that in 1998 Husain's house was attacked by Bajrang Dal activists and artworks were vandalised. Protests against Husain also led to the closure of an exhibition in London. Eight criminal complaints were filed against him. In 2004, the Delhi HC dismissed these complaints.

• On February 6, 2006, India Today published an advertisement titled "Art For Mission Kashmir". This advertisement had a painting of Bharatmata as a nude woman posed across a map of India. Organisations like Hindu Jagruti Samiti and VHP protested against Husain displaying the painting on websites and in exhibitions in north Europe. On February 7, 2006, Husain apologised and promised to withdraw the painting from an auction. The painting later appeared on his website.

• In February 2006, Husain was charged with hurting sentiments of people because of his nude portraits of Hindu deities. A series of cases were filed against him in Pandharpur (Maharashtra), Indore (Madhya Pradesh) and Rajkot (Gujarat). A non-bailable warrant was issued against Husain after he failed to respond to summons. The artist left the country stating that "matters are so legally complicated that I have been advised not to return home". The apex court clubbed these complaints together on a plea by Husain, who said he was too old and ill to travel to fight the cases, and sent them to the High Court in September last year. On May 8 this year, the Delhi High Court dismissed the criminal complaints. Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul said the allegation that Husain's paintings were obscene were baseless. On September 8, the Supreme Court upheld the HC ruling and dropped legal proceedings in three cases against him.

• At the age of 92 Husain was to be given the Raja Ravi Varma award by the Kerala Government. The announcement led to controversy and Sangh Parivar organisations campaigned against the granting of the award and petitioned the Kerala courts. The Kerala High Court granted an interim order to stay the granting of the award until the petition had been disposed of.

And they were targeted too

1949: An F N Souza work was termed "obscene" and the police removed it from a Bombay Art Society exhibition. His flat was raided and he shifted base to London.

1954: Akbar Padamsee was arrested for displaying a canvas titled Lovers at Jehangir Art Gallery. The police arrested him and pointed out that under Section 292 of the IPC, the painting was obscene. However, the court exonerated him, ruling that Section 292 cannot be applied to artists exhibiting in galleries.

2005: Chintan Upadhyay sparked off controversy when he sat nude as part of his exhibition titled Baar Baar, Har Baar, Kitni Baar? in Vadodara. The artist was protesting against the 2002 Gujarat riots.

2006: Rajendra Kapse's show titled Goddy was pulled down at Tao Art Gallery, Mumbai, after anonymous threat calls were received.

2006: A police complain was launched against Sanjeev Khandekar and Vaishali Narkar for artwork created by them and put on display at the Jehangir Art Gallery in an exhibition titled Tits Clits n Elephant Dick. The complainant had described the paintings and sculptures as "semi-pornographic".

2007: VHP activists stormed into the exhibition hall of MS University, Vadodara, and vandalised the paintings of final-year postgraduate student Chandramohan, terming them as "vulgar". Chandramohan's arrest was followed by protest meets organised by artists, after which he was released.

Heading: Ahead of India visit, Prachanda stuck between Govt, party agenda - Indian Express
Content:
The Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) has received an unusual complaint from a 'victim' of the file-noting disclosure regime ushered in by the Right to Information (RTI) Act.

The complainant is none other than A N Tewari, former DoPT secretary who was responsible for drafting the RTI Act and, shortly after its enactment, was appointed Central Information Commissioner. In his three years in the Central Information Commission (CIC) Tewari was known to be walking a tightrope since he advocated a practical disclosure of file notings as against what he described as an idealistic disclosure.

But little did he realise that he would become party to the perils of file disclosures and end up with a legal notice with a demand of compensation of Rs 1 crore.

Tewari, last month, informed Chief Information Commissioner Wajahat Habibullah as well as the DoPT about the legal notice he received, thanks to disclosure of notings of a sensitive appointment file he signed in 2004.

The controversy comes at a time when the DoPT continues to maintain on its website that file notings were exempt from disclosure via the RTI Act, which has been challenged by the CIC, resulting in disclosure of notings in hundreds of cases.

The file in question dealt with the appointment of James K Joseph, a former accountant general of Kerala, who was selected as the administrative member of the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) located at Kochi. The selection committee was headed by Justice K G Balakrishnan (the present Chief Justice of India), but due to objections raised by DoPT officials and the Intelligence Bureau, Tewari revoked the selection order.

The notings of the sensitive file were given by the DoPT to an RTI applicant in Jharkhand, who had applied for the post of being a judicial member of the CAT and shared these with Joseph, whose earlier request for the same file notings had been turned down by the DoPT.

Joseph's legal notice, dated May 2008, available with The Indian Express, names Tewari as well as the former joint secretary and Director of the DoPT, both of whom wrote lengthy observations on the appointment file.

It has charged the three officers with making notings which are "malicious" and "defamatory" and alleges that the complainant was "injured and pained on getting the information about the file notings which contains malicious and fabricated imputations, this is a wilful omission and breach of statutory duty".

When contacted, Tewari said the Joseph case had been taken up by him at a meeting of the CIC and that he had also informed the DoPT about the development.

He said, "This is an example of the perils of indiscriminate disclosure of file notings. While there is much in favour of disclosure of file notings, it should be done in a limited and restrained manner. Some guidelines are needed on which file notings should be given to RTI applicants and others kept out of the transparency regime."

Heading: MNS rejects Jaya apology, stir on - Indian Express
Content:
The CBI on Tuesday filed a chargesheet against Uttar Pradesh Home Secretary Mahesh Kumar Gupta and two others for alleged manipulation in selecting candidates for the state Information Department in 1998 and taking "illegal gratification".

The chargesheet was filed in the designated CBI court at Lucknow against Gupta, a 1987 batch IAS officer, Prabhat Kumar Sinha, a Provincial Civil Services officer and the then Additional Director, and Raj Gopal Singh Verma, the then Deputy Director of UP Information Department.

According to the chargesheet, Gupta, during his tenure as Director of Information, was heading a committee which would make appointments for Group C in the Information Department. The CBI alleged that Verma, who was appointed as nodal officer by the committee, tabulated the results of the written test in a computer, copied it in a floppy and loaded it in his home computer.

"Thereafter, they started contacting the prospective candidates and collected illegal gratification from them for selecting them for the posts," the chargesheet claimed. It annexed statements of candidates recorded by the CBI that they had paid money to the Deputy Director when he visited their homes.

The list of successful candidates so selected was prepared and put up after being duly approved by Gupta but was shot down by the then Chief Minister Kalyan Singh. The appointments file was sent to him without the sheets showing the marks obtained by the candidates in the written test and the interview.

(with PTI)

WHAT CBI SAYS

UP Home Secretary Mahesh Kumar Gupta had, as Director of Information 10 years ago, accepted bribes to appoint Group C staff in the Information Department.

Raj Gopal Singh Verma, then Deputy Director in the Department, asked candidates for money, which another officer, Prabhat Kumar Sinha, then delivered to Gupta.

Then CM Kalyan Singh, however, shot down the list sent by Gupta. A candidate filed a petition in the Allahabad HC, and the court called in the CBI.

Heading: Cabinet may take up Services’ pay  grievances - Indian Express
Content:
A day after a fiery speech by Raj Thackeray addressed to a gathering of mediapersons and a consequent gag order served by the police, at least 1,000 Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) workers across the state were served prohibitory orders under Section 144 of the Criminal Procedure Code even as hundreds were detained in Mumbai by policemen keen to avert trouble.

Though Jaya Bachchan apologised in an interview published on Tuesday morning, the MNS said it would not suffice, and demanded that the SP leader apologise publicly, on television if necessary. "Our stance will remain the same and the agitation will continue till she (Jaya Bachchan) renders a public apology," said Nitin Sardesai, a spokesperson for the party. "The police have detained several party workers — at least five to seven persons at each police station," he added.

On Monday, the MNS chief had demanded that all films and promotional campaigns featuring Amitabh Bachchan and his family members be banned after Rajya Sabha MP Jaya Bachchan made an apparent light-hearted remark that she would speak in Hindi as she belonged to Uttar Pradesh.

"It seems like the democracy of this government is of the people, by the people and for the people of UP and Bihar. The police are using any excuse to detain our workers. They are hunting and searching out our workers," said Shirish Parkar, another MNS spokesperson.

Shubho Shekhar Bhattacharjee, CEO of Planman Motion Pictures, producers of The Last Lear, said there will be no change in the release date of the film. "We're going ahead on September 12. Our promotional campaign is on. We've got the go ahead from the Censor Board and other important film bodies to release the film. Beyond this, we don't think any outside party can dictate terms to us. The Last Lear will release this Friday," he said.

Heading: Limited appeal - Indian Express
Content:
Grievances of the Armed Forces about the 'lowering of status of defence officers and men' in the new pay panel are likely to be taken up at a meeting of the Union Cabinet on Thursday. Sources said the Cabinet was set to discuss the issue after chiefs of the Armed Forces insisted that the matter be resolved at the top political decision-making level in a letter to the Defence Minister.

While a representation on the issue has been forwarded to the Defence Ministry and Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, the forces have firmed up a detailed note, bringing out seven major points that need to be addressed to keep the parity of Armed Forces personnel with their civilian counterparts.

The disparity of pay bands, where the director rank has been moved into Pay Band 4 but the Lt Col and equivalent rank has been retained in Pay Band 3, is a major issue of contention. The Armed Forces are contending that while earlier, a Lt Col got the same pay as an IAS director and Rs 800 more than a non-IAS director, after the new pay panel, he gets Rs 14,000 less than an IAS director and Rs 11,000 less than a non-IAS director.

Heading: Roger Gets the Final Word - Indian Express
Content:
• Shekhar Gupta has rightly asserted in his 'India Waiting' that India's political leadership has failed to encourage the emergence of young, ambitious, articulate and talented leaders at the national level. Even the rise of Mayawati does not hold much promise for national politics because of her casteist approach. A young and talented leader with a secular frame of mind could give the country and its polity a new direction. If we could have fixed a retirement age in politics, the old order might have yielded to a new one.

— Ved Guliani Hisar

Another time

• Shekhar Gupta has made an interesting observation. It strikes me that India's failure to regenerate its political leadership is a post-independence phenomenon. Before 1947, all sections of society threw up bright and dedicated leaders who sacrificed everything they had for the country. Those who join politics today, do so for power and wealth. Moreover, the lack of intra-party democracy stops honest and capable aspirants in their tracks. Given such conditions, can we really expect self-respecting, dedicated and selfless young people to work in politics?

— Satish Dayal Delhi

 

Truth tellers

• The Indian ethos of being true to one's words is still alive. The NSG waiver is a testimony to this. Decades earlier, A.B. Vajpayee promised a suspension of nuclear testing, and his successors kept that promise. Today, India's on the moral high ground. Despite the reservations of some NSG members, a statement by India's foreign minister on nuclear tests and non-proliferation is enough for India to get a consensus waiver. Internal differences aside, let us take pride in India's unwavering moral compass.

— R. Narayanan

Ghaziabad      

 

Almost there

• Yet another hurdle has been crossed by the Indo-US nuclear deal. It's now a win-win situation for the UPA government. The NSG states approved the US proposal to lift the embargo on nuclear trade with India. Now the US Congress will have to ratify the deal. After so many impediments, beginning with the Left pullout, the trust vote, the leak of the nuke letter, India's status as a nuclear power has finally been acknowledged by the international community.

— Mohd Mubarak Ranchi

 

Come clear

• Is the ecstasy surrounding the nuclear deal waiver justified? The PM repeatedly assured Parliament and the people that our sovereign right to nuclear tests remains unaltered. His foreign minister, however, told the NSG that our commitment to a moratorium on nuclear testing was virtually permanent. Why hasn't the NSG endorsed our nuclear weapons programme? In effect, haven't we accepted the non-proliferation regime? If it is so, why not sign the NPT and the CTBT, instead of playing deceitful games?

— M. Ratan Delhi

Heading: Capello’s England take on familiar foes Croatia - Indian Express
Content:
It's just possible that Roger Federer might have won more public love from a single defeat — that epic Wimbledon final — than he won from four entire years of incomprehensible dominance.

Once he arrived here for the US Open, his winking wit seemed to return, and he said strangers wished him back to No. 1 from his newfound settlement at No. 2 behind Rafael Nadal. The 27-year-old man from one of the world's most un-New York places — the staid Basel, Switzerland — repeatedly said he felt like a New Yorker.

So as the grand arc of Federer's celestial tennis career resumed its upward track Monday evening, the Arthur Ashe Stadium DJ played Still The One, and Federer soon said puckishly, "It's great, the guy putting on the music being my fan, right?"

He had summoned much of his vast repertoire and sapped the drama out of a US Open final and his 6-2, 7-5, 6-2 victory over first-time Grand Slam finalist Andy Murray of Scotland loosed a barrage of edits to the tennis record books.

It made Federer the first player with five consecutive US Open titles since Bill Tilden won six from 1920-25. It made Federer the first player to win five consecutive titles at two different Grand Slam tournaments because he won five straight Wimbledon titles between 2003 and 2007. It gave Federer 13 Grand Slam titles, halving his deficit behind Pete Sampras's record 14. It gave Federer 34 straight wins in Flushing Meadows, 35 if you count a walkover in the fourth round of the 2004 tournament.

Perhaps most poignantly, though, it gave Federer one Grand Slam title in 2008 that might quickly climb his rankings of most cherished, and it made him a de facto New Yorker.

"It's incredible the amount of people here in New York that just come up to me and recognise me now and sort of wish me luck, cab drivers screaming out I'm still the guy, and, 'You can do it.' It's great, you know. "I think the French Open loss was brutal, but I got over that one pretty easily, played great on the grass, and had a really tough loss at Wimbledon which, you know, I was proud to be part of such a great match, but at the same time, you know, it just sort of made me sad, you know, not having won that great epic match. Maybe I was always dreaming about it and not winning it, you know.

'Always positive'

"I was always positive, you know."

All along, as he lost 12 different matches to nine different players and struggled in the hardcourt season, losing an Olympic quarter-final to James Blake, he dealt with the world's acknowledgement of his fresh imperfections while winning only two titles before the US Open.

The US Open cured that, even if he still doesn't feel he's moving as he once did.

After a frenetic final point on which Federer, 27, menaced at the net and Murray, 21, scampered around using his uncommon court coverage, Federer finally hit an overhead that Murray couldn't quite squeeze back. He then sank to his knees and rolled around on the New York concrete.

"This is a very special moment in my career," he said immediately afterward.

His slightly muddled year ended with one heck of a New York garnish.

Heading: Thousands flock to Bolt’s homecoming - Indian Express
Content:
Fabio Capello faces his first real test as England coach when his team plays old adversary Croatia in a tricky World Cup qualifier on Wednesday.

The Italian has so far led England only in friendlies and in Saturday's stuttering 2-0 win over lowly Andorra in the first qualifier for the 2010 World Cup.

Croatia have never lost a home competitive game and knocked England out of contention for the 2008 European Championship with double qualifying victories over Capello's predecessor, Steve McClaren. England will be missing key midfielder Steven Gerrard, who underwent groin surgery late last month. England's defensive stability could be partially satisfied by the return of central defender Rio Ferdinand. The Manchester United player missed the Andorra match because of back and neck injuries, but has returned to training. Striker Jermain Defoe acknowledged that England would be happy with a draw. "A draw would be a great result in Croatia," he said.

But, the Croats, ranked fifth in the world, are confident. Luka Modric — who was instrumental in Croatia's 3-2 Wembley win last November — is adamant that he and his team mates have only improved over the period.

Heading: Despite loss, Murray has reason to smile - Indian Express
Content:
Thousands of Jamaicans braved heavy rain to give triple Olympic gold medallist Usain Bolt a rapturous welcome home.

Fans lined roads leading from the Norman Manley International airport to the heart of New Kingston to cheer Bolt, who electrified the Beijing Games with his 100m-200m sprint double and 4x100m relay triumph — all in world record times.

Bolt, 22, arrived from London shortly before 2pm on Monday and was mobbed by fans, mostly airport workers who abandoned their posts to get a glimpse of him. More official greeters, including Prime Minister Bruce Golding, were pushed aside in the rush to welcome the athlete.

Mad scramble

Members of the throng banged on the sides and trunk of the bright red BMW convertible that was provided by one of Bolt's local sponsors to show their appreciation, while reporters and photographers scrambled for good vantage points.

A motorcade of at least 15 vehicles wound its way from the airport to a New Kingston hotel, where a welcome reception was held.

The reception started nearly two and a half hours late because of the massive crowd and the rain. "I am feeling good right now," said Bolt, who had gone from his Beijing triumph in August to competition in Europe. "I am glad for this turnout and I am just happy to be home now."

World records

Bolt's three gold medals in Beijing all came in world-record times. He won the 100m in a stunning 9.69 seconds, beating his own 9.72sec set in May in New York. He lowered American Michael Johnson's 200m world record to 19.30sec, while the Jamaican relay team, on which he ran the third leg, clocked 37.10sec.

Golding said Monday's function was just a precursor to an official welcome home celebration for all Olympians from Jamaica, with plans in the works for a four-day celebration for the entire team to start on October 3.

Heading: In top gear, but ready to slow down - Indian Express
Content:
Andy Murray had plenty to smile about after his rousing run at the US Open came to a shuddering halt at the hands of Roger Federer.

The sixth-seeded Briton had shocked Spanish world number one Rafael Nadal in four sets in the previous round to reach his first Grand Slam final at the age of 21.

"I'm disappointed right now and I wish I could have done a few things better and given myself a few more opportunities," Murray told reporters.

"But whenever it sort of sinks in, it's obviously been a very good couple of weeks. I'll try my best to work on my game, work harder and hopefully come back and do better next time."

Murray, who had been bidding to become the first British man to win a Grand Slam since Fred Perry won the US title in 1936, was especially pleased with his fitness levels during the tournament.

"That was the most important thing for me over the whole two weeks," said the Scot, who increased the intensity of his training at the end of last season to improve his all-round strength and agility.

Overall, Murray has been delighted with his 2008 campaign. He has won three ATP titles, all of them on hardcourt surfaces, with a win-loss record of 41-14.

Heading: Dhawal hits the right spot - Indian Express
Content:
It takes a lot to fill Virender Sehwag's shoes. If you're a couple of months short of turning 20, have just about begun wearing the India cap, and first faced a seasoned bowler when Viru was already busy thumping the best in the world, perhaps it's asking for too much.

It's hard to imagine what could've been running in the mind of a young Virat Kohli when he was asked to walk out with Gautam Gambhir to open in the first one-dayer against Sri Lanka. As he faced 22 balls, struck a boundary, scored 12 runs and then lost his wicket to Nuwan Kulasekara — all in less than 25 minutes — Kohli first experienced what pressure meant at the highest level.

"My father passed away when I was 18 and it was a shock that I'm yet to get over. But it did make me a lot tougher mentally. Today, being able to cope with pressure is a way of life," he says. The 94 he scored for Delhi on the day his father passed away, and numerous innings of significance at the India A level, have all brought him to the point from where every emerging cricketer begins to focus on the big leap.

Starting early

"There is always pressure and you need to deal with it. I have always believed in my ability," says Kohli. No wonder then, that making his debut against the Lankans in their own backyard in place of an injured Sehwag didn't worry Kohli as much as it could have. What came to fore in the series was his positive approach and the confidence that made him look comfortable.

"I was nervous when I was asked to open but it wasn't like I was opening the innings for the first time. The crowd pressure and playing against (Chaminda) Vaas affected my performance a little. But after the first game I started to believe in myself more," says Kohli.

He says that because he's been playing in the middle-order for long, he's accustomed to a different mental set-up. As a middle-order batsman, "one has to be prepared for a lot of things." With Tendulkar and Sehwag sure to return, Kohli knows that for sometime in the future he'll have to settle for a place on the bench. "Let's see what happens. Everything keeps happening all the time," he says with a wave of his hand.

Long way to go

Dav Whatmore, who coached India's under-19 World Cup winning squad says Kohli's got the ability but still has to truly prove himself. "There is no doubt about his potential but he has just played only one series. Let him play some more matches and then he will be in a better position to judge for himself. There is no doubt in his ability," he says.

Kohli might have proven he's good enough to reach where he has, but now the pressure is on him to stay there.

Heading: Game over for Symonds? - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai mediumpacer Dhawal Kulkarni can count himself among the few lucky players who've managed to play for India A before making their Ranji debut. The last cricketer to do so was Rohit Sharma, the current India player and now, Kulkarni can only hope to follow in his footsteps.

It isn't common knowledge that Kulkarni was on the selection radar when Dilip Vengsarkar and his colleagues picked players for India's one-day series in Sri Lanka. More than pace, it was his consistency that made them take notice.

Representing India A against Australia A in Hyderabad, Kulkarni's two for 21 reduced the visitors to 62-3 on the rain-marred first day on Tuesday. Kulkarni is a prime example of cricketers coming to the fore through the Indian Premier League T20 tournament earlier this year.

At 19, when most players are searching for mentors, he got busy bowling alongside former South Africa skipper Shaun Pollock in the Mumbai Indians squad.

"It changed my career. There were certain things Pollock taught me and they're helping me now," he says. Kulkarni's eyes still reveal the excitement of having met and learnt from Pollock. Those numerous afternoon net sessions, bowling to the likes of Jayasuriya, gave him goose-bumps to last a lifetime.

"He taught me to bowl six to seven yards from the crease. If you can bowl and maintain a certain length, no batsman in the world can get you. He told me that you bowl to the batsman, and it's not the other way round. The batsman gets what you serve him," Kulkarni recalls.

Words like these changed the youngster for good. Throughout this India A series, he's been the most consistent and is fast getting well-versed in finding key breakthroughs.

"I am only trying to ensure that I bowl in the right areas. This has helped me lot. Earlier I used to feel the pressure of picking wickets but now I maintain a sort of calm and let the batsmen make a mistake. Pollock also told me how pressure helps you to rejuvenate," he added.

Eleven wickets in ten matches for Mumbai Indians in IPL gave Kulkarni a chance in the India A side for the Emerging players tournament in Australia last month. Now he's taken another step ahead.

Heading: Time & again: Advani beats Sethi to enter final - Indian Express
Content:
All-rounder Andrew Symonds may already have played his last match for Australia, Cricket Australia has indicated.

In a clear indication that the board is looking at life beyond Symonds, the CA chief executive James Sutherland said Symonds may have well be "lost to the team" but asserted there are plenty of quality players who can fill the void. "It would be a great loss but, at the same time, one of the great things Australian cricket is lucky to have is exciting young talent that is knocking on the door, waiting on the fringes," Sutherland told ABC Radio.

Symonds' absence would provide a gilt-edged opportunity to players like Shane Watson, Sutherland said. "People like Shane Watson may well get the opportunity they've yearned for so long in his absence." Symonds' career hit crossroads after he was sent home for going on a fishing trip instead of attending a compulsory team meeting. Symonds's act had the Australian leadership group enraged and CA was not amused either.

On his chances of never playing for Australia again, Sutherland said, "I don't think that's impossible. I think the message the Australian players have sent is that we want Andrew Symonds in our team, but we want Andrew Symonds absolutely committed and wanting to be there. They're really asking him that question," Sutherland said. "If he can't answer that question, it may well be that he's lost to the team," he added.

On whether the IPL money was behind Symonds's change in attitude, Sutherland said, "It's hard to say. He only played in the IPL for two weeks. I think there are a whole lot of factors and without Andrew sitting down and talking through some of his issues I don't think anyone really knows the answer to how he's been affected," he added.

Sutherland was also happy with the way the leadership group handled the episode. "I was really proud of them the way they did it. They could have taken a short-term view of it," Sutherland said.

Heading: Boxers switch sides, disqualified - Indian Express
Content:
Pankaj Advani is on a roll. After annexing the points format crown last week, the 23-year-old Bangalore lad inched closer to repeating the feat when he edged past Geet Sethi 1269-1003 in the semi-final of the time format at the World Billiards Championship on Tuesday.

Except for a brief period early on, Advani held the upper hand throughout the match and will now take on Devendra Joshi in the title clash on Wednesday. Joshi put it across Rupesh Shah 1228-820 in the other semi-final.

In the four-hour semi-final, Advani displayed his classic touch, making canons and playing with red ball at the top table. Though he had just three century breaks, it was the variety of knocking and compilation of breaks that really set him apart from Sethi.

"Full credit to the young lad for performing consistently," said Sethi. The eight-time world champion played well in patches and could have turned the tables when he was 300-plus behind with 18 minutes remaining —-Sethi had made some of the biggest breaks in this competition, but it simply was not his day.

"I thought I could have overcome the deficit at the end, but I missed badly," said Sethi. "I simply failed to maintain any consistency. Look at my breaks graph in the tournament, it kept on going down. First I had made the break of 885 in the first match, then 750, and then 400 and now I failed to catch Advani today though I could have done that. It's very frustrating," said Sethi.

And as Sethi, who generally never shows emotions, realised he was losing the game, he allowed himself to be human, breaking into a smile. "Today, I just cracked up. Not under pressure, but I thought my hand became heavy and I could not get the ball moving the way I wanted," he said of the narrow misses on the top table that halted his progress. "It was the same table and same balls I was playing with, but I could not do anything with it," he added.

Advani, on the other hand, couldn't hold back his joy. "When you know you are defending the title and when you come from 300 points down with less than 20 minutes remaining, it's special". Advani said he carried on his good form from the quarter-final win against Sourav Kothari. "But I never relaxed even though I had a 400-point lead with 20 minutes remaining," said Advani.
