Heading: Disco Dhamaka - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Punjab does a first, introduces environment education in schools - Indian Express
Content:
You have tried bungee jumping, hurdled through the white waters, and climbed a steep rock. You have parasailed high in the sky and you have tasted saltwater thrills on the crest of the waves. So, what next? Well, how about getting strapped-up inside an enormous plastic, air-cushioned ball and getting rolled down with a small push. I bet for adrenalin junkies and weak-hearted fun lovers. Zorbing or sphering, is something you wouldn't want to try. But the best part remains that no formal training is required to experience it.

The Beginning
The game began six years ago when inventors Dwane van der Sluis and Andrew Akers created unique PVC spheres called zorbs and rolled them down slopes with people inside. Since then, the sport has travelled to other corners of the globe with slight changes here and there. In India too, zorbing sees a slight change in the diameter of a zorb. The current diameter is either 10 feet or 12 feet depending on the number of people that are harnessed inside. There are nylon ropes in the transparent zorbs that keep the brave souls inside firmly in position throughout the entire topsy-turvy ride.

About Zorbing
Zorbing is the practice of travelling in a sphere, generally made of transparent plastic. The exercise is done usually for fun. Sphering or globe-riding is generally performed on a gentle slope, allowing the rider to roll downhill. It can also be done on a level surface or on water, permitting more rider control.

As of the sphere, it is a double-hulled sphere, with one ball inside the other with an air layer in between. Many spheres have straps to hold the rider in place, while others leave the rider free to walk the sphere around or be tossed about freely by the rolling motion. The inner and outer spheres are connected by hundreds of small ropes. Spheres generally have one or two tunnel-like entrances. At least two adults or three kids can be safely ensconced inside the bouncing bubble.

The sport can be enjoyed by people of all ages who don't mind being strapped inside an enormous clear plastic, air-cushioned ball. As the ball rolls down a long grass-covered slope, you spin around in a virtual anti-gravity form of weightlessness like an intoxicated space traveller. As you tumble head over heels, the build up of centrifugal force keeps you pressed hard against the plastic wall, so it's easy to 'go with the flow' and enjoy the revolving view outside.

Ideal Surface
There are specifications that have to be kept in mind while adapting this sport to Indian conditions. Zorbing is best experienced on golf courses and open manicured grounds with a slight elevation where there is an absence of sharp objects. Uneven plains that are interspersed with pebbles and rocks are likely to cause punctures in the zorbs.

Where to Head
Countries abroad have regular zorbing events, but it has caught up in India, especially Himachal Pradesh. The Solang Valley Resort in Himachal Pradesh and Dhanaulti Woods Swiss Camp in Uttaranchal have slopes that are ideal for zorbs to roll down at a uniform speed.

Precautions
Like any other adventure sport, Zorbing too needs to be carried out with certain precautionary measures. To begin with-
* Usually a team of four people handles the zorbing sessions and keeps an eye on the comfort levels of the zorbonauts.
* The team is responsible for pushing the transparent bubble, controlling its direction and stopping it immediately if any participant is scared.
* The ball usually traverses a distance of anything between 35mt and 50mt, but the maximum limit has been fixed at 100mt.
The writer owns adventure club, www.clubfootloose.com, and is a city based gemologist. Mail him at soli@clubfootloose.com

Heading: EVMs all set to debut in Kharar - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab has become the first state in the country to introduce environment education as a compulsory subject for all classes from I to XII in the state.

For the successful implementation and strengthening of environment education, the Union Ministry of Environment and Forests (MoEF) has released a monitory assistance of Rs 9 lakh to the state government.

The Punjab School Education Board (PSEB), which was assigned the job, started the first two-day workshop for teachers, educationists and writers from across the state in Mohali on Wednesday.

Speaking to Newsline on the sidelines of the workshop, PSEB senior scientific officer Shruti Shukla, who is the nodal officer for the project implementation, said while the textbooks of environment education for classes III-XII have already been prepared, a handbook to sensitise the teachers was being prepared.

"For development of the handbooks, which will be in four sections of primary, middle, matric and secondary, the suggestions and guidelines from eminent educationists and writers were procured during the workshop," Shukla said.

She added the two-year programme will involve training of the teachers and the incorporating of environment education in the school education. While environment education is separate subject from Classes III-V and XI-XII, it was included in other related subjects from Classes VI-X. The study and clearance of environment education is compulsory in all classes.

"We plan to come out with around 150 pages handbook with the help of 300-400 resource persons who have joined us in the workshop," Shukla said.

Addressing the workshop, PSEB vice-chairman Ranjit Singh Bajwa said many states had submitted proposals to MoEF to get this project, for which only Punjab was selected.

Since environment education is a new subject, which has been recently introduced under the directions of the Supreme Court, teachers are finding it difficult to teach.

"By propagation of environment education, Punjab will not only achieve sustainable development but will also improve the general environment of state and lives of common people," Bajwa said.

During the workshop, core groups will be formed to provide study material for the publication of handbook.

Heading: Patiala civic body employee attempts suicide, arrested - Indian Express
Content:
For the first time, the electronic voting machines (EVMs) will be used in the ensuing civic polls on September 14. One EVM will be installed in each of the 30 polling booths for electorates to exercise their franchise in electing 15 members to the Kharar Municipal Council (MC).

Kharar Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Rajeev Kumar Gupta, who is the Returning Officer (RO) for the MC polls, told Newsline that two polling booths have been established for each of the 15 MC wards.

The use of EVMs will not only facilitate early polling but will also help the counting process as the machines will take just nearly 15 minutes to count the polled votes, disclosed Gupta.

The polling, to be held from 8 am to 4 pm, will be followed by counting of votes at the respective polling booths and the results will thereafter be declared by the RO.

With a total of 29,873 electorates, including 15,474 males and 14,399 females, each ward on an average has 2,000 voters.

The low-key electioneering, meanwhile, has failed to enthuse the electorates and the usual blaring loudspeakers, poster war and election meetings still appears missing with barely three days to go for the civic polls.

The SAD-BJP combine, on Tuesday, had held the first massive election rally, which was addressed by its president Sukhbir Badal. Much to the surprise of the locals, Sukhbir, during his address, said the SAD-BJP combine had never ruled the Kharar MC ever since its inception after independence. It, however, seemed that Sukhbir was kept in the dark by local party leaders as the president of the previous elected body of the MC Ranbir Singh was from the SAD.

Punjab Cooperation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh and his son Jasjit Singh Bunny (Punjab State Cooperative Bank Limited Chairman), on Wednesday, addressed over a dozen election rallies in different parts of the town to garner support for the SAD-BJP combine nominees contesting on the "Rising Sun" election symbol.

Kharar Congress MLA Balbir Sidhu has, meanwhile, alleged widespread bungling in the preparation of electoral rolls and expressed apprehensions of rigging in the civic polls by the ruling alliance. Congress has fielded its candidates from all 15 wards on its party symbol "Hand".

Coded rules for polling day
Mohali District Magistrate Rahul Bhandari, on Wednesday issued certain prohibitions under Section 144 of the CrPC during the civic polls in Kharar on September 14. The carrying of arms, firearms, explosives and sharp-edged weapons has been banned within the Kharar MC limits on polling day. The polling day has also been declared as "dry day" with all liquor shops and taverns asked to remain shut and the hotels and restaurants prohibited from the service of liquor.

Heading: ‘Actors, directors have to prove - Indian Express
Content:
High drama was witnessed at the Patiala Municipal Corporation building where an employee, sweeper by profession, attempted suicide in full public and media glare.

Ravi Kumar, who had allegedly not reported to work for the past four months, was arrested by the police and charged with "attempt to suicide".

Eyewitnesses said Ravi came to the Corporation office in the morning accompanied by his family and a few photographers. He claimed he had not been paid salary for four months and was living in penury. Fed up, he said he wanted to commit suicide. After entering the MC Hall, he doused himself with kerosene oil and attempted suicide.

The MC staff, however, prevented him from igniting fire. The police was immediately called in and Ravi was arrested.

Mayor Ajit Pal Singh Kohli said Ravi had not reported to work despite requisite notices that were sent to him.

Heading: More outsiders than students on campaign trail - Indian Express
Content:
"Punjab is full of talented youth, who have enough talent to bag opportunities in movies, given their nature to work hard," said noted filmmaker Harry Baweja today.

Baweja senior was in the city to promote the Centre for Media and Entertainment Studies (CMES), which is due to start in Chandigarh and train students in various fields of the entertainment industry.

Talking to Newsline, co-chairman, CMES, Baweja said Bollywood lacks technicians and persons with talent. "The industry lacks trained manpower. I believe that if proper training is made available, students will definitely succeed in bagging good opportunities in the film industry," he said.

He said the institute will organise a North India Acting Contest that will provide new actors with a platform to showcase their skills. "If someone has good acting skills, he or she will definitely get a chance to perform on this platform. Though I might not take them in my movies, they would surely get a platform to showcase their talent," he said.

"All good actors and directors have had to prove their mettle to be at the top. People like Rajesh Khanna and Shahrukh Khan have all had to prove that they are talented as no producer will finance a project, which has people who do not have talent," Baweja said while talking to Newsline.

Refusing to shed light on his plans after Love Story 2050, he said he is working on the project. "I had taken some time off after the completion of my last project, and will now concentrate on the next venture," he said.

The auditions for the contest will be held at the Punjabi University in Patiala on September 17. Apart from that, auditions will also be held in other parts of North India. "The winner will get an opportunity to dance and dine with Harman Baweja, of Love Story 2050 fame," said Gulshan Sharma, CEO ITFT Education Group.

Heading: Accidents on Kharar-Mohali stretch claim 2 lives - Indian Express
Content:
PU elections: Lyngdoh Committee recommendations violated with impunity

With the Lyngdoh Committee recommendations making it mandatory that only regular students can contest the elections, all candidates are first-timers this year. The university, however, seems to have failed to notice the outsiders who are busy campaigning for their parties.

According to the guidelines issued by Panjab University, no outsider is to be allowed inside the campus during the campaigning and the election process. It is, however, the senior leaders of parties — they no longer study in PU and have a number of criminal cases registered against them — who seem to have taken the responsibility of campaigning.

Barinder Dhillon is one of them. He can be seen busy canvassing for SOPU. While most students on the campus have never seen Sahil Nanda, the presidential candidate for SOPU, it is Dhillon who is always addressing the people.

Another such SOPU leader is Dalvir Singh Goldy. He has completed his studies but is busy with the elections.

Among the other outsiders seen in the campus are Avneesh Pande, an NSUI member from Delhi who specially came to announce the panel and their u-turn on the alliance with SOPU. The party's new ally is PUSU.

Though Dhillon had got his admission cleared by Vice-Chancellor Prof R C Sobti, Department of Laws Chairperson Prof Shashi Sharma did not allow him to attend classes. Prof Sharma said: "His name figures in an FIR and according to the regulations we cannot clear admission of any student who is facing criminal charges. This makes him an outsider to the varsity."

In his defence, Dhillon said: "My admission had been cleared and I had submitted the required documents, but my case is not being considered." He is facing three cases, of which two are for stabbing a student at the UILS in the examination hall. While two of the cases are pending in courts, a challan has been issued in the third. On the other hand, Dalvir Singh Goldy has two cases against him, both for disturbing peace. Goldy recently made a comeback to SOPU after a brief stint with the NSUI in Punjab.

Dean Students Welfare Prof Naval Kishore said: "I am doing whatever I can. Acting according to the Lyngdoh Committee recommendations, explanation notices have been issued against the parties against whom I had received complaints of violating the norms."

The university had earlier issued explanation notices to PUSU for carrying out a vehicle rally, but action is pending till date.

Heading: UT Police set to nail accused professor - Indian Express
Content:
A Newly-wed youth and a sexagenarian lost their lives while those accompanying them sustained serious injuries in separate accidents on the Mohali-Kharar stretch of the busy National Highway-21 on Wednesday.

The deceased are Balwinder Singh, who was in his early 20s and Harkishan Singh, around 60. While Balwinder was an agriculturist from Jhungian village near Kharar, Harkishan was a resident of Rama Mandi in Jalandhar.

The first accident took place around 2 pm near Daon village when a recklessly driven truck-tipper, on its way from Mohali towards Kharar, rammed into a Hero Honda motorcycle, Balongi police post head Harpal Singh told Newsline.

As Balwinder, who was riding the bike, and his newly-wed wife Kuldeep fell on the highway, his head was crushed under the wheels of the truck-tipper. He died on the spot, while Kuldeep was rushed to the Mohali Civil Hospital, said the police officer.

Balwinder and Kuldeep were married around four months ago and were returning from Dadumajra after meeting a relative, said Balwinder's cousin Jaspal Singh.

In the second accident, a truck loaded with cement, on its way to Mohali from Kharar, collided head-on with a Maruti 800 near the Quila Complex around 4 pm, said Kharar City SHO Manjit Singh.

Harkishan sustained serious head injuries and died on his way to the PGI. His son Sarwan Singh, who was driving the car, and daughter-in-law sustained injuries.

Drivers of both the trucks managed to flee, leaving the vehicles. They have been booked.

'Mistreatment' at hospital
A severely injured Kuldeep was denied treatment for around 3 hours at the Mohali Civil Hospital, the police said. The emergency medical officer (EMO) refused to admit her or even administer first-aid, said Balongi police post head Harpal Singh. "The EMO kept arguing that the accident spot was outside Mohali limits and asked us to take the accident victim to the Kharar Civil Hospital," said Singh, adding that it was only after their repeated insistence that the EMO agreed to admit her, but not before 5 pm. Senior Medical Officer Dr H S Sarang said immediately after the EMO, Dr Tammana, consulted him about the case, he had asked her to admit and treat the patient without disputing the jurisdiction issue.

Heading: GMADA gets nod to acquire 1,000 acres - Indian Express
Content:
GMCH SUICIDE : Based on the reports submitted by the hospital, CFSL and PGI, cops to file chargesheet against N K Goel who faces abetment charges

More than eight months after the body of a student of the Government Medical College and Hospital (GMCH), Sector 32, was found hanging in the library, the police are all set to file a chargesheet against the professor who was earlier booked on charges of abetment to suicide.

Jaspreet Singh, an MBBS final year student, had committed suicide on January 28. Based on an inquiry report submitted by a GMCH committee, the Central Forensic Science Laboratory (CFSL) report of the suicide note and a revaluation of the exam papers of the deceased by a PGI board, the police are all set to nail Prof N K Goel, head of the department of community medicine.

The police have also added the SC/ST Act in the case registered under Section 306 (abetment to suicide) of the IPC at the Sector 34 police station. Goel, who has been granted interim bail in the case, was booked a day after Jaspreet killed himself and an inquiry was initiated.

A three-member board was formed by the PGI to re-evaluate the examination papers in which Jaspreet had failed. His family had alleged that the accused professor did not give him pass marks deliberately, because he had got admission under the scheduled caste quota, forcing him to take the extreme step.

"The PGI board found that the student deserved more marks," said UT Senior Superintendent of Police S S Srivastava.

The PGI report said the student deserved 16.5 marks out of 30, while he was given only 14 marks by the professor. Jaspreet needed 15 marks to pass. The SSP said the internal inquiry report conducted by the GMCH committee, too, pointed out that the student had told his friends that he was being harassed.

Jaspreet's suicide note, recovered four hours after his death, had accused the professor of stopping him from reappearing in the exam and harassing him because he was from the scheduled caste category.

The CFSL had in April confirmed the handwriting in the note as that of Jaspreet.

In the note, Jaspreet had also accused his two friends — Deepak Vashisht and Ajay Parveen — of harassing him. Senior officers, however, said the police investigation had so far not found any evidence against the two, as they too belonged to the SC category.

Goel could not be contacted for comments despite repeated attempts.

'I know we will get justice'
The last line of Jaspreet's suicide note read: "Sorry Dad, Sorry Mom, Sorry Didi and Preeti." His grieving family — parents and three sisters — is still finding it hard to come to terms with the reality that the bright youth who wanted to be a doctor is no more. With tears in his eyes, his father Charan Singh said: "I know we will get justice, I won't leave any stone unturned." Charan Singh has been relentlessly pursuing the matter with National Commission of Scheduled Castes (NCSC) chairman Buta Singh, who inquired about the present status of the case from senior police officers at a meeting on Tuesday.

SSP says challan filed, IO says will file today
While SSP S S Srivastava said the challan in the case was filed on September 8, Newsline found that the police were yet to produce it in court. The IG, too, had told Buta Singh on Tuesday that a chargesheet had already been filed. "The challan has been prepared and has passed the scrutiny. We are ready to file it in the court at 10 am, tomorrow," said investigating officer (IO) Harminder Singh.

Heading: School denied child his right to education: report - Indian Express
Content:
The Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) has got the district administration's nod to acquire almost 1,000 acres of additional land for road connectivity to the upcoming international airport and commercial exploitation in the proposed mixed land use zone along the roads.

The commercial exploitation will enable GMADA to bear the costs of land acquisition, construction and other requisite infrastructure in and around the airport terminal.

The Deputy Commissioner has issued a no-objection certificate to the GMADA, which has now moved the State-Level Land Acquisition Board (SLLAB) for the final nod before issuing a notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act. The 1,000 acres would be in addition to almost 306 acres already acquired in Jheourheri village for the airport terminal, GMADA Chief Administrator Vivek Partap Singh told Newsline.

The SLLAB, headed by the Financial Commissioner, Revenue, will take up GMADA's case at its next meeting expected shortly.

In view of the record compensation award of Rs 1.5 crore per acre, which has already been paid to 222 owners of the land acquired for the airport, GMADA will require almost Rs 1,500 crore for the future land acquisition.

Since a major part of the acquired land would be used for building road network, the Land Pooling Scheme, which was implemented last month for making landowners partners in the land developed after acquisition, would be adopted in this acquisition, confirmed Singh. He added that cash compensation would be offered to the landowners as per the rate fixed by the District Land Price Fixation Committee.

The additional land will be acquired to provide connectivity to the airport from Sector 20, Panchkula, through Zirakpur and also from Mohali as per the alignments approved recently by the GMADA Executive Committee, headed by Punjab Chief Secretary Ramesh Inder Singh.

Besides a six-lane road from Chandigarh to the airport, another approach road has been planned from Chhat village on the Patiala-Zirakpur highway.

The Chief Secretary has asked the public works department to take up the matter with the National Highway Authority of India to construct arms of the upcoming flyover at Zirakpur towards the Patiala highway, which would provide a smooth passage to the airport traffic coming from Shimla and Ambala.

Heading: Landscaping at Himalaya Marg in a shambles as UT, pvt firm lock horns - Indian Express
Content:
Inquiry committee recommends action against Bhavan Vidyalaya in Panchkula

After a four-month-long battle for the right to education, Nidhish Sarin, whose parents were asked to withdraw him from a Panchkula school, has a reason to rejoice. In its report submitted to the Director General, Department of School Education, Haryana, and the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights, New Delhi, a special inquiry committee formed to look into the matter finds the Bhavan Vidyalaya, Panchkula, at fault and recommends action against it.

The inquiry was conducted by District Child Welfare Officer (DCWO) Virender Singh and Programme Officer, Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) Suraj Lamba.

Four-and-a-half-year-old Nidhish was a student of UKG and had attended classes for three weeks, when the school decided to cancel his admission on the plea that he did not know cursive writing.

After Chandigarh Newsline reported the family's plight, District Commissioner Rajendra Kataria formed the special committee to inquire into the matter.

Commenting on the report, Kataria said: "The report clearly finds the school authorities guilty of denying education to the child. It suggests strict action against the school."

The decision has brought relief to Nidhish's parents who are now eagerly waiting for the action to be taken against the school.

"This is certainly a decision in favour of Nidhish who underwent a lot of mental harassment. It was very difficult for us to make him understand why he was made to sit at home. It is now to see what action is taken against the principal of the school," said Sabina Sarin, Nidhish's mother.

Principal Shashi Banerjee, however, expressed her ignorance on the report. "Let me get information about the report from the authorities first. I have no clue about it."

Blaming the school authorities for asking the parents to withdraw the child from the school, the report said there was no other reason for them to take the child back to his previous school. It said the school could not shirk their responsibility of providing education, adding that had the school acted in a more responsible manner, the child and his parents would have been spared the unnecessary harassment.

Heading: HC recalls interim relief to Chahal - Indian Express
Content:
The ongoing tiff between a private company and the UT Administration over the display of advertisement boards on the road berms has messed up the entire landscaping at Himalaya Marg.

Both the sides of one of the busiest roads of the city (road dividing Sector 34-35, 21-22, 17-18 upto Sukhna Lake road) lies in a shambles at present as the company has stopped maintenance of the landscaping done. This, after the UT Administration refused the company to fix the advertisement boards on the road berms along the road.

The agreement between the UT Administration and Tycoon Events and Promotions on behalf of a multinational cellular operator company was signed on September 2007. According to the agreement (a copy of which is with the Chandigarh Newsline), the company was supposed to do landscaping on an area measuring about 5,600 metres at Himalaya Marg. It was also responsible for the maintenance of the landscaping.

The agreement specifically mentions, "The organisation/company can display their advertisement on the allocated area by putting up billboards of size (3x2 feet) with height of 1.5 feet from the ground level. Billboards will be poles at 200 MT C/C as approved by UT Chief Architect, Chandigarh Administration."

The agreement even went to the extent of permitting the company for putting advertisement of another company as well, by mentioning a clause - "The organisation to which the permission is granted can put advertisement board of any other agency with the prior approval of UT Administration".

"The only clause, whereby which the Administration could have stopped us from putting up the advertisement boards on the road berms was if we had violated the terms and conditions of the agreement or failed to have maintained the landscaping properly, which is not so. In fact, we have even received an appreciation letter from UT Administration, which read — 'We want to appreciate Tycoon Events and Promotions on having completed the work with such panache and helping us keep the city environment healthy and beautiful'.

How could the Administration now violate the agreement, on which we have already spent Rs 25 lakh? The agreement is valid till August 2010, till which we are responsible for maintenance of the landscaping," said Jasmeet Singh, one of the directors of Tycoon Events and Promotions.

When asked, UT Home-cum-Finance Secretary Sanjay Kumar said, "We have given the road to the company for landscaping and its maintenance. They cannot put rampant advertisements on the road berms. It is not the policy of the Chandigarh Administration to allow such advertisements to be put up on road berms. Our own staff will maintain the landscaping."

Heading: Develop proper mechanism to ensure release of prisoners granted bail - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has recalled the interim relief given to B I S Chahal, media adviser to former Punjab chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh.

The court had last month directed the Punjab government to issue three days' notice prior to arresting Chahal in any fresh case.

The government had then moved the High Court, seeking recalling of the relief given to Chahal. The government took the plea that it had not been given an opportunity to put forth its case.

Allowing the application on Wednesday, the High Court recalled the interim relief granted to Chahal.

The former media adviser had moved the court, demanding blanket bail raising fears that he might be falsely implicated by the Punjab Vigilance Bureau or the police.

Chahal had alleged that he might be made a victim of political vendetta for his close association with Captain Amarinder Singh.

Heading: Full Bench to decide on petitions challenging Sikh Gurdwara Act - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court today directed the Haryana Government to evolve a firm mechanism to ensure that the prisoners who have been granted bail are released immediately and do not languish in jail once a release warrant has been issued.

The court ordered Director-General (Prosecution), Director-General (Prisons) and Director-General (Police) to jointly conduct a meeting to put in place an effective mechanism to ensure proper procedure with regard to release of prisoners after grant of bail.

The order came in response to a petition filed by social activist Hemant Goswami which listed the widespread anomalies in the system. He referred to a particular case wherein one Hawa Singh continued to languish in jail even after five days of issuance of release warrant.

During the hearing, Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur observed that there has to be no need for the guarantor or a relative of an undertrial to appease the court officials to send the release warrant to the prison or to pursue the court officers to send the release order urgently.

The responsibility was of the state and so the mechanism has to work automatically, it was stated.

On September 24, the Haryana government has been asked to inform the court about the concrete steps undertaken in this regard.

Heading: ‘Virk not cooperating with investigations’ - Indian Express
Content:
A Bunch of petitions challenging the Sikh Gurdwara Act and demanding clarity in the definition of a Sikh will now be decided by the Full Bench of the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

The High Court had issued notices to the Shiromani Gurdwara Prabhandak Committee (SGPC), Baba Farid University of Health Sciences and others on a petition by five students.

The Sikh students from various parts of Punjab had alleged that they were denied admission by Guru Ram Das Institute affiliated to Baba Farid University on the grounds that they trim their beard, pluck eyebrows and as such do not profess the Sikh religion.

The students stated they were denied admission to MBBS despite the fact that they had secured much higher marks than those who were granted admission. The petitioners were eligible for taking admission to MBBS course. It was submitted that the college conducted its own test for remaining 50 per cent seats for MBBS course which are to be filled up from amongst students, who profess Sikh religion.

"The students secured more marks than others and were still denied admission because they trim their beard or pluck their eyebrows and as such do not profess Sikh religion," argued the counsel for the five students.

The students had sought directions to the college to grant them admission even if the admissions already granted to others had to be cancelled.

The counsel for the petitioners had contented that there is no distinction between various clans of Sikhs viz, Amritdhari, Sahajdhari, Keshdhari and others.

After the High Court issued notices, the jurisdiction of the petition was widened to Haryana and Himachal since the Gurdwara Act is applicable to the two states as well.

Heading: SBI held guilty of ‘deficiency in service’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab government moved the Punjab and Haryana High Court today, seeking cancellation of bail granted to S S Virk, former director general of police (DGP), Punjab.

The Punjab government filed the petition on the ground that Virk was not cooperating with the special investigating team (SIT), constituted to probe into the disproportionate assets case pending against him.

The Punjab government further alleged that apart from not appearing in Court, he was not appearing in the trial court. The SIT had earlier sought issuance of non-bailable warrants from a lower court against Virk. Challenging the warrants sought, Virk had moved the district court in Mohali, seeking directions to restrain the SIT from evaluating his property and house in Chandigarh in Sector 27.

Virk had said that the one-member SIT, headed by S K Asthana, senior superintendent of police (SSP), Patiala, was trying to obtain non-bailable warrants for his arrest, without understanding the legal complications.

Heading: Sahara Pariwar to shell out Rs 1 lakh for harassment - Indian Express
Content:
After a widow was made to run from pillar to post for the righteous gratuity claims of her husband, the district consumer forum has directed the bank to compensate for deficiency in services. The State Bank of India (SBI) has been directed to pay Rs 5,000 as compensation, Rs 1.7 lakh gratuity claim and Rs 1,500 as litigation cost.

The complainant, one Bhagwati Devi, was an account holder with the SBI. After her husband, a peon in the office of Registrar, Cooperative Societies, Chandigarh, passed away in 2003, all the service benefits payable to her on account of her husband's death (pension, leave encashment, gratuity) were to be credited to her account. For the payment of the gratuity amount, the office of Punjab Accountant General forwarded a voucher to the treasury office with a copy to her.

She was told that the treasury office will send the voucher to SBI in Sector 7 and after clearance, will be sent to the SBI in Sector 34. After she failed to receive the amount, she approached the treasury office and was told that the endorsement has been sent to the bank.

Despite a number of visits later, she was made to run from pillar to post for more than three years. After not receiving the amount, Devi moved the forum. The complainant was supplied a copy of the letter dated addressed to SBI in Sector 34 by SBI in Sector 7 asking to intimate the Punjab Treasury Office for the issue of duplicate DCRG. After she approached the office of Accountant General requesting to issue duplicate DCRG and in pursuance to the said request of the complainant, IT prepared a duplicate DCRG towards payment of gratuity of Rs 1,77,232 and forwarded to the Treasury Office. She was told the amount will be credited within a week, but it never was. The bank authorities also refrained from attending the proceedings of the case.

The forum found that there is a marked and perceptible deficiency in service on part of the bank in not giving the credit of Rs 1,77,232 to the account of the complainant.

Heading: The show goes on - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed Sahara India Pariwar to pay Rs 1 lakh compensation for causing mental and physical harassment by rendering deficient services. The company was similarly directed to pay Rs 2.5 lakh in a case on Tuesday.

The company has also been directed to pay Rs 2,621 deducted by them as TDS on the amount of Rs 1,22,289 refunded to the complainant in addition of the litigation cost of Rs 2,100.

The complainant, Malkiat Singh Rahui, had availed the Sahara City Home Township scheme and deposited Rs 1,00,000 towards allotment of an independent flat with four bedrooms on the area of 8,844 square feet. The price of the said flat was Rs 45.21 lakh. According to the said scheme, the complainant was to be given top priority in the allotment of housing unit on the first-come-first-serve basis. The complainant said that the company informed him that the allotment of the first phase was completed but his name was not considered by mistake. His grievance failed to evoke any response and thus he moved the forum.

Sahara India, in its reply, stated that they have returned Rs 1,22,289 after deducting Rs 2,621 as tax to the complainant, which was received by him on March 25, 2008. It said the scheme was tentative and was subject to various other visible terms and conditions contained in the brochure and passbook-cum-certificate.

The forum found that Sahara India failed to show any document, which proves that the policy adopted by them was truly 'first-come- first-serve' basis. "They had not brought on record any such list of applicants with dates and nor any list was submitted by them for allotting the flats to the persons, who had registered with them," ruled the forum.

Heading: INLD and BJP councillors walk out of MC meet - Indian Express
Content:
At the Department of Indian Theatre, the stage is always set for creative acts

Year after year, the talented few take their first step towards Act One, on the wooden stage of the Department of Indian Theatre, Panjab University. Here, dreams are nurtured, creativity chiselled and love for theatre given movement and motivation. Here, there is scope for drama and ingenuity. It is a place where there is no method to the madness. Just passion, pure passion for theatre is the rule and exception.

It began with one man's dream to nurture talent in this part of the country and give those with a fire in their bellies and a vision in their eyes to become complete theatre-persons, an opportunity at par with the best in the country.

"We owe it all to the vision of Balwant Gargi," chairperson of the department and Sangeet Natak Akademi award winner Prof (Dr) Mahendra Kumar looks back with pride and fondness.

Kumar has seen the department since the first session in 1972 and has numerous dramatic stories to narrate.

"I have been here since 1969, before the department came into being. It all began when Balwant Gargi came here to stage a play and proposed a department of theatre to the then vice-chancellor, Suraj Bhan, who immediately invited him to be a part and initiator of it," says Kumar, who was then a student at the Government College of Arts.

After returning from the US, it was Gargi's first job, and he chose to stay on the campus and began scouting for talent from various departments of the university to stage a play, Gagan Main Thal. The search for an art director, a field which was given top priority by Gargi in his plays, led him to the Arts College and then to Kumar, who had keen interest in literature and was a fabulous painter with a splendid sense of design. And so started an association which was to go a long way and result in establishment of a department, which is now a name to reckon with, having produced actors like Anupam and Kirron Kher, Mangal Dhillon, Meeta Vashisht, Navneet Nishaan, Anita Kanwar and also Harry Baweja, Amrik Gill, Rani Balbir Kaur, Channi, Umesh Kant to name a few.

Gargi infused life and art into an empty, deserted, but aesthetic building, which already had an open-air theatre and it was Kumar who designed each nook and corner, chairs, tables, green rooms and studio theatre of the department. "The vision and imagination was all Gargi's," Kumar puts it modestly.

The small studio theatre, which had a wooden floor and was designed in such a way that audiences could sit on three sides, was the place for the first rehearsal, performance, research and many a heart-to-heart. And artistes like Karanth, Bansi Kaul, Elkazi, Raina came to the department on the invitation of Gargi to teach and share their experience and talent.

"Theatre came to Chandigarh with this department, with top theatre directors of the country choosing to stage their best productions here. After establishing and actively being part of the department, Gargi retired in 1977 and here we are, keeping his dreams alive and giving many the opportunity to understand and live this complete art — theatre," Kumar looks ahead.

Yes, the show must go on...

Heading: Four cops suspended for manhandling woman - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP and INLD councillors boycotted the general body meeting of the Municipal Council held on Wednesday at the Indradhanush Auditorium, Sector 5, Panchkula.

While the councillors claimed that the meeting was being conducted in the presence of outsiders, Executive Officer (MC) O P Sihag said the outsiders were family members of the nominated councillors who had come to take the oath of office.

"After we learnt that the general body meeting of the MC was being held in the presence of more than 150 outsiders, we decided to stage a walkout. President Ravinder Rawal was told that it was a special meeting of the councillors and not a public meeting," said BJP councillor V K Sood. He added that holding the meeting at the Indradhanush Auditorium in Sector 5 instead of the MC office was also objected.

Sood added that it made little sense in wasting money for booking the auditorium when the meeting has been held at the MC office for long.

"Though we requested to remove the oath-taking ceremony of the nominated councillors from the agenda so that their family members and supporters could be asked to leave, they did not agree. We, therefore, decided to stage a walkout", added Sood.

The INLD councillors also boycotted the meeting. Talking to Newsline, O P Sihag said, "Three nominated councillors were to be administered oath because of which their family members and supporters had gathered. They were to leave the auditorium immediately after the ceremony."

The main points in the 32-point agenda of the meeting included the installation of sodium vapour lights for internal roads, road gullies to be repaired by the Haryana Urban Development Authority and maintained by the MC and special machines to clean the city roads.

Heading: 200 BPL members trained under job scheme awarded - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana Police today suspended four police officers who had allegedly manhandled a Yamunanagar woman in 2007. Shamshida, a resident of village Mustafabad in Yamunanagar, had met DGP Ranjiv Dalal on September 8 at the police headquarters in Sector 6, Panchkula, and threatened to kill herself if the guilty were not brought to book.

The woman had claimed in her complaint that two shopkeepers of Yamunanagar, along with the village sarpanch and four police officers, including the SHO of the Chappar police station, manhandled her, after which she suffered a miscarriage in 2007.

The four police officers suspended late in the evening are SHO Inspector Ram Datt, ASI Rajeshwar, Head Constable Ishwar and Subhash. "After Shamshida met the DGP on September 8, he had assured her of justice and set up an enquiry committee under the leadership of Charu Bali, AIG (Administration). Shamshida was specially escorted by the women police officials and was dropped back to her village in a police van and was provided complete security till the time Charu Bali reached the village to investigate into the matter the next morning," said a spokesperson of the DGP office.

It was found that the four police officials were not only involved in the case but had also implicated the woman in a false case.

"The woman had claimed that she had purchased a washing machine in 2004 from the shop of Sonu and Monu at Yamunanagar. As the piece was defective, she asked them to replace the machine but they refused. The woman then approached the police. The shopkeepers, on the other hand, connived with the sarpanch and the four police officials and beat her up to the extend that she suffered miscarriage on the intervening night of April 13 and 14, 2007," said the spokesperson.

An FIR was registered only on July 12, 2008, on the complaint of the woman but no action had been taken against the accused till now.

Heading: Snag stalls rail bookings at reservation counter - Indian Express
Content:
At a function organised by the Jan Shikshan Sansthan on Wednesday, nearly 200 persons from the Below Poverty Line (BPL) category were awarded certificates and stipends. The beneficiaries were those who had completed courses started by JSS in collaboration with the Municipal Corporation under Swaran Jayanti Shahri Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY).

The courses, including computer application, cutting and tailoring and soft toy making, aimed at upgrading the economic standards of the poor by providing them skills to support themselves. A stipend of Rs 1.19 lakh was distributed among the beneficiaries.

Municipal Commissioner Dr Roshan Sunkaria, the chief guest, urged bankers to relax conditions for credit to the BPL families. He assured help for marketing the products prepared by the beneficiaries of JSS.

K L Zakir, chairman of JSS advised BPL beneficiaries to form self-help groups to collaboratively help increase their earnings.

Heading: Mohali to have yet another township soon - Indian Express
Content:
Residents who had gone to the railway reservation counter at ISBT, Sector 17, to book train tickets had a harrowing time on Wednesday, owing to a technical fault in the server. "I have been standing in the queue for an hour, waiting for the server to start functioning. It is very difficult to stand in such a cramped place, without proper ventilation. On top of it, we do not know when the error will be rectified," said Rahul, who had come to book a ticket for the Shatabdi Express.

The booking officials, meanwhile, said the error was due to the failure of the postal and telegraph microwave server and efforts were being made to check and correct the same. The public heaved a sigh of relief after the services were reinstalled after nearly two hours.

Heading: By month-end, enjoy your favourite snacks late in the night - Indian Express
Content:
Adding to the existing real estate development in Mohali, JTPL City, an integrated township, is coming up on 85 acres in the town. JTPL Townships Private Ltd, the developer, has already obtained the approved licence from the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) for 70 acres.

JTPL City Mohali, a new generation township is a self-contained residential, commercial, entertainment and recreational hub for people from different walks of life. A mall and a hotel are also in the pipeline, to be developed within the township.

Located on the Kharar-Landran road next to Sector 104, the JTPL City offers numerous location and accessibility advantages like access to the railway station and upcoming international airport. It has been strategically planned and is an impeccable township with vaastu and numerological compliance. Most significantly, it will offer a contemporary and elite environment along with modern conveniences exuding an international experience.

JTPL Townships is a part of JMD Conglomerate. The group is known for its range of edible oils and packaged drinking water. The company has ventured into real estate industry with a mission to set up a network of completely self-contained townships across the country.

Dr V P Gupta, chairman, said: "Mohali has become one of the most preferred cities in the world. We are proud to come up with an integrated township in such a strategically located place. This township is our sincere endeavour to provide people with world-class infrastructural facilities".
